```ts
// The runner's layout (design 7.2): its own state under AGFLOW_HOME/runner, the vaults and the attempt clones, plus
// the short private directories under /tmp that Claude attempts use as CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR.
import { createHash, getRandomValues } from 'node:crypto';
import { chmodSync, lstatSync, mkdirSync, realpathSync } from 'node:fs';
import { homedir } from 'node:os';
import { join, resolve } from 'node:path';

export interface RunnerPaths {
  /** AGFLOW_HOME, ~/.agflow by default. */
  home: string;
  /** Runner state; agents read only their own Claude project directory in it (design 7.6). */
  runner: string;
  config: string;
  db: string;
  lock: string;
  socket: string;
  logs: string;
  runnerLog: string;
  attemptLog(attemptId: string): string;
  homes: {
    /** CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for agents. */
    claude: string;
    /** CODEX_HOME for agents. */
    codex: string;
    /** The empty HOME of the codex app-server process. */
    codexUser: string;
  };
  /** Pinned vendor binaries; vendorBinary gives paths relative to `runner`. */
  vendor: string;
  /** GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL of the runner's own git. */
  gitConfig: string;
  gitExcludes: string;
  /** Dependency caches and tmp of one project. */
  prep(project: string): string;
  /** An agent's .git, moved aside at take-over. */
  forensics(attemptId: string): string;
  vaults: string;
  vault(project: string): string;
  quarantine(project: string, attemptId: string): string;
  /** A base checkout of main, Claude's project config root. */
  baseCheckout(project: string, sha: string): string;
  work: string;
  /** The attempt clone, the agent's cwd. */
  clone(project: string, attemptId: string): string;
}

/** AGFLOW_HOME, or ~/.agflow, always absolute: agents get paths under it from a different working directory. */
export function agflowHome(env: Record<string, string | undefined> = process.env): string {
  return resolve(env.AGFLOW_HOME || join(homedir(), '.agflow'));
}

// Project keys and attempt ids become directory names; anything else that reaches here is a bug, not a path.
const SAFE_NAME = /^(?!\.\.?$)[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/;

function segment(name: string): string {
  if (!SAFE_NAME.test(name)) throw new Error(`not a safe path name: ${JSON.stringify(name)}`);
  return name;
}

export function runnerPaths(home: string = agflowHome()): RunnerPaths {
  const runner = join(home, 'runner');
  const logs = join(runner, 'logs');
  const vaults = join(home, 'vaults');
  const work = join(home, 'work');
  return {
    home,
    runner,
    config: join(runner, 'runner.json'),
    db: join(runner, 'runner.db'),
    lock: join(runner, 'runner.lock'),
    socket: join(runner, 'runner.sock'),
    logs,
    runnerLog: join(logs, 'runner.log'),
    attemptLog: (attemptId) => join(logs, 'attempts', `${segment(attemptId)}.log`),
    homes: {
      claude: join(runner, 'homes', 'claude'),
      codex: join(runner, 'homes', 'codex'),
      codexUser: join(runner, 'homes', 'codex-user'),
    },
    vendor: join(runner, 'vendor'),
    gitConfig: join(runner, 'git', 'local.gitconfig'),
    gitExcludes: join(runner, 'git', 'excludes'),
    prep: (project) => join(runner, 'prep', segment(project)),
    forensics: (attemptId) => join(runner, 'forensics', segment(attemptId)),
    vaults,
    vault: (project) => join(vaults, `${segment(project)}.git`),
    quarantine: (project, attemptId) => join(vaults, `${segment(project)}.quarantine`, segment(attemptId)),
    baseCheckout: (project, sha) => {
      if (!/^[0-9a-f]{12,40}$/.test(sha)) throw new Error(`expected a commit sha, not ${JSON.stringify(sha)}`);
      return join(vaults, `${segment(project)}.base`, sha.slice(0, 12));
    },
    work,
    clone: (project, attemptId) => join(work, segment(project), segment(attemptId)),
  };
}

/**
 * A filesystem-safe id for one project of one hub: a readable slug of the name and a hash of the hub URL and the
 * name, so two hubs with a project of the same name never share a vault. It stays short, because clone paths end up
 * in Claude's project directory names.
 */
export function projectKey(hubUrl: string, projectName: string): string {
  const slug =
    projectName
      .toLowerCase()
      .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-')
      .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '')
      .slice(0, 24)
      .replace(/-+$/, '') || 'project';
  const hash = createHash('sha256')
    .update(`${hubUrl.replace(/\/+$/, '')}\n${projectName}`)
    .digest('hex')
    .slice(0, 10);
  return `${slug}-${hash}`;
}

/** Beyond this length of <dir>/claude-<uid>, Claude Code silently falls back to the shared /tmp/claude-<uid>. */
export const MAX_CLAUDE_TMP_BYTES = 44;

const ID_ALPHABET = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789';

function randomTmpId(): string {
  return Array.from(getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(6)), (byte) => ID_ALPHABET[byte % ID_ALPHABET.length]).join('');
}

export interface AttemptTmpDirOptions {
  /** /tmp by default. */
  root?: string;
  uid?: number;
  randomId?: () => string;
}

/**
 * Creates a new private <root>/agf/<6 chars> directory (mode 0700) for one Claude attempt. It refuses a root whose
 * <dir>/claude-<uid> would exceed 44 bytes, measured on both the given and the real path, since the CLI may see
 * either.
 */
export function makeAttemptTmpDir(options: AttemptTmpDirOptions = {}): string {
  const root = options.root ?? '/tmp';
  const uid = options.uid ?? process.getuid?.() ?? 0;
  const randomId = options.randomId ?? randomTmpId;
  const tail = `/agf/${'x'.repeat(6)}/claude-${uid}`;
  const longest = Math.max(Buffer.byteLength(root + tail), Buffer.byteLength(realpathSync(root) + tail));
  if (longest > MAX_CLAUDE_TMP_BYTES) {
    throw new Error(
      `the temporary root ${root} is too long: ${root}${tail} must fit in ${MAX_CLAUDE_TMP_BYTES} bytes, ` +
        `or Claude Code falls back to the shared /tmp/claude-${uid}`,
    );
  }
  const parent = join(root, 'agf');
  mkdirSync(parent, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
  // A shared /tmp lets anyone create agf first; only a real directory of our own will do.
  const stat = lstatSync(parent);
  if (!stat.isDirectory() || (process.getuid && stat.uid !== process.getuid())) {
    throw new Error(`${parent} is not a private directory of this user`);
  }
  chmodSync(parent, 0o700);
  for (let tries = 0; tries < 100; tries += 1) {
    const dir = join(parent, randomId());
    try {
      mkdirSync(dir, { mode: 0o700 });
    } catch (error) {
      if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'EEXIST') continue;
      throw error;
    }
    chmodSync(dir, 0o700);
    return dir;
  }
  throw new Error(`no free directory name under ${parent}`);
}
```

```ts
// The one place for each vendor binary the runner runs (design 7.1, X-10). The runner installs its own pinned
// binaries under runner/vendor and never uses or changes the owner's installs.
import { join } from 'node:path';
import type { Vendor } from '@agflow/core';

export interface VendorPin {
  /** The version `<binary> --version` prints. */
  version: string;
  /** The npm package the binary comes from, at packageVersion. */
  package: string;
  packageVersion: string;
}

export interface ClaudePin extends VendorPin {
  /** The @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk version that bundles this CLI; packages/runner depends on it. */
  sdkVersion: string;
}

export interface PlatformPins {
  claude: ClaudePin;
  codex: VendorPin;
}

/** Keyed by `<process.platform>-<process.arch>`. M2 pins darwin-arm64 only; elsewhere preflight reports it. */
export const VENDOR_PINS: Partial<Record<string, PlatformPins>> = {
  'darwin-arm64': {
    // The claude file of the SDK's platform package, which ships the CLI the SDK was built with.
    claude: {
      version: '2.1.285',
      sdkVersion: '0.3.285',
      package: '@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64',
      packageVersion: '0.3.285',
    },
    // Codex has no separate platform package; the platform build of @openai/codex carries the whole vendor tree.
    codex: { version: '0.159.2', package: '@openai/codex', packageVersion: '0.159.2-darwin-arm64' },
  },
};

export function vendorPlatform(platform: string = process.platform, arch: string = process.arch): string {
  return `${platform}-${arch}`;
}

const VERSION = /^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/;

/** A vendor binary's path relative to RunnerPaths.runner; callers join it. */
export function vendorBinary(vendor: Vendor, version: string): string {
  if (!VERSION.test(version)) throw new Error(`not a vendor version: ${JSON.stringify(version)}`);
  return vendor === 'claude'
    ? join('vendor', 'claude', version, 'claude')
    : join('vendor', 'codex', version, 'bin', 'codex');
}

const VERSION_OUTPUT: Record<Vendor, RegExp> = {
  claude: /^(\d+\.\d+\.\d+) \(Claude Code\)$/,
  codex: /^codex-cli (\d+\.\d+\.\d+)$/,
};

/** The version in a vendor binary's `--version` output, or null for any other output. */
export function parseVendorVersion(vendor: Vendor, output: string): string | null {
  return output.trim().match(VERSION_OUTPUT[vendor])?.[1] ?? null;
}
```

### Task 2: packages/testkit: git fixtures and the refusing proxy

`packages/testkit` is the shared test package of M2 (design 13, 15.1, X-20, X-44). Its git fixtures (`gitIn`, `originRepo`, `commitFiles`) make local bare origins with a clean git environment: no inherited `GIT_*` variable, no system or global config and no `~/.config/git`, so the owner's ignore and attribute files never reach a test. `startRefusingProxy` refuses and records every CONNECT and absolute-URI request, so the vendor suites can assert that no external connection succeeded. The testkit's main entry imports runner types only; the runner devDepends on the testkit, a workspace cycle that Bun 1.3.11 installs and resolves.

```ts
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { commitFiles, gitIn, type OriginRepo, originRepo } from '../src/git-fixtures';

// Every test here runs git or agent processes, which take several times as long on a machine loaded by other suites.
setDefaultTimeout(30_000);

const origins: OriginRepo[] = [];
const dirs: string[] = [];
afterEach(() => {
  for (const origin of origins.splice(0)) origin.remove();
  for (const dir of dirs.splice(0)) rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
});

async function origin(files: Record<string, string>): Promise<OriginRepo> {
  const made = await originRepo(files);
  origins.push(made);
  return made;
}

function tempDir(): string {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'agflow-gitfix-'));
  dirs.push(dir);
  return dir;
}

describe('originRepo', () => {
  test('makes a bare origin whose main holds the files', async () => {
    const repo = await origin({ 'README.md': '# demo\n', 'src/app.ts': 'export {};\n' });
    expect(await gitIn(repo.path, ['rev-parse', '--is-bare-repository'])).toBe('true');
    expect(await gitIn(repo.path, ['symbolic-ref', 'HEAD'])).toBe('refs/heads/main');
    expect(await gitIn(repo.path, ['rev-parse', 'refs/heads/main'])).toBe(repo.mainSha);
    expect(repo.mainSha).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{40}$/);
    expect((await gitIn(repo.path, ['ls-tree', '-r', '--name-only', 'main'])).split('\n')).toEqual([
      'README.md',
      'src/app.ts',
    ]);
    expect(await gitIn(repo.path, ['show', 'main:src/app.ts'])).toBe('export {};');
  });

  test('remove() deletes the origin and its directory', async () => {
    const repo = await originRepo({ a: '1\n' });
    repo.remove();
    expect(await Bun.file(join(repo.path, 'HEAD')).exists()).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe('commitFiles', () => {
  test('writes, deletes and commits files on a new branch from main and pushes it', async () => {
    const repo = await origin({ 'a.txt': 'a\n', 'gone.txt': 'x\n' });
    const sha = await commitFiles(repo.path, {
      branch: 'agflow/T-1-feature',
      files: { 'a.txt': 'changed\n', 'gone.txt': null, 'deep/new.txt': 'new\n' },
      message: 'work on T-1',
    });
    expect(await gitIn(repo.path, ['rev-parse', 'refs/heads/agflow/T-1-feature'])).toBe(sha);
    expect(await gitIn(repo.path, ['rev-parse', `${sha}^`])).toBe(repo.mainSha);
    expect(await gitIn(repo.path, ['log', '-1', '--format=%s', sha])).toBe('work on T-1');
    expect((await gitIn(repo.path, ['ls-tree', '-r', '--name-only', sha])).split('\n')).toEqual([
      'a.txt',
      'deep/new.txt',
    ]);
    expect(await gitIn(repo.path, ['show', `${sha}:a.txt`])).toBe('changed');
    expect(await gitIn(repo.path, ['rev-parse', 'refs/heads/main'])).toBe(repo.mainSha);
  });

  test('builds on the tip of an existing branch', async () => {
    const repo = await origin({ 'a.txt': 'a\n' });
    const first = await commitFiles(repo.path, { branch: 'topic', files: { 'b.txt': 'b\n' } });
    const second = await commitFiles(repo.path, { branch: 'topic', files: { 'c.txt': 'c\n' } });
    expect(await gitIn(repo.path, ['rev-parse', `${second}^`])).toBe(first);
    expect((await gitIn(repo.path, ['ls-tree', '-r', '--name-only', second])).split('\n')).toEqual([
      'a.txt',
      'b.txt',
      'c.txt',
    ]);
  });

  test('can start a new branch from another commit and move main', async () => {
    const repo = await origin({ 'a.txt': 'a\n' });
    const topic = await commitFiles(repo.path, { branch: 'topic', files: { 'b.txt': 'b\n' } });
    const fork = await commitFiles(repo.path, { branch: 'fork', from: topic, files: { 'c.txt': 'c\n' } });
    expect(await gitIn(repo.path, ['rev-parse', `${fork}^`])).toBe(topic);
    const main = await commitFiles(repo.path, { branch: 'main', files: { 'a.txt': 'a2\n' } });
    expect(await gitIn(repo.path, ['rev-parse', 'refs/heads/main'])).toBe(main);
    expect(await gitIn(repo.path, ['rev-parse', `${main}^`])).toBe(repo.mainSha);
  });

  test('commits with the testkit identity', async () => {
    const repo = await origin({ 'a.txt': 'a\n' });
    expect(await gitIn(repo.path, ['log', '-1', '--format=%an <%ae>|%cn <%ce>', 'main'])).toBe(
      'agflow test <test@agflow.invalid>|agflow test <test@agflow.invalid>',
    );
  });
});

describe('gitIn', () => {
  test("runs git without the user's global or system config or inherited GIT_ variables", async () => {
    const repo = await origin({ 'a.txt': 'a\n' });
    const global = join(tempDir(), 'gitconfig');
    writeFileSync(global, '[core]\n\thooksPath = /planted-global\n');
    const system = join(tempDir(), 'system-gitconfig');
    writeFileSync(system, '[core]\n\thooksPath = /planted-system\n');
    const saved = { GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: process.env.GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GIT_DIR: process.env.GIT_DIR };
    process.env.GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL = global;
    process.env.GIT_DIR = join(tempDir(), 'not-a-repo');
    try {
      expect(await gitIn(repo.path, ['config', '--get', 'core.hooksPath'], { allowFailure: true })).toBe('');
      // GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM wins over a system file named by GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM.
      expect(
        await gitIn(repo.path, ['config', '--get', 'core.hooksPath'], {
          env: { GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM: system },
          allowFailure: true,
        }),
      ).toBe('');
      expect(await gitIn(repo.path, ['rev-parse', 'main'])).toBe(repo.mainSha);
      const scopes = await gitIn(repo.path, ['config', '--show-scope', '--list']);
      const outside = scopes.split('\n').filter((line) => !/^(local|command)\t/.test(line));
      expect(outside).toEqual([]);
    } finally {
      for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(saved)) {
        if (value === undefined) delete process.env[name];
        else process.env[name] = value;
      }
    }
  });

  test("ignores the user's default ignore and attributes files under ~/.config/git", async () => {
    const repo = await origin({ 'a.txt': 'a\n' });
    const home = tempDir();
    mkdirSync(join(home, '.config', 'git'), { recursive: true });
    writeFileSync(join(home, '.config', 'git', 'ignore'), '.env\n.claude/.cc-writes/\n');
    writeFileSync(join(home, '.config', 'git', 'attributes'), '* planted=yes\n');
    const saved = { HOME: process.env.HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME: process.env.XDG_CONFIG_HOME };
    process.env.HOME = home;
    delete process.env.XDG_CONFIG_HOME;
    try {
      const sha = await commitFiles(repo.path, {
        branch: 'topic',
        files: { '.env': 'SECRET=1\n', '.claude/.cc-writes/staged.json': '{}\n' },
      });
      expect((await gitIn(repo.path, ['ls-tree', '-r', '--name-only', sha])).split('\n')).toEqual([
        '.claude/.cc-writes/staged.json',
        '.env',
        'a.txt',
      ]);
      const work = tempDir();
      await gitIn(work, ['clone', '--quiet', repo.path, '.']);
      expect(await gitIn(work, ['check-attr', '-a', '--', 'a.txt'])).toBe('');
    } finally {
      for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(saved)) {
        if (value === undefined) delete process.env[name];
        else process.env[name] = value;
      }
    }
  });

  test("throws with git's message on failure, unless failure is allowed", async () => {
    const dir = tempDir();
    await expect(gitIn(dir, ['rev-parse', 'HEAD'])).rejects.toThrow(
      /git rev-parse HEAD failed .*not a git repository/s,
    );
    expect(await gitIn(dir, ['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], { allowFailure: true })).toBe('');
  });

  test('passes stdin and extra environment variables', async () => {
    const repo = await origin({ 'a.txt': 'a\n' });
    expect(await gitIn(repo.path, ['hash-object', '--stdin'], { input: 'hello\n' })).toBe(
      'ce013625030ba8dba906f756967f9e9ca394464a',
    );
    expect(await gitIn(repo.path, ['var', 'GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT'], { env: { GIT_AUTHOR_NAME: 'Someone' } })).toMatch(
      /^Someone <test@agflow\.invalid>/,
    );
  });
});
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join, relative, resolve } from 'node:path';

const testkit = join(import.meta.dir, '..');
const src = join(testkit, 'src');
const transpiler = new Bun.Transpiler({ loader: 'ts' });

/** A relative specifier as Bun resolves it: the file itself, with .ts, or its index.ts. */
function resolveRelative(from: string, specifier: string): string {
  const base = resolve(dirname(from), specifier);
  const found = [base, `${base}.ts`, join(base, 'index.ts')].find((path) => existsSync(path) && path.endsWith('.ts'));
  if (!found) throw new Error(`${relative(testkit, from)} imports ${specifier}, which does not resolve`);
  return found;
}

/**
 * Every source file the main entry reaches through its relative imports and re-exports. Other entries (harness/,
 * scenarios/, live.ts, the vendor fakes) are not reached and may import the runner (design 13).
 */
function mainSources(): string[] {
  const reached = new Set<string>();
  const pending = [join(src, 'index.ts')];
  for (let file = pending.pop(); file !== undefined; file = pending.pop()) {
    if (reached.has(file)) continue;
    reached.add(file);
    // scanImports covers import and export ... from statements and leaves out type-only ones.
    for (const { path } of transpiler.scanImports(readFileSync(file, 'utf8'))) {
      if (path.startsWith('./') || path.startsWith('../')) pending.push(resolveRelative(file, path));
    }
  }
  return [...reached];
}

describe('the testkit package', () => {
  test('its main entry imports runner types only', () => {
    const files = mainSources();
    expect(files).toContain(join(src, 'index.ts'));
    expect(files).toContain(join(src, 'git-fixtures.ts'));
    for (const file of files) {
      const runtime = transpiler.scanImports(readFileSync(file, 'utf8')).map((entry) => entry.path);
      const runner = runtime.filter((path) => path.startsWith('@agflow/runner'));
      expect({ file: relative(testkit, file), runner }).toEqual({ file: relative(testkit, file), runner: [] });
    }
  });

  test('has no exports map, so deep imports of its sources resolve', () => {
    const manifest = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(testkit, 'package.json'), 'utf8'));
    expect(manifest.exports).toBeUndefined();
    expect(manifest.main).toBe('./src/index.ts');
    expect(manifest.devDependencies['@anthropic-ai/sdk']).toBe('1.3.0');
  });

  test('resolves the runner and its sources by deep import, and the runner resolves the testkit', () => {
    expect(Bun.resolveSync('@agflow/runner/src/vendor/pins.ts', testkit)).toBe(
      join(testkit, '..', 'runner', 'src', 'vendor', 'pins.ts'),
    );
    expect(Bun.resolveSync('@agflow/testkit/src/git-fixtures.ts', join(testkit, '..', 'runner'))).toBe(
      join(src, 'git-fixtures.ts'),
    );
    expect(Bun.resolveSync('@agflow/testkit', join(testkit, '..', 'runner'))).toBe(join(src, 'index.ts'));
  });
});
```

```ts
import { afterEach, describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { connect } from 'node:net';
import { type RefusingProxy, startRefusingProxy } from '../src/refusing-proxy';

const proxies: RefusingProxy[] = [];
afterEach(async () => {
  for (const proxy of proxies.splice(0)) await proxy.close();
});

async function proxy(): Promise<RefusingProxy> {
  const started = await startRefusingProxy();
  proxies.push(started);
  return started;
}

/** A request that never got a successful answer, whether the client threw or saw the proxy's refusal. */
async function outcome(request: Promise<Response>): Promise<number | 'failed'> {
  return request.then(
    (response) => response.status,
    () => 'failed' as const,
  );
}

describe('startRefusingProxy', () => {
  test('refuses and records a CONNECT tunnel', async () => {
    const refusing = await proxy();
    expect(refusing.url).toMatch(/^http:\/\/127\.0\.0\.1:\d+$/);
    expect([403, 'failed']).toContain(await outcome(fetch('https://example.com/', { proxy: refusing.url })));
    expect(refusing.refused).toEqual([
      { kind: 'connect', method: 'CONNECT', target: 'example.com:443', at: expect.any(Number) },
    ]);
  });

  test('answers an absolute-URI request with 403 and records it', async () => {
    const refusing = await proxy();
    const response = await fetch('http://example.com/path?q=1', { proxy: refusing.url });
    expect(response.status).toBe(403);
    expect(refusing.refused).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(refusing.refused[0]).toMatchObject({ kind: 'http', method: 'GET' });
    expect(refusing.refused[0]?.target).toMatch(/^http:\/\/example\.com(:80)?\/path\?q=1$/);
  });

  test('a request sent to the proxy as a server, or to a local server without it, is not recorded', async () => {
    const refusing = await proxy();
    const direct = await fetch(`${refusing.url}/`);
    expect(direct.status).toBe(400);
    expect(refusing.refused).toEqual([]);
    const server = Bun.serve({ port: 0, hostname: '127.0.0.1', fetch: () => new Response('ok') });
    try {
      const response = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${server.port}/`);
      expect(await response.text()).toBe('ok');
    } finally {
      server.stop(true);
    }
    expect(refusing.refused).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('close() stops the proxy', async () => {
    const refusing = await startRefusingProxy();
    await refusing.close();
    const refusedConnection = await new Promise<boolean>((resolve) => {
      const socket = connect(refusing.port, '127.0.0.1');
      socket.on('connect', () => {
        socket.destroy();
        resolve(false);
      });
      socket.on('error', () => resolve(true));
    });
    expect(refusedConnection).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

```ts
// Local bare origins for runner tests (design 15): nothing here reaches the network, and no git command reads the
// developer's own git configuration.
import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';

/** The author and committer of every fixture commit. */
export const FIXTURE_IDENTITY = { name: 'agflow test', email: 'test@agflow.invalid' } as const;

export interface GitInOptions {
  /** Added after the clean environment, so a test can set its own GIT_ variables. */
  env?: Record<string, string>;
  input?: string;
  /** Answer '' instead of throwing when git exits non-zero. */
  allowFailure?: boolean;
}

/** Holds no git files, so git's default ignore and attributes files ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/...) do not exist. */
const NO_XDG_CONFIG = '/nonexistent/agflow-testkit';

/**
 * The caller's environment without its GIT_ variables (a hook's GIT_DIR would point git at the wrong repository),
 * without the global and system config files, and without the default ~/.config/git/ignore and attributes, which git
 * reads even when GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL is /dev/null and which would silently leave files such as .env out of commits.
 */
function cleanEnv(extra: Record<string, string> = {}): Record<string, string> {
  const env: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(process.env)) {
    if (value !== undefined && !name.startsWith('GIT_')) env[name] = value;
  }
  return {
    ...env,
    GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: '1',
    GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: '/dev/null',
    GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: '0',
    XDG_CONFIG_HOME: NO_XDG_CONFIG,
    ...extra,
  };
}

const FIXTURE_FLAGS = [
  '-c',
  `user.name=${FIXTURE_IDENTITY.name}`,
  '-c',
  `user.email=${FIXTURE_IDENTITY.email}`,
  '-c',
  'init.defaultBranch=main',
];

/** Runs git in dir and gives its trimmed output. It throws with git's own message when git fails. */
export async function gitIn(dir: string, args: string[], options: GitInOptions = {}): Promise<string> {
  const proc = Bun.spawn(['git', ...FIXTURE_FLAGS, ...args], {
    cwd: dir,
    env: cleanEnv(options.env),
    stdin: options.input === undefined ? 'ignore' : Buffer.from(options.input),
    stdout: 'pipe',
    stderr: 'pipe',
  });
  const [stdout, stderr, code] = await Promise.all([
    new Response(proc.stdout).text(),
    new Response(proc.stderr).text(),
    proc.exited,
  ]);
  if (code === 0) return stdout.trim();
  if (options.allowFailure) return '';
  throw new Error(`git ${args.join(' ')} failed (exit ${code}) in ${dir}: ${stderr.trim()}`);
}

export interface OriginRepo {
  /** The temporary directory that holds the origin. */
  root: string;
  /** The bare repository, usable as a remote URL. */
  path: string;
  /** main's first commit, which holds the files. */
  mainSha: string;
  remove(): void;
}

/** A new bare origin under a temporary directory, whose main holds the files in one commit. */
export async function originRepo(files: Record<string, string>): Promise<OriginRepo> {
  const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'agflow-origin-'));
  const path = join(root, 'origin.git');
  try {
    await gitIn(root, ['init', '--quiet', '--bare', '--initial-branch=main', path]);
    const mainSha = await commitFiles(path, { branch: 'main', files, message: 'initial commit' });
    return { root, path, mainSha, remove: () => rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true }) };
  } catch (error) {
    rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true });
    throw error;
  }
}

export interface FileChange {
  branch: string;
  /** Content to write, or null to delete the file. Directories are created as needed. */
  files: Record<string, string | null>;
  message?: string;
  /** The commit a new branch starts from; main by default. An existing branch always builds on its tip. */
  from?: string;
}

/**
 * Commits the change on a branch of a fresh working clone of the origin and pushes it, as a person or another
 * machine would. It gives the new commit's sha.
 */
export async function commitFiles(origin: string, change: FileChange): Promise<string> {
  const work = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'agflow-work-'));
  try {
    await gitIn(work, ['clone', '--quiet', origin, '.']);
    const has = async (ref: string) =>
      (await gitIn(work, ['rev-parse', '--verify', '--quiet', ref], { allowFailure: true })) !== '';
    if (await has(`refs/remotes/origin/${change.branch}`)) {
      await gitIn(work, ['checkout', '--quiet', '-B', change.branch, `refs/remotes/origin/${change.branch}`]);
    } else if (change.from !== undefined) {
      await gitIn(work, ['checkout', '--quiet', '-B', change.branch, change.from]);
    } else if (await has('refs/remotes/origin/main')) {
      await gitIn(work, ['checkout', '--quiet', '-B', change.branch, 'refs/remotes/origin/main']);
    } else {
      await gitIn(work, ['checkout', '--quiet', '--orphan', change.branch]);
    }
    for (const [file, content] of Object.entries(change.files)) {
      const target = join(work, file);
      if (content === null) {
        rmSync(target, { force: true });
      } else {
        mkdirSync(dirname(target), { recursive: true });
        writeFileSync(target, content);
      }
    }
    await gitIn(work, ['add', '--all']);
    await gitIn(work, ['commit', '--quiet', '--allow-empty', '-m', change.message ?? `change ${change.branch}`]);
    await gitIn(work, ['push', '--quiet', 'origin', `HEAD:refs/heads/${change.branch}`]);
    return await gitIn(work, ['rev-parse', 'HEAD']);
  } finally {
    rmSync(work, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}
```

```ts
// An HTTP proxy that refuses everything (design 15.1). Tests point HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY and ALL_PROXY at it, so any
// connection a vendor CLI tries to an external host is refused and recorded, and a test can assert that none
// succeeded. Local servers are reached through NO_PROXY and never pass through it.
import { createServer } from 'node:http';
import type { AddressInfo } from 'node:net';

export interface RefusedRequest {
  /** connect: a CONNECT tunnel (https); http: a plain request with an absolute URI. */
  kind: 'connect' | 'http';
  method: string;
  /** host:port for a tunnel, the absolute URI for a plain request. */
  target: string;
  at: number;
}

export interface RefusingProxy {
  /** http://127.0.0.1:<port> */
  url: string;
  port: number;
  /** Every refused request, in arrival order. */
  refused: RefusedRequest[];
  close(): Promise<void>;
}

export async function startRefusingProxy(): Promise<RefusingProxy> {
  const refused: RefusedRequest[] = [];
  const server = createServer((request, response) => {
    const target = request.url ?? '';
    // A request in origin form ("GET /") was sent to the proxy as a server, not through it: nothing to record.
    if (!/^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:\/\//i.test(target)) {
      response.writeHead(400, { 'content-type': 'text/plain' }).end('this is a refusing proxy\n');
      return;
    }
    refused.push({ kind: 'http', method: request.method ?? 'GET', target, at: Date.now() });
    response.writeHead(403, { 'content-type': 'text/plain' }).end('refused by the agflow test proxy\n');
  });
  server.on('connect', (request, socket) => {
    refused.push({ kind: 'connect', method: 'CONNECT', target: request.url ?? '', at: Date.now() });
    socket.on('error', () => {});
    socket.end('HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n');
  });
  await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
    server.once('error', reject);
    server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', () => resolve());
  });
  const { port } = server.address() as AddressInfo;
  return {
    url: `http://127.0.0.1:${port}`,
    port,
    refused,
    close: () =>
      new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
        server.close(() => resolve());
        server.closeAllConnections();
      }),
  };
}
```

### Task 3: runner.json: schema, defaults, timings, test mode and the settings snapshot

`runner.json` (design 7.1, 12, 15.1) holds the runner's identity, capacity, profile, models, ceilings, paid-usage switches, vendor homes, the captured PATH and connectivity variables, the commit identity, every runner timing, the test block and the snapshot of the last hub-confirmed settings. It loads with defaults, names the field it refuses, refuses timings below the production minimums unless `AGFLOW_TEST=1` and `test.allowShortTimings` are both set (X-30), honours the test block only in test mode, and writes atomically with mode 0600 and no secret. The settings sync rules of design 6.3 are pure functions here (X-12): `settingsOf` gives hello's snapshot, `localSettingsEdits` the local edits since it, and `applySettingsEcho` applies an `update_settings` echo and returns the edits still pending.

```ts
  /** A runner whose settings the hub confirmed at version 3, and which was then drained while offline. */
  function drainedOffline(): RunnerConfig {
    const confirmed = config({ capacity: 2 });
    const snapshot = { ...settingsOf(confirmed), version: 3 };
    return { ...confirmed, confirmedSettings: snapshot, draining: true };
  }

  test('settingsOf gives the confirmed snapshot and its version, never a local edit', () => {
    const runner = drainedOffline();
    const settings = settingsOf(runner);
    expect(settings.draining).toBe(false);
    expect(settings.version).toBe(3);
    expect(RunnerSettingsSchema.parse(settings)).toEqual(settings);
  });

  test('localSettingsEdits lists the fields runner.json changed since the snapshot', () => {
    expect(localSettingsEdits(drainedOffline())).toEqual({ draining: true });
    const ceilings = { ...drainedOffline().ceilings, codex: { fiveHour: 0.5, weekly: 0.9 } };
    const edited = { ...drainedOffline(), ceilings };
    expect(localSettingsEdits(edited)).toEqual({ draining: true, ceilings: { codex: { fiveHour: 0.5, weekly: 0.9 } } });
  });

  test('an in-place edit of the live settings never reaches the snapshot', () => {
    const runner = config();
    runner.allowPaidUsage.claude = true;
    runner.ceilings.codex.weekly = 0.5;
    expect(localSettingsEdits(runner)).toEqual({
      allowPaidUsage: { claude: true },
      ceilings: { codex: { fiveHour: 0.85, weekly: 0.5 } },
    });
    const { config: next } = applySettingsEcho(runner, { settings: {}, version: 1 });
    next.allowPaidUsage.codex = true;
    expect(localSettingsEdits(next)).toEqual({
      allowPaidUsage: { claude: true, codex: true },
      ceilings: { codex: { fiveHour: 0.85, weekly: 0.5 } },
    });
  });

  test("an echo takes the browser's capacity and the version and keeps the pending drain to send again", () => {
    // The hub had the browser's capacity at version 4, so it answers hello with all of its settings.
    const { version: _confirmed, ...hub } = settingsOf(drainedOffline());
    const { config: next, pending } = applySettingsEcho(drainedOffline(), {
      settings: { ...hub, capacity: 4 },
      version: 4,
    });
    expect(next.capacity).toBe(4);
    expect(next.draining).toBe(true);
    expect(settingsOf(next)).toMatchObject({ capacity: 4, draining: false, version: 4 });
    expect(pending).toEqual({ draining: true });
    expect(localSettingsEdits(next)).toEqual({ draining: true });
  });

  test('an echo that carries the edit clears it', () => {
    const first = applySettingsEcho(drainedOffline(), { settings: { capacity: 4 }, version: 4 }).config;
    const { config: next, pending } = applySettingsEcho(first, { settings: { draining: true }, version: 5 });
    expect(pending).toEqual({});
    expect(next.draining).toBe(true);
    expect(next.capacity).toBe(4);
    expect(settingsOf(next)).toMatchObject({ capacity: 4, draining: true, version: 5 });
    expect(localSettingsEdits(next)).toEqual({});
  });

  test('an echo replaces fields without a local edit and merges per-vendor records', () => {
    const runner = config();
    const { config: next, pending } = applySettingsEcho(runner, {
      settings: {
        keepAwake: 'always',
        ceilings: { codex: { fiveHour: 0.5, weekly: 0.6 } },
        allowPaidUsage: { claude: true },
      },
      version: 1,
    });
    expect(pending).toEqual({});
    expect(next.keepAwake).toBe('always');
    expect(next.ceilings).toEqual({ claude: { fiveHour: 0.85, weekly: 0.85 }, codex: { fiveHour: 0.5, weekly: 0.6 } });
    expect(next.allowPaidUsage).toEqual({ claude: true, codex: false });
    expect(settingsOf(next)).toMatchObject({ keepAwake: 'always', version: 1, ceilings: next.ceilings });
    expect(localSettingsEdits(next)).toEqual({});
  });

  /** Settings the hub confirmed at version 3, with paid usage on for Claude only. */
  function confirmedAt3(): RunnerConfig {
    const confirmed = config({ allowPaidUsage: { claude: true, codex: false } });
    return { ...confirmed, confirmedSettings: { ...structuredClone(settingsOf(confirmed)), version: 3 } };
  }

  test("an offline edit of one vendor's paid usage and the browser's edit of the other both survive", () => {
    const runner = confirmedAt3();
    runner.allowPaidUsage = { claude: true, codex: true };
    expect(localSettingsEdits(runner)).toEqual({ allowPaidUsage: { codex: true } });
    const { version: _v, ...hub } = settingsOf(runner);
    const { config: next, pending } = applySettingsEcho(runner, {
      settings: { ...hub, allowPaidUsage: { claude: false, codex: false } },
      version: 4,
    });
    expect(next.allowPaidUsage).toEqual({ claude: false, codex: true });
    expect(pending).toEqual({ allowPaidUsage: { codex: true } });
    expect(localSettingsEdits(next)).toEqual({ allowPaidUsage: { codex: true } });
  });

  test("an offline edit of one vendor's ceiling and the browser's edit of the other both survive", () => {
    const runner = confirmedAt3();
    runner.ceilings = { ...runner.ceilings, codex: { fiveHour: 0.5, weekly: 0.85 } };
    const { config: next, pending } = applySettingsEcho(runner, {
      settings: { ceilings: { claude: { fiveHour: 0.85, weekly: 0.4 }, codex: { fiveHour: 0.85, weekly: 0.85 } } },
      version: 4,
    });
    expect(next.ceilings).toEqual({ claude: { fiveHour: 0.85, weekly: 0.4 }, codex: { fiveHour: 0.5, weekly: 0.85 } });
    expect(pending).toEqual({ ceilings: { codex: { fiveHour: 0.5, weekly: 0.85 } } });
    expect(settingsOf(next).ceilings).toEqual({
      claude: { fiveHour: 0.85, weekly: 0.4 },
      codex: { fiveHour: 0.85, weekly: 0.85 },
    });
  });

  test('a local edit the echo already matches is not pending', () => {
    const runner = { ...config(), capacity: 6 };
    const { config: next, pending } = applySettingsEcho(runner, { settings: { capacity: 6 }, version: 2 });
    expect(pending).toEqual({});
    expect(next.capacity).toBe(6);
  });
});
```

```ts
// runner.json (design 7.1, 12 and 15.1): the runner's identity, its settings and the snapshot of the ones the hub
// last confirmed, the environment captured at setup, and every runner timing. It holds no secrets and no vendor
// pins (those live in vendor/pins.ts, X-10). The settings sync rules of design 6.3 are pure functions here (X-12),
// so the executor and the runtime only call them.
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import {
  chmodSync,
  existsSync,
  mkdirSync,
  readFileSync,
  realpathSync,
  renameSync,
  rmSync,
  writeFileSync,
} from 'node:fs';
import { basename, dirname, isAbsolute, join, normalize } from 'node:path';
import { type RunnerSettings, RunnerSettingsSchema, type Vendor, VendorSchema } from '@agflow/core';
import { z } from 'zod';
import type { RunnerPaths } from './paths';

/** The connectivity variables setup captures from the owner's login shell and agents inherit (design 7.1, 7.6). */
export const CONNECTIVITY_VARS = [
  'HTTP_PROXY',
  'HTTPS_PROXY',
  'NO_PROXY',
  'ALL_PROXY',
  'NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS',
  'SSL_CERT_FILE',
  'SSL_CERT_DIR',
  'REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE',
  'CURL_CA_BUNDLE',
  'GIT_SSL_CAINFO',
] as const;
export type ConnectivityVar = (typeof CONNECTIVITY_VARS)[number];

const Ms = z.number().int().positive();

/** A delay that starts at base and doubles up to cap. */
function doubling(base: number, cap: number) {
  return z
    .strictObject({ base: Ms.default(base), cap: Ms.default(cap) })
    .prefault({})
    .refine((delay) => delay.cap >= delay.base, { error: 'cap must be at least base' });
}

const SECOND = 1_000;
const MINUTE = 60 * SECOND;
const HOUR = 60 * MINUTE;

/** Design 12's runner timings in milliseconds. Outside test mode the defaults are also the minimums (X-30). */
export const RunnerTimingsSchema = z
  .strictObject({
    /** Overridden by welcome.timings. */
    heartbeat: Ms.default(15 * SECOND),
    /** Overridden by welcome.timings. */
    deadLink: Ms.default(45 * SECOND),
    handshake: Ms.default(10 * SECOND),
    backoffBase: Ms.default(SECOND),
    backoffCap: Ms.default(30 * SECOND),
    tickGap: Ms.default(5 * SECOND),
    continuationWait: Ms.default(5 * SECOND),
    hold: Ms.default(2 * MINUTE),
    /** Overridden by welcome.timings. */
    handoff: Ms.default(3 * MINUTE),
    wip: Ms.default(10 * MINUTE),
    finalPush: Ms.default(60 * SECOND),
    /** AGFLOW_BRIDGE_POLL_MS for the bridge. */
    bridgePoll: Ms.default(2 * SECOND),
    /** AGFLOW_BRIDGE_POLL_MAX_MS for the bridge. */
    bridgePollMax: Ms.default(3 * MINUTE),
    suspend: Ms.default(45 * SECOND),
    wakeHold: Ms.default(2 * MINUTE),
    crashLoopWindow: Ms.default(10 * MINUTE),
    loginProbe: Ms.default(60 * SECOND),
    stopInterrupt: Ms.default(5 * SECOND),
    stopClose: Ms.default(2 * SECOND),
    stopKill: Ms.default(5 * SECOND),
    vendorErrorBackoff: doubling(30 * SECOND, 10 * MINUTE),
    /** Turn retries in quota_wait when the reset time is unknown. */
    quotaUnknown: Ms.default(30 * MINUTE),
    /** Late-work pushes after a pushError. */
    lateRetry: doubling(30 * SECOND, 10 * MINUTE),
    /** How long remote failures of a submission push are retried. */
    submitRetry: Ms.default(15 * MINUTE),
    /** One dependency preparation. */
    prep: Ms.default(15 * MINUTE),
    preflightEvery: Ms.default(6 * HOUR),
    /** How long acknowledged events are kept, so a restored hub can catch up. */
    eventRetention: Ms.default(48 * HOUR),
  })
  .prefault({});
export type RunnerTimings = z.output<typeof RunnerTimingsSchema>;

export const DEFAULT_TIMINGS: RunnerTimings = RunnerTimingsSchema.parse({});

/** A canonical absolute path: what realpath gives, without a trailing slash. */
const CanonicalPath = z
  .string()
  .refine((path) => isAbsolute(path), { error: 'must be an absolute path' })
  .refine((path) => path === '/' || !path.endsWith('/'), { error: 'must not end with a trailing slash' })
  .refine((path) => normalize(path) === path, { error: 'must be a canonical path' });

const Name = z.string().min(1);
const Ceilings = z.strictObject({ fiveHour: z.number().min(0).max(1), weekly: z.number().min(0).max(1) });

const ceilings = () => Ceilings.prefault({ fiveHour: 0.85, weekly: 0.85 });
const paidUsage = () => z.boolean().default(false);
const models = (lead: string, worker: string) =>
  z.strictObject({ lead: Name.default(lead), worker: Name.default(worker) }).prefault({});

/** Section 15.1. Honoured only with AGFLOW_TEST=1 (isTestMode); `agflow runner install` refuses it. */
export const RunnerTestBlockSchema = z.strictObject({
  /** Added to Claude's environment after the allowlist. */
  claudeEnv: z.record(z.string(), z.string()).default({}),
  /** Given to Codex as -c flags, one per top-level key; no config.toml is written. */
  codexConfig: z.record(z.string(), z.json()).default({}),
  /** Preflight reports the vendor ready with problem and plan 'test mode' and core's TEST_ACCOUNT_ID. */
  skipAuthChecks: z.boolean().default(false),
  /** Accept any positive timing, below the production minimums too. */
  allowShortTimings: z.boolean().default(false),
});
export type RunnerTestBlock = z.output<typeof RunnerTestBlockSchema>;

export const RunnerConfigSchema = z
  .strictObject({
    runnerKey: Name,
    /** The Mac's IOPlatformUUID; a copied home folder is refused at start. */
    machineId: Name,
    name: Name,
    // The settings the hub shows and the owner may change (RunnerSettings, design 6.3).
    capacity: z.number().int().min(1).max(16).default(2),
    keepAwake: z.enum(['off', 'ac', 'always']).default('ac'),
    draining: z.boolean().default(false),
    ceilings: z.strictObject({ claude: ceilings(), codex: ceilings() }).prefault({}),
    allowPaidUsage: z.strictObject({ claude: paidUsage(), codex: paidUsage() }).prefault({}),
    /** The snapshot of the settings the hub last confirmed; a new runner.json confirms its own at version 0. */
    confirmedSettings: RunnerSettingsSchema.optional(),
    profile: z.enum(['standard', 'auto']).default('standard'),
    models: z
      .strictObject({
        claude: models('claude-opus-5-5', 'claude-sonnet-5-5'),
        codex: models('gpt-6.1-sol', 'gpt-6.1-sol'),
      })
      .prefault({}),
    minFreeGb: z.number().min(0).default(10),
    batteryDrainPercent: z.number().min(0).max(100).default(20),
    /** CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and CODEX_HOME exactly as setup created them; null means the layout's homes (vendorHomes). */
    homes: z
      .strictObject({ claude: CanonicalPath.nullable().default(null), codex: CanonicalPath.nullable().default(null) })
      .prefault({}),
    /** The owner's login-shell PATH, captured at setup. */
    capturedPath: z.string().min(1).default('/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin'),
    connectivity: z.partialRecord(z.enum(CONNECTIVITY_VARS), z.string()).default({}),
    /** The author and committer of agent commits; setup takes the owner's git identity. */
    commitIdentity: z
      .strictObject({ name: Name, email: Name })
      .default({ name: 'agflow agent', email: 'agent@agflow.invalid' }),
    timings: RunnerTimingsSchema,
    test: RunnerTestBlockSchema.optional(),
  })
  .transform((config) => ({
    ...config,
    // A copy, so an in-place edit of the live settings never changes the snapshot too.
    confirmedSettings: config.confirmedSettings ?? { ...structuredClone(localSettings(config)), version: 0 },
  }));
export type RunnerConfig = z.output<typeof RunnerConfigSchema>;
export type RunnerConfigInput = z.input<typeof RunnerConfigSchema>;

type Env = Record<string, string | undefined>;

/** Test mode needs both AGFLOW_TEST=1 and a test block in runner.json. */
export function isTestMode(config: Pick<RunnerConfig, 'test'>, env: Env = process.env): boolean {
  return env.AGFLOW_TEST === '1' && config.test !== undefined;
}

function describeIssues(error: z.ZodError): string {
  return error.issues
    .flatMap((issue) => {
      if (issue.code === 'unrecognized_keys') {
        return issue.keys.map((key) => `runner.json: ${[...issue.path, key].join('.')}: unknown field`);
      }
      return [`runner.json: ${issue.path.join('.') || '(root)'}: ${issue.message}`];
    })
    .join('\n');
}

function parseConfig(value: unknown): RunnerConfig {
  const parsed = RunnerConfigSchema.safeParse(value);
  if (!parsed.success) throw new Error(describeIssues(parsed.error));
  return parsed.data;
}

/** Timings below the defaults, unless test mode allows short ones. */
function checkMinimums(config: RunnerConfig, env: Env): void {
  if (isTestMode(config, env) && config.test?.allowShortTimings) return;
  const problems: string[] = [];
  const check = (name: string, value: number, minimum: number) => {
    if (value < minimum) {
      problems.push(`runner.json: timings.${name}: ${value} ms is below the minimum of ${minimum} ms`);
    }
  };
  for (const [name, minimum] of Object.entries(DEFAULT_TIMINGS)) {
    const value = config.timings[name as keyof RunnerTimings];
    if (typeof minimum === 'number' && typeof value === 'number') {
      check(name, value, minimum);
    } else if (typeof minimum === 'object' && typeof value === 'object') {
      check(`${name}.base`, value.base, minimum.base);
      check(`${name}.cap`, value.cap, minimum.cap);
    }
  }
  if (problems.length > 0) {
    throw new Error(`${problems.join('\n')}\n(shorter timings need AGFLOW_TEST=1 and test.allowShortTimings)`);
  }
}

/** Reads runner.json with its defaults; an invalid file is refused with the field named. */
export function loadRunnerConfig(path: string, env: Env = process.env): RunnerConfig {
  if (!existsSync(path)) throw new Error(`${path} does not exist; run agflow runner setup`);
  let raw: unknown;
  try {
    raw = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, 'utf8'));
  } catch (error) {
    throw new Error(`${path} is not valid JSON: ${(error as Error).message}`);
  }
  const config = parseConfig(raw);
  checkMinimums(config, env);
  return config;
}

/**
 * Writes runner.json atomically (a temporary file renamed over it) with mode 0600. The config is validated first, so
 * nothing outside the schema, a secret included, is ever written.
 */
export function saveRunnerConfig(path: string, config: RunnerConfig): void {
  const valid = parseConfig(config);
  mkdirSync(dirname(path), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
  const temporary = join(dirname(path), `.runner.json.${randomUUID()}.tmp`);
  try {
    writeFileSync(temporary, `${JSON.stringify(valid, null, 2)}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
    chmodSync(temporary, 0o600);
    renameSync(temporary, path);
  } finally {
    rmSync(temporary, { force: true });
  }
}

/**
 * The real path of the nearest existing ancestor joined with the rest, so a home that does not exist yet is still
 * canonical when AGFLOW_HOME sits behind a symlink (/tmp, /var/folders, a moved ~/.agflow).
 */
function canonicalPath(path: string): string {
  const missing: string[] = [];
  let existing = path;
  while (!existsSync(existing)) {
    missing.unshift(basename(existing));
    existing = dirname(existing);
  }
  return join(realpathSync(existing), ...missing);
}

/**
 * The vendor homes: runner.json's canonical strings, or the layout's made canonical when setup recorded none. Claude's
 * guard compares real paths with <CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/projects/, so a symlinked home would let it fail open (7.6).
 */
export function vendorHomes(config: RunnerConfig, paths: RunnerPaths): Record<Vendor, string> {
  return {
    claude: config.homes.claude ?? canonicalPath(paths.homes.claude),
    codex: config.homes.codex ?? canonicalPath(paths.homes.codex),
  };
}

// Settings sync (design 6.3). hello carries the confirmed snapshot only; local edits travel as runner.settings after
// welcome; an update_settings echo replaces the snapshot and runner.json, except pending local edits. Ceilings and
// paid usage are records per vendor, and both sides treat each vendor's entry as its own field: an edit names only
// the vendors it changed, and an echo naming one vendor leaves the other as it was.

export type SettingsValues = Omit<RunnerSettings, 'version'>;
export type SettingsEdits = Partial<SettingsValues>;

const SCALAR_FIELDS = ['capacity', 'keepAwake', 'draining'] as const;
const VENDOR_FIELDS = ['ceilings', 'allowPaidUsage'] as const;
const VENDORS = VendorSchema.options;

function localSettings(config: SettingsValues): SettingsValues {
  const { capacity, keepAwake, draining, ceilings, allowPaidUsage } = config;
  return { capacity, keepAwake, draining, ceilings, allowPaidUsage };
}

/** The snapshot hello reports: the last settings the hub confirmed, with their version. */
export function settingsOf(config: RunnerConfig): RunnerSettings {
  return config.confirmedSettings;
}

/**
 * The fields runner.json changed since the snapshot, and for the per-vendor records only the vendors it changed; sent
 * as runner.settings after each welcome.
 */
export function localSettingsEdits(config: RunnerConfig): SettingsEdits {
  const local = localSettings(config);
  const snapshot = config.confirmedSettings;
  const result: Record<string, unknown> = {};
  for (const field of SCALAR_FIELDS) {
    if (local[field] !== snapshot[field]) result[field] = local[field];
  }
  for (const field of VENDOR_FIELDS) {
    const changed = VENDORS.filter(
      (vendor) => local[field][vendor] !== undefined && !Bun.deepEquals(local[field][vendor], snapshot[field][vendor]),
    );
    if (changed.length > 0) {
      result[field] = Object.fromEntries(changed.map((vendor) => [vendor, structuredClone(local[field][vendor])]));
    }
  }
  return result as SettingsEdits;
}

/**
 * Applies an update_settings echo: it becomes the snapshot, and runner.json takes its values except for pending local
 * edits (fields, or vendors of the per-vendor records, that differed from the old snapshot and differ from the echo),
 * which keep their value and are returned to be sent again.
 */
export function applySettingsEcho(
  config: RunnerConfig,
  echo: { settings: SettingsEdits; version: number },
): { config: RunnerConfig; pending: SettingsEdits } {
  const old = config.confirmedSettings;
  const given = structuredClone(echo.settings);
  const snapshot: RunnerSettings = {
    capacity: given.capacity ?? old.capacity,
    keepAwake: given.keepAwake ?? old.keepAwake,
    draining: given.draining ?? old.draining,
    ceilings: { ...structuredClone(old.ceilings), ...given.ceilings },
    allowPaidUsage: { ...old.allowPaidUsage, ...given.allowPaidUsage },
    version: echo.version,
  };
  const local = localSettings(config);
  const pending: Record<string, unknown> = {};
  const next: RunnerConfig = { ...config, confirmedSettings: snapshot };
  for (const field of SCALAR_FIELDS) {
    if (local[field] !== old[field] && local[field] !== snapshot[field]) pending[field] = local[field];
    else Object.assign(next, { [field]: snapshot[field] });
  }
  for (const field of VENDOR_FIELDS) {
    const merged: Record<string, unknown> = {};
    const kept: Record<string, unknown> = {};
    for (const vendor of VENDORS) {
      const mine = local[field][vendor];
      const theirs = snapshot[field][vendor];
      const pendingHere =
        mine !== undefined && !Bun.deepEquals(mine, old[field][vendor]) && !Bun.deepEquals(mine, theirs);
      if (pendingHere) kept[vendor] = structuredClone(mine);
      merged[vendor] = structuredClone(pendingHere || theirs === undefined ? mine : theirs);
    }
    Object.assign(next, { [field]: merged });
    if (Object.keys(kept).length > 0) pending[field] = kept;
  }
  return { config: next, pending: pending as SettingsEdits };
}
```

### Task 4: The awake clock and backoffs

The runner measures every age on an awake clock (design 6.3, 7.5). A 1 s tick notices a wall-clock step over `tickGap`, reports the gap once and counts only one tick of it as awake time, so a sleeping Mac neither ages its facts nor looks stalled; `awakeNow()` also checks the step since the last tick, so an age read right after a wake already leaves the sleep out. `Backoff` gives full-jitter reconnect delays that reset once the link has been up 60 s, and `doublingDelay` the doubling delays of runner.json's `{ base, cap }` timings (design 12). Both take an injected clock source, so tests never wait in real time.

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { Backoff, doublingDelay } from '../src/backoff';
import { AwakeClock, type ClockGap, type ClockSource, systemClock } from '../src/clock';
import { DEFAULT_TIMINGS } from '../src/config';
import { memoryLogger } from '../src/log';

/** A wall clock the test moves by hand, with intervals and timeouts that fire only when the test says so. */
class ManualClock implements ClockSource {
  t = Date.UTC(2026, 9, 29, 9, 0, 0);
  private nextId = 1;
  readonly timers = new Map<number, { fn: () => void; ms: number; repeat: boolean }>();
  now = (): number => this.t;
  setTimeout = (fn: () => void, ms: number): number => this.add(fn, ms, false);
  clearTimeout = (handle: unknown): void => void this.timers.delete(handle as number);
  setInterval = (fn: () => void, ms: number): number => this.add(fn, ms, true);
  clearInterval = (handle: unknown): void => void this.timers.delete(handle as number);
  private add(fn: () => void, ms: number, repeat: boolean): number {
    const id = this.nextId++;
    this.timers.set(id, { fn, ms, repeat });
    return id;
  }
  /** Moves wall time and runs every timer once, as a tick that arrives after the move would. */
  step(ms: number): void {
    this.t += ms;
    for (const [id, timer] of [...this.timers]) {
      if (!timer.repeat) this.timers.delete(id);
      timer.fn();
    }
  }
}

function started(source = new ManualClock()) {
  const clock = new AwakeClock({ source, tickMs: 1_000, gapMs: 5_000 });
  const gaps: ClockGap[] = [];
  clock.onGap((gap) => gaps.push(gap));
  clock.start();
  return { source, clock, gaps };
}

describe('AwakeClock', () => {
  test('reports a wall-clock jump larger than tickGap once, as one gap', () => {
    const { source, gaps } = started();
    source.step(1_000);
    source.step(1_000);
    source.step(60_000);
    source.step(1_000);
    expect(gaps).toEqual([{ at: source.t - 1_000, ms: 60_000 }]);
  });

  test('ignores jitter below tickGap', () => {
    const { source, gaps } = started();
    for (const ms of [1_000, 2_500, 4_900, 5_000, 300, 1_200]) source.step(ms);
    expect(gaps).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('awakeNow advances with wall time but not across a gap', () => {
    const { source, clock } = started();
    const start = clock.awakeNow();
    source.step(1_000);
    source.step(1_000);
    expect(clock.awakeNow() - start).toBe(2_000);
    // The laptop sleeps for an hour; the tick after it reports the gap.
    source.step(3_600_000);
    expect(clock.awakeNow() - start).toBe(3_000);
    source.t += 400;
    expect(clock.awakeNow() - start).toBe(3_400);
  });

  test('an age measured across a sleep excludes it, even before the next tick', () => {
    const { source, clock, gaps } = started();
    const since = clock.awakeNow();
    source.step(1_000);
    // Woken up, but no tick has run yet: reading the clock notices the gap itself.
    source.t += 30 * 60_000;
    expect(clock.awakeNow() - since).toBe(2_000);
    expect(gaps).toHaveLength(1);
    source.step(1_000);
    expect(gaps).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(clock.awakeNow() - since).toBe(3_000);
  });

  test('a backward clock step is not a gap and never makes awakeNow go backwards', () => {
    const { source, clock, gaps } = started();
    source.step(1_000);
    const before = clock.awakeNow();
    source.step(-120_000);
    expect(clock.awakeNow()).toBe(before);
    source.step(1_000);
    expect(clock.awakeNow()).toBe(before + 1_000);
    expect(gaps).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('stop() ends the tick; a later read still notices a gap, and an unsubscribed listener hears nothing', () => {
    const { source, clock, gaps } = started();
    const other: ClockGap[] = [];
    const unsubscribe = clock.onGap((gap) => other.push(gap));
    unsubscribe();
    clock.stop();
    expect(source.timers.size).toBe(0);
    source.step(60_000);
    expect(gaps).toEqual([]);
    expect(clock.awakeNow()).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(gaps).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(other).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('ticks once a second by default', () => {
    const source = new ManualClock();
    new AwakeClock({ source, gapMs: DEFAULT_TIMINGS.tickGap }).start();
    expect([...source.timers.values()].map(({ ms, repeat }) => ({ ms, repeat }))).toEqual([
      { ms: 1_000, repeat: true },
    ]);
  });

  test('runs on the system clock when given no source', () => {
    const clock = new AwakeClock({ gapMs: DEFAULT_TIMINGS.tickGap });
    const before = clock.awakeNow();
    expect(clock.awakeNow()).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(before);
    expect(systemClock.now()).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(Date.now() - 1_000);
    clock.start();
    clock.stop();
  });

  test('a throwing listener neither stops the next one nor escapes from the tick or a read', () => {
    const source = new ManualClock();
    const logger = memoryLogger();
    const clock = new AwakeClock({ source, tickMs: 1_000, gapMs: 5_000, logger });
    const heard: ClockGap[] = [];
    clock.onGap(() => {
      throw new Error('listener broke');
    });
    clock.onGap((gap) => heard.push(gap));
    clock.start();
    expect(() => source.step(60_000)).not.toThrow();
    expect(heard).toHaveLength(1);
    source.t += 60_000;
    expect(() => clock.awakeNow()).not.toThrow();
    expect(heard).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(logger.entries.map(({ level, message }) => ({ level, message }))).toEqual([
      { level: 'error', message: 'a clock gap listener failed' },
      { level: 'error', message: 'a clock gap listener failed' },
    ]);
    expect(logger.entries[0]?.fields.error).toContain('listener broke');
  });
});

/** A random source that returns the given values in turn. */
function sequence(...values: number[]): () => number {
  let index = 0;
  return () => values[index++ % values.length] as number;
}

describe('Backoff', () => {
  test('gives full-jitter delays within [0, min(cap, base * 2^attempt)]', () => {
    const backoff = new Backoff({ base: 1_000, cap: 30_000, random: sequence(0.999999) });
    const delays = Array.from({ length: 8 }, () => backoff.next());
    expect(delays).toEqual([999, 1_999, 3_999, 7_999, 15_999, 29_999, 29_999, 29_999]);
    const low = new Backoff({ base: 1_000, cap: 30_000, random: sequence(0) });
    expect(Array.from({ length: 4 }, () => low.next())).toEqual([0, 0, 0, 0]);
  });

  test('stays within bounds for any random value and many attempts', () => {
    const backoff = new Backoff({ base: 1_000, cap: 30_000 });
    for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 200; attempt += 1) {
      const delay = backoff.next();
      expect(delay).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
      expect(delay).toBeLessThanOrEqual(Math.min(30_000, 1_000 * 2 ** attempt));
    }
  });

  test('resets after the link has been up for the reset interval', () => {
    const clock = new ManualClock();
    const backoff = new Backoff({
      base: 1_000,
      cap: 30_000,
      resetAfterMs: 60_000,
      now: clock.now,
      random: sequence(0.5),
    });
    backoff.next();
    backoff.next();
    backoff.next();
    expect(backoff.attempt).toBe(3);
    // Up for 59 s: still backing off from where it was.
    backoff.connected();
    clock.t += 59_000;
    backoff.disconnected();
    expect(backoff.attempt).toBe(3);
    expect(backoff.next()).toBe(4_000);
    // Up for a full minute: the next reconnect starts from base again.
    backoff.connected();
    clock.t += 60_000;
    backoff.disconnected();
    expect(backoff.attempt).toBe(0);
    expect(backoff.next()).toBe(500);
  });

  test('resets after a minute up by default', () => {
    const clock = new ManualClock();
    const backoff = new Backoff({ base: 1_000, cap: 30_000, now: clock.now, random: sequence(0.5) });
    backoff.next();
    backoff.connected();
    clock.t += 59_000;
    backoff.disconnected();
    expect(backoff.attempt).toBe(1);
    backoff.connected();
    clock.t += 60_000;
    backoff.disconnected();
    expect(backoff.attempt).toBe(0);
  });

  test('a link that never came up does not reset it', () => {
    const clock = new ManualClock();
    const backoff = new Backoff({ base: 1_000, cap: 30_000, now: clock.now, random: sequence(0.5) });
    backoff.next();
    clock.t += 120_000;
    backoff.disconnected();
    expect(backoff.attempt).toBe(1);
  });
});

describe('doublingDelay', () => {
  test('doubles from 30 s and stays at 10 min', () => {
    const delays = Array.from({ length: 8 }, (_, attempt) => doublingDelay(attempt, DEFAULT_TIMINGS.lateRetry));
    expect(delays).toEqual([30_000, 60_000, 120_000, 240_000, 480_000, 600_000, 600_000, 600_000]);
    expect(doublingDelay(1_000, DEFAULT_TIMINGS.vendorErrorBackoff)).toBe(600_000);
  });

  test('takes short test timings and refuses a negative attempt', () => {
    expect(doublingDelay(2, { base: 10, cap: 25 })).toBe(25);
    expect(() => doublingDelay(-1, { base: 10, cap: 25 })).toThrow('attempt');
  });
});
```

```ts
// Retry delays (design 6.3, 12): full-jitter backoff for reconnects, and the doubling delays of vendor-error retries,
// late-work pushes and submission retries.

export interface BackoffOptions {
  /** runner.json's timings.backoffBase. */
  base: number;
  /** runner.json's timings.backoffCap. */
  cap: number;
  /** A link that stayed up this long starts the next backoff from base again; 60 s. */
  resetAfterMs?: number;
  now?: () => number;
  random?: () => number;
}

// 2^30 times any base is far beyond every cap, and stopping there keeps the arithmetic finite.
const MAX_EXPONENT = 30;

export class Backoff {
  private readonly options: Required<BackoffOptions>;
  private attempts = 0;
  private upSince: number | null = null;

  constructor(options: BackoffOptions) {
    this.options = {
      base: options.base,
      cap: options.cap,
      resetAfterMs: options.resetAfterMs ?? 60_000,
      now: options.now ?? (() => Date.now()),
      random: options.random ?? Math.random,
    };
  }

  /** How many delays were given since the last reset. */
  get attempt(): number {
    return this.attempts;
  }

  /** The next reconnect delay: a uniform draw from [0, min(cap, base * 2^attempt)). */
  next(): number {
    const { base, cap, random } = this.options;
    const ceiling = Math.min(cap, base * 2 ** Math.min(this.attempts, MAX_EXPONENT));
    this.attempts += 1;
    return Math.floor(random() * ceiling);
  }

  /** The link is up. */
  connected(): void {
    this.upSince = this.options.now();
  }

  /** The link dropped; it resets the backoff when it had been up for resetAfterMs. */
  disconnected(): void {
    if (this.upSince !== null && this.options.now() - this.upSince >= this.options.resetAfterMs) this.reset();
    this.upSince = null;
  }

  reset(): void {
    this.attempts = 0;
  }
}

/** The delay before retry number `attempt` (from 0): base, doubling up to cap. */
export function doublingDelay(attempt: number, delay: { base: number; cap: number }): number {
  if (!Number.isInteger(attempt) || attempt < 0) {
    throw new Error(`attempt must be a whole number from 0, not ${attempt}`);
  }
  return Math.min(delay.cap, delay.base * 2 ** Math.min(attempt, MAX_EXPONENT));
}
```

```ts
// The awake clock (design 6.3, 7.5): a 1 s wall-clock tick notices sleep and freezes, so every age and activeMs the
// runner reports leaves them out, and the link reconnects at once after one.
import { type Logger, noopLogger } from './log';

/** Wall time and timers, injectable so tests never wait in real time. */
export interface ClockSource {
  now(): number;
  setTimeout(fn: () => void, ms: number): unknown;
  clearTimeout(handle: unknown): void;
  setInterval(fn: () => void, ms: number): unknown;
  clearInterval(handle: unknown): void;
}

export const systemClock: ClockSource = {
  now: () => Date.now(),
  setTimeout: (fn, ms) => setTimeout(fn, ms),
  clearTimeout: (handle) => clearTimeout(handle as Timer),
  setInterval: (fn, ms) => setInterval(fn, ms),
  clearInterval: (handle) => clearInterval(handle as Timer),
};

export interface ClockGap {
  /** Wall time when the gap was noticed. */
  at: number;
  /** Wall time between the last observation before the gap and the first after it. */
  ms: number;
}

export interface AwakeClockOptions {
  source?: ClockSource;
  /** 1 s. */
  tickMs?: number;
  /** runner.json's timings.tickGap: a longer step between two observations is a sleep or a freeze. */
  gapMs: number;
  /** Where a throwing gap listener is reported. */
  logger?: Logger;
}

export class AwakeClock {
  private readonly source: ClockSource;
  private readonly tickMs: number;
  private readonly gapMs: number;
  private readonly logger: Logger;
  private readonly listeners = new Set<(gap: ClockGap) => void>();
  private lastWall: number;
  private awake: number;
  private timer: unknown = null;

  constructor(options: AwakeClockOptions) {
    this.source = options.source ?? systemClock;
    this.tickMs = options.tickMs ?? 1_000;
    this.gapMs = options.gapMs;
    this.logger = options.logger ?? noopLogger;
    this.lastWall = this.source.now();
    // Starts at wall time, so awake times read like timestamps; only differences between them mean anything.
    this.awake = this.lastWall;
  }

  start(): void {
    if (this.timer === null) this.timer = this.source.setInterval(() => this.observe(), this.tickMs);
  }

  stop(): void {
    if (this.timer !== null) this.source.clearInterval(this.timer);
    this.timer = null;
  }

  /** Called once per gap, from the tick or from the read that notices it first. Returns the unsubscribe. */
  onGap(listener: (gap: ClockGap) => void): () => void {
    this.listeners.add(listener);
    return () => this.listeners.delete(listener);
  }

  /** The awake time in ms: it advances with wall time, but not across sleeps, freezes or backward steps. */
  awakeNow(): number {
    this.observe();
    return this.awake;
  }

  private observe(): void {
    const now = this.source.now();
    const step = now - this.lastWall;
    this.lastWall = now;
    // A backward step (an NTP correction, say) adds nothing; time runs on from the new wall time.
    if (step <= 0) return;
    if (step <= this.gapMs) {
      this.awake += step;
      return;
    }
    // Only the tick interval before the gap counts as awake; the rest was spent asleep or frozen.
    this.awake += this.tickMs;
    const gap = { at: now, ms: step };
    // Each listener hears the gap even if another throws: the gap is reported only once, and a throw would otherwise
    // escape into whatever read the clock, or out of the tick and end the process.
    for (const listener of [...this.listeners]) {
      try {
        listener(gap);
      } catch (error) {
        this.logger.error('a clock gap listener failed', { error: String(error) });
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Task 5: runner.db: outbox, command journal, attempt records and the process registry

`runner.db` is the runner's durable state in `bun:sqlite` (design 6.3, 7.2, 7.4). The outbox keeps events under an epoch that is new with every new database, never reuses a seq after pruning, takes cumulative acks, and gives `firstSeq` and `lastSeq` for hello (X-1), `waitAcked`, `pruneAcked` and `pruneBefore` (X-7). The journal records each command as running and then done, keyed by command id and by design 6.3's idempotency keys, with the outbox position the command arrived at, which Task 35's settings echoes read. Attempt records and the process registry keep what a restart needs, never the agent token: `lateWorkSha` marks work that still waits for a late-work ref (Task 26). `openRunnerDb(path, { migrations })` lets M2c add its own tables without editing `db.ts`. `AttemptRecord.finalizedAt` is the durable finalization marker, separate from process state and delivery to origin; new and migrated records default to null.
