```ts
import { afterEach, describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { existsSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { type AttemptSpec, AttemptSpecSchema, type RunnerCommand } from '@agflow/core';
import { AttemptStore } from '../src/attempt-store';
import { openRunnerDb, type RunnerDb } from '../src/db';
import { idempotencyKey, Journal } from '../src/journal';
import { MAX_EVENT_BYTES, Outbox } from '../src/outbox';

const dirs: string[] = [];
const dbs: RunnerDb[] = [];
afterEach(() => {
  for (const db of dbs.splice(0)) db.close();
  for (const dir of dirs.splice(0)) rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
});

function dbPath(): string {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'agflow-runner-db-'));
  dirs.push(dir);
  return join(dir, 'runner.db');
}

function open(path = dbPath(), options: Parameters<typeof openRunnerDb>[1] = {}): RunnerDb {
  const db = openRunnerDb(path, options);
  dbs.push(db);
  return db;
}

function reopen(db: RunnerDb, options: Parameters<typeof openRunnerDb>[1] = {}): RunnerDb {
  db.close();
  dbs.splice(dbs.indexOf(db), 1);
  return open(db.path, options);
}

const TOKEN = `agt_${'Q'.repeat(43)}`;
const fence = { epoch: 1, counter: 7 };

function spec(overrides: Partial<AttemptSpec> = {}): AttemptSpec {
  return AttemptSpecSchema.parse({
    attemptId: 'T-4-a1',
    taskId: 'T-4',
    role: 'worker',
    vendor: 'claude',
    model: null,
    fence,
    agentToken: TOKEN,
    hubUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:7000',
    repo: { url: '/tmp/origin.git', mainBranch: 'main' },
    start: { ref: 'refs/heads/main', sha: null },
    branch: 'agflow/T-4-tidy',
    wipRef: 'refs/agflow/T-4/a1',
    restore: { paths: ['.claude/**'], base: 'refs/heads/main' },
    acceptanceIds: ['A1'],
    toolCaps: { defaultMs: 600_000, longMs: 1_800_000, checks: [] },
    taskPack: '# T-4',
    brief: 'brief',
    firstPrompt: 'start',
    successor: false,
    ...overrides,
  });
}

function stateEvent(detail: string) {
  return { type: 'runner.state', data: { state: 'ok', detail } } as const;
}

/** A clock the test sets by hand. */
function manualNow(start = 1_000_000) {
  const clock = { t: start, now: () => clock.t };
  return clock;
}

describe('openRunnerDb', () => {
  test('a new runner.db gets a fresh outboxEpoch that survives reopening; a recreated one gets a new one', () => {
    const path = dbPath();
    const first = open(path);
    const epoch = first.outboxEpoch;
    expect(epoch).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/);
    const again = reopen(first);
    expect(again.outboxEpoch).toBe(epoch);
    again.close();
    dbs.splice(dbs.indexOf(again), 1);
    for (const suffix of ['', '-wal', '-shm']) rmSync(`${path}${suffix}`, { force: true });
    expect(open(path).outboxEpoch).not.toBe(epoch);
  });

  test('refuses a schema newer than the code', () => {
    const db = open();
    db.sqlite.run('INSERT INTO schema_migrations (version, applied_at) VALUES (99, 0)');
    const path = db.path;
    db.close();
    dbs.splice(dbs.indexOf(db), 1);
    expect(() => openRunnerDb(path)).toThrow(/schema version 99 is newer/);
  });

  test('runs extra named migrations once each, in order', () => {
    const a = { name: 'm2c.health', sql: 'CREATE TABLE health (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, note TEXT NOT NULL);' };
    const b = { name: 'm2c.health-seed', sql: "INSERT INTO health (note) VALUES ('seeded');" };
    const c = { name: 'm2c.health-more', sql: "INSERT INTO health (note) VALUES ('more');" };
    const db = open(dbPath(), { migrations: [a, b] });
    const again = reopen(db, { migrations: [a, b, c] });
    const notes = again.sqlite.query('SELECT note FROM health ORDER BY id').all() as { note: string }[];
    expect(notes.map((row) => row.note)).toEqual(['seeded', 'more']);
    expect(again.appliedMigrations()).toEqual(['m2c.health', 'm2c.health-seed', 'm2c.health-more']);
  });

  test('refuses two extra migrations with one name', () => {
    const twice = { name: 'm2c.x', sql: 'SELECT 1;' };
    expect(() => open(dbPath(), { migrations: [twice, twice] })).toThrow(/m2c.x/);
  });

  test('keeps lastHubEpoch, wipRefPrefix and the project in meta', () => {
    const db = open();
    expect(db.meta('lastHubEpoch')).toBeNull();
    expect(db.meta('wipRefPrefix')).toBeNull();
    expect(db.meta('project')).toBeNull();
    db.setMeta('lastHubEpoch', 3);
    db.setMeta('wipRefPrefix', 'refs/agflow/');
    db.setMeta('project', { name: 'demo', repo: 'git@example.com:demo.git' });
    const again = reopen(db);
    expect(again.meta('lastHubEpoch')).toBe(3);
    expect(again.meta('wipRefPrefix')).toBe('refs/agflow/');
    expect(again.meta('project')).toEqual({ name: 'demo', repo: 'git@example.com:demo.git' });
  });
});

describe('Outbox', () => {
  test('append assigns increasing seqs and eventsAfter returns them in order', () => {
    const clock = manualNow();
    const outbox = new Outbox(open(), { now: clock.now });
    const first = outbox.append(stateEvent('one'));
    clock.t += 5;
    const second = outbox.append({
      type: 'attempt.activity',
      attemptId: 'T-4-a1',
      fence,
      data: { kind: 'note', summary: 'two' },
    });
    expect(first).toEqual({ seq: 1, at: 1_000_000, type: 'runner.state', data: { state: 'ok', detail: 'one' } });
    expect(second.seq).toBe(2);
    expect(second.at).toBe(1_000_005);
    expect(outbox.eventsAfter(0)).toEqual([first, second]);
    expect(outbox.eventsAfter(1)).toEqual([second]);
    expect(outbox.eventsAfter(0, 1)).toEqual([first]);
  });

  test('append refuses an event the hub could not read', () => {
    const outbox = new Outbox(open());
    const unreadable = { type: 'runner.state', data: { state: 'asleep', detail: null } } as never;
    expect(() => outbox.append(unreadable)).toThrow(/runner.state/);
    expect(outbox.lastSeq()).toBe(0);
  });

  test('append refuses an event over MAX_EVENT_BYTES, which no hub message could carry', () => {
    const outbox = new Outbox(open());
    outbox.append(stateEvent('kept'));
    expect(() => outbox.append(stateEvent('x'.repeat(MAX_EVENT_BYTES)))).toThrow(/too large/);
    expect(outbox.lastSeq()).toBe(1);
    // Just under the cap is fine.
    const fits = stateEvent('x'.repeat(MAX_EVENT_BYTES - 200));
    expect(outbox.append(fits).seq).toBe(2);
  });

  test('tells listeners about each appended event after the append returns', async () => {
    const outbox = new Outbox(open());
    const seen: number[] = [];
    const stop = outbox.onAppend((event) => seen.push(event.seq));
    outbox.append(stateEvent('one'));
    outbox.append(stateEvent('two'));
    expect(seen).toEqual([]);
    await Promise.resolve();
    expect(seen).toEqual([1, 2]);
    stop();
    outbox.append(stateEvent('three'));
    await Promise.resolve();
    expect(seen).toEqual([1, 2]);
  });

  test('listeners hear only committed events: a rolled-back append is never announced', async () => {
    const db = open();
    const outbox = new Outbox(db);
    const seen: { seq: number; detail: string }[] = [];
    outbox.onAppend((event) => seen.push({ seq: event.seq, detail: (event.data as { detail: string }).detail }));
    outbox.append(stateEvent('one'));
    const rolledBack = db.sqlite.transaction(() => {
      outbox.append(stateEvent('rolled back'));
      throw new Error('the surrounding update failed');
    });
    expect(() => rolledBack()).toThrow(/surrounding/);
    // SQLite rolls AUTOINCREMENT back too, so the next event reuses seq 2.
    outbox.append(stateEvent('two'));
    await Promise.resolve();
    expect(seen).toEqual([
      { seq: 1, detail: 'one' },
      { seq: 2, detail: 'two' },
    ]);
  });

  test('ack is cumulative and ignores another outbox epoch', () => {
    const db = open();
    const outbox = new Outbox(db);
    for (const detail of ['a', 'b', 'c']) outbox.append(stateEvent(detail));
    expect(outbox.ackedSeq()).toBe(0);
    expect(outbox.ack('another-epoch', 3)).toBe(false);
    expect(outbox.ackedSeq()).toBe(0);
    expect(outbox.ack(db.outboxEpoch, 2)).toBe(true);
    expect(outbox.ack(db.outboxEpoch, 1)).toBe(true);
    expect(outbox.ackedSeq()).toBe(2);
    expect(new Outbox(reopen(db)).ackedSeq()).toBe(2);
  });

  test('pruneAcked drops only acknowledged events older than the cutoff', () => {
    const clock = manualNow();
    const db = open();
    const outbox = new Outbox(db, { now: clock.now });
    outbox.append(stateEvent('old acked'));
    outbox.append(stateEvent('old unacked'));
    clock.t += 60_000;
    outbox.append(stateEvent('new'));
    outbox.ack(db.outboxEpoch, 1);
    clock.t += 1_000;
    expect(outbox.pruneAcked(30_000)).toBe(1);
    expect(outbox.eventsAfter(0).map((event) => event.seq)).toEqual([2, 3]);
    // Acknowledging the rest still keeps the young event.
    outbox.ack(db.outboxEpoch, 3);
    expect(outbox.pruneAcked(30_000)).toBe(1);
    expect(outbox.eventsAfter(0).map((event) => event.seq)).toEqual([3]);
  });

  test('pruneBefore drops events older than a time, acknowledged or not, so firstSeq rises', () => {
    const clock = manualNow();
    const outbox = new Outbox(open(), { now: clock.now });
    outbox.append(stateEvent('a'));
    clock.t += 10;
    outbox.append(stateEvent('b'));
    clock.t += 10;
    outbox.append(stateEvent('c'));
    // One of the two old events is acknowledged and the other is not; both go.
    outbox.ack(outbox.epoch, 1);
    expect(outbox.pruneBefore(1_000_015)).toBe(2);
    expect(outbox.firstSeq()).toBe(3);
    expect(outbox.lastSeq()).toBe(3);
  });

  test('firstSeq and lastSeq describe the kept range, and an empty outbox reports lastSeq = firstSeq - 1', () => {
    const clock = manualNow();
    const db = open();
    const outbox = new Outbox(db, { now: clock.now });
    expect([outbox.firstSeq(), outbox.lastSeq()]).toEqual([1, 0]);
    outbox.append(stateEvent('a'));
    outbox.append(stateEvent('b'));
    expect([outbox.firstSeq(), outbox.lastSeq()]).toEqual([1, 2]);
    clock.t += 10;
    outbox.pruneBefore(clock.t);
    // Seqs are never reused, so the empty outbox continues after the pruned ones.
    expect([outbox.firstSeq(), outbox.lastSeq()]).toEqual([3, 2]);
    expect(outbox.append(stateEvent('c')).seq).toBe(3);
    expect([outbox.firstSeq(), outbox.lastSeq()]).toEqual([3, 3]);
    const again = new Outbox(reopen(db));
    expect([again.firstSeq(), again.lastSeq()]).toEqual([3, 3]);
  });

  test('waitAcked resolves true once an ack reaches the seq, at once if it has, and false on timeout', async () => {
    const db = open();
    const outbox = new Outbox(db);
    outbox.append(stateEvent('a'));
    outbox.append(stateEvent('b'));
    outbox.ack(db.outboxEpoch, 1);
    expect(await outbox.waitAcked(1, 10)).toBe(true);
    const waiting = outbox.waitAcked(2, 5_000);
    setTimeout(() => outbox.ack(db.outboxEpoch, 2), 5);
    expect(await waiting).toBe(true);
    const started = Date.now();
    expect(await outbox.waitAcked(3, 30)).toBe(false);
    expect(Date.now() - started).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(25);
  });
});

      [
        { kind: 'prepare_takeover', attemptId: 'T-4-a1', fence, person: 'alice' },
        { kind: 'prepare_takeover', attemptId: 'T-4-a1', fence, person: 'alice' },
      ],
      [decide(approval), decide(approval)],
    ];
    let seq = 1;
    for (const [first, second] of commands) {
      const journal2 = new Journal(open());
      const firstId = `1-R-1-${seq++}`;
      const secondId = `1-R-1-${seq++}`;
      expect(idempotencyKey(first)).not.toBeNull();
      expect(idempotencyKey(second)).toBe(idempotencyKey(first));
      expect(journal2.begin(firstId, 1, first)).toEqual({ state: 'new' });
      expect(journal2.begin(secondId, 2, second)).toEqual({ state: 'running', commandId: firstId });
      journal2.finish(firstId, { ok: true });
      expect(journal2.begin(secondId, 2, second)).toEqual({ state: 'done', commandId: firstId, result: { ok: true } });
    }
    // Another fence, another submission or another approval is another command.
    expect(idempotencyKey(stop(8))).not.toBe(idempotencyKey(stop(7)));
    expect(idempotencyKey(decide('1b4e28ba-2fa1-41d2-883f-0016d3cca427'))).not.toBe(idempotencyKey(decide(approval)));
    expect(idempotencyKey({ kind: 'hold_attempt', attemptId: 'T-4-a1', fence })).not.toBe(idempotencyKey(stop(7)));
    // Commands without a key are told apart by their id alone.
    expect(idempotencyKey({ kind: 'cleanup_attempt', attemptId: 'T-4-a1' })).toBeNull();
    expect(journal.begin('1-R-1-90', 90, { kind: 'cleanup_attempt', attemptId: 'T-4-a1' })).toEqual({ state: 'new' });
    expect(journal.begin('1-R-1-91', 91, { kind: 'cleanup_attempt', attemptId: 'T-4-a1' })).toEqual({ state: 'new' });
  });

  test('pruneBefore drops journal rows older than a time and keeps newer ones', () => {
    const clock = manualNow();
    const journal = new Journal(open(), { now: clock.now });
    journal.begin('1-R-1-1', 1, { kind: 'cleanup_attempt', attemptId: 'T-4-a1' });
    journal.finish('1-R-1-1', { ok: true });
    clock.t += 100;
    journal.begin('1-R-1-2', 2, { kind: 'cleanup_attempt', attemptId: 'T-5-a1' });
    expect(journal.pruneBefore(clock.t - 50)).toBe(1);
    expect(journal.get('1-R-1-1')).toBeNull();
    expect(journal.get('1-R-1-2')).not.toBeNull();
  });
});

describe('AttemptStore', () => {
  test('migrates a version 1 database without claiming its stopped attempts were finalized', () => {
    const db = open();
    const store = new AttemptStore(db);
    store.create(spec(), { clone: '/w/kept', tmpDir: null, cliVersion: null });
    store.update('T-4-a1', { state: 'stopped', wipSha: 'a'.repeat(40), pushError: 'unresolved' });
    const columns = db.sqlite.query('PRAGMA table_info(attempts)').all() as { name: string }[];
    if (columns.some(({ name }) => name === 'finalized_at')) db.sqlite.run('ALTER TABLE attempts DROP COLUMN finalized_at');
    db.sqlite.run('DELETE FROM schema_migrations WHERE version > 1');
    const migrated = reopen(db);
    expect(new AttemptStore(migrated).get('T-4-a1')).toMatchObject({
      state: 'stopped', clone: '/w/kept', wipSha: 'a'.repeat(40), pushError: 'unresolved', finalizedAt: null,
    });
    expect(migrated.sqlite.query('SELECT MAX(version) AS v FROM schema_migrations').get()).toEqual({ v: 2 });
    expect(new AttemptStore(reopen(migrated)).get('T-4-a1')?.finalizedAt).toBeNull();
  });

  test('round-trips every field of an attempt record through its states', () => {
    const clock = manualNow();
    let db = open();
    let store = new AttemptStore(db, { now: clock.now });
    const created = store.create(spec(), { clone: '/w/demo/T-4-a1', tmpDir: '/tmp/agf/abc123', cliVersion: '2.1.285' });
    expect(created).toEqual({
      attemptId: 'T-4-a1',
      spec: expect.not.objectContaining({ agentToken: expect.anything() }),
      fence,
      state: 'starting',
      sessionRef: null,
      clone: '/w/demo/T-4-a1',
      tmpDir: '/tmp/agf/abc123',
      wipSha: null,
      pushedSha: null,
      lastPushAt: null,
      lateWorkCount: 0,
      lateWorkSha: null,
      cliVersion: '2.1.285',
      endedAt: null,
      finalizedAt: null,
      pushError: null,
      createdAt: 1_000_000,
      updatedAt: 1_000_000,
    });
    expect(created.spec).not.toHaveProperty('agentToken');
    for (const state of ['running', 'idle', 'stopped', 'suspended', 'ended'] as const) {
      clock.t += 1;
      store.update('T-4-a1', { state });
      db = reopen(db);
      store = new AttemptStore(db, { now: clock.now });
      expect(store.get('T-4-a1')?.state).toBe(state);
    }
    const sha = (digit: string) => digit.repeat(40);
    clock.t += 1;
    const updated = store.update('T-4-a1', {
      fence: { epoch: 1, counter: 9 },
      sessionRef: 'session-1',
      wipSha: sha('a'),
      pushedSha: sha('b'),
      lastPushAt: 999,
      lateWorkCount: 2,
      lateWorkSha: sha('c'),
      endedAt: 1_234,
      finalizedAt: 1_235,
      pushError: 'remote: rejected',
    });
    db = reopen(db);
    const reread = new AttemptStore(db).get('T-4-a1');
    expect(reread).toEqual(updated);
    expect(reread).toMatchObject({
      fence: { epoch: 1, counter: 9 },
      sessionRef: 'session-1',
      wipSha: sha('a'),
      pushedSha: sha('b'),
      lastPushAt: 999,
      lateWorkCount: 2,
      lateWorkSha: sha('c'),
      cliVersion: '2.1.285',
      endedAt: 1_234,
      finalizedAt: 1_235,
      pushError: 'remote: rejected',
      updatedAt: 1_000_006,
    });
    const reset = new AttemptStore(db);
    reset.update('T-4-a1', { finalizedAt: null });
    expect(new AttemptStore(reopen(db)).get('T-4-a1')?.finalizedAt).toBeNull();
  });

  test('lists and removes attempts, and refuses to update an unknown one', () => {
    const store = new AttemptStore(open());
    store.create(spec(), { clone: '/w/a', tmpDir: null, cliVersion: '2.1.285' });
    store.create(spec({ attemptId: 'T-5-a2', taskId: 'T-5', branch: 'agflow/T-5-x', wipRef: 'refs/agflow/T-5/a2' }), {
      clone: '/w/b',
      tmpDir: null,
      cliVersion: '2.1.285',
    });
    expect(store.list().map((record) => record.attemptId)).toEqual(['T-4-a1', 'T-5-a2']);
    store.remove('T-4-a1');
    expect(store.get('T-4-a1')).toBeNull();
    expect(() => store.update('T-4-a1', { state: 'running' })).toThrow(/T-4-a1/);
  });

  test('the process registry stores and lists recorded groups per attempt', () => {
    const store = new AttemptStore(open());
    const lstart = 'Thu Oct 29 13:04:14 2026';
    store.recordProcess({ attemptId: 'T-4-a1', pid: 100, pgid: 100, lstart, clone: '/w/a' });
    store.recordProcess({ attemptId: 'T-4-a1', pid: 140, pgid: 140, lstart, clone: '/w/a' });
    store.recordProcess({ attemptId: 'T-5-a2', pid: 200, pgid: 200, lstart, clone: '/w/b' });
    // Recording a group again replaces it.
    const later = 'Thu Oct 29 13:05:00 2026';
    store.recordProcess({ attemptId: 'T-4-a1', pid: 100, pgid: 100, lstart: later, clone: '/w/a' });
    expect(store.processes('T-4-a1')).toEqual([
      { attemptId: 'T-4-a1', pid: 100, pgid: 100, lstart: later, clone: '/w/a' },
      { attemptId: 'T-4-a1', pid: 140, pgid: 140, lstart, clone: '/w/a' },
    ]);
    expect(store.processes().map((record) => record.pgid)).toEqual([100, 140, 200]);
    store.forgetProcess('T-4-a1', 140);
    expect(store.processes('T-4-a1').map((record) => record.pgid)).toEqual([100]);
    store.forgetProcesses('T-4-a1');
    expect(store.processes('T-4-a1')).toEqual([]);
    expect(store.processes('T-5-a2')).toHaveLength(1);
  });
});
```

```ts
// Attempt records and the process registry (design 6.3, 7.4). A record outlives the attempt's process, so a restart
// can report it in hello and finish its work; the registry lists every process group the runner recorded for it, so
// a restart can kill what a crash left behind. The spec is kept without its agent token (design 7.2): after a
// restart, the hub's resent command or resume carries a new one.
import type { AttemptSpec, Fence } from '@agflow/core';
import type { RunnerDb } from './db';

/** Design 6.3's LiveAttempt states, plus ended: the hub ended the attempt and its clone waits for cleanup. */
export type LocalAttemptState = 'starting' | 'running' | 'idle' | 'stopped' | 'suspended' | 'ended';

export type StoredAttemptSpec = Omit<AttemptSpec, 'agentToken'>;

export interface AttemptRecord {
  attemptId: string;
  /** The last start or resume's spec: a resume recomputes taskPack, restore and acceptanceIds. */
  spec: StoredAttemptSpec;
  /** The current fence: the spec's, then each resume's. */
  fence: Fence;
  state: LocalAttemptState;
  sessionRef: string | null;
  /** The clone's path. */
  clone: string | null;
  /** The private /tmp/agf/<id> directory of a Claude attempt. */
  tmpDir: string | null;
  /** The newest harvested work, held in the vault until it is pushed. */
  wipSha: string | null;
  /** What the WIP ref holds as last pushed: the lease of the next push. */
  pushedSha: string | null;
  lastPushAt: number | null;
  /** Late-work refs pushed so far; the next one is <attempt>-late-<count + 1>. */
  lateWorkCount: number;
  /**
   * Work held in the vault that waits for a late-work ref: set as its retries start (a final push, or a cleanup's push,
   * that failed or was refused), cleared when attempt.late_work reports it landed, when the cleanup pushed or dropped
   * it, or when a hand-back's push replaced it. A restart retries it after the first welcome, so it outlives the
   * process; while it is set, the attempt's work is not all on the origin (the unpushed-work marker).
   */
  lateWorkSha: string | null;
  /** The CLI version the attempt started with; every resume and take-over uses it (X-13). */
  cliVersion: string | null;
  endedAt: number | null;
  /** Final-work outcome and pending late work are durable; null before work or after crash recovery. */
  finalizedAt: number | null;
  /** The unresolved final-work error; successful late work, hand-back or cleanup resolution clears it. */
  pushError: string | null;
  createdAt: number;
  updatedAt: number;
}

/** The fields update may change. */
export type AttemptPatch = Partial<Omit<AttemptRecord, 'attemptId' | 'spec' | 'createdAt' | 'updatedAt'>> & {
  spec?: StoredAttemptSpec;
};

/** One recorded process group: its leader's identity and the clone it works in. */
export interface ProcessRecord {
  attemptId: string;
  pid: number;
  pgid: number;
  /** ps's lstart of the leader; with pid, the identity checked before every group kill. */
  lstart: string;
  clone: string | null;
}

interface AttemptRow {
  attempt_id: string;
  spec: string;
  fence: string;
  state: LocalAttemptState;
  session_ref: string | null;
  clone: string | null;
  tmp_dir: string | null;
  wip_sha: string | null;
  pushed_sha: string | null;
  last_push_at: number | null;
  late_work_count: number;
  late_work_sha: string | null;
  cli_version: string | null;
  ended_at: number | null;
  finalized_at: number | null;
  push_error: string | null;
  created_at: number;
  updated_at: number;
}

function recordOf(row: AttemptRow): AttemptRecord {
  return {
    attemptId: row.attempt_id,
    spec: JSON.parse(row.spec) as StoredAttemptSpec,
    fence: JSON.parse(row.fence) as Fence,
    state: row.state,
    sessionRef: row.session_ref,
    clone: row.clone,
    tmpDir: row.tmp_dir,
    wipSha: row.wip_sha,
    pushedSha: row.pushed_sha,
    lastPushAt: row.last_push_at,
    lateWorkCount: row.late_work_count,
    lateWorkSha: row.late_work_sha,
    cliVersion: row.cli_version,
    endedAt: row.ended_at,
    finalizedAt: row.finalized_at,
    pushError: row.push_error,
    createdAt: row.created_at,
    updatedAt: row.updated_at,
  };
}

// A caller may hand over the full spec; the token is dropped here, whatever the static type says.
function withoutToken(spec: StoredAttemptSpec & { agentToken?: string }): StoredAttemptSpec {
  const { agentToken: _token, ...rest } = spec;
  return rest;
}

export class AttemptStore {
  private readonly now: () => number;

  constructor(
    private readonly db: RunnerDb,
    options: { now?: () => number } = {},
  ) {
    this.now = options.now ?? Date.now;
  }

  /** Records a new attempt as starting. */
  create(
    spec: AttemptSpec | StoredAttemptSpec,
    init: { clone: string | null; tmpDir: string | null; cliVersion: string | null },
  ): AttemptRecord {
    const at = this.now();
    const stored = withoutToken(spec);
    this.db.sqlite
      .query(
        `INSERT INTO attempts (attempt_id, spec, fence, state, clone, tmp_dir, cli_version, created_at, updated_at)
         VALUES ($attemptId, $spec, $fence, 'starting', $clone, $tmpDir, $cliVersion, $at, $at)`,
      )
      .run({
        attemptId: stored.attemptId,
        spec: JSON.stringify(stored),
        fence: JSON.stringify(stored.fence),
        clone: init.clone,
        tmpDir: init.tmpDir,
        cliVersion: init.cliVersion,
        at,
      });
    return this.get(stored.attemptId) as AttemptRecord;
  }

  get(attemptId: string): AttemptRecord | null {
    const row = this.db.sqlite.query('SELECT * FROM attempts WHERE attempt_id = $attemptId').get({ attemptId });
    return row ? recordOf(row as AttemptRow) : null;
  }

  /** Every record, oldest first. */
  list(): AttemptRecord[] {
    const rows = this.db.sqlite.query('SELECT * FROM attempts ORDER BY created_at, rowid').all() as AttemptRow[];
    return rows.map(recordOf);
  }

  update(attemptId: string, patch: AttemptPatch): AttemptRecord {
    const current = this.get(attemptId);
    if (!current) throw new Error(`no attempt record for ${attemptId}`);
    const next: AttemptRecord = { ...current, ...patch, updatedAt: this.now() };
    if (patch.spec) next.spec = withoutToken(patch.spec);
    this.db.sqlite
      .query(
        `UPDATE attempts SET spec = $spec, fence = $fence, state = $state, session_ref = $sessionRef, clone = $clone,
           tmp_dir = $tmpDir, wip_sha = $wipSha, pushed_sha = $pushedSha, last_push_at = $lastPushAt,
           late_work_count = $lateWorkCount, late_work_sha = $lateWorkSha, cli_version = $cliVersion,
           ended_at = $endedAt, finalized_at = $finalizedAt, push_error = $pushError, updated_at = $updatedAt
         WHERE attempt_id = $attemptId`,
      )
      .run({
        attemptId,
        spec: JSON.stringify(next.spec),
        fence: JSON.stringify(next.fence),
        state: next.state,
        sessionRef: next.sessionRef,
        clone: next.clone,
        tmpDir: next.tmpDir,
        wipSha: next.wipSha,
        pushedSha: next.pushedSha,
        lastPushAt: next.lastPushAt,
        lateWorkCount: next.lateWorkCount,
        lateWorkSha: next.lateWorkSha,
        cliVersion: next.cliVersion,
        endedAt: next.endedAt,
        finalizedAt: next.finalizedAt,
        pushError: next.pushError,
        updatedAt: next.updatedAt,
      });
    return next;
  }

  /** Forgets the attempt and its recorded groups (cleanup_attempt). */
  remove(attemptId: string): void {
    this.db.sqlite.transaction(() => {
      this.db.sqlite.query('DELETE FROM attempts WHERE attempt_id = $attemptId').run({ attemptId });
      this.forgetProcesses(attemptId);
    })();
  }

  /** Records a process group, replacing an earlier record of the same group. */
  recordProcess(record: ProcessRecord): void {
    this.db.sqlite
      .query(
        `INSERT INTO processes (attempt_id, pgid, pid, lstart, clone, recorded_at)
         VALUES ($attemptId, $pgid, $pid, $lstart, $clone, $at)
         ON CONFLICT (attempt_id, pgid) DO UPDATE SET pid = $pid, lstart = $lstart, clone = $clone, recorded_at = $at`,
      )
      .run({ ...record, at: this.now() });
  }

  /** The recorded groups of one attempt, or of every attempt, in the order they were first recorded. */
  processes(attemptId?: string): ProcessRecord[] {
    const where = attemptId === undefined ? '' : 'WHERE attempt_id = $attemptId';
    const rows = this.db.sqlite.query(`SELECT * FROM processes ${where} ORDER BY rowid`).all(
      attemptId === undefined ? {} : { attemptId },
    ) as { attempt_id: string; pid: number; pgid: number; lstart: string; clone: string | null }[];
    return rows.map((row) => ({
      attemptId: row.attempt_id,
      pid: row.pid,
      pgid: row.pgid,
      lstart: row.lstart,
      clone: row.clone,
    }));
  }

  forgetProcess(attemptId: string, pgid: number): void {
    this.db.sqlite
      .query('DELETE FROM processes WHERE attempt_id = $attemptId AND pgid = $pgid')
      .run({ attemptId, pgid });
  }

  forgetProcesses(attemptId: string): void {
    this.db.sqlite.query('DELETE FROM processes WHERE attempt_id = $attemptId').run({ attemptId });
  }
}
```

```ts
// runner.db (design 6.3, 7.4): the runner's durable state in bun:sqlite. The outbox, the command journal, the attempt
// records, the process registry and a little meta live here; nothing in it is secret (design 7.2). Versioned
// migrations work like the hub's db.ts, and callers may add named migrations of their own (M2c's tables), so no
// other plan has to edit this file.
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { Database } from 'bun:sqlite';

const SCHEMA_V1 = `
CREATE TABLE meta (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE outbox (
  seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  type TEXT NOT NULL,
  attempt_id TEXT,
  event TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX outbox_at ON outbox (at);

CREATE TABLE outbox_ack (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK (id = 1), seq INTEGER NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO outbox_ack (id, seq) VALUES (1, 0);

CREATE TABLE journal (
  command_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  seq INTEGER NOT NULL,
  kind TEXT NOT NULL,
  attempt_id TEXT,
  idempotency_key TEXT UNIQUE,
  command TEXT NOT NULL,
  outbox_seq INTEGER,
  state TEXT NOT NULL,
  result TEXT,
  started_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  finished_at INTEGER
);
CREATE INDEX journal_state ON journal (state);
CREATE INDEX journal_started ON journal (started_at);

CREATE TABLE attempts (
  attempt_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  spec TEXT NOT NULL,
  fence TEXT NOT NULL,
  state TEXT NOT NULL,
  session_ref TEXT,
  clone TEXT,
  tmp_dir TEXT,
  wip_sha TEXT,
  pushed_sha TEXT,
  last_push_at INTEGER,
  late_work_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  late_work_sha TEXT,
  cli_version TEXT,
  ended_at INTEGER,
  push_error TEXT,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE processes (
  attempt_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  pgid INTEGER NOT NULL,
  pid INTEGER NOT NULL,
  lstart TEXT NOT NULL,
  clone TEXT,
  recorded_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (attempt_id, pgid)
);
`;

const MIGRATIONS: readonly string[] = [SCHEMA_V1, 'ALTER TABLE attempts ADD COLUMN finalized_at INTEGER;'];

/** A migration another plan adds; it runs once, identified by its name, after the runner's own. */
export interface RunnerMigration {
  name: string;
  sql: string;
}

/** The meta values the runner keeps between runs. */
export interface RunnerMeta {
  /** The hub epoch of the last welcome; hello reports it, so a restored hub knows to reconcile. */
  lastHubEpoch: number | null;
  /** The last welcome's wipRefPrefix, for pushes made before the next welcome. */
  wipRefPrefix: string | null;
  /** The project's name and repo from GET /api/status; the project key names the vault and work directories. */
  project: { name: string; repo: string } | null;
}

const OUTBOX_EPOCH = 'outboxEpoch';

export class RunnerDb {
  /** New whenever runner.db is new, so the hub can tell a fresh outbox from one it has acknowledged before. */
  readonly outboxEpoch: string;

  constructor(
    readonly sqlite: Database,
    readonly path: string,
  ) {
    const row = sqlite.query('SELECT value FROM meta WHERE key = $key').get({ key: OUTBOX_EPOCH }) as {
      value: string;
    } | null;
    if (!row) throw new Error(`${path} has no outbox epoch`);
    this.outboxEpoch = JSON.parse(row.value) as string;
  }

  meta<K extends keyof RunnerMeta>(key: K): RunnerMeta[K] {
    const row = this.sqlite.query('SELECT value FROM meta WHERE key = $key').get({ key }) as { value: string } | null;
    return row ? (JSON.parse(row.value) as RunnerMeta[K]) : null;
  }

  setMeta<K extends keyof RunnerMeta>(key: K, value: RunnerMeta[K]): void {
    this.sqlite
      .query('INSERT INTO meta (key, value) VALUES ($key, $value) ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET value = $value')
      .run({ key, value: JSON.stringify(value) });
  }

  /** The names of the extra migrations applied so far, in the order they ran. */
  appliedMigrations(): string[] {
    const rows = this.sqlite.query('SELECT name FROM extra_migrations ORDER BY rowid').all() as { name: string }[];
    return rows.map((row) => row.name);
  }

  close(): void {
    this.sqlite.close();
  }
}

export function openRunnerDb(path: string, options: { migrations?: readonly RunnerMigration[] } = {}): RunnerDb {
  const sqlite = new Database(path, { create: true, strict: true });
  try {
    sqlite.run('PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;');
    sqlite.run('PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000;');
    migrate(sqlite);
    migrateExtra(sqlite, options.migrations ?? []);
    // Written once, by whoever creates the database: a deleted and recreated runner.db gets a new epoch.
    sqlite
      .query('INSERT OR IGNORE INTO meta (key, value) VALUES ($key, $value)')
      .run({ key: OUTBOX_EPOCH, value: JSON.stringify(randomUUID()) });
    return new RunnerDb(sqlite, path);
  } catch (error) {
    sqlite.close();
    throw error;
  }
}

function migrate(sqlite: Database): void {
  sqlite.run('CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations (version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, applied_at INTEGER NOT NULL)');
  const row = sqlite.query('SELECT MAX(version) AS v FROM schema_migrations').get() as { v: number | null };
  const version = row.v ?? 0;
  // Older code on a newer schema (after a downgrade) would misread the data.
  if (version > MIGRATIONS.length) {
    throw new Error(
      `runner.db schema version ${version} is newer than this runner supports (${MIGRATIONS.length}); ` +
        'run a newer agflow',
    );
  }
  for (let index = version; index < MIGRATIONS.length; index++) {
    const sql = MIGRATIONS[index] as string;
    sqlite.transaction(() => {
      sqlite.run(sql);
      sqlite
        .query('INSERT INTO schema_migrations (version, applied_at) VALUES ($version, $at)')
        .run({ version: index + 1, at: Date.now() });
    })();
  }
}

function migrateExtra(sqlite: Database, migrations: readonly RunnerMigration[]): void {
  const names = new Set<string>();
  for (const { name } of migrations) {
    if (names.has(name)) throw new Error(`two runner.db migrations are named ${name}`);
    names.add(name);
  }
  sqlite.run('CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS extra_migrations (name TEXT PRIMARY KEY, applied_at INTEGER NOT NULL)');
  const applied = sqlite.query('SELECT 1 FROM extra_migrations WHERE name = $name');
  for (const { name, sql } of migrations) {
    if (applied.get({ name })) continue;
    sqlite.transaction(() => {
      sqlite.run(sql);
      sqlite.query('INSERT INTO extra_migrations (name, applied_at) VALUES ($name, $at)').run({ name, at: Date.now() });
    })();
  }
}
```

```ts
// The command journal (design 6.3, "Commands"): each command is recorded as running before it executes and as done
// with its result after, so a resent command is never executed twice. Commands are matched by id and by the
// idempotency keys of design 6.3, because the hub may resend a command under a new id (after a restore, or with a
// fresh agent token). Agent tokens are dropped before anything is stored (design 7.2).
import { type AttemptSpec, formatFence, type RunnerCommand, type RunnerMessage } from '@agflow/core';
import type { RunnerDb } from './db';

/** What a command answers: the result message without its envelope. */
export type CommandResult = Omit<Extract<RunnerMessage, { t: 'result' }>, 't' | 'commandId'>;

type ResumeCommand = Extract<RunnerCommand, { kind: 'resume_attempt' }>;

/** A command as the journal keeps it: start_attempt and resume_attempt without their agent token. */
export type JournaledCommand =
  | Exclude<RunnerCommand, { kind: 'start_attempt' | 'resume_attempt' }>
  | { kind: 'start_attempt'; attempt: Omit<AttemptSpec, 'agentToken'> }
  | Omit<ResumeCommand, 'agentToken'>;

export interface JournalEntry {
  commandId: string;
  seq: number;
  kind: RunnerCommand['kind'];
  attemptId: string | null;
  /** idempotencyKey(command), or null when only the id identifies the command. */
  key: string | null;
  command: JournaledCommand;
  /**
   * The outbox's newest seq when the command first arrived, as the executor gives it to begin; null when none was
   * given. An update_settings echo answers only the settings edits appended before it (X-12), after a restart too.
   */
  outboxSeq: number | null;
  state: 'running' | 'done';
  result: CommandResult | null;
  startedAt: number;
  finishedAt: number | null;
}

/**
 * What begin found. new: the caller executes the command. running: an execution of the same command (this id, or
 * the first id with the same key) has not finished; its result answers this one too. done: answer the stored result.
 */
export type JournalBegin =
  | { state: 'new' }
  | { state: 'running'; commandId: string }
  | { state: 'done'; commandId: string; result: CommandResult };

/**
 * Design 6.3's idempotency keys: start and resume by attempt and fence, push_submission by submission, stop, hold
 * and prepare_takeover by fence, decide_approval by approval. Every other command is identified by its id alone.
 */
export function idempotencyKey(command: RunnerCommand): string | null {
  switch (command.kind) {
    case 'start_attempt':
      return `${command.kind}:${command.attempt.attemptId}:${formatFence(command.attempt.fence)}`;
    case 'resume_attempt':
    case 'stop_attempt':
    case 'hold_attempt':
    case 'prepare_takeover':
      return `${command.kind}:${command.attemptId}:${formatFence(command.fence)}`;
    case 'push_submission':
      return `${command.kind}:${command.submissionId}`;
    case 'decide_approval':
      return `${command.kind}:${command.approvalId}`;
    default:
      return null;
  }
}

/** The command without its agent token. */
export function journaledCommand(command: RunnerCommand): JournaledCommand {
  if (command.kind === 'start_attempt') {
    const { agentToken: _token, ...attempt } = command.attempt;
    return { kind: command.kind, attempt };
  }
  if (command.kind === 'resume_attempt') {
    const { agentToken: _token, ...rest } = command;
    return rest;
  }
  return command;
}

/** The attempt a command is about, if any. */
function attemptOf(command: RunnerCommand): string | null {
  if (command.kind === 'start_attempt') return command.attempt.attemptId;
  return 'attemptId' in command ? command.attemptId : null;
}

interface JournalRow {
  command_id: string;
  seq: number;
  kind: RunnerCommand['kind'];
  attempt_id: string | null;
  idempotency_key: string | null;
  command: string;
  outbox_seq: number | null;
  state: 'running' | 'done';
  result: string | null;
  started_at: number;
  finished_at: number | null;
}

function entryOf(row: JournalRow): JournalEntry {
  return {
    commandId: row.command_id,
    seq: row.seq,
    kind: row.kind,
    attemptId: row.attempt_id,
    key: row.idempotency_key,
    command: JSON.parse(row.command) as JournaledCommand,
    outboxSeq: row.outbox_seq,
    state: row.state,
    result: row.result === null ? null : (JSON.parse(row.result) as CommandResult),
    startedAt: row.started_at,
    finishedAt: row.finished_at,
  };
}

export class Journal {
  private readonly now: () => number;

  constructor(
    private readonly db: RunnerDb,
    options: { now?: () => number } = {},
  ) {
    this.now = options.now ?? Date.now;
  }

  /**
   * Records the command as running unless this id or its idempotency key is already journaled, with the outbox
   * position it arrived at; a resend leaves the first one's.
   */
  begin(commandId: string, seq: number, command: RunnerCommand, outboxSeq: number | null = null): JournalBegin {
    const key = idempotencyKey(command);
    return this.db.sqlite.transaction((): JournalBegin => {
      const existing = this.db.sqlite
        .query('SELECT * FROM journal WHERE command_id = $commandId OR idempotency_key = $key ORDER BY rowid LIMIT 1')
        .get({ commandId, key }) as JournalRow | null;
      if (existing) {
        const { commandId: first, state, result } = entryOf(existing);
        if (state === 'done' && result) return { state, commandId: first, result };
        return { state: 'running', commandId: first };
      }
      this.db.sqlite
        .query(
          `INSERT INTO journal
             (command_id, seq, kind, attempt_id, idempotency_key, command, outbox_seq, state, started_at)
           VALUES ($commandId, $seq, $kind, $attemptId, $key, $command, $outboxSeq, 'running', $at)`,
        )
        .run({
          commandId,
          seq,
          kind: command.kind,
          attemptId: attemptOf(command),
          key,
          command: JSON.stringify(journaledCommand(command)),
          outboxSeq,
          at: this.now(),
        });
      return { state: 'new' };
    })();
  }

  /** Records the result of a command begin returned new for. */
  finish(commandId: string, result: CommandResult): void {
    const { changes } = this.db.sqlite
      .query("UPDATE journal SET state = 'done', result = $result, finished_at = $at WHERE command_id = $commandId")
      .run({ commandId, result: JSON.stringify(result), at: this.now() });
    if (changes === 0) throw new Error(`command ${commandId} is not in the journal`);
  }

  get(commandId: string): JournalEntry | null {
    const row = this.db.sqlite.query('SELECT * FROM journal WHERE command_id = $commandId').get({ commandId });
    return row ? entryOf(row as JournalRow) : null;
  }

  /** Commands a previous run left running, in arrival order; the executor re-runs or answers them after a restart. */
  running(): JournalEntry[] {
    const rows = this.db.sqlite.query("SELECT * FROM journal WHERE state = 'running' ORDER BY rowid").all();
    return (rows as JournalRow[]).map(entryOf);
  }

  /** Drops rows started before at (M2c's 14-day cutoff). Gives how many. */
  pruneBefore(at: number): number {
    return this.db.sqlite.query('DELETE FROM journal WHERE started_at < $at').run({ at }).changes;
  }
}
```

```ts
// The outbox (design 6.3, "Events"): every event the runner reports is stored here with an AUTOINCREMENT seq before
// it is sent, and replayed after each welcome until the hub acknowledges it. Acknowledgements are cumulative and
// belong to one outbox epoch. M2c's retention prunes it (X-7); the runtime schedules nothing here.
import { parseRunnerEvent, type RunnerEvent } from '@agflow/core';
import type { RunnerDb } from './db';

/** An event as the outbox stores and sends it. */
export type StoredEvent = RunnerEvent;

type WithoutStamp<E> = E extends RunnerEvent ? Omit<E, 'seq' | 'at'> : never;
/** An event before the outbox gives it its seq and time. */
export type NewEvent = WithoutStamp<RunnerEvent>;

/**
 * The largest event the outbox stores, as serialized JSON: 1 MiB, far under the hub's 16 MB message limit, so the
 * link can always send one event alone. Producers clip agent-controlled lists to stay under it.
 */
export const MAX_EVENT_BYTES = 1024 * 1024;

interface Waiter {
  seq: number;
  resolve(acked: boolean): void;
  timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>;
}

export class Outbox {
  private readonly now: () => number;
  private readonly listeners = new Set<(event: StoredEvent) => void>();
  private readonly waiters = new Set<Waiter>();
  /** The highest seq announced to the listeners. */
  private announcedSeq = 0;
  private announcing = false;

  constructor(
    private readonly db: RunnerDb,
    options: { now?: () => number } = {},
  ) {
    this.now = options.now ?? Date.now;
  }

  /** The epoch hello reports and acks name. */
  get epoch(): string {
    return this.db.outboxEpoch;
  }

  /**
   * Stores an event and tells the listeners (the link streams it). The hub would only reject an event its schema
   * cannot read, so such an event is refused here, where the bug is; so is one over MAX_EVENT_BYTES, which would
   * block every event after it. An append may share a synchronous transaction with other writes.
   */
  append(event: NewEvent): StoredEvent {
    const at = this.now();
    const parsed = parseRunnerEvent({ seq: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, at, ...event });
    if (!parsed.ok) throw new Error(`the outbox refused an event: ${parsed.error}`);
    const json = JSON.stringify(event);
    // The stored event adds its seq and at to this; 64 bytes covers both.
    const bytes = Buffer.byteLength(json) + 64;
    if (bytes > MAX_EVENT_BYTES) {
      throw new Error(`the outbox refused a ${event.type} event of ${bytes} bytes: too large (${MAX_EVENT_BYTES} max)`);
    }
    const attemptId = 'attemptId' in event ? event.attemptId : null;
    const { seq } = this.db.sqlite
      .query(`INSERT INTO outbox (at, type, attempt_id, event) VALUES ($at, $type, $attemptId, $event) RETURNING seq`)
      .get({ at, type: event.type, attemptId, event: json }) as { seq: number };
    this.scheduleAnnounce();
    return { seq, at, ...event } as StoredEvent;
  }

  /**
   * Called with each committed event, in seq order, from a microtask after the append: by then a surrounding
   * transaction has committed or rolled back, and a rolled-back event (whose seq SQLite hands out again) is never
   * announced. Returns the unsubscribe.
   */
  onAppend(listener: (event: StoredEvent) => void): () => void {
    // Nothing is announced while nobody listens, so a first listener starts from the events still to come.
    if (this.listeners.size === 0) this.announcedSeq = this.lastAssigned();
    this.listeners.add(listener);
    return () => this.listeners.delete(listener);
  }

  /** The kept events after seq, in seq order. */
  eventsAfter(seq: number, limit = Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER): StoredEvent[] {
    const rows = this.db.sqlite
      .query('SELECT seq, at, event FROM outbox WHERE seq > $seq ORDER BY seq LIMIT $limit')
      .all({ seq, limit }) as { seq: number; at: number; event: string }[];
    return rows.map((row) => ({ seq: row.seq, at: row.at, ...JSON.parse(row.event) }) as StoredEvent);
  }

  /** The lowest kept seq, or the next seq when none is kept. */
  firstSeq(): number {
    const row = this.db.sqlite.query('SELECT MIN(seq) AS seq FROM outbox').get() as { seq: number | null };
    return row.seq ?? this.lastAssigned() + 1;
  }

  /** The highest seq held, or firstSeq - 1 when the outbox is empty (X-1). */
  lastSeq(): number {
    const row = this.db.sqlite.query('SELECT MAX(seq) AS seq FROM outbox').get() as { seq: number | null };
    return row.seq ?? this.firstSeq() - 1;
  }

  /** The highest seq the hub has acknowledged in this outbox epoch. */
  ackedSeq(): number {
    return (this.db.sqlite.query('SELECT seq FROM outbox_ack WHERE id = 1').get() as { seq: number }).seq;
  }

  /** A cumulative ack. An ack of another epoch (an older runner.db) is ignored; gives whether it applied. */
  ack(epoch: string, seq: number): boolean {
    if (epoch !== this.epoch) return false;
    this.db.sqlite.query('UPDATE outbox_ack SET seq = MAX(seq, $seq) WHERE id = 1').run({ seq });
    const acked = this.ackedSeq();
    for (const waiter of [...this.waiters]) {
      if (waiter.seq <= acked) this.settle(waiter, true);
    }
    return true;
  }

  /** Resolves true once the hub has acknowledged seq (at once if it has), false after timeoutMs. */
  waitAcked(seq: number, timeoutMs: number): Promise<boolean> {
    if (seq <= this.ackedSeq()) return Promise.resolve(true);
    return new Promise((resolve) => {
      const waiter: Waiter = { seq, resolve, timer: setTimeout(() => this.settle(waiter, false), timeoutMs) };
      this.waiters.add(waiter);
    });
  }

  /** Drops acknowledged events older than olderThanMs, the 48 h retention (design 6.3). Gives how many. */
  pruneAcked(olderThanMs: number): number {
    return this.db.sqlite
      .query('DELETE FROM outbox WHERE seq <= (SELECT seq FROM outbox_ack WHERE id = 1) AND at < $cutoff')
      .run({ cutoff: this.now() - olderThanMs }).changes;
  }

  /** Drops every event older than at, acknowledged or not (M2c's 14-day cutoff). Gives how many. */
  pruneBefore(at: number): number {
    return this.db.sqlite.query('DELETE FROM outbox WHERE at < $at').run({ at }).changes;
  }

  // AUTOINCREMENT never reuses a seq, so after a prune the outbox continues from the last one it assigned.
  private lastAssigned(): number {
    const row = this.db.sqlite.query("SELECT seq FROM sqlite_sequence WHERE name = 'outbox'").get() as {
      seq: number;
    } | null;
    return row?.seq ?? 0;
  }

  private scheduleAnnounce(): void {
    if (this.announcing || this.listeners.size === 0) return;
    this.announcing = true;
    queueMicrotask(() => {
      this.announcing = false;
      if (this.listeners.size === 0) return;
      const events = this.eventsAfter(this.announcedSeq);
      const last = events.at(-1);
      if (!last) return;
      this.announcedSeq = last.seq;
      for (const event of events) {
        for (const listener of [...this.listeners]) listener(event);
      }
    });
  }

  private settle(waiter: Waiter, acked: boolean): void {
    if (!this.waiters.delete(waiter)) return;
    clearTimeout(waiter.timer);
    waiter.resolve(acked);
  }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run the tests and see them pass**

Run: `bun test packages/runner/test/db.test.ts && bun test && bun run typecheck`
Expected: the task's tests pass; then the whole suite passes (`0 fail`) and `tsc` exits 0.

`Outbox.append` validates every event with core's `parseRunnerEvent` and refuses one over 1 MiB (`MAX_EVENT_BYTES`), because the hub would only acknowledge an unreadable event as a reject. Idempotency keys include the command kind, so a stop and a hold with one fence stay apart. `Journal.begin(id, seq, command, outboxSeq?)` keeps the first arrival's position when a resend joins it. The test greps the database file, its `-wal` and its `-shm` for the agent token. `SCHEMA_V1` holds the `outbox_seq` and `late_work_sha` columns; these earlier schema-1 additions predate shipping, so databases predating them must be recreated. Preserve schema 1; migration 2 adds nullable `finalized_at` to existing version-1 databases.

Add migration 2, ALTER TABLE attempts ADD COLUMN finalized_at INTEGER; preserve migration 1. Add AttemptRecord.finalizedAt: number | null, AttemptRow.finalized_at, recordOf mapping and AttemptStore.update persistence. New and migrated records default to null. Tests: populated version-1 migration, timestamp round-trip, explicit reset to null across reopening. pushError is the unresolved final-work error, cleared by successful work resolution.

### Task 6: Process identity, recorded groups, descendants and sweeps

Design 7.4's process tools. A process is known by pid, pgid and lstart, read with one `ps` call under `LC_ALL=C` and `TZ=UTC`, and a group is signalled only while a member still matches its recorded identity, because macOS pids wrap; groups 0 and 1 are never signalled. `DescendantTracker` snapshots an attempt's process tree and remembers groups whose members were reparented, and `sweepCloneProcesses` kills, after an identity check, the processes whose working directory is inside a clone (found with `lsof`). `drainToLog` and `boundedWait` keep a child's pipes drained and a stop bounded, and the ps and lsof parsers are pure exports that M2g's harness reuses (X-42). Task 6 also adds `packages/runner/test/prerequisites.ts` and `prerequisites.test.ts`. The shared `requireLsofOnMacOS` helper fails before fixtures are created when macOS cannot find `lsof` on PATH; its diagnostic explicitly says to include `/usr/sbin`. A subprocess regression removes lsof from PATH and proves the clone-sweep test fails instead of skipping.

```ts
/** Call before creating fixtures in macOS process-sweep and clone hand-back tests. */
export function requireLsofOnMacOS(
  platform: NodeJS.Platform = process.platform,
  which: (command: string) => string | null = Bun.which,
): void {
  if (platform === 'darwin' && which('lsof') === null) {
    throw new Error('macOS test prerequisite: lsof must be available on PATH (include /usr/sbin)');
  }
}
```

```ts
import { afterEach, describe, expect, setDefaultTimeout, test } from 'bun:test';
import { chmodSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { AttemptStore } from '../src/attempt-store';
import { openRunnerDb } from '../src/db';
import {
  boundedWait,
  DescendantTracker,
  drainToLog,
  killGroup,
  listProcesses,
  parseLsofCwds,
  PS_COLUMNS,
  PS_ENV,
  parsePs,
  type ProcessIdentity,
  processIdentity,
  recordGroup,
  sameProcess,
  sweepCloneProcesses,
} from '../src/processes';
import { requireLsofOnMacOS } from './prerequisites';

// Every test here runs git or agent processes, which take several times as long on a machine loaded by other suites.
setDefaultTimeout(30_000);

const dirs: string[] = [];
const groups = new Set<number>();
afterEach(() => {
  for (const pgid of groups) {
    try {
      process.kill(-pgid, 'SIGKILL');
    } catch {
      // Already gone.
    }
  }
  groups.clear();
  for (const dir of dirs.splice(0)) rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
});

function tempDir(prefix: string): string {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), prefix));
  dirs.push(dir);
  return dir;
}

/** Starts a shell script as the leader of its own group, as the runner starts agents. */
function spawnGroup(script: string, options: { cwd?: string; stdin?: 'pipe' | 'ignore' } = {}) {
  const proc = Bun.spawn(['sh', '-c', script], {
    cwd: options.cwd,
    detached: true,
    stdin: options.stdin ?? 'ignore',
    stdout: 'ignore',
    stderr: 'ignore',
  });
  groups.add(proc.pid);
  return proc;
}

/** True once the process is gone or only a zombie waiting to be reaped. */
async function gone(pid: number): Promise<boolean> {
  const rows = await listProcesses();
  const row = rows.find((candidate) => candidate.pid === pid);
  return row === undefined || row.stat.startsWith('Z');
}

async function until(check: () => Promise<boolean> | boolean, timeoutMs = 15_000): Promise<void> {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  while (!(await check())) {
    if (Date.now() > deadline) throw new Error('timed out waiting for a condition');
    await Bun.sleep(20);
  }
}

/** A pid written by the script, once the file holds a whole line. */
async function pidFrom(file: string): Promise<number> {
  let text = '';
  await until(() => {
    try {
      text = readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
    } catch {
      return false;
    }
    return text.endsWith('\n');
  });
  return Number(text.trim());
}

const LSTART = /^[A-Z][a-z]{2} [A-Z][a-z]{2} {1,2}\d{1,2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2} \d{4}$/;

describe('processIdentity and recordGroup', () => {
  test('a detached child has its own group and an lstart, and recordGroup stores it for the attempt', async () => {
    const proc = spawnGroup('exec sleep 30');
    const identity = await processIdentity(proc.pid);
    expect(identity).toEqual({ pid: proc.pid, pgid: proc.pid, lstart: expect.stringMatching(LSTART) });
    const db = openRunnerDb(join(tempDir('agflow-proc-db-'), 'runner.db'));
    try {
      const store = new AttemptStore(db);
      const record = recordGroup(store, 'T-4-a1', '/w/demo/T-4-a1', identity as ProcessIdentity);
      expect(record).toEqual({ attemptId: 'T-4-a1', clone: '/w/demo/T-4-a1', ...(identity as ProcessIdentity) });
      expect(store.processes('T-4-a1')).toEqual([record]);
    } finally {
      db.close();
    }
  });

  test('a process that is gone has no identity', async () => {
    const proc = Bun.spawn(['true'], { stdout: 'ignore', stderr: 'ignore' });
    await proc.exited;
    expect(await processIdentity(proc.pid)).toBeNull();
  });

  test('sameProcess compares pid and lstart', () => {
    const a = { pid: 10, pgid: 10, lstart: 'Thu Oct 29 13:04:14 2026' };
    const regrouped: ProcessIdentity = { ...a, pgid: 11 };
    expect(sameProcess(a, regrouped)).toBe(true);
    expect(sameProcess(a, { ...a, lstart: 'Thu Oct 29 13:04:15 2026' })).toBe(false);
    expect(sameProcess(a, { ...a, pid: 11 })).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe('killGroup', () => {
  test('signals the whole group while the identity matches', async () => {
    const dir = tempDir('agflow-proc-kill-');
    const proc = spawnGroup(`sleep 30 & echo $! > ${dir}/member; wait`);
    const member = await pidFrom(join(dir, 'member'));
    const identity = (await processIdentity(proc.pid)) as ProcessIdentity;
    expect(await killGroup(identity, 'SIGKILL')).toBe(true);
    await until(() => gone(proc.pid));
    await until(() => gone(member));
  });

  test('signals nothing when the recorded lstart differs, as after PID reuse', async () => {
    const proc = spawnGroup('exec sleep 30');
    const identity = (await processIdentity(proc.pid)) as ProcessIdentity;
    const reused = { ...identity, lstart: 'Thu Jan  1 00:00:00 1970' };
    expect(await killGroup(reused, 'SIGKILL')).toBe(false);
    await Bun.sleep(50);
    expect(await processIdentity(proc.pid)).toEqual(identity);
  });

  test('never signals process group 1 or 0, even for the real identity of pid 1', async () => {
    const launchd = (await processIdentity(1)) as ProcessIdentity;
    expect(launchd.pgid).toBe(1);
    // A real kill(-1) would signal every process the user owns, so the signals are recorded instead.
    const sent: [number, string | number | undefined][] = [];
    const realKill = process.kill;
    process.kill = ((pid: number, signal?: string | number) => {
      sent.push([pid, signal]);
      return true;
    }) as typeof process.kill;
    try {
      expect(await killGroup(launchd, 'SIGKILL')).toBe(false);
      expect(await killGroup({ pid: 0, pgid: 0, lstart: launchd.lstart }, 'SIGKILL')).toBe(false);
    } finally {
      process.kill = realKill;
    }
    expect(sent).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('DescendantTracker', () => {
  test('a snapshot keeps a grandchild that started its own group after its parent exited', async () => {
    const dir = tempDir('agflow-proc-tree-');
    // The middle shell starts the grandchild in a group of its own, then waits for a line on stdin and exits.
    const middle = `sh -c 'perl -e "setpgrp(0, 0); exec @ARGV" sleep 30 & echo $! > ${dir}/grandchild; read line'`;
    const agent = spawnGroup(`${middle}; sleep 30`, { stdin: 'pipe' });
    const grandchild = await pidFrom(join(dir, 'grandchild'));
    groups.add(grandchild);
    await until(async () => (await processIdentity(grandchild))?.pgid === grandchild);
    const root = (await processIdentity(agent.pid)) as ProcessIdentity;
    const tracker = new DescendantTracker();
    await tracker.snapshot([root]);
    expect(tracker.groups().map((group) => group.pgid)).toContain(grandchild);
    // The middle shell exits; the grandchild is reparented and no longer descends from the agent.
    const parent = (await listProcesses()).find((row) => row.pid === grandchild)?.ppid as number;
    expect(parent).not.toBe(root.pid);
    const stdin = agent.stdin as import('bun').FileSink;
    stdin.write('go\n');
    await stdin.end();
    await until(() => gone(parent));
    await tracker.snapshot([root]);
    const tracked = tracker.groups().find((group) => group.pgid === grandchild) as ProcessIdentity;
    expect(tracked).toEqual((await processIdentity(grandchild)) as ProcessIdentity);
    expect(tracker.groups().map((group) => group.pgid)).toContain(root.pgid);
    expect(await killGroup(tracked, 'SIGKILL')).toBe(true);
    await until(() => gone(grandchild));
    // A group whose members are all gone is forgotten.
    await tracker.snapshot([root]);
    expect(tracker.groups().map((group) => group.pgid)).not.toContain(grandchild);
  });

  test('works from injected ps rows: descendants of the roots and their groups', async () => {
    const lstart = 'Thu Oct 29 13:04:14 2026';
    const row = (pid: number, ppid: number, pgid: number) => ({ pid, ppid, pgid, stat: 'S', lstart, command: 'x' });
    let rows = [row(100, 1, 100), row(101, 100, 100), row(102, 101, 102), row(103, 102, 102), row(200, 1, 200)];
    const tracker = new DescendantTracker(async () => rows);
    await tracker.snapshot([{ pid: 100, pgid: 100, lstart }]);
    expect(tracker.groups()).toEqual([
      { pid: 100, pgid: 100, lstart },
      { pid: 102, pgid: 102, lstart },
    ]);
    // 102 exits and 103 is reparented to launchd: its group is still known through 103.
    rows = [row(100, 1, 100), row(101, 100, 100), row(103, 1, 102), row(200, 1, 200)];
    await tracker.snapshot([{ pid: 100, pgid: 100, lstart }]);
    expect(tracker.groups()).toEqual([
      { pid: 100, pgid: 100, lstart },
      { pid: 103, pgid: 102, lstart },
    ]);
    // A new process that reuses a remembered pid with another start time is not adopted.
    rows = [row(100, 1, 100), { ...row(103, 1, 102), lstart: 'Thu Oct 29 14:00:00 2026' }];
    await tracker.snapshot([{ pid: 100, pgid: 100, lstart }]);
    expect(tracker.groups()).toEqual([{ pid: 100, pgid: 100, lstart }]);
  });
});

describe('sweepCloneProcesses', () => {
  test.skipIf(process.platform !== 'darwin')(
    'kills a process whose cwd is inside the clone and leaves one outside it (the runner supports darwin-arm64 only; design 7.1)',
    async () => {
      requireLsofOnMacOS();
      const clone = tempDir('agflow-proc-clone-');
      mkdirSync(join(clone, 'src', 'deep'), { recursive: true });
      const outside = tempDir('agflow-proc-outside-');
      const inside = spawnGroup('exec sleep 30', { cwd: join(clone, 'src', 'deep') });
      const elsewhere = spawnGroup('exec sleep 30', { cwd: outside });
      await until(async () => (await processIdentity(inside.pid)) !== null);
      const result = await sweepCloneProcesses(clone);
      expect(result).toEqual({ killed: [inside.pid], skipped: null });
      await until(() => gone(inside.pid));
      expect(await gone(elsewhere.pid)).toBe(false);
    },
  );

  test('refuses an empty, relative or root clone path before running lsof', async () => {
    const dir = tempDir('agflow-proc-lsof-');
    const marker = join(dir, 'ran');
    const lsof = join(dir, 'lsof');
    writeFileSync(lsof, `#!/bin/sh\ntouch '${marker}'\n`);
    chmodSync(lsof, 0o755);
    for (const clone of ['', 'work/T-4-a1', '/', '/tmp/../']) {
      await expect(sweepCloneProcesses(clone, { lsof })).rejects.toThrow(/clone/);
    }
    expect(existsSync(marker)).toBe(false);
  });

  test('is skipped with a reason where lsof is missing', async () => {
    const clone = tempDir('agflow-proc-clone-');
    expect(await sweepCloneProcesses(clone, { lsof: '/nonexistent/lsof' })).toEqual({
      killed: [],
      skipped: 'lsof is not available (/nonexistent/lsof)',
    });
  });
});

describe('parsers', () => {
  test('parsePs reads rows whose commands contain spaces, with padded days', () => {
    const output = [
      '    1     0     1 Ss   Fri Oct 23 21:09:55 2026     /sbin/launchd',
      '  335     1   335 Ss   Fri Oct  2 21:10:36 2026     /usr/libexec/UserEventAgent (System)',
      '73157 66440 73157 S+   Thu Oct 29 13:46:05 2026     /bin/zsh -c echo "a  b" && sleep 1',
      '  400   335   335 Z    Thu Oct 29 13:46:05 2026     ',
      '',

    expect(parsePs(output)).toEqual([
      { pid: 1, ppid: 0, pgid: 1, stat: 'Ss', lstart: 'Fri Oct 23 21:09:55 2026', command: '/sbin/launchd' },
      {
        pid: 335,
        ppid: 1,
        pgid: 335,

        lstart: 'Fri Oct  2 21:10:36 2026',

  test('ps run with PS_COLUMNS and PS_ENV gives rows whose lstart matches processIdentity', async () => {
    // PS_ENV wins over a caller's own locale and time zone.
    const local = { ...process.env, LC_ALL: 'de_DE.UTF-8', TZ: 'Asia/Tokyo' };
    const proc = Bun.spawn(['ps', '-axo', PS_COLUMNS], { env: { ...local, ...PS_ENV }, stdout: 'pipe' });
    const rows = parsePs(await new Response(proc.stdout).text());
    const own = rows.find((row) => row.pid === process.pid);

describe('drainToLog and boundedWait', () => {
  test('drainToLog keeps at most its bound and never stalls the writer', async () => {
    const log = join(tempDir('agflow-proc-log-'), 'logs', 'T-4-a1.log');
    const script = 'head -c 2000000 /dev/zero | tr "\\0" x';
    const proc = Bun.spawn(['sh', '-c', script], { stdout: 'pipe', stderr: 'ignore' });
    const drained = await drainToLog(proc.stdout, log, { maxBytes: 1_000 });
    expect(await proc.exited).toBe(0);
    expect(drained).toEqual({ bytes: 2_000_000, kept: 1_000 });
    const text = readFileSync(log, 'utf8');
    expect(text.startsWith('x'.repeat(1_000))).toBe(true);
    expect(text.slice(1_000)).toBe('\n[agflow: output truncated after 1000 bytes]\n');
    expect(statSync(log).size).toBeLessThan(1_100);
  });

  test('drainToLog appends to a log that other writers share', async () => {
    const log = join(tempDir('agflow-proc-log-'), 'attempt.log');
    writeFileSync(log, 'runner: started\n');
    const proc = Bun.spawn(['sh', '-c', 'echo agent output'], { stdout: 'pipe', stderr: 'ignore' });
    expect(await drainToLog(proc.stdout, log, { maxBytes: 1_000 })).toEqual({ bytes: 13, kept: 13 });
    expect(readFileSync(log, 'utf8')).toBe('runner: started\nagent output\n');
  });

  test('boundedWait returns after its bound while a grandchild still holds the pipe', async () => {
    const log = join(tempDir('agflow-proc-log-'), 'attempt.log');
    const script = 'sleep 30 & echo started';
    const proc = Bun.spawn(['sh', '-c', script], { detached: true, stdout: 'pipe', stderr: 'ignore' });
    groups.add(proc.pid);
    const drain = drainToLog(proc.stdout, log, { maxBytes: 1_000 });
    expect(await proc.exited).toBe(0);
    const started = Date.now();
    expect(await boundedWait(drain, 150)).toEqual({ done: false });
    expect(Date.now() - started).toBeLessThan(1_000);
    process.kill(-proc.pid, 'SIGKILL');
    expect(await boundedWait(drain, 5_000)).toEqual({ done: true, value: { bytes: 8, kept: 8 } });
    expect(readFileSync(log, 'utf8')).toBe('started\n');
  });
});
```

```ts
// Process tools (design 7.4): identities, recorded groups, descendant snapshots, clone sweeps and bounded pipe
// drains. macOS PIDs wrap at 99,999, so a group is signalled only while a process recorded in it still has the same
// pid and start time. Every ps and lsof call is async, so heartbeats never stall behind one. The parsers are pure
// and exported for M2g's harness (X-42).
import { realpathSync } from 'node:fs';
import { mkdir, open } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { dirname, isAbsolute, resolve, sep } from 'node:path';
import type { AttemptStore, ProcessRecord } from './attempt-store';

/** A process as ps names it: lstart, ps's start time to the second, tells a reused pid apart. */
export interface ProcessIdentity {
  pid: number;
  pgid: number;
  /** ps's lstart in the C locale and UTC (PS_ENV), such as "Thu Oct  2 13:04:14 2026". */
  lstart: string;
}

/** One row of `ps -o PS_COLUMNS` run with PS_ENV; listProcesses gives these. */
export interface PsRow extends ProcessIdentity {
  ppid: number;
  stat: string;
  command: string;
}

/** The ps columns parsePs reads, in its order. */
export const PS_COLUMNS = 'pid=,ppid=,pgid=,stat=,lstart=,command=';

/**
 * The environment every ps call adds to its own: the C locale and UTC make lstart one fixed format, the same for the
 * service, a terminal's agflow and M2g's harness. Without it parsePs reads no rows in another locale, and in another
 * time zone lstart never matches a recorded identity.
 */
export const PS_ENV: Readonly<Record<'LC_ALL' | 'TZ', string>> = { LC_ALL: 'C', TZ: 'UTC' };

// pid, ppid, pgid, stat, then lstart ("Thu Oct  2 13:04:14 2026") and the command, which may hold any spaces.
const LSTART = '[A-Z][a-z]{2} [A-Z][a-z]{2} [ \\d]\\d \\d{2}:\\d{2}:\\d{2} \\d{4}';
const PS_ROW = new RegExp(`^\\s*(\\d+)\\s+(\\d+)\\s+(\\d+)\\s+(\\S+)\\s+(${LSTART})(?: +(.*))?$`);

/**
 * Reads the output of `ps -o PS_COLUMNS` run with PS_ENV (listProcesses runs it); lines it cannot read are skipped,
 * so output in another locale gives no rows.
 */
export function parsePs(output: string): PsRow[] {
  const rows: PsRow[] = [];
  for (const line of output.split('\n')) {
    const match = line.match(PS_ROW);
    if (!match) continue;
    rows.push({
      pid: Number(match[1]),
      ppid: Number(match[2]),
      pgid: Number(match[3]),
      stat: match[4] as string,
      lstart: match[5] as string,
      command: (match[6] ?? '').trimEnd(),
    });
  }
  return rows;
}

async function run(argv: string[], env: Record<string, string | undefined> = process.env): Promise<string> {
  const proc = Bun.spawn(argv, { env, stdin: 'ignore', stdout: 'pipe', stderr: 'pipe' });
  // Both pipes are read, because Bun buffers unread pipes without limit.
  const [stdout] = await Promise.all([new Response(proc.stdout).text(), new Response(proc.stderr).text()]);
  await proc.exited;
  return stdout;
}

/** One ps call (about 17 ms) with PS_COLUMNS and PS_ENV: every process, or only the given pids. */
export async function listProcesses(pids?: readonly number[]): Promise<PsRow[]> {
  if (pids?.length === 0) return [];
  const select = pids ? ['-p', pids.join(',')] : ['-A'];
  return parsePs(await run(['ps', ...select, '-o', PS_COLUMNS], { ...process.env, ...PS_ENV }));
}

/** The pid's identity now, or null when no such process exists. */
export async function processIdentity(pid: number): Promise<ProcessIdentity | null> {
  const row = (await listProcesses([pid])).find((candidate) => candidate.pid === pid);
  return row ? { pid: row.pid, pgid: row.pgid, lstart: row.lstart } : null;
}

/** True when both name the same process: the same pid, started at the same time. */
export function sameProcess(a: Pick<ProcessIdentity, 'pid' | 'lstart'>, b: Pick<ProcessIdentity, 'pid' | 'lstart'>) {
  return a.pid === b.pid && a.lstart === b.lstart;
}

function signal(target: number, name: NodeJS.Signals): boolean {
  try {
    process.kill(target, name);
    return true;
  } catch (error) {
    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'ESRCH') return false;
    throw error;
  }
}

/**
 * Signals the group of a recorded process (its leader, or a member a snapshot found) while that process still has
 * the same pid, start time and group. Gives whether it signalled. Groups 0 and 1 are never signalled: kill(0) is the
 * caller's own group and kill(-1) every process the user owns.
 */
export async function killGroup(identity: ProcessIdentity, name: NodeJS.Signals = 'SIGKILL'): Promise<boolean> {
  if (identity.pgid <= 1) return false;
  const now = await processIdentity(identity.pid);
  if (!now || !sameProcess(now, identity) || now.pgid !== identity.pgid) return false;
  return signal(-identity.pgid, name);
}

/** Signals one process while it still has the same pid and start time. */
export async function killProcess(identity: ProcessIdentity, name: NodeJS.Signals = 'SIGKILL'): Promise<boolean> {
  if (identity.pid <= 1) return false;
  const now = await processIdentity(identity.pid);
  if (!now || !sameProcess(now, identity)) return false;
  return signal(identity.pid, name);
}

/** Records a process group in the attempt's registry, before the agent's first output is read (design 7.4). */
export function recordGroup(
  store: AttemptStore,
  attemptId: string,
  clone: string | null,
  identity: ProcessIdentity,
): ProcessRecord {
  const record = { attemptId, pid: identity.pid, pgid: identity.pgid, lstart: identity.lstart, clone };
  store.recordProcess(record);
  return record;
}

/**
 * One attempt's descendants and their groups (design 7.4, "Descendant snapshots"). Each snapshot walks the process
 * tree from the attempt's recorded processes and from every process it saw before, so a group whose members were
 * reparented to launchd is still known through those members. A member counts only while its pid and start time
 * match, so a reused pid is never adopted; a group with no such member left is forgotten.
 */
export class DescendantTracker {
  // pgid -> pid -> lstart of the members seen.
  private members = new Map<number, Map<number, string>>();

  constructor(private readonly list: () => Promise<PsRow[]> = () => listProcesses()) {}

  async snapshot(roots: readonly ProcessIdentity[]): Promise<void> {
    const rows = await this.list();
    const byPid = new Map(rows.map((row) => [row.pid, row]));
    const children = new Map<number, PsRow[]>();
    for (const row of rows) {
      const siblings = children.get(row.ppid);
      if (siblings) siblings.push(row);
      else children.set(row.ppid, [row]);
    }
    const seenBefore = [...this.members.values()].flatMap((group) =>
      [...group].map(([pid, lstart]) => ({ pid, lstart })),
    );
    const queue = [...roots, ...seenBefore].flatMap((known) => {
      const row = byPid.get(known.pid);
      return row && sameProcess(row, known) ? [row] : [];
    });
    const next = new Map<number, Map<number, string>>();
    const seen = new Set<number>();
    while (queue.length > 0) {
      const row = queue.shift() as PsRow;
      if (seen.has(row.pid)) continue;
      seen.add(row.pid);
      const group = next.get(row.pgid) ?? new Map<number, string>();
      group.set(row.pid, row.lstart);
      next.set(row.pgid, group);
      queue.push(...(children.get(row.pid) ?? []));
    }
    this.members = next;
  }

  /** One identity per known group, for killGroup: its leader when the leader is still alive, else a member. */
  groups(): ProcessIdentity[] {
    return [...this.members]
      .sort(([a], [b]) => a - b)
      .map(([pgid, group]) => {
        const lstart = group.get(pgid);
        if (lstart !== undefined) return { pid: pgid, pgid, lstart };
        const [pid, memberStart] = [...group].sort(([a], [b]) => a - b)[0] as [number, string];
        return { pid, pgid, lstart: memberStart };
      });
  }
}

/** Reads `lsof -Fpn` output (p, f and n records) into each process's cwd; lsof gives resolved paths. */
export function parseLsofCwds(output: string): { pid: number; cwd: string }[] {
  const result: { pid: number; cwd: string }[] = [];
  let pid: number | null = null;
  for (const line of output.split('\n')) {
    if (line.startsWith('p')) pid = Number(line.slice(1));
    else if (line.startsWith('n') && pid !== null && Number.isInteger(pid)) {
      result.push({ pid, cwd: line.slice(1) });
      pid = null;
    }
  }
  return result;
}

export interface SweepResult {
  /** The pids signalled. */
  killed: number[];
  /** Why no sweep ran, such as a missing lsof. */
  skipped: string | null;
}

function inside(path: string, root: string): boolean {
  return path === root || path.startsWith(root.endsWith(sep) ? root : root + sep);
}

/**
 * Ladder step 4 (design 7.4): finds the user's processes whose cwd is inside the clone with
 * `lsof -a -d cwd -u <uid> -Fpn` and kills each one after an identity check. The clone must be an absolute path at
 * least two levels deep: a relative one would resolve against the runner's cwd, which is / under launchd, and a sweep
 * of / kills every process of the owner.
 */
export async function sweepCloneProcesses(
  clone: string,
  options: { signal?: NodeJS.Signals; lsof?: string } = {},
): Promise<SweepResult> {
  const lsof = options.lsof ?? 'lsof';
  if (!isAbsolute(clone)) throw new Error(`refusing to sweep a clone path that is not absolute: '${clone}'`);
  let root: string;
  try {
    root = realpathSync(clone);
  } catch {
    root = resolve(clone);
  }
  if (root.split(sep).filter(Boolean).length < 2) {
    throw new Error(`refusing to sweep processes under ${root}: too wide for a clone`);
  }
  let output: string;
  try {
    output = await run([lsof, '-w', '-a', '-d', 'cwd', '-u', String(process.getuid?.() ?? 0), '-Fpn']);
  } catch {
    return { killed: [], skipped: `lsof is not available (${lsof})` };
  }
  const found = parseLsofCwds(output).filter((entry) => inside(entry.cwd, root) && entry.pid !== process.pid);
  const pids = [...new Set(found.map((entry) => entry.pid))];
  const killed: number[] = [];
  for (const row of await listProcesses(pids)) {
    if (await killProcess(row, options.signal ?? 'SIGKILL')) killed.push(row.pid);
  }
  return { killed, skipped: null };
}

export interface DrainResult {
  /** Bytes read from the pipe. */
  bytes: number;
  /** Bytes written to the log. */
  kept: number;
}

/**
 * Reads a child's pipe to its end and appends at most maxBytes of it to the log, then a truncation note. It keeps
 * reading past the bound, so the child never blocks on a full pipe and Bun never buffers it. The log is opened for
 * appending, so the runner's own lines may share it.
 */
export async function drainToLog(
  stream: AsyncIterable<Uint8Array | string> | null,
  logPath: string,
  options: { maxBytes: number },
): Promise<DrainResult> {
  const result: DrainResult = { bytes: 0, kept: 0 };
  if (!stream) return result;
  await mkdir(dirname(logPath), { recursive: true });
  const file = await open(logPath, 'a');
  let noted = false;
  try {
    for await (const chunk of stream) {
      const bytes = typeof chunk === 'string' ? Buffer.from(chunk) : chunk;
      result.bytes += bytes.length;
      const room = options.maxBytes - result.kept;
      if (room > 0) {
        const part = bytes.subarray(0, room);
        await file.write(part);
        result.kept += part.length;
      }
      if (bytes.length > room && !noted) {
        noted = true;
        await file.write(`\n[agflow: output truncated after ${options.maxBytes} bytes]\n`);
      }
    }
  } catch {
    // A pipe that errors (its process killed mid-write) ends the drain like its end would.
  } finally {
    await file.close();
  }
  return result;
}

/**
 * Waits for a promise at most ms. A stop waits for the agent's pipes this way, because an escaped process that
 * inherited them can hold them open long after the agent exited.
 */
export async function boundedWait<T>(
  promise: Promise<T>,
  ms: number,
): Promise<{ done: true; value: T } | { done: false }> {
  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
  const timeout = new Promise<{ done: false }>((resolveTimeout) => {
    timer = setTimeout(() => resolveTimeout({ done: false }), ms);
  });
  try {
    return await Promise.race([promise.then((value) => ({ done: true as const, value })), timeout]);
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timer);
  }
}
```

### Task 7: The link client

The link client is the runner's WebSocket to `/api/runner/ws` (design 6.3), signed in with the CLI token from a credentials provider that returns core's `Credentials` (X-8). It sends hello, applies welcome's cumulative ack, replays the outbox after it in seq order and streams new events; it sends heartbeats after welcome, terminates a link silent for `deadLink`, times out handshakes, and reconnects with full-jitter backoff, or at once after a clock gap. Commands go to the handler in arrival order, and the link itself answers `unsupported` to a command it cannot read; a handler that answers null sends no result, so the hub sends the command again after the next welcome. Two hooks serve Task 37's settings sync (X-12): `resent` names events the replay leaves out, and `reconnectNow` ends the connection and connects again at once. For `canPushWip` (X-11) the link tracks, in awake time, whether a welcome came after the last clock gap and when the last ack arrived. `test/fake-hub.ts` is a scripted hub that validates every runner message with core's schemas; later tests reuse it. A whole events-message failure closes the hub link with 1011 and no ack; the client reconnects through normal backoff and replays after `welcome.ackedSeq`. `reconnectWithBackoff` also lets failed restore bookkeeping drop the socket and retry safely.
