### Task 9: Git environments and the async git runner

Design 7.3 runs runner git in three environments, and this task builds them with one async runner. `runGit` uses `Bun.spawn` with argument arrays, never a shell or `spawnSync`, so heartbeats keep flowing during long git work; git runs in its own process group, and a timeout kills the whole group. The local environment is an allowlist with no system or global config, `HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` in the runner's `git/` directory, and the `-c` pins of every program-valued key. The remote environment keeps the owner's config, adds the hook and fsmonitor pins and a BatchMode SSH command unless the owner set `core.sshCommand`, and times out after 2 minutes; `agentGitEnv` gives the agent's credential-free git, and no inherited `GIT_*` variable reaches runner git.

**Files:**
- Create: `packages/runner/src/git/run.ts`
- Modify: `packages/runner/src/index.ts`
- Test: `packages/runner/test/git-run.test.ts`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

**File:** `packages/runner/test/git-run.test.ts` (new)

```ts
import { afterEach, describe, expect, setDefaultTimeout, test } from 'bun:test';
import {
  existsSync,
  mkdirSync,
  mkdtempSync,
  readFileSync,
  realpathSync,
  rmSync,
  statSync,
  writeFileSync,
} from 'node:fs';
import { createServer, type Server, type Socket } from 'node:net';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { originRepo } from '@agflow/testkit';
import {
  agentGitEnv,
  ensureRunnerGitFiles,
  GitError,
  gitOk,
  LOCAL_GIT_PINS,
  localGitEnv,
  RUN_DIR_EXCLUDE,
  remoteGitEnv,
  runGit,
} from '../src/git/run';
import { runnerPaths } from '../src/paths';

// Every test here runs git or agent processes, which take several times as long on a machine loaded by other suites.
setDefaultTimeout(30_000);

const cleanups: (() => void | Promise<void>)[] = [];
afterEach(async () => {
  for (const cleanup of cleanups.splice(0).reverse()) await cleanup();
});

function tempDir(prefix = 'agflow-gitrun-'): string {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), prefix));
  cleanups.push(() => rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }));
  return dir;
}

/** Sets process variables for one test and restores them afterwards. */
function withEnv(values: Record<string, string | undefined>): void {
  const saved = Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(values).map((name) => [name, process.env[name]]));
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(values)) {
    if (value === undefined) delete process.env[name];
    else process.env[name] = value;
  }
  cleanups.push(() => {
    for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(saved)) {
      if (value === undefined) delete process.env[name];
      else process.env[name] = value;
    }
  });
}

/** A runner layout with its git files written. */
function runnerHome() {
  const paths = runnerPaths(tempDir('agflow-home-'));
  ensureRunnerGitFiles(paths);
  return paths;
}

/**
 * A TCP server that accepts connections and never answers, so a git fetch from it hangs. open() counts the accepted
 * connections that are still open: only a killed client (git's remote helper) closes one.
 */
async function silentServer(): Promise<{ url: string; open: () => number }> {
  const sockets: Socket[] = [];
  const closed = new Set<Socket>();
  const server: Server = createServer((socket) => {
    sockets.push(socket);
    socket.on('error', () => {});
    socket.on('close', () => closed.add(socket));
  });
  await new Promise<void>((resolve) => server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', resolve));
  cleanups.push(
    () =>
      new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
        for (const socket of sockets) socket.destroy();
        server.close(() => resolve());
      }),
  );
  const address = server.address();
  if (address === null || typeof address === 'string') throw new Error('no port');
  return {
    url: `http://127.0.0.1:${address.port}/repo.git`,
    open: () => sockets.filter((socket) => !closed.has(socket)).length,
  };
}

const PINS = [
  'core.hooksPath=/dev/null',
  'core.fsmonitor=false',
  'core.pager=cat',
  'core.editor=false',
  'core.sshCommand=false',
  'core.askPass=',
  'credential.helper=',
  'diff.external=',
  'sequence.editor=false',
  'gpg.program=false',
  'protocol.allow=never',
  'protocol.file.allow=always',
  'gc.auto=0',
];

describe('the local environment', () => {
  test('carries GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM, its global config, --no-optional-locks, the excludes and every pin', async () => {
    const paths = runnerHome();
    const local = localGitEnv(paths);
    expect(local.name).toBe('local');
    expect(local.env.GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM).toBe('1');
    expect(local.env.GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL).toBe(paths.gitConfig);
    expect(local.args).toContain('--no-optional-locks');
    expect<readonly string[]>(LOCAL_GIT_PINS).toEqual(PINS);
    const pairs = local.args.flatMap((arg, index) => (local.args[index - 1] === '-c' ? [arg] : []));
    expect(pairs).toEqual([`core.excludesFile=${paths.gitExcludes}`, ...PINS]);
    // git itself sees each pin, whatever the repository's own config says.
    const repo = tempDir();
    await runGit(local, ['init', '--quiet', repo]);
    const planted = '[core]\n\thooksPath = planted-hooks\n\tpager = less\n';
    writeFileSync(join(repo, '.git', 'config'), planted, { flag: 'a' });
    const listed = (await runGit(local, ['config', '--list', '--show-scope'], { cwd: repo })).stdout;
    // git lists keys in lower case.
    for (const pin of PINS) {

      expect(listed).toContain(`command\t${key.toLowerCase()}=${value}\n`);

      '/dev/null',

  });

    const paths = runnerHome();
    expect(readFileSync(paths.gitExcludes, 'utf8')).toBe('.agflow/run/\n.claude/.cc-writes/\n');
    expect(existsSync(paths.gitConfig)).toBe(true);

    const paths = runnerHome();

    await runGit(localGitEnv(paths), ['init', '--quiet', repo]);
    const bogus = join(tempDir(), 'nowhere');
    withEnv({

      GIT_WORK_TREE: bogus,
      GIT_INDEX_FILE: join(bogus, 'index'),

      GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: 'user.counted',

    expect(remote.env.GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT).toBe('0');
    expect(remote.env.GIT_SSH_COMMAND).toBe('ssh -o BatchMode=yes');
    expect(remote.env.HOME).toBe(home);
    expect(remote.args).toEqual(['-c', 'core.hooksPath=/dev/null', '-c', 'core.fsmonitor=false']);
    const cwd = tempDir();
    expect((await runGit(remote, ['config', '--get', 'credential.helper'], { cwd })).stdout.trim()).toBe(
      'planted-helper',
    );
    expect((await runGit(remote, ['config', '--get', 'core.hooksPath'], { cwd })).stdout.trim()).toBe('/dev/null');
    expect((await runGit(remote, ['config', '--get', 'core.fsmonitor'], { cwd })).stdout.trim()).toBe('false');
  });

  test("leaves the owner's core.sshCommand in force", async () => {
    const home = tempDir();
    writeFileSync(join(home, '.gitconfig'), '[core]\n\tsshCommand = ssh -i ~/.ssh/work\n');
    withEnv({ HOME: home, XDG_CONFIG_HOME: undefined });
    const remote = await remoteGitEnv();
    expect(remote.env.GIT_SSH_COMMAND).toBeUndefined();
  });

  test("probes core.sshCommand in the vault's context, so a conditional include of the owner's applies", async () => {
    const home = tempDir();
    writeFileSync(
      join(home, '.gitconfig'),
      '[includeIf "hasconfig:remote.*.url:git@github.com:work-org/**"]\n\tpath = ~/.gitconfig-work\n',
    );
    writeFileSync(join(home, '.gitconfig-work'), '[core]\n\tsshCommand = ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_work\n');
    withEnv({ HOME: home, XDG_CONFIG_HOME: undefined });
    const vault = join(tempDir(), 'demo.git');
    const local = localGitEnv(runnerHome());
    await runGit(local, ['init', '--quiet', '--bare', vault]);
    await runGit(local, [`--git-dir=${vault}`, 'config', 'remote.origin.url', 'git@github.com:work-org/demo.git']);
    expect((await remoteGitEnv({ gitDir: vault })).env.GIT_SSH_COMMAND).toBeUndefined();
    expect((await remoteGitEnv()).env.GIT_SSH_COMMAND).toBe('ssh -o BatchMode=yes');
  });

  test('is killed at the timeout with every helper git started, without blocking the event loop', async () => {
    const { url, open } = await silentServer();
    // A scratch HOME and no proxy variables, so git goes to the silent server and nowhere else.
    const remote = await remoteGitEnv({ base: { PATH: process.env.PATH ?? '', HOME: tempDir() }, timeoutMs: 400 });
    let ticks = 0;
    const ticker = setInterval(() => {
      ticks += 1;
    }, 20);
    const started = Date.now();
    const error = await runGit(remote, ['ls-remote', url], { cwd: tempDir() }).catch((caught: unknown) => caught);
    clearInterval(ticker);
    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(GitError);
    expect(error).toMatchObject({ timedOut: true });
    expect((error as GitError).message).toContain(`git ls-remote ${url} timed out after 400 ms`);
    expect(Date.now() - started).toBeLessThan(3_000);
    expect(ticks).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(10);
    // git's remote helper held the connection; killing the whole group closes it.
    const deadline = Date.now() + 2_000;
    while (open() > 0 && Date.now() < deadline) await Bun.sleep(20);
    expect(open()).toBe(0);
  });
});
```

```ts
// The runner's git (design 7.3): three environments and one async runner for the two the runner itself uses.
//
// - local: everything that touches the vault, a quarantine or a clone's files. It reads no configuration of the
//   owner's (no system file, the runner's own global file, no default ignore or attributes file) and pins every
//   program-valued key, so nothing an agent planted in a clone can run.
// - remote: fetch, push and ls-remote between the vault and origin. It keeps the owner's environment and git
//   configuration (credential helper, SSH config), runs no hooks and never prompts, and is killed after 2 minutes.
// - agent: the variables an agent's own git gets, with no credentials at all.
//
// Git runs through Bun.spawn with argument arrays, never a shell and never spawnSync, so heartbeats keep flowing
// during long git work. GIT_* variables inherited by the runner (a hook's GIT_DIR, say) never reach its git.
import { chmodSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname } from 'node:path';
import { CONNECTIVITY_VARS } from '../config';
import type { RunnerPaths } from '../paths';
import { boundedWait } from '../processes';

type Env = Record<string, string | undefined>;

export interface GitEnvironment {
  name: 'local' | 'remote';
  /** The whole environment of the git process; nothing else is inherited. */
  env: Record<string, string>;
  /** Placed before the subcommand: -c pins and --no-optional-locks. */
  args: string[];
  /** Kill git after this long; null for no limit. */
  timeoutMs: number | null;
}

export interface GitResult {
  code: number;
  stdout: string;
  stderr: string;
  timedOut: boolean;
}

export class GitError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly args: string[],
    readonly code: number,
    readonly stderr: string,
    readonly timedOut: boolean,
    timeoutMs: number | null,
  ) {
    const command = `git ${args.join(' ')}`;
    super(
      timedOut
        ? `${command} timed out after ${timeoutMs} ms`
        : `${command} failed (exit ${code}): ${stderr.trim() || '(no output)'}`,
    );
    this.name = 'GitError';
  }
}

/** The second layer of the local environment: every program-valued key, pinned on the command line. */
export const LOCAL_GIT_PINS = [
  'core.hooksPath=/dev/null',
  'core.fsmonitor=false',
  'core.pager=cat',
  'core.editor=false',
  'core.sshCommand=false',
  'core.askPass=',
  'credential.helper=',
  'diff.external=',
  'sequence.editor=false',
  'gpg.program=false',
  'protocol.allow=never',
  'protocol.file.allow=always',
  'gc.auto=0',
] as const;

/** Runner commands that take paths add this, so a clone's runner-owned .agflow/run/ never takes part. */
export const RUN_DIR_EXCLUDE = ':(exclude,top).agflow/run';

/** What git/excludes lists: the runner's own directory and the Claude CLI's staging directory (X-28). */
const RUNNER_EXCLUDES = '.agflow/run/\n.claude/.cc-writes/\n';

/** Writes the runner's git/excludes and an empty git/local.gitconfig, in a private git/ directory. */
export function ensureRunnerGitFiles(paths: Pick<RunnerPaths, 'gitConfig' | 'gitExcludes'>): void {
  const dir = dirname(paths.gitConfig);
  mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
  chmodSync(dir, 0o700);
  if (!existsSync(paths.gitExcludes) || readFileSync(paths.gitExcludes, 'utf8') !== RUNNER_EXCLUDES) {
    writeFileSync(paths.gitExcludes, RUNNER_EXCLUDES, { mode: 0o600 });
  }
  if (!existsSync(paths.gitConfig)) {
    writeFileSync(paths.gitConfig, '# The global config of the agflow runner\'s local git; the runner owns it.\n', {
      mode: 0o600,
    });
  }
}

/** Variables the local environment keeps: who and where the user is, and nothing that configures git. */
function localAllowed(name: string): boolean {
  return ['PATH', 'USER', 'LOGNAME', 'LANG', 'TMPDIR', 'TZ'].includes(name) || name.startsWith('LC_');
}

/**
 * The local environment. HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME point at the runner's git directory, so git's default
 * ~/.config/git/ignore and attributes, which it reads even with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL set, are never the owner's.
 */
export function localGitEnv(
  paths: Pick<RunnerPaths, 'gitConfig' | 'gitExcludes'>,
  base: Env = process.env,
): GitEnvironment {
  const env: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(base)) {
    if (value !== undefined && localAllowed(name)) env[name] = value;
  }
  const gitDir = dirname(paths.gitConfig);
  Object.assign(env, {
    HOME: gitDir,
    XDG_CONFIG_HOME: gitDir,
    GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: '1',
    GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: paths.gitConfig,
    GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: '0',
  });
  const pins = [`core.excludesFile=${paths.gitExcludes}`, ...LOCAL_GIT_PINS].flatMap((pin) => ['-c', pin]);
  return { name: 'local', env, args: ['--no-optional-locks', ...pins], timeoutMs: null };
}

/** The remote environment's limit: 2 minutes. */
export const REMOTE_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000;

const CONNECTIVITY = new Set<string>(CONNECTIVITY_VARS);

/**
 * The remote environment: the owner's environment without inherited GIT_* variables (GIT_SSL_CAINFO, a captured
 * connectivity variable, stays), with the hook pins, no prompts, and SSH in batch mode unless the owner's own git
 * configuration sets core.sshCommand, which GIT_SSH_COMMAND would override. gitDir is the repository the commands
 * will run in (the vault): the probe runs there, so the owner's includes conditional on it (includeIf
 * "hasconfig:remote.*.url:...", the usual way to pick an SSH key per organisation) apply.
 */
export async function remoteGitEnv(
  options: { base?: Env; timeoutMs?: number; gitDir?: string } = {},
): Promise<GitEnvironment> {
  const env: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(options.base ?? process.env)) {
    if (value !== undefined && (!name.startsWith('GIT_') || CONNECTIVITY.has(name))) env[name] = value;
  }
  env.GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT = '0';
  const environment: GitEnvironment = {
    name: 'remote',
    env,
    args: ['-c', 'core.hooksPath=/dev/null', '-c', 'core.fsmonitor=false'],
    timeoutMs: options.timeoutMs ?? REMOTE_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS,
  };
  const repository = options.gitDir === undefined ? [] : [`--git-dir=${options.gitDir}`];
  const configured = await runGit(environment, [...repository, 'config', '--get', 'core.sshCommand'], {
    check: false,
  });
  if (configured.code !== 0 || configured.stdout.trim() === '') env.GIT_SSH_COMMAND = 'ssh -o BatchMode=yes';
  return environment;
}

/** The paths agentGitEnv names, all inside the clone's .agflow/run/ (task 11 writes them). */
export interface AgentGitPaths {
  /** The agent's GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: identity, no credential helper, local protocols only. */
  gitconfig: string;
  /** A script that refuses every SSH connection with an explanation. */
  sshRefusal: string;
  /** Empty directories, so gh and glab find no login. */
  ghConfigDir: string;
  glabConfigDir: string;
}

/** git runs GIT_SSH_COMMAND through the shell, so a path with spaces (a home folder, say) is quoted. */
function shellWord(path: string): string {
  return /^[A-Za-z0-9_\/.:=@%+-]+$/.test(path) ? path : `'${path.replace(/'/g, `'\\''`)}'`;
}

/** A value that is set but is no token, so gh and glab never look further for one. */
const DUMMY_TOKEN = 'agflow-no-token';

/** The agent's git variables: no system config, its own global config, no prompts, no credentials, no SSH. */
export function agentGitEnv(paths: AgentGitPaths): Record<string, string> {
  return {
    GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: paths.gitconfig,
    GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: '1',
    GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: '0',
    GIT_ASKPASS: '/usr/bin/false',
    GIT_SSH_COMMAND: shellWord(paths.sshRefusal),
    GIT_SSH_VARIANT: 'ssh',
    GH_CONFIG_DIR: paths.ghConfigDir,
    GLAB_CONFIG_DIR: paths.glabConfigDir,
    GH_TOKEN: DUMMY_TOKEN,
    GITLAB_TOKEN: DUMMY_TOKEN,
  };
}

export interface RunGitOptions {
  /** '/' by default, which is in no repository: commands name their repository with --git-dir. */
  cwd?: string;
  /** Added to the environment's variables, GIT_INDEX_FILE for a temporary index, say. */
  env?: Record<string, string>;
  input?: string | Uint8Array;
  /** Overrides the environment's limit. */
  timeoutMs?: number | null;
  /** Throw a GitError when git fails or times out; true by default. */
  check?: boolean;
}

/** After a kill, a child git started (ssh, a remote helper) may hold the pipes; its output is not worth waiting for. */
const OUTPUT_AFTER_KILL_MS = 1_000;

/**
 * Runs git in its own process group, so a timeout kills git and every helper it started. The output is raw: -z
 * output keeps its NUL separators and trailing newlines are the caller's to trim.
 */
export async function runGit(
  environment: GitEnvironment,
  args: string[],
  options: RunGitOptions = {},
): Promise<GitResult> {
  const timeoutMs = options.timeoutMs === undefined ? environment.timeoutMs : options.timeoutMs;
  const proc = Bun.spawn(['git', ...environment.args, ...args], {
    cwd: options.cwd ?? '/',
    env: { ...environment.env, ...options.env },
    stdin: options.input === undefined ? 'ignore' : Buffer.from(options.input),
    stdout: 'pipe',
    stderr: 'pipe',
    detached: true,
  });
  let timedOut = false;
  const timer =
    timeoutMs === null
      ? undefined
      : setTimeout(() => {
          timedOut = true;
          try {
            process.kill(-proc.pid, 'SIGKILL');
          } catch {
            proc.kill('SIGKILL');
          }
        }, timeoutMs);
  const output = Promise.all([new Response(proc.stdout).text(), new Response(proc.stderr).text()]);
  const code = await proc.exited;
  clearTimeout(timer);
  let stdout = '';
  let stderr = '';
  if (timedOut) {
    const read = await boundedWait(output, OUTPUT_AFTER_KILL_MS);
    if (read.done) [stdout, stderr] = read.value;
  } else {
    [stdout, stderr] = await output;
  }
  const result: GitResult = { code, stdout, stderr, timedOut };
  if (options.check !== false && (code !== 0 || timedOut)) {
    throw new GitError(args, code, stderr, timedOut, timeoutMs);
  }
  return result;
}

/** Whether git succeeds: `cat-file -e`, `rev-parse --verify --quiet` and the like. */
export async function gitOk(
  environment: GitEnvironment,
  args: string[],
  options: Omit<RunGitOptions, 'check'> = {},
): Promise<boolean> {
  const result = await runGit(environment, args, { ...options, check: false });
  return result.code === 0 && !result.timedOut;
}
```

`runGit`'s default cwd is `/`, so a command that forgets `--git-dir` never acts on the runner's own repository. `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` runs through the shell, so the SSH refusal path is shell-quoted. `remoteGitEnv({ gitDir })` probes `core.sshCommand` in the vault's context, so `includeIf hasconfig:remote.*.url` applies.

### Task 10: The vault

Each project has one bare vault that only the runner writes (design 7.3). Before starts, WIP pushes and `refresh_vault` it fetches main, the task's WIP refs and `refs/heads/agflow/<task>-*` with the remote environment, then the start ref and the start sha by SHA when they are still missing. It resolves a start position to the tip it actually holds, pins each clone's objects under `refs/agflow-local/`, serialises ref changes per vault path, creates and releases base checkouts of main by reference count, and consolidates with `--keep-unreachable` while clones exist (M2c schedules it daily, X-7). Refspecs and pin names come from core's naming (X-18).

```ts
import { afterEach, describe, expect, setDefaultTimeout, test } from 'bun:test';
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { localPinRefs } from '@agflow/core';
import { commitFiles, gitIn, type OriginRepo, originRepo } from '@agflow/testkit';
import { ensureRunnerGitFiles, gitOk, localGitEnv, remoteGitEnv, runGit } from '../src/git/run';
import { Vault } from '../src/git/vault';
import { type RunnerPaths, runnerPaths } from '../src/paths';

// Every test here runs git or agent processes, which take several times as long on a machine loaded by other suites.
setDefaultTimeout(30_000);

const cleanups: (() => void | Promise<void>)[] = [];
afterEach(async () => {
  for (const cleanup of cleanups.splice(0).reverse()) await cleanup();
});

const PREFIX = 'refs/agflow/';
const PROJECT = 'demo-0123456789';

function tempDir(prefix: string): string {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), prefix));
  cleanups.push(() => rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }));
  return dir;
}

async function origin(files: Record<string, string> = { 'README.md': '# demo\n' }): Promise<OriginRepo> {
  const made = await originRepo(files);
  cleanups.push(() => made.remove());
  return made;
}

interface Setup {
  paths: RunnerPaths;
  vault: Vault;
  /** Runs local git in the vault. */
  git(args: string[]): Promise<string>;
  has(sha: string): Promise<boolean>;
}

async function setup(repo: OriginRepo): Promise<Setup> {
  const paths = runnerPaths(tempDir('agflow-vault-'));
  ensureRunnerGitFiles(paths);
  // The owner's environment, but with a scratch HOME, so the developer's own git config plays no part.
  const home = tempDir('agflow-owner-');
  const vault = new Vault({
    paths,
    project: PROJECT,
    repo: { url: repo.path, mainBranch: 'main' },
    remote: () => remoteGitEnv({ base: { ...process.env, HOME: home, XDG_CONFIG_HOME: undefined } }),
  });
  await vault.ensure();
  const local = localGitEnv(paths);
  const git = async (args: string[]) =>
    (await runGit(local, [`--git-dir=${vault.path}`, ...args])).stdout.trim();
  const has = (sha: string) => gitOk(local, [`--git-dir=${vault.path}`, 'cat-file', '-e', `${sha}^{commit}`]);
  return { paths, vault, git, has };
}

describe('Vault.ensure', () => {
  test('creates the bare vault once, with the origin URL and gc.auto=0', async () => {
    const repo = await origin();
    const { vault, paths, git } = await setup(repo);
    expect(vault.path).toBe(paths.vault(PROJECT));
    expect(await git(['rev-parse', '--is-bare-repository'])).toBe('true');
    expect(await git(['config', '--get', 'remote.origin.url'])).toBe(repo.path);
    expect(await git(['config', '--get', 'gc.auto'])).toBe('0');
    expect(await git(['symbolic-ref', 'HEAD'])).toBe('refs/heads/main');
    // A second ensure keeps what is there.
    await vault.fetchForAttempt({ taskId: null, start: { ref: 'refs/heads/main', sha: null } }, PREFIX);
    await git(['update-ref', 'refs/agflow-local/T-1-a1/start', repo.mainSha]);
    await vault.ensure();
    expect(await git(['rev-parse', 'refs/agflow-local/T-1-a1/start'])).toBe(repo.mainSha);
  });

  test('follows a changed origin URL', async () => {
    const repo = await origin();
    const { paths, git } = await setup(repo);
    const moved = new Vault({ paths, project: PROJECT, repo: { url: '/elsewhere/origin.git', mainBranch: 'main' } });
    await moved.ensure();
    expect(await git(['config', '--get', 'remote.origin.url'])).toBe('/elsewhere/origin.git');
  });
});

describe('Vault.fetchForAttempt', () => {
  test("brings main, the task's WIP refs and its agflow/<task>-* branches, and nothing else", async () => {
    const repo = await origin();
    const wip = await commitFiles(repo.path, { branch: 'placeholder', files: { 'w.txt': 'w\n' } });
    // WIP refs are written straight into the origin, as a runner's push would leave them.
    await gitIn(repo.path, ['update-ref', `${PREFIX}T-4/a1`, wip]);
    await gitIn(repo.path, ['update-ref', `${PREFIX}T-5/a1`, wip]);
    const branch = await commitFiles(repo.path, { branch: 'agflow/T-4-parser', files: { 'b.txt': 'b\n' } });
    await commitFiles(repo.path, { branch: 'agflow/T-40-other', files: { 'c.txt': 'c\n' } });
    const { vault, git } = await setup(repo);
    await vault.fetchForAttempt({ taskId: 'T-4', start: { ref: `${PREFIX}T-4/a1`, sha: wip } }, PREFIX);
    const refs = (await git(['for-each-ref', '--format=%(refname) %(objectname)'])).split('\n').sort();
    expect(refs).toEqual(
      [`refs/agflow/T-4/a1 ${wip}`, `refs/heads/agflow/T-4-parser ${branch}`, `refs/heads/main ${repo.mainSha}`].sort(),
    );
  });

  test('then fetches start.sha by SHA when it is still missing', async () => {
    const repo = await origin();
    const elsewhere = await commitFiles(repo.path, { branch: 'scratch', files: { 'x.txt': 'x\n' } });
    const { vault, has } = await setup(repo);
    expect(await has(elsewhere)).toBe(false);
    await vault.fetchForAttempt({ taskId: 'T-4', start: { ref: 'refs/heads/main', sha: elsewhere } }, PREFIX);
    expect(await has(elsewhere)).toBe(true);
  });

  test('fetches a start ref that the task refspecs do not cover', async () => {
    const repo = await origin();
    const feature = await commitFiles(repo.path, { branch: 'feature', files: { 'f.txt': 'f\n' } });
    const { vault, git } = await setup(repo);
    await vault.fetchForAttempt({ taskId: 'T-4', start: { ref: 'refs/heads/feature', sha: null } }, PREFIX);
    expect(await git(['rev-parse', 'refs/heads/feature'])).toBe(feature);
  });

  test('names git and its stderr when origin cannot be read', async () => {
    const repo = await origin();
    const { paths } = await setup(repo);
    const broken = new Vault({
      paths,
      project: 'broken-0123456789',
      repo: { url: join(tempDir('agflow-missing-'), 'nothing.git'), mainBranch: 'main' },
    });
    await broken.ensure();
    await expect(
      broken.fetchForAttempt({ taskId: null, start: { ref: 'refs/heads/main', sha: null } }, PREFIX),
    ).rejects.toThrow(
      / fetch --quiet --no-tags origin \S+ failed \(exit 128\): fatal: .*does not appear to be a git repository/,
    );
  });

  test('a start ref deleted on origin is absent, not a failure: main and the WIP refs still arrive', async () => {
    const repo = await origin();
    // A person handed back on my-fix, which was merged into main and deleted afterwards.
    const fix = await commitFiles(repo.path, { branch: 'my-fix', files: { 'fix.txt': 'fix\n' } });
    await gitIn(repo.path, ['update-ref', 'refs/heads/main', fix]);
    await gitIn(repo.path, ['update-ref', '-d', 'refs/heads/my-fix']);
    const wip = await commitFiles(repo.path, { branch: 'placeholder', files: { 'w.txt': 'w\n' } });
    await gitIn(repo.path, ['update-ref', `${PREFIX}T-4/a1`, wip]);
    const { vault, git } = await setup(repo);
    const start = { ref: 'refs/heads/my-fix', sha: fix };
    await vault.fetchForAttempt({ taskId: 'T-4', start }, PREFIX);
    expect(await git(['rev-parse', 'refs/heads/main'])).toBe(fix);
    expect(await git(['rev-parse', `${PREFIX}T-4/a1`])).toBe(wip);
    expect(await vault.resolveStart(start)).toEqual({ ref: start.ref, sha: fix, recordedSha: fix, differs: false });
  });

  test('a recorded sha that origin no longer serves starts from the tip of the start ref', async () => {
    const repo = await origin();
    const tip = await commitFiles(repo.path, { branch: 'agflow/T-4-parser', files: { 'a.txt': '1\n' } });
    const { vault } = await setup(repo);
    // The WIP ref was rewritten: the recorded commit is gone from origin.
    const start = { ref: 'refs/heads/agflow/T-4-parser', sha: 'e'.repeat(40) };
    await vault.fetchForAttempt({ taskId: 'T-4', start }, PREFIX);
    expect(await vault.resolveStart(start)).toMatchObject({ sha: tip, differs: true });
  });

  test('an abbreviated recorded sha is resolved in the vault, never fetched by SHA', async () => {
    const repo = await origin();
    const first = await commitFiles(repo.path, { branch: 'agflow/T-4-parser', files: { 'a.txt': '1\n' } });
    const second = await commitFiles(repo.path, { branch: 'agflow/T-4-parser', files: { 'a.txt': '2\n' } });
    const { vault } = await setup(repo);
    const ref = 'refs/heads/agflow/T-4-parser';
    await vault.fetchForAttempt({ taskId: 'T-4', start: { ref, sha: second.slice(0, 12) } }, PREFIX);
    expect(await vault.resolveStart({ ref, sha: second.slice(0, 12) })).toEqual({
      ref,
      sha: second,
      recordedSha: second.slice(0, 12),
      differs: false,
    });
    expect(await vault.resolveStart({ ref, sha: first.slice(0, 7) })).toMatchObject({ sha: second, differs: true });
    // With the ref gone, the abbreviation names the commit to start from.
    expect(await vault.resolveStart({ ref: `${PREFIX}T-4/a1`, sha: first.slice(0, 7) })).toMatchObject({
      sha: first,
      differs: false,
    });
  });
});

describe('Vault.resolveStart', () => {
  test('returns the fetched tip of start.ref and reports when it differs from start.sha', async () => {
    const repo = await origin();
    const first = await commitFiles(repo.path, { branch: 'agflow/T-4-parser', files: { 'a.txt': '1\n' } });
    const second = await commitFiles(repo.path, { branch: 'agflow/T-4-parser', files: { 'a.txt': '2\n' } });
    const { vault } = await setup(repo);
    const start = { ref: 'refs/heads/agflow/T-4-parser', sha: first };
    await vault.fetchForAttempt({ taskId: 'T-4', start }, PREFIX);
    expect(await vault.resolveStart(start)).toEqual({
      ref: start.ref,
      sha: second,
      recordedSha: first,
      differs: true,
    });
    expect(await vault.resolveStart({ ref: start.ref, sha: second })).toMatchObject({ sha: second, differs: false });
    expect(await vault.resolveStart({ ref: 'refs/heads/main', sha: null })).toEqual({
      ref: 'refs/heads/main',
      sha: repo.mainSha,
      recordedSha: null,
      differs: false,
    });
  });

  test('resolves a refs/agflow-local/ start inside the vault, and fetchForAttempt never fetches it', async () => {
    const repo = await origin();
    const { vault, git, paths } = await setup(repo);
    await vault.fetchForAttempt({ taskId: null, start: { ref: 'refs/heads/main', sha: null } }, PREFIX);
    // A harvest the vault alone holds: origin has never seen this commit.
    const tree = await git(['rev-parse', `${repo.mainSha}^{tree}`]);
    const identity = {
      GIT_AUTHOR_NAME: 'a',
      GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL: 'a@b',
      GIT_COMMITTER_NAME: 'a',
      GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL: 'a@b',
    };
    const commitTree = [`--git-dir=${vault.path}`, 'commit-tree', tree, '-p', repo.mainSha];
    const made = await runGit(localGitEnv(paths), commitTree, { input: 'harvested\n', env: identity });
    const harvested = made.stdout.trim();
    await vault.pin('T-4-a1', { head: harvested });
    const pins = localPinRefs('T-4-a1');
    const position = { ref: pins.head, sha: harvested };
    await vault.fetchForAttempt({ taskId: 'T-4', start: position }, PREFIX);
    expect(await git(['rev-parse', pins.head])).toBe(harvested);
    expect(await vault.resolveStart(position)).toEqual({
      ref: pins.head,
      sha: harvested,
      recordedSha: harvested,
      differs: false,
    });
  });

  test('falls back to a recorded sha the vault holds, and refuses an unknown position', async () => {
    const repo = await origin();
    const { vault } = await setup(repo);
    await vault.fetchForAttempt({ taskId: null, start: { ref: 'refs/heads/main', sha: null } }, PREFIX);
    expect(await vault.resolveStart({ ref: `${PREFIX}T-4/a1`, sha: repo.mainSha })).toMatchObject({
      sha: repo.mainSha,
      differs: false,
    });
    await expect(vault.resolveStart({ ref: `${PREFIX}T-4/a1`, sha: null })).rejects.toThrow(
      'the start position refs/agflow/T-4/a1 is not in the vault',
    );
    await expect(vault.resolveStart({ ref: `${PREFIX}T-4/a1`, sha: 'f'.repeat(40) })).rejects.toThrow(
      'not in the vault',
    );
  });
});

describe('refresh and pins', () => {
  test('refresh fetches the named refs with the task refspecs', async () => {
    const repo = await origin();
    const { vault, git } = await setup(repo);
    const late = await commitFiles(repo.path, { branch: 'placeholder', files: { 'l.txt': 'l\n' } });
    await gitIn(repo.path, ['update-ref', `${PREFIX}T-4/a1-late-1`, late]);
    const other = await commitFiles(repo.path, { branch: 'handback', files: { 'h.txt': 'h\n' } });
    await vault.refresh('T-4', [`${PREFIX}T-4/a1-late-1`, 'refs/heads/handback'], PREFIX);
    expect(await git(['rev-parse', `${PREFIX}T-4/a1-late-1`])).toBe(late);
    expect(await git(['rev-parse', 'refs/heads/handback'])).toBe(other);
    expect(await git(['rev-parse', 'refs/heads/main'])).toBe(repo.mainSha);
    await expect(vault.refresh('T-4', ['refs/agflow-local/T-4-a1/head'], PREFIX)).rejects.toThrow('local pin');
  });

  test('pins are written per attempt, and deletePins removes only that attempt', async () => {
    const repo = await origin();
    const { vault, git } = await setup(repo);
    await vault.fetchForAttempt({ taskId: null, start: { ref: 'refs/heads/main', sha: null } }, PREFIX);
    await vault.pin('T-4-a1', { start: repo.mainSha, head: repo.mainSha });
    await vault.pin('T-4-a10', { start: repo.mainSha });
    await vault.pin('T-5-a1', { head: repo.mainSha });
    const pinned = async () => (await git(['for-each-ref', '--format=%(refname)', 'refs/agflow-local/'])).split('\n');
    expect(await pinned()).toEqual([
      localPinRefs('T-4-a1').head,
      localPinRefs('T-4-a1').start,
      localPinRefs('T-4-a10').start,
      localPinRefs('T-5-a1').head,
    ]);
    await vault.deletePins('T-4-a1');
    expect(await pinned()).toEqual([localPinRefs('T-4-a10').start, localPinRefs('T-5-a1').head]);
    await vault.deletePins('T-4-a1');
  });

  test('two concurrent ref updates of one vault run one after the other', async () => {
    const repo = await origin();
    const { vault, paths, git } = await setup(repo);
    const steps: string[] = [];
    const slow = vault.withLock(async () => {
      steps.push('a start');
      await Bun.sleep(50);
      steps.push('a end');
    });
    // Another Vault object for the same vault shares the lock.
    const twin = new Vault({ paths, project: PROJECT, repo: { url: repo.path, mainBranch: 'main' } });
    const fast = twin.withLock(async () => {
      steps.push('b start');
      steps.push('b end');
    });
    await Promise.all([slow, fast]);
    expect(steps).toEqual(['a start', 'a end', 'b start', 'b end']);
    // A failure releases the lock.
    await expect(vault.withLock(async () => Promise.reject(new Error('boom')))).rejects.toThrow('boom');
    expect(await vault.withLock(async () => 'next')).toBe('next');
    await vault.fetchForAttempt({ taskId: null, start: { ref: 'refs/heads/main', sha: null } }, PREFIX);
    const pinned = async () => (await git(['for-each-ref', '--format=%(refname)', 'refs/agflow-local/'])).split('\n');
    // A pin waits while another holder has the lock.
    let open!: () => void;
    const held = vault.withLock(() => new Promise<void>((resolve) => (open = resolve)));
    let landed = false;
    const pin = vault.pin('T-4-a1', { head: repo.mainSha }).then(() => {
      landed = true;
    });
    await Bun.sleep(100);
    expect(landed).toBe(false);
    expect(await pinned()).toEqual(['']);
    open();
    await Promise.all([held, pin]);
    expect(await pinned()).toEqual([localPinRefs('T-4-a1').head]);
    // Real ref updates in parallel all land.
    const ids = Array.from({ length: 8 }, (_, index) => `T-4-a${index + 1}`);
    await Promise.all(ids.map((id) => vault.pin(id, { start: repo.mainSha, head: repo.mainSha })));
    await Promise.all([...ids.map((id) => vault.deletePins(id)), vault.pin('T-9-a1', { head: repo.mainSha })]);
    expect(await pinned()).toEqual([localPinRefs('T-9-a1').head]);
  });
});

describe('base checkouts', () => {
  test('are created detached at the main sha, shared between attempts and removed after the last release', async () => {
    const repo = await origin({ 'CLAUDE.md': '# rules\n', '.claude/settings.json': '{}\n' });
    const { vault, paths, git } = await setup(repo);
    await vault.fetchForAttempt({ taskId: null, start: { ref: 'refs/heads/main', sha: null } }, PREFIX);
    const first = await vault.acquireBaseCheckout('T-4-a1');
    expect(first.path).toBe(paths.baseCheckout(PROJECT, repo.mainSha));
    expect(first.sha).toBe(repo.mainSha);
    expect(readFileSync(join(first.path, 'CLAUDE.md'), 'utf8')).toBe('# rules\n');
    expect(readFileSync(join(first.path, '.claude/settings.json'), 'utf8')).toBe('{}\n');
    const head = await runGit(localGitEnv(paths), ['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], { cwd: first.path });
    expect(head.stdout.trim()).toBe(repo.mainSha);
    expect(await gitOk(localGitEnv(paths), ['symbolic-ref', '-q', 'HEAD'], { cwd: first.path })).toBe(false);
    const second = await vault.acquireBaseCheckout('T-5-a1', repo.mainSha);
    expect(second.path).toBe(first.path);
    await first.release();
    // Released twice by mistake: still counted once.
    await first.release();
    expect(existsSync(first.path)).toBe(true);
    await second.release();
    expect(existsSync(first.path)).toBe(false);
    expect(await git(['worktree', 'list', '--porcelain'])).not.toContain(first.path);
  });

  test('two Vault objects of one vault share the count: only the last release removes the checkout', async () => {
    const repo = await origin({ 'CLAUDE.md': '# rules\n' });
    const { vault, paths, git } = await setup(repo);
    await vault.fetchForAttempt({ taskId: null, start: { ref: 'refs/heads/main', sha: null } }, PREFIX);
    const twin = new Vault({ paths, project: PROJECT, repo: { url: repo.path, mainBranch: 'main' } });
    const first = await vault.acquireBaseCheckout('T-4-a1');
    const second = await twin.acquireBaseCheckout('T-5-a1');
    expect(second.path).toBe(first.path);
    await first.release();
    expect(existsSync(join(first.path, 'CLAUDE.md'))).toBe(true);
    await second.release();
    expect(existsSync(first.path)).toBe(false);
    expect(await git(['worktree', 'list', '--porcelain'])).not.toContain(first.path);
  });

  test('a checkout no attempt uses is made again, not reused because its HEAD matches', async () => {
    const repo = await origin({ 'CLAUDE.md': '# rules\n' });
    const { vault, paths } = await setup(repo);
    await vault.fetchForAttempt({ taskId: null, start: { ref: 'refs/heads/main', sha: null } }, PREFIX);
    // Left by an earlier runner process whose worktree add stopped half way: HEAD is set, a file is missing.
    const path = paths.baseCheckout(PROJECT, repo.mainSha);
    const add = ['worktree', 'add', '--quiet', '--detach', path, repo.mainSha];
    await runGit(localGitEnv(paths), [`--git-dir=${vault.path}`, ...add]);
    rmSync(join(path, 'CLAUDE.md'));
    const checkout = await vault.acquireBaseCheckout('T-4-a1');
    expect(checkout.path).toBe(path);
    expect(readFileSync(join(path, 'CLAUDE.md'), 'utf8')).toBe('# rules\n');
    await checkout.release();
  });

  test('a newer main gets its own checkout', async () => {
    const repo = await origin();
    const { vault } = await setup(repo);
    await vault.fetchForAttempt({ taskId: null, start: { ref: 'refs/heads/main', sha: null } }, PREFIX);
    const old = await vault.acquireBaseCheckout('T-4-a1');
    const newer = await commitFiles(repo.path, { branch: 'main', files: { 'n.txt': 'n\n' } });
    await vault.fetchForAttempt({ taskId: null, start: { ref: 'refs/heads/main', sha: null } }, PREFIX);
    const fresh = await vault.acquireBaseCheckout('T-5-a1');
    expect(fresh.sha).toBe(newer);
    expect(fresh.path).not.toBe(old.path);
    await old.release();
    await fresh.release();
  });
});

describe('Vault.consolidate', () => {
  test('keeps unreachable objects while any clone exists and prunes only when none does', async () => {
    const repo = await origin();
    const { vault, paths, git } = await setup(repo);
    await vault.fetchForAttempt({ taskId: null, start: { ref: 'refs/heads/main', sha: null } }, PREFIX);
    const loose = await runGit(localGitEnv(paths), [`--git-dir=${vault.path}`, 'hash-object', '-w', '--stdin'], {
      input: 'unreachable\n',
    });
    const blob = loose.stdout.trim();
    const exists = () => gitOk(localGitEnv(paths), [`--git-dir=${vault.path}`, 'cat-file', '-e', blob]);
    const clone = paths.clone(PROJECT, 'T-4-a1');
    mkdirSync(clone, { recursive: true });
    expect(await vault.consolidate()).toEqual({ pruned: false });
    expect(await exists()).toBe(true);
    expect(await git(['count-objects', '-v'])).toMatch(/^count: 0$/m);
    rmSync(clone, { recursive: true });
    expect(await vault.consolidate()).toEqual({ pruned: true });
    expect(await exists()).toBe(false);
    expect(await git(['rev-parse', 'refs/heads/main'])).toBe(repo.mainSha);
  });
});
```

```ts
// The vault (design 7.3): one bare repository per project, written only by the runner. It fetches from origin with
// the remote environment, holds each clone's pins under refs/agflow-local/, serves base checkouts of main as
// Claude's project configuration root, and consolidates its objects without ever pruning what a clone may borrow.
// Every change to its refs or worktrees runs under one lock per vault, shared by every Vault object for that path,
// as are the base checkouts' reference counts.
import { existsSync, readdirSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { localPinRefs, taskRefGlob } from '@agflow/core';
import type { RunnerPaths } from '../paths';
import { type GitEnvironment, GitError, gitOk, localGitEnv, type RunGitOptions, remoteGitEnv, runGit } from './run';

/** A position to start from: the hub's work-position ref and the sha it recorded, if any (AttemptSpec.start). */
export interface StartRef {
  ref: string;
  sha: string | null;
}

/** The commit an attempt actually starts from. */
export interface StartPosition {
  ref: string;
  sha: string;
  /** The sha the hub recorded for the position. */
  recordedSha: string | null;
  /** The tip differs from the recorded sha: pre-fence work the hub had not heard of (attempt.spawned.startSha). */
  differs: boolean;
}

/** A base checkout of main in use by one attempt; release it when the attempt no longer runs. */
export interface BaseCheckout {
  path: string;
  sha: string;
  release(): Promise<void>;
}

export interface VaultOptions {
  paths: RunnerPaths;
  /** The project key (projectKey) naming the vault and the work directories. */
  project: string;
  repo: { url: string; mainBranch: string };
  /** The local environment; localGitEnv(paths) by default. */
  local?: GitEnvironment;
  /**
   * Built for each fetch, so a change to the owner's git configuration applies; remoteGitEnv for the vault by
   * default.
   */
  remote?: () => Promise<GitEnvironment>;
}

const LOCAL_PINS = 'refs/agflow-local/';
const SHA = /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/;
/** A recorded sha: core's CommitShaSchema allows abbreviations, which M1's records may hold. */
const RECORDED_SHA = /^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$/;

/** The tail of the lock chain of each vault path. */
const locks = new Map<string, Promise<void>>();
/** The attempts using each base checkout, by vault path and sha; read and changed only under the vault's lock. */
const baseUsers = new Map<string, Map<string, Set<string>>>();

export class Vault {
  readonly path: string;
  readonly project: string;
  readonly mainBranch: string;
  private readonly paths: RunnerPaths;
  private readonly url: string;
  private readonly local: GitEnvironment;
  private readonly remote: () => Promise<GitEnvironment>;

  constructor(options: VaultOptions) {
    this.paths = options.paths;
    this.project = options.project;
    this.path = options.paths.vault(options.project);
    this.url = options.repo.url;
    this.mainBranch = options.repo.mainBranch;
    this.local = options.local ?? localGitEnv(options.paths);
    // The owner's includes conditional on the repository (an SSH key per organisation, say) apply to the vault.
    this.remote = options.remote ?? (() => remoteGitEnv({ gitDir: this.path }));
  }

  /** Runs fn once every earlier holder of this vault's lock is done; a failure releases it too. */
  async withLock<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
    const previous = locks.get(this.path) ?? Promise.resolve();
    let release!: () => void;
    const mine = new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
      release = resolve;
    });
    const tail = previous.then(() => mine);
    locks.set(this.path, tail);
    await previous;
    try {
      return await fn();
    } finally {
      release();
      if (locks.get(this.path) === tail) locks.delete(this.path);
    }
  }

  /** Creates the bare vault if needed, and keeps its origin URL, HEAD and gc.auto=0 as the runner wants them. */
  async ensure(): Promise<void> {
    await this.withLock(async () => {
      if (!existsSync(join(this.path, 'HEAD'))) {
        await runGit(this.local, ['init', '--quiet', '--bare', `--initial-branch=${this.mainBranch}`, this.path]);
      }
      await this.git(['config', 'remote.origin.url', this.url]);
      await this.git(['config', 'gc.auto', '0']);
      await this.git(['symbolic-ref', 'HEAD', `refs/heads/${this.mainBranch}`]);
    });
  }

  /**
   * Before a start or resume: fetches main, the task's refs under the WIP prefix and its agflow/<task>-* branches,
   * then a start ref none of those cover, then start.sha by SHA if the vault still lacks it. A local pin is never
   * fetched. Only the first fetch must succeed: a start ref gone from origin is absent, and a sha origin no longer
   * serves is not needed once the ref resolved. resolveStart reports a position the vault does not hold.
   */
  async fetchForAttempt(
    attempt: { taskId: string | null; start: StartRef },
    wipRefPrefix: string,
  ): Promise<void> {
    await this.fetch(this.taskRefspecs(attempt.taskId, wipRefPrefix));
    const { ref, sha } = attempt.start;
    if (!ref.startsWith(LOCAL_PINS) && !this.covered(ref, attempt.taskId, wipRefPrefix)) {
      await this.fetchIfPresent(ref);
    }
    // git cannot fetch an abbreviation; resolveStart resolves one the vault holds.
    if (sha === null || !SHA.test(sha) || (await this.hasCommit(sha))) return;
    try {
      await this.fetch([sha]);
    } catch (error) {
      if ((await this.commitOf(ref)) === null) throw error;
    }
  }

  /** refresh_vault: the task's refspecs and the named refs, so a late-work ref is there before the holder merges it. */
  async refresh(taskId: string, refs: string[], wipRefPrefix: string): Promise<void> {
    const refspecs = this.taskRefspecs(taskId, wipRefPrefix);
    for (const ref of refs) {
      if (ref.startsWith(LOCAL_PINS)) throw new Error(`${ref} is a local pin and is never fetched`);
      if (!this.covered(ref, taskId, wipRefPrefix)) refspecs.push(`+${ref}:${ref}`);
    }
    await this.fetch(refspecs);
  }

  /**
   * The tip the vault holds for a start position; a ref it lacks falls back to the recorded sha, if held. A
   * recorded abbreviation counts as the commit it names in the vault.
   */
  async resolveStart(start: StartRef): Promise<StartPosition> {
    const recorded = start.sha === null ? null : await this.resolveCommit(start.sha);
    const sha = (await this.commitOf(start.ref)) ?? recorded;
    if (sha === null) {
      const at = start.sha === null ? '' : ` (recorded at ${start.sha})`;
      throw new Error(`the start position ${start.ref}${at} is not in the vault`);
    }
    return { ref: start.ref, sha, recordedSha: start.sha, differs: start.sha !== null && sha !== recorded };
  }

  /** Whether the vault holds the commit. */
  hasCommit(sha: string): Promise<boolean> {
    if (!SHA.test(sha)) return Promise.resolve(false);
    return gitOk(this.local, [`--git-dir=${this.path}`, 'cat-file', '-e', `${sha}^{commit}`]);
  }

  /** Writes an attempt's pins of the objects its clone borrows. */
  async pin(attemptId: string, shas: { start?: string; head?: string }): Promise<void> {
    const refs = localPinRefs(attemptId);
    const lines = (['start', 'head'] as const).flatMap((name) => {
      const sha = shas[name];
      if (sha === undefined) return [];
      if (!SHA.test(sha)) throw new Error(`not a commit sha: ${JSON.stringify(sha)}`);
      return [`update ${refs[name]} ${sha}\n`];
    });
    if (lines.length === 0) return;
    await this.withLock(() => this.git(['update-ref', '--stdin'], { input: lines.join('') }));
  }

  /** cleanup_attempt: removes every pin of this attempt and of no other. */
  async deletePins(attemptId: string): Promise<void> {
    const { start } = localPinRefs(attemptId);
    const prefix = start.slice(0, start.lastIndexOf('/') + 1);
    await this.withLock(async () => {
      const listed = await this.git(['for-each-ref', '--format=%(refname)', prefix]);
      const refs = listed.stdout.split('\n').filter((ref) => ref.startsWith(prefix));
      if (refs.length === 0) return;
      await this.git(['update-ref', '--stdin'], { input: refs.map((ref) => `delete ${ref}\n`).join('') });
    });
  }

  /**
   * A checkout of main for one attempt at <vaults>/<project>.base/<sha12>, detached at sha (the vault's main by
   * default). Attempts on the same sha share it; the last release removes it.
   */
  async acquireBaseCheckout(attemptId: string, sha?: string): Promise<BaseCheckout> {
    const target = sha ?? (await this.commitOf(`refs/heads/${this.mainBranch}`));
    if (target === null) throw new Error(`the vault has no ${this.mainBranch} to check out`);
    const path = this.paths.baseCheckout(this.project, target);
    await this.withLock(async () => {
      const bases = this.bases();
      const users = bases.get(target) ?? new Set<string>();
      // A directory no attempt uses may be a checkout an earlier process left half done: made again, never trusted.
      if (users.size === 0) {
        await this.removeCheckout(path);
        await this.git(['worktree', 'add', '--quiet', '--detach', path, target]);
      }
      users.add(attemptId);
      bases.set(target, users);
    });
    return { path, sha: target, release: () => this.releaseBaseCheckout(attemptId, target) };
  }

  private async releaseBaseCheckout(attemptId: string, sha: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.withLock(async () => {
      const bases = this.bases();
      const users = bases.get(sha);
      if (!users?.delete(attemptId) || users.size > 0) return;
      bases.delete(sha);
      await this.removeCheckout(this.paths.baseCheckout(this.project, sha));
    });
  }

  /** This vault's base checkouts by sha, with the attempts that use each, shared by every Vault object for it. */
  private bases(): Map<string, Set<string>> {
    let bases = baseUsers.get(this.path);
    if (!bases) {
      bases = new Map();
      baseUsers.set(this.path, bases);
    }
    return bases;
  }

  /**
   * Packs the vault's objects. While any clone of the project exists it keeps every unreachable object, which a
   * clone may still borrow (repack -a -d --keep-unreachable); only when none exists does it prune.
   */
  async consolidate(): Promise<{ pruned: boolean }> {
    return this.withLock(async () => {
      if (this.clonesExist()) {
        await this.git(['repack', '-a', '-d', '-q', '--keep-unreachable']);
        return { pruned: false };
      }
      await this.git(['repack', '-a', '-d', '-q']);
      await this.git(['prune', '--expire=now']);
      await this.git(['worktree', 'prune']);
      return { pruned: true };
    });
  }

  private clonesExist(): boolean {
    const work = join(this.paths.work, this.project);
    return existsSync(work) && readdirSync(work).length > 0;
  }

  private taskRefspecs(taskId: string | null, wipRefPrefix: string): string[] {
    const main = `refs/heads/${this.mainBranch}`;
    const refspecs = [`+${main}:${main}`];
    if (taskId !== null) {
      const wip = taskRefGlob(wipRefPrefix, taskId);
      const branches = `refs/heads/agflow/${taskId}-*`;
      refspecs.push(`+${wip}:${wip}`, `+${branches}:${branches}`);
    }
    return refspecs;
  }

  /** Whether the task refspecs already fetch this ref. */
  private covered(ref: string, taskId: string | null, wipRefPrefix: string): boolean {
    if (ref === `refs/heads/${this.mainBranch}`) return true;
    if (taskId === null) return false;
    return (
      ref.startsWith(taskRefGlob(wipRefPrefix, taskId).slice(0, -1)) || ref.startsWith(`refs/heads/agflow/${taskId}-`)
    );
  }

  private async fetch(refspecs: string[]): Promise<void> {
    const remote = await this.remote();
    await this.withLock(() =>
      runGit(remote, [`--git-dir=${this.path}`, 'fetch', '--quiet', '--no-tags', 'origin', ...refspecs]),
    );
  }

  /**
   * Fetches one ref, which origin may no longer have (a hand-back branch merged and deleted, say). Whether it is
   * gone is asked with ls-remote --exit-code (2: no such ref), since git's own message may be translated.
   */
  private async fetchIfPresent(ref: string): Promise<void> {
    try {
      await this.fetch([`+${ref}:${ref}`]);
    } catch (error) {
      if (!(error instanceof GitError) || error.timedOut) throw error;
      const remote = await this.remote();
      const listed = await runGit(remote, [`--git-dir=${this.path}`, 'ls-remote', '--exit-code', 'origin', ref], {
        check: false,
      });
      if (listed.code !== 2) throw error;
    }
  }

  private async commitOf(ref: string): Promise<string | null> {
    const result = await this.git(['rev-parse', '--verify', '--quiet', `${ref}^{commit}`], { check: false });
    const sha = result.stdout.trim();
    return result.code === 0 && SHA.test(sha) ? sha : null;
  }

  /** The full sha of a recorded sha (7 to 40 hex) the vault holds; an ambiguous abbreviation counts as missing. */
  private async resolveCommit(sha: string): Promise<string | null> {
    return RECORDED_SHA.test(sha) ? this.commitOf(sha) : null;
  }

  private async removeCheckout(path: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.git(['worktree', 'remove', '--force', path], { check: false });
    rmSync(path, { recursive: true, force: true });
    await this.git(['worktree', 'prune']);
  }

  private git(args: string[], options: RunGitOptions = {}) {
    return runGit(this.local, [`--git-dir=${this.path}`, ...args], options);
  }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run the tests and see them pass**

Run: `bun test packages/runner/test/vault.test.ts && bun test && bun run typecheck`
Expected: the task's tests pass; then the whole suite passes (`0 fail`) and `tsc` exits 0.

The lock chain and the base-checkout users live at module level, keyed by vault path, so two `Vault` objects for one path share them, and a checkout no attempt uses is always made again. An abbreviated recorded sha is resolved in the vault and never fetched by SHA. A start ref whose fetch fails counts as absent only when `ls-remote --exit-code` exits 2, because git's messages may be translated.

### Task 11: Agent environment, permission profile and the .agflow/run directory

Design 7.6's agent environment is built only from an allowlist: user variables, the captured connectivity variables, per-vendor homes and temporary directories, package caches, PATH with refusing shims first, the agent git variables and the bridge variables, plus test mode's `claudeEnv`. `userVariables(base)` is the one list of user variables (USER, LOGNAME, LANG, SHELL, LC_*) that `buildAgentEnv` starts from and M2e's Codex process reuses, and `bridgeEnvOf` gives the bridge its own environment (X-32). `profile.ts` defines the permission profile and the denied read and write paths as data the adapters render. `run-dir.ts` writes the clone's `.agflow/run/` (task.md, brief.md, home, cache, tmp and the empty `AGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR`) and a read-only tools directory outside the clone with the agent gitconfig, the SSH refusal script and the gh and glab shims (design 7.2, 7.3; see Decisions).

```ts
      tree(`${owner}/.config/agflow`),
      tree(`${owner}/Library/LaunchAgents`),
      file(`${owner}/.zshrc`),
      file(`${owner}/.zprofile`),
      file(`${owner}/.zshenv`),
      file(`${owner}/.bashrc`),
      file(`${owner}/.bash_profile`),
      file(`${owner}/.profile`),
      file(`${owner}/.gitconfig`),
    ]);
  });

  test('never name the work root or a clone, and refuse a layout where one would', () => {
    for (const denied of [...deniedReadPaths({ home: owner, paths, vendorHomes }), ...deniedWritePaths({ home: owner, paths, vendorHomes })]) {
      expect(`${CLONE}/`.startsWith(`${denied.path}/`)).toBe(false);
      expect(`${paths.work}/`.startsWith(`${denied.path}/`)).toBe(false);
      expect(denied.path.startsWith(paths.work)).toBe(false);
    }
    const inside = runnerPaths(`${owner}/.codex/agflow`);
    expect(() => deniedReadPaths({ home: owner, paths: inside, vendorHomes })).toThrow('work root');
    expect(() => deniedWritePaths({ home: owner, paths: inside, vendorHomes })).toThrow('work root');
  });

  test('add the vendor homes runner.json puts outside the runner tree', () => {
    const shared = { claude: '/shared/homes/claude', codex: '/shared/homes/codex' };
    const read = deniedReadPaths({ home: owner, paths, vendorHomes: shared });
    const write = deniedWritePaths({ home: owner, paths, vendorHomes: shared });
    for (const denied of [read, write]) {
      expect(denied).toContainEqual(tree('/shared/homes/claude'));
      expect(denied).toContainEqual(tree('/shared/homes/codex'));
    }
    expect(read).toHaveLength(deniedReadPaths({ home: owner, paths, vendorHomes }).length + 2);
    expect(write).toHaveLength(deniedWritePaths({ home: owner, paths, vendorHomes }).length + 2);
    // A home that holds the work root would deny the agent its clone.
    const covering = { ...shared, codex: '/h' };
    expect(() => deniedReadPaths({ home: owner, paths, vendorHomes: covering })).toThrow('work root');
  });

  test('refuse a relative home', () => {
    expect(() => deniedReadPaths({ home: 'Users/owner', paths, vendorHomes })).toThrow('absolute');
  });
});
```

```ts
import { afterEach, describe, expect, setDefaultTimeout, test } from 'bun:test';
import {
  existsSync,
  lstatSync,
  mkdirSync,
  mkdtempSync,
  readdirSync,
  readFileSync,
  rmSync,
  statSync,
  symlinkSync,
  writeFileSync,
} from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { gitIn, type OriginRepo, originRepo } from '@agflow/testkit';
import { RunnerConfigSchema } from '../src/config';
import { buildAgentEnv } from '../src/env';
import { runnerPaths } from '../src/paths';
import { removeAgentTools, runDirOf, writeRunDir, withWorkingDirectory } from '../src/run-dir';

// Every test here runs git or agent processes, which take several times as long on a machine loaded by other suites.
setDefaultTimeout(30_000);

const cleanups: (() => void)[] = [];
afterEach(() => {
  for (const cleanup of cleanups.splice(0).reverse()) cleanup();
});

function tempDir(prefix = 'agflow-rundir-'): string {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), prefix));
  cleanups.push(() => rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }));
  return dir;
}

/** A runner-owned tools directory for one attempt; read-only once written, so the cleanup makes it writable. */
function toolsDir(): string {
  const tools = join(tempDir('agflow-tools-'), 'demo.agent', 'T-4-a1');
  cleanups.push(() => removeAgentTools(tools));
  return tools;
}

const identity = { name: 'Jane "JD" Doe', email: 'jane@example.com' };

function written(clone = tempDir(), tools = toolsDir()) {
  const runDir = writeRunDir({
    clone,
    tools,
    taskPack: '# T-4\nDo the thing.\n',
    brief: 'You are a worker.',
    identity,
  });
  return { clone, tools, runDir };
}

async function run(argv: string[], options: { cwd: string; env: Record<string, string> }) {
  const proc = Bun.spawn(argv, { ...options, stdin: 'ignore', stdout: 'pipe', stderr: 'pipe' });
  const [stdout, stderr, code] = await Promise.all([
    new Response(proc.stdout).text(),
    new Response(proc.stderr).text(),
    proc.exited,
  ]);
  return { code, stdout, stderr };
}

describe('runDirOf', () => {
  test("names the clone's .agflow/run/ and, outside the clone, what unsandboxed processes run or read", () => {
    const run = '/w/T-4-a1/.agflow/run';
    const tools = '/h/vaults/demo.agent/T-4-a1';
    expect(runDirOf('/w/T-4-a1', tools)).toEqual({
      root: run,
      taskMd: `${run}/task.md`,
      briefMd: `${run}/brief.md`,
      home: `${run}/home`,
      cache: `${run}/cache`,
      tmp: `${run}/tmp`,
      config: `${run}/config`,
      tools,
      gitconfig: `${tools}/gitconfig`,
      bin: `${tools}/bin`,
      sshRefusal: `${tools}/ssh-refusal`,
      ghConfigDir: `${tools}/gh-config`,
      glabConfigDir: `${tools}/glab-config`,
    });
  });
});

describe('writeRunDir', () => {
  test('writes task.md, brief.md, an empty config/ directory and the other directories', () => {
    const { clone, tools, runDir } = written();
    expect(runDir).toEqual(runDirOf(clone, tools));
    expect(readFileSync(runDir.taskMd, 'utf8')).toBe('# T-4\nDo the thing.\n');
    expect(readFileSync(runDir.briefMd, 'utf8')).toBe('You are a worker.\n');
    expect(readdirSync(runDir.config)).toEqual([]);
    for (const dir of [runDir.home, runDir.cache, runDir.tmp, runDir.ghConfigDir, runDir.glabConfigDir]) {
      expect(statSync(dir).isDirectory()).toBe(true);
    }
    expect(readdirSync(runDir.ghConfigDir)).toEqual([]);
    expect(readdirSync(runDir.bin).sort()).toEqual(['gh', 'glab']);
    expect(readdirSync(tools).sort()).toEqual(['bin', 'gh-config', 'gitconfig', 'glab-config', 'ssh-refusal']);
  });

  test('makes the tools directory read-only, and removeAgentTools removes it', () => {
    const { tools, runDir } = written();
    for (const dir of [tools, runDir.bin, runDir.ghConfigDir, runDir.glabConfigDir]) {
      expect(statSync(dir).mode & 0o777).toBe(0o555);
    }
    expect(statSync(runDir.gitconfig).mode & 0o777).toBe(0o444);
    for (const script of [join(runDir.bin, 'gh'), join(runDir.bin, 'glab'), runDir.sshRefusal]) {
      expect(statSync(script).mode & 0o777).toBe(0o555);
    }
    removeAgentTools(tools);
    expect(existsSync(tools)).toBe(false);
    removeAgentTools(tools);
  });

  test('writes a gitconfig with the commit identity, no credential helper and local protocols only', async () => {
    const { runDir } = written();
    const get = (key: string) => gitIn(tmpdir(), ['config', '--file', runDir.gitconfig, '--get-all', key]);
    expect(await get('user.name')).toBe('Jane "JD" Doe');
    expect(await get('user.email')).toBe('jane@example.com');
    expect(await get('credential.helper')).toBe('');
    expect(await gitIn(tmpdir(), ['config', '--file', runDir.gitconfig, '--list'])).toContain('credential.helper=');
    expect(await get('protocol.allow')).toBe('never');
    expect(await get('protocol.file.allow')).toBe('always');
  });

  test('refuses an identity git config cannot hold', () => {
    const clone = tempDir();
    expect(() =>
      writeRunDir({ clone, tools: toolsDir(), taskPack: '', brief: '', identity: { name: 'a\nb', email: 'x@y' } }),
    ).toThrow('identity');
  });

  test('the gh and glab shims and the SSH refusal script exit non-zero with an explanation', async () => {
    const { clone, runDir } = written();
    for (const [argv, name] of [
      [[join(runDir.bin, 'gh'), 'pr', 'create'], 'gh'],
      [[join(runDir.bin, 'glab'), 'mr', 'create'], 'glab'],
      [[runDir.sshRefusal, 'git@github.com', 'git-receive-pack', 'x'], 'SSH'],
    ] as const) {
      const [script, ...args] = argv;
      // Executable shell scripts; run through /bin/sh, because macOS checks each new executable on its first run.
      expect(statSync(script).mode & 0o111).toBe(0o111);
      expect(readFileSync(script, 'utf8').startsWith('#!/bin/sh\n')).toBe(true);
      const result = await run(['/bin/sh', script, ...args], { cwd: clone, env: { PATH: '/usr/bin:/bin' } });
      expect(result.code).not.toBe(0);
      expect(result.stderr).toContain(name);
      expect(result.stderr).toContain('the runner pushes');
    }
  });

  test('writing again replaces the files and keeps what the agent put in its directories', () => {
    const { clone, tools, runDir } = written();
    mkdirSync(join(runDir.cache, 'npm'), { recursive: true });
    writeRunDir({ clone, tools, taskPack: 'new pack\n', brief: 'new brief\n', identity });
    expect(readFileSync(runDir.taskMd, 'utf8')).toBe('new pack\n');
    expect(readFileSync(runDir.briefMd, 'utf8')).toBe('new brief\n');
    expect(existsSync(join(runDir.cache, 'npm'))).toBe(true);
  });

  test('follows no link the agent planted, and writes nothing outside the clone', () => {
    const outside = tempDir('agflow-outside-');
    const profile = join(outside, '.zshrc');
    writeFileSync(profile, 'export PATH=/usr/bin\n');
    const elsewhere = join(outside, 'dir');
    mkdirSync(elsewhere);
    const snapshot = () => [readFileSync(profile, 'utf8'), readdirSync(elsewhere)];
    const before = snapshot();
    const check = (clone: string) => {
      const runDir = runDirOf(clone, '/unused');
      expect(snapshot()).toEqual(before);
      for (const dir of [join(clone, '.agflow'), runDir.root, runDir.config, runDir.cache, runDir.home, runDir.tmp]) {
        expect(lstatSync(dir).isDirectory()).toBe(true);
      }
      for (const file of [runDir.taskMd, runDir.briefMd]) expect(lstatSync(file).isFile()).toBe(true);
    };
    // The whole run directory is a link.
    const linkedRun = tempDir();
    mkdirSync(join(linkedRun, '.agflow'));
    symlinkSync(elsewhere, join(linkedRun, '.agflow', 'run'));
    written(linkedRun);
    check(linkedRun);
    // .agflow itself is a link.
    const linkedAgflow = tempDir();
    symlinkSync(elsewhere, join(linkedAgflow, '.agflow'));
    written(linkedAgflow);
    check(linkedAgflow);
    // Files and directories inside it are links, as a committed `.agflow/run/task.md -> ~/.zshrc` would leave them.
    const { clone, tools } = written();
    const runDir = runDirOf(clone, tools);
    rmSync(runDir.taskMd);
    symlinkSync(profile, runDir.taskMd);
    rmSync(runDir.briefMd);
    symlinkSync(profile, runDir.briefMd);
    rmSync(runDir.config, { recursive: true });
    symlinkSync(elsewhere, runDir.config);
    rmSync(runDir.cache, { recursive: true });
    symlinkSync(elsewhere, runDir.cache);
    writeRunDir({ clone, tools, taskPack: 'pack\n', brief: 'brief', identity });
    check(clone);
    expect(readFileSync(runDir.taskMd, 'utf8')).toBe('pack\n');
  });

  test('replaces a tools directory someone changed, whatever is in it', () => {
    const { clone, tools, runDir } = written();
    removeAgentTools(tools);
    mkdirSync(runDir.bin, { recursive: true });
    writeFileSync(join(runDir.bin, 'git'), '#!/bin/sh\n');
    writeFileSync(runDir.gitconfig, '[core]\n\tfsmonitor = /tmp/x.sh\n');
    writeRunDir({ clone, tools, taskPack: '', brief: '', identity });
    expect(readdirSync(runDir.bin).sort()).toEqual(['gh', 'glab']);
    expect(readFileSync(runDir.gitconfig, 'utf8')).not.toContain('fsmonitor');
  });
});

describe('withWorkingDirectory', () => {
  test("appends 'Your working directory: <clone>'", () => {
    expect(withWorkingDirectory('You are a worker.', '/w/T-4-a1')).toBe(
      'You are a worker.\n\nYour working directory: /w/T-4-a1',
    );
    expect(withWorkingDirectory('You are a worker.\n', '/w/T-4-a1')).toBe(
      'You are a worker.\n\nYour working directory: /w/T-4-a1',
    );
  });

describe('git with the agent environment', () => {
  let repo: OriginRepo;

  async function agentClone() {
    repo = await originRepo({ 'a.txt': 'a\n' });
    cleanups.push(() => repo.remove());
    const clone = join(tempDir(), 'T-4-a1');
    await gitIn(tmpdir(), ['clone', '--quiet', repo.path, clone]);
    const tools = toolsDir();
    const runDir = writeRunDir({ clone, tools, taskPack: '', brief: '', identity });
    const config = RunnerConfigSchema.parse({ runnerKey: 'rk', machineId: 'M', name: 'laptop' });
    const env = buildAgentEnv({
      vendor: 'codex',
      spec: { attemptId: 'T-4-a1', role: 'worker', agentToken: 'agt', hubUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:9' },
      clone,
      tools,
      tmpDir: null,
      config,
      paths: runnerPaths(tempDir()),
      base: { HOME: tempDir(), USER: 'owner' },
      env: {},
    });
    return { clone, runDir, env };
  }

  // git runs the freshly written SSH refusal script, and macOS checks each new executable on its first run.
  test('a push to an http or an ssh remote fails at once without prompting', async () => {
    const { clone, env } = await agentClone();
    // A remote that asks for a login, as a git host does.
    const server = Bun.serve({
      port: 0,
      hostname: '127.0.0.1',
      fetch: () =>
        new Response('login required', { status: 401, headers: { 'WWW-Authenticate': 'Basic realm="git"' } }),
    });
    cleanups.push(() => server.stop(true));
    const http = `http://127.0.0.1:${server.port}/acme/demo.git`;
    const ssh = 'ssh://git@127.0.0.1:1/acme/demo.git';
    // The agent gitconfig's protocol.allow=never stops both first.
    for (const url of [http, ssh]) {
      const started = Date.now();
      const result = await run(['git', 'push', url, 'HEAD:refs/heads/main'], { cwd: clone, env });
      expect(result.code).not.toBe(0);
      expect(result.stderr).toMatch(/transport '(http|ssh)' not allowed/);
      expect(Date.now() - started).toBeLessThan(5_000);
    }
    // Past it, the refusal script answers SSH, and no prompt is shown for http.
    const allowed = ['git', '-c', 'protocol.allow=always', 'push'];
    const overSsh = await run([...allowed, ssh, 'HEAD:refs/heads/main'], { cwd: clone, env });
    expect(overSsh.code).not.toBe(0);
    expect(overSsh.stderr).toContain('is not available to runner agents');
    const started = Date.now();
    const overHttp = await run([...allowed, http, 'HEAD:refs/heads/main'], { cwd: clone, env });
    expect(overHttp.code).not.toBe(0);
    expect(overHttp.stderr).toContain('terminal prompts disabled');
    expect(Date.now() - started).toBeLessThan(5_000);
    // A fetch from the vault-like origin path still works: local protocols are allowed.
    expect((await run(['git', 'fetch', 'origin', 'main'], { cwd: clone, env })).code).toBe(0);
  }, 30_000);

  test('the agent git config is read-only: git config --global fails and changes nothing', async () => {
    const { clone, runDir, env } = await agentClone();
    const before = readFileSync(runDir.gitconfig, 'utf8');
    const result = await run(['git', 'config', '--global', 'core.fsmonitor', '/tmp/x.sh'], { cwd: clone, env });
    expect(result.code).not.toBe(0);
    expect(readFileSync(runDir.gitconfig, 'utf8')).toBe(before);
    expect((await run(['git', 'config', '--get', 'user.name'], { cwd: clone, env })).stdout.trim()).toBe(
      identity.name,
    );
  });
});
```

**File:** `packages/runner/src/env.ts` (new)

```ts
// The agent environment (design 7.6): built only from an allowlist, never by removing variables from the runner's
// own environment, so a secret the runner happens to hold (an API key, an SSH agent, a cloud credential) never
// reaches an agent. Test mode's claudeEnv comes after the allowlist (15.1).
import { homedir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import type { AttemptSpec, Vendor } from '@agflow/core';
import { CONNECTIVITY_VARS, isTestMode, type RunnerConfig, vendorHomes } from './config';
import { agentGitEnv } from './git/run';
import type { RunnerPaths } from './paths';
import { runDirOf } from './run-dir';

type Env = Record<string, string | undefined>;

export interface AgentEnvInput {
  vendor: Vendor;
  spec: Pick<AttemptSpec, 'attemptId' | 'role' | 'agentToken' | 'hubUrl'>;
  clone: string;
  /** The attempt's runner-owned tools directory, paths.agentTools(project, attemptId). */
  tools: string;
  /** Claude's CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR, /tmp/agf/<id> (makeAttemptTmpDir); null for Codex. */
  tmpDir: string | null;
  config: RunnerConfig;
  paths: RunnerPaths;
  /** The runner's own environment, read only for the user and system variables and the owner's HOME. */
  base?: Env;
  /** Where AGFLOW_TEST is read; process.env by default. */
  env?: Env;
}

/** Carried from the runner's environment as they are. */
function userVariable(name: string): boolean {
  return ['USER', 'LOGNAME', 'LANG', 'SHELL'].includes(name) || name.startsWith('LC_');
}

/** What an agent environment carries from base as it is: USER, LOGNAME, LANG, SHELL and the LC_ variables. */
export function userVariables(base: Env): Record<string, string> {
  const env: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(base)) {
    if (value !== undefined && userVariable(name)) env[name] = value;
  }
  return env;
}

/** The package managers' caches, per attempt inside the clone. */
const CACHES = {
  BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR: 'bun',
  npm_config_cache: 'npm',
  PIP_CACHE_DIR: 'pip',
  UV_CACHE_DIR: 'uv',
  GOMODCACHE: 'go-mod',
  CARGO_HOME: 'cargo',
} as const;

const BRIDGE_PREFIX = 'AGFLOW_';
const CONNECTIVITY = new Set<string>(CONNECTIVITY_VARS);

export function buildAgentEnv(input: AgentEnvInput): Record<string, string> {
  const base = input.base ?? process.env;
  const runDir = runDirOf(input.clone, input.tools);
  const homes = vendorHomes(input.config, input.paths);
  const env = userVariables(base);
  env.TERM = 'dumb';
  env.NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA = '1';
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(input.config.connectivity)) {
    if (value !== undefined) env[name] = value;
  }
  if (input.vendor === 'claude') {
    if (input.tmpDir === null) throw new Error('a Claude attempt needs its private CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR');
    // The CLI process needs the owner's HOME for its login; its tools are confined by the sandbox and the guard.
    env.HOME = base.HOME ?? homedir();
    env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR = homes.claude;
    env.CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR = input.tmpDir;
    env.CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS = '1';
  } else {
    // An empty HOME, so the owner's ~/.agents/skills do not load into the app-server.
    env.HOME = input.paths.homes.codexUser;
    env.CODEX_HOME = homes.codex;
  }
  env.DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER = '1';
  for (const [name, dir] of Object.entries(CACHES)) env[name] = join(runDir.cache, dir);
  env.PATH = `${runDir.bin}:${input.config.capturedPath}`;
  Object.assign(env, agentGitEnv(runDir));
  Object.assign(env, {
    AGFLOW_AGENT_TOKEN: input.spec.agentToken,
    AGFLOW_HUB_URL: input.spec.hubUrl,
    AGFLOW_ATTEMPT_ID: input.spec.attemptId,
    AGFLOW_ROLE: input.spec.role,
    AGFLOW_CLONE: input.clone,
    AGFLOW_BRIDGE_POLL_MS: String(input.config.timings.bridgePoll),
    AGFLOW_BRIDGE_POLL_MAX_MS: String(input.config.timings.bridgePollMax),
    // Empty and per attempt, so the bridge never reads the owner's CLI credentials (X-32).
    AGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR: runDir.config,
  });
  if (input.vendor === 'claude' && isTestMode(input.config, input.env ?? process.env)) {
    Object.assign(env, input.config.test?.claudeEnv);
  }
  return env;
}

/**
 * The bridge's own environment (AgentLaunch.bridge.env, X-32): the AGFLOW_* variables, NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA and the
 * connectivity variables of an agent environment. Codex forwards exactly these names to the bridge.
 */
export function bridgeEnvOf(agentEnv: Record<string, string>): Record<string, string> {
  return Object.fromEntries(
    Object.entries(agentEnv).filter(
      ([name]) => name.startsWith(BRIDGE_PREFIX) || name === 'NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA' || CONNECTIVITY.has(name),
    ),
  );
}
```
