```ts
// The permission profile and the denied paths of design 7.6, as data. The vendor adapters render them: Claude's
// permission rules and sandbox settings (M2d), Codex's sandbox (M2e), and dependency preparation's sandbox (M2c).
import { isAbsolute, join } from 'node:path';
import type { Vendor } from '@agflow/core';
import type { RunnerConfig } from './config';
import type { RunnerPaths } from './paths';

export interface PermissionProfile {
  /** Claude: acceptEdits with the sandbox, or auto mode with the sandbox. */
  name: 'standard' | 'auto';
  /** The hosts agent tool commands may reach (Claude's sandbox). */
  network: { allowedDomains: string[] };
  /** WebFetch and WebSearch (Claude), web search (Codex). */
  webTools: boolean;
}

/** The package registries of the default profile. */
const REGISTRIES = [
  'registry.npmjs.org',
  'registry.yarnpkg.com',
  'bun.sh',
  'pypi.org',
  'files.pythonhosted.org',
  'proxy.golang.org',
  'sum.golang.org',
  'crates.io',
  'static.crates.io',
  'index.crates.io',
];

/** The default profile. Frozen: profileOf gives copies to change. */
export const standardProfile: PermissionProfile = Object.freeze({
  name: 'standard',
  network: Object.freeze({ allowedDomains: Object.freeze([...REGISTRIES]) as string[] }),
  webTools: false,
});

/**
 * The profile runner.json asks for. Whether the account offers auto mode is the Claude adapter's to check; it falls
 * back to standard and reports so.
 */
export function profileOf(config: Pick<RunnerConfig, 'profile'>): PermissionProfile {
  return { name: config.profile, network: { allowedDomains: [...REGISTRIES] }, webTools: false };
}

/** An absolute path; tree marks a directory whose whole contents are meant. */
export interface DeniedPath {
  path: string;
  tree: boolean;
}

export interface DeniedPathsInput {
  /** The owner's home, given rather than read from the process. */
  home: string;
  paths: Pick<RunnerPaths, 'runner' | 'vaults' | 'work'>;
  /** vendorHomes(config, paths): runner.json may put them outside the runner tree, shared by several runners. */
  vendorHomes: Record<Vendor, string>;
}

const tree = (path: string): DeniedPath => ({ path, tree: true });
const file = (path: string): DeniedPath => ({ path, tree: false });

/** The vendor homes the runner tree does not already cover: their logins, transcripts and .claude.json. */
function outsideHomes(input: DeniedPathsInput): DeniedPath[] {
  const runner = `${input.paths.runner}/`;
  const homes = [...new Set(Object.values(input.vendorHomes))];
  return homes.filter((home) => !`${home}/`.startsWith(runner)).map(tree);
}

/**
 * A denied path that holds the work root would deny the agent its own clone: deny rules cannot be re-allowed, and
 * Claude copies Edit denials into the sandbox's denyWrite (7.6).
 */
function checked(input: DeniedPathsInput, denied: DeniedPath[]): DeniedPath[] {
  if (!isAbsolute(input.home)) throw new Error(`the owner's home must be an absolute path, not ${input.home}`);
  for (const { path } of denied) {
    if (`${input.paths.work}/`.startsWith(`${path}/`) || path.startsWith(`${input.paths.work}/`)) {
      throw new Error(`the denied path ${path} would cover the work root ${input.paths.work}; move AGFLOW_HOME`);
    }
  }
  return denied;
}

/**
 * Paths agents may not read: credentials, vendor and CLI state, the whole runner tree and vendor homes outside it.
 * The Claude adapter names only the runner tree's sensitive parts in its Read rules, keeps its allowRead for the
 * attempt's own project directory, and adds the work root to its sandbox's denyRead with the clone allowed; neither
 * is listed here.
 */
export function deniedReadPaths(input: DeniedPathsInput): DeniedPath[] {
  const home = (...parts: string[]) => join(input.home, ...parts);
  return checked(input, [
    tree(home('.ssh')),
    file(home('.netrc')),
    file(home('.git-credentials')),
    tree(home('.config', 'gh')),
    tree(home('.config', 'glab-cli')),
    tree(home('.config', 'agflow')),
    tree(input.paths.runner),
    ...outsideHomes(input),
    tree(home('.claude')),
    file(home('.claude.json')),
    tree(home('.codex')),
    tree(home('Library', 'Keychains')),
    tree(home('.aws')),
    tree(home('.config', 'gcloud')),
    tree(home('.kube')),
    file(home('.docker', 'config.json')),
  ]);
}

/**
 * Paths agents may not write: runner state, vendor homes outside it and the vaults (with the attempts' tools
 * directories), vendor and CLI config, LaunchAgents and shell profiles.
 */
export function deniedWritePaths(input: DeniedPathsInput): DeniedPath[] {
  const home = (...parts: string[]) => join(input.home, ...parts);
  return checked(input, [
    tree(input.paths.runner),
    ...outsideHomes(input),
    tree(input.paths.vaults),
    tree(home('.claude')),
    file(home('.claude.json')),
    tree(home('.codex')),
    tree(home('.config', 'agflow')),
    tree(home('Library', 'LaunchAgents')),
    ...['.zshrc', '.zprofile', '.zshenv', '.bashrc', '.bash_profile', '.profile', '.gitconfig'].map((name) =>
      file(home(name)),
    ),
  ]);
}
```

```ts
// A clone's .agflow/run/ (design 7.2): runner-owned, untracked and never committed. It holds the task pack and the
// brief, the Codex tool HOME, per-attempt package caches, a temporary directory and the bridge's empty
// AGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR (X-32).
//
// What processes outside the sandbox run or read as git config stays out of the clone, which the agent can write:
// the Claude CLI runs git in the clone for its context, and sources the owner's shell profile, with the agent's
// environment. So the agent gitconfig, the refusal scripts on PATH and gh's and glab's config directories live in a
// read-only tools directory under vaults/ (paths.agentTools), which agents may read but never write.
//
// The runner writes all of this with the owner's full rights and outside any sandbox, into a tree the agent may have
// prepared (a clone it kept, or a committed `.agflow/run/task.md -> ~/.zshrc`), so it never follows a link there.
import {
  chmodSync,
  closeSync,
  fchmodSync,
  lstatSync,
  mkdirSync,
  openSync,
  readdirSync,
  realpathSync,
  rmSync,
  type Stats,
  writeSync,
} from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join, sep } from 'node:path';
import type { AgentGitPaths } from './git/run';

export interface RunDir extends AgentGitPaths {
  /** <clone>/.agflow/run. */
  root: string;
  taskMd: string;
  briefMd: string;
  /** The Codex tool commands' HOME. */
  home: string;
  /** Per-attempt package caches. */
  cache: string;
  /** The Codex tool commands' TMPDIR. */
  tmp: string;
  /** AGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR for the bridge and the brief hook: no credentials, only hook.log. */
  config: string;
  /** The runner-owned, read-only tools directory outside the clone; cleanup removes it with removeAgentTools. */
  tools: string;
  /** First on the agent's PATH: the gh and glab shims. */
  bin: string;
}

export function runDirOf(clone: string, tools: string): RunDir {
  const root = join(clone, '.agflow', 'run');
  return {
    root,
    taskMd: join(root, 'task.md'),
    briefMd: join(root, 'brief.md'),
    home: join(root, 'home'),
    cache: join(root, 'cache'),
    tmp: join(root, 'tmp'),
    config: join(root, 'config'),
    tools,
    gitconfig: join(tools, 'gitconfig'),
    bin: join(tools, 'bin'),
    sshRefusal: join(tools, 'ssh-refusal'),
    ghConfigDir: join(tools, 'gh-config'),
    glabConfigDir: join(tools, 'glab-config'),
  };
}

/** The line the hub cannot write, since it does not know the clone's path (X-17). */
export function withWorkingDirectory(brief: string, clone: string): string {
  return `${brief.replace(/\n+$/, '')}\n\nYour working directory: ${clone}`;
}

/** A value in git's config syntax: quoted, with backslashes and quotes escaped; a newline cannot be held. */
function configValue(value: string, what: string): string {
  if (/[\n\r\0]/.test(value)) throw new Error(`the commit identity's ${what} cannot hold a line break`);
  return `"${value.replace(/\\/g, '\\\\').replace(/"/g, '\\"')}"`;
}

function agentGitconfig(identity: { name: string; email: string }): string {
  return [
    '# Written by the agflow runner. Agents cannot push: the runner pushes for them.',
    '[user]',
    `\tname = ${configValue(identity.name, 'name')}`,
    `\temail = ${configValue(identity.email, 'email')}`,
    '[credential]',
    '\thelper =',
    '[protocol]',
    '\tallow = never',
    '[protocol "file"]',
    '\tallow = always',
    '',
  ].join('\n');
}

function refusal(what: string): string {
  const explanation =
    `agflow: ${what} is not available to runner agents. ` + 'Commit on your task branch; the runner pushes for you.';
  return ['#!/bin/sh', `echo "${explanation}" >&2`, 'exit 1', ''].join('\n');
}

function lstatOrNull(path: string): Stats | null {
  try {
    return lstatSync(path);
  } catch (error) {
    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'ENOENT') return null;
    throw error;
  }
}

/** Makes path a real directory, keeping one that is: a link or a file there is removed, never followed. */
function realDirectory(path: string): void {
  const stat = lstatOrNull(path);
  if (stat?.isDirectory()) return;
  if (stat) rmSync(path, { force: true });
  mkdirSync(path);
}

/**
 * Writes a new file: whatever is at path goes first (rmSync removes a link, not its target), and O_EXCL refuses a
 * link that appears meanwhile. The mode is set on the open file, never through the path.
 */
function writeNew(path: string, content: string, mode: number): void {
  rmSync(path, { recursive: true, force: true });
  const fd = openSync(path, 'wx', mode);
  try {
    fchmodSync(fd, mode);
    writeSync(fd, content);
  } finally {
    closeSync(fd);
  }
}

function inside(child: string, parent: string): boolean {
  return child.startsWith(parent.endsWith(sep) ? parent : `${parent}${sep}`);
}

/** Removes an attempt's tools directory, read-only as writeRunDir leaves it; nothing there is no error. */
export function removeAgentTools(tools: string): void {
  const stat = lstatOrNull(tools);
  if (!stat) return;
  if (stat.isDirectory()) {
    // Its directories are read-only: writable again first, or their entries cannot be removed.
    const writable = (dir: string) => {
      chmodSync(dir, 0o700);
      for (const entry of readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
        if (entry.isDirectory()) writable(join(dir, entry.name));
      }
    };
    writable(tools);
  }
  rmSync(tools, { recursive: true, force: true });
}

export interface RunDirInput {
  clone: string;
  /** paths.agentTools(project, attemptId). */
  tools: string;
  /** AttemptSpec.taskPack. */
  taskPack: string;
  /** The brief as the agent gets it, withWorkingDirectory applied. */
  brief: string;
  /** runner.json's commitIdentity. */
  identity: { name: string; email: string };
}

/**
 * Writes the clone's .agflow/run/ and the attempt's tools directory. Writing again replaces the runner's files,
 * keeps what the agent put in its directories (caches, say), and makes the tools directory anew.
 */
export function writeRunDir(input: RunDirInput): RunDir {
  const gitconfig = agentGitconfig(input.identity);
  const dir = runDirOf(input.clone, input.tools);
  realDirectory(join(input.clone, '.agflow'));
  realDirectory(dir.root);
  const clone = realpathSync(input.clone);
  if (!inside(realpathSync(dir.root), clone)) throw new Error(`${dir.root} is not inside the clone ${clone}`);
  for (const path of [dir.home, dir.cache, dir.tmp, dir.config]) realDirectory(path);
  writeNew(dir.taskMd, input.taskPack, 0o644);
  writeNew(dir.briefMd, input.brief.endsWith('\n') ? input.brief : `${input.brief}\n`, 0o644);

  removeAgentTools(dir.tools);
  mkdirSync(dirname(dir.tools), { recursive: true });
  for (const path of [dir.tools, dir.bin, dir.ghConfigDir, dir.glabConfigDir]) mkdirSync(path, { mode: 0o700 });
  writeNew(dir.gitconfig, gitconfig, 0o444);
  writeNew(join(dir.bin, 'gh'), refusal('gh'), 0o555);
  writeNew(join(dir.bin, 'glab'), refusal('glab'), 0o555);
  writeNew(dir.sshRefusal, refusal('SSH (git push, fetch or clone over ssh)'), 0o555);
  // Read-only, so not even the agent's own git, running as the owner, can change it.
  for (const path of [dir.ghConfigDir, dir.glabConfigDir, dir.bin, dir.tools]) chmodSync(path, 0o555);
  return dir;
}
```

### Task 12: The adapter interface and a basic fake adapter

Design 13's adapter interface is the contract between the runner core and the vendor plans, so it is written exactly (X-5): `VendorAdapter`, `PreflightResult`, `AdapterFactory`, `AgflowCommand`, `AgentLaunch`, `AgentSession`, `AgentEvent` and `ExitInfo`. Testkit gets a fake adapter whose agent is a real child process (`fake-agent.ts`, run with `process.execPath`) in its own process group, so runner tests exercise real signals, groups and git (design 15). This task covers its basic script: files, commits with the launch's git identity, tool children (one may outlive the agent, X-15), text, terminal tools, messages, interrupt and close, and ignoring stdin EOF mid-turn as Claude does. With `skipAuthChecks` its preflight reports ready, 'test mode' and `TEST_ACCOUNT_ID` (X-21), and its `weakened` list is empty.

```ts
import { afterEach, describe, expect, setDefaultTimeout, test } from 'bun:test';
import { appendFileSync, existsSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { TEST_ACCOUNT_ID } from '@agflow/core';
import {
  type AgentEvent,
  type AgentLaunch,
  type AgentSession,
  agentGitEnv,
  processIdentity,
  removeAgentTools,
  standardProfile,
  writeRunDir,
} from '@agflow/runner';
import { FAKE_AGENT_PATH, FakeAdapter, type FakeAdapterOptions, type FakeScript } from '../src/fake-adapter';
import { gitIn, originRepo } from '../src/git-fixtures';

const cleanups: (() => void)[] = [];
afterEach(() => {
  for (const cleanup of cleanups.splice(0).reverse()) cleanup();
});

// Every test here runs git or agent processes, which take several times as long on a machine loaded by other suites.
setDefaultTimeout(30_000);

function tempDir(prefix: string): string {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), prefix));
  cleanups.push(() => rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }));
  return dir;
}

/** Kills a process group at the end of the test, whatever state it is in. */
function killLater(pgid: number): void {
  cleanups.push(() => {
    try {
      process.kill(-pgid, 'SIGKILL');
    } catch {
      // Already gone.
    }
  });
}

const IDENTITY = { name: 'Agent Smith', email: 'agent@agflow.invalid' };

/** A clone on its task branch with the agent's .agflow/run/, and a launch for it. */
async function setup(overrides: Partial<AgentLaunch> = {}): Promise<{ launch: AgentLaunch; clone: string }> {
  const origin = await originRepo({ 'README.md': '# demo\n' });
  cleanups.push(() => origin.remove());
  const clone = join(tempDir('agflow-fake-clone-'), 'T-4-a1');
  await gitIn(tmpdir(), ['clone', '--quiet', origin.path, clone]);
  await gitIn(clone, ['checkout', '--quiet', '-b', 'agflow/T-4-tidy']);
  const tools = join(tempDir('agflow-fake-tools-'), 'T-4-a1');
  cleanups.push(() => removeAgentTools(tools));
  const runDir = writeRunDir({ clone, tools, taskPack: '# T-4\n', brief: 'brief', identity: IDENTITY });
  // As the runner's clones do, so the agent's `git add -A` leaves .agflow/run/ out.
  appendFileSync(join(clone, '.git', 'info', 'exclude'), '/.agflow/run/\n');
  const env = { PATH: process.env.PATH ?? '/usr/bin:/bin', HOME: tempDir('agflow-fake-home-'), ...agentGitEnv(runDir) };
  const launch: AgentLaunch = {
    attemptId: 'T-4-a1',
    role: 'worker',
    model: 'fake-model',
    cliVersion: '9.9.9',
    clone,
    baseCheckout: null,
    projectConfigVerified: true,
    tmpDir: runDir.tmp,
    env,
    bridge: { command: '/bin/false', args: [], env: {} },
    profile: standardProfile,
    brief: 'brief',
    firstPrompt: 'start working',
    resume: null,
    logFile: join(tempDir('agflow-fake-logs-'), 'T-4-a1.log'),
    registerProcess: () => {},
    ...overrides,
  };
  return { launch, clone };
}

async function start(
  launch: AgentLaunch,
  script: FakeScript,
  options: Omit<FakeAdapterOptions, 'script'> = {},
): Promise<AgentSession> {
  const session = await new FakeAdapter({ ...options, script }).start(launch);
  killLater(session.pid);
  return session;
}

/** Reads every event of a session in the background. */
function record(session: AgentSession) {
  const events: AgentEvent[] = [];
  void (async () => {
    for await (const event of session.events) events.push(event);
  })();
  return {
    events,
    types: () =>
      events.map((event) =>
        event.type === 'delivered' || event.type === 'acknowledged' ? `${event.type} ${event.id}` : event.type,
      ),
    async waitFor(check: (event: AgentEvent) => boolean, timeoutMs = 5_000): Promise<AgentEvent> {
      const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
      for (;;) {
        const found = events.find(check);
        if (found) return found;
        if (Date.now() > deadline) throw new Error(`no such event in ${JSON.stringify(events)}`);
        await Bun.sleep(5);
      }
    },
  };
}

const turnEnded = (event: AgentEvent) => event.type === 'turn_ended';
const countOf = (events: AgentEvent[], type: AgentEvent['type']) =>
  events.filter((event) => event.type === type).length;

async function waitFile(path: string): Promise<string> {
  const deadline = Date.now() + 5_000;
  while (!existsSync(path) || readFileSync(path, 'utf8').trim() === '') {
    if (Date.now() > deadline) throw new Error(`${path} never appeared`);
    await Bun.sleep(10);
  }
  return readFileSync(path, 'utf8').trim();
}

describe('FakeAdapter.start', () => {
  test('runs the fake agent detached in its own group, registered before its output is read', async () => {

    expect(FAKE_AGENT_PATH.endsWith('fake-agent.ts')).toBe(true);

    expect(reader.types()).toEqual([
      'started',
      'delivered m1',
      'turn_started',
      'text',
      'turn_ended',
      'acknowledged m1',
    ]);
  });
});

describe('the fake agent script', () => {
  test('writes files, commits with the launch identity, runs a tool in its own group and emits text', async () => {
    const { launch, clone } = await setup();
    const out = join(tempDir('agflow-fake-out-'), 'tool');
    const session = await start(launch, {
      turns: [
        [
          { do: 'write', path: 'src/a.ts', content: 'export const a = 1;\n' },
          { do: 'write', path: 'README.md', content: null },
          { do: 'commit', message: 'add a' },
          { do: 'tool', command: `echo "$$ $(ps -o pgid= -p $$)" > '${out}'` },
          { do: 'text', text: 'all done' },
        ],
      ],
    });
    const reader = record(session);
    const ended = await reader.waitFor(turnEnded);
    expect(ended).toEqual({ type: 'turn_ended', outcome: 'completed', toolCalls: 4, error: null, errorKind: null });
    expect(reader.types()).toEqual([
      'started',
      'turn_started',
      ...Array.from({ length: 4 }, () => ['tool_started', 'tool_ended']).flat(),
      'text',
      'turn_ended',
    ]);
    const tools = reader.events.filter((event) => event.type === 'tool_started');
    expect(tools.map((event) => event.type === 'tool_started' && [event.name, event.command])).toEqual([
      ['Write', null],
      ['Write', null],
      ['Bash', "git add -A && git commit -q -m 'add a'"],
      ['Bash', `echo "$$ $(ps -o pgid= -p $$)" > '${out}'`],
    ]);
    const results = reader.events.flatMap((event) => (event.type === 'tool_ended' ? [event.ok] : []));
    expect(results).toEqual([true, true, true, true]);
    expect(reader.events.find((event) => event.type === 'text')).toEqual({ type: 'text', text: 'all done' });
    expect(await gitIn(clone, ['log', '-1', '--format=%an <%ae>|%cn <%ce>|%s'])).toBe(
      'Agent Smith <agent@agflow.invalid>|Agent Smith <agent@agflow.invalid>|add a',
    );
    expect(await gitIn(clone, ['ls-tree', '-r', '--name-only', 'HEAD'])).toBe('src/a.ts');
    expect(await gitIn(clone, ['status', '--porcelain'])).toBe('');
    const [pid, pgid] = (await waitFile(out)).split(/\s+/).map(Number);
    expect(pgid).toBe(pid as number);
    expect(pgid).not.toBe(session.pid);
  });

  test('terminal tools report terminal on success only, and a hub-unreachable answer sets hubUnreachable', async () => {
    const { launch } = await setup();
    const session = await start(launch, {
      turns: [
        [
          { do: 'terminal', tool: 'submit' },
          { do: 'terminal', tool: 'blocked' },
          { do: 'terminal', tool: 'impossible' },
          { do: 'terminal', tool: 'released' },
          { do: 'terminal', tool: 'handoff' },
          { do: 'terminal', tool: 'submit', answer: 'refused' },
          { do: 'terminal', tool: 'submit', answer: 'hub_unreachable' },
        ],
      ],
    });
    const reader = record(session);
    await reader.waitFor(turnEnded);
    const names = reader.events.flatMap((event) => (event.type === 'tool_started' ? [event.name] : []));
    expect(names).toEqual([
      'mcp__agflow__submit',
      'mcp__agflow__declare_blocked',
      'mcp__agflow__declare_impossible',
      'mcp__agflow__release_task',
      'mcp__agflow__write_handoff',
      'mcp__agflow__submit',
      'mcp__agflow__submit',
    ]);
    const ended = reader.events.flatMap((event) =>
      event.type === 'tool_ended' ? [[event.ok, event.terminal, event.hubUnreachable, event.denied]] : [],
    );
    expect(ended).toEqual([
      [true, 'submit', false, false],
      [true, 'blocked', false, false],
      [true, 'impossible', false, false],
      [true, 'released', false, false],
      [true, 'handoff', false, false],
      [false, null, false, false],
      [false, null, true, false],
    ]);
  });

  test('a scripted tool child in its own group keeps running after the agent exits', async () => {
    const { launch } = await setup();
    const out = join(tempDir('agflow-fake-out-'), 'pid');
    const session = await start(launch, {
      turns: [[{ do: 'tool', command: `echo $$ > '${out}'; exec sleep 30`, wait: false }, { do: 'exit', code: 3 }]],
    });
    const reader = record(session);
    expect(await session.exited).toEqual({ code: 3, signal: null });
    const pid = Number(await waitFile(out));
    killLater(pid);
    const tool = await processIdentity(pid);
    expect(tool?.pgid).toBe(pid);
    expect(countOf(reader.events, 'turn_ended')).toBe(0);
  });
});

describe('FakeAdapter sessions', () => {
  test('send() emits delivered when the input is taken and acknowledged when its turn ends', async () => {
    const { launch } = await setup();
    const session = await start(launch, {
      turns: [[{ do: 'sleep', ms: 300 }, { do: 'text', text: 'first' }], [{ do: 'text', text: 'second' }]],
    });
    const reader = record(session);
    await reader.waitFor((event) => event.type === 'turn_started');
    // Taken mid-turn at the next step, as Claude folds a message into the running turn.
    await session.send({ id: 'm1', text: 'also this', authority: 'person' });
    await reader.waitFor(turnEnded);
    await reader.waitFor((event) => event.type === 'acknowledged');
    await session.send({ id: 'm2', text: 'next', authority: 'agent' });
    await reader.waitFor((event) => event.type === 'acknowledged' && event.id === 'm2');
    expect(reader.types()).toEqual([
      'started',
      'turn_started',
      'delivered m1',
      'text',
      'turn_ended',
      'acknowledged m1',
      'delivered m2',
      'turn_started',
      'text',
      'turn_ended',
      'acknowledged m2',
    ]);
  });

  test('interrupt() ends the turn as interrupted; queued messages run next unless cancelled', async () => {
    const { launch } = await setup();
    const session = await start(launch, {
      turns: [[{ do: 'sleep', ms: 30_000 }], [{ do: 'text', text: 'after' }], [{ do: 'sleep', ms: 30_000 }]],
    });
    const reader = record(session);
    await reader.waitFor((event) => event.type === 'turn_started');
    await session.send({ id: 'm1', text: 'queued', authority: 'person' });
    await Bun.sleep(50);
    await session.interrupt();
    await reader.waitFor((event) => event.type === 'acknowledged' && event.id === 'm1');
    await session.send({ id: 'm2', text: 'long one', authority: 'person' });
    await reader.waitFor((event) => event.type === 'delivered' && event.id === 'm2');
    await session.send({ id: 'm3', text: 'dropped', authority: 'person' });
    await Bun.sleep(50);
    await session.interrupt({ cancelQueued: true });
    await reader.waitFor((event) => event.type === 'acknowledged' && event.id === 'm2');
    await Bun.sleep(200);
    expect(reader.types()).toEqual([
      'started',
      'turn_started',
      'turn_ended',
      'delivered m1',
      'turn_started',
      'text',
      'turn_ended',
      'acknowledged m1',
      'delivered m2',
      'turn_started',
      'turn_ended',
      'acknowledged m2',
    ]);
    const outcomes = reader.events.flatMap((event) => (event.type === 'turn_ended' ? [event.outcome] : []));
    expect(outcomes).toEqual(['interrupted', 'completed', 'interrupted']);
  });

  test('interrupt() during a tool that waits ends the turn and fails the tool', async () => {
    const { launch } = await setup();
    const out = join(tempDir('agflow-fake-out-'), 'pid');
    const session = await start(launch, {
      turns: [[{ do: 'tool', command: `echo $$ > '${out}'; exec sleep 30` }, { do: 'text', text: 'never' }]],
    });
    const reader = record(session);
    killLater(Number(await waitFile(out)));
    await session.interrupt();
    expect(await reader.waitFor(turnEnded)).toEqual({
      type: 'turn_ended',
      outcome: 'interrupted',
      toolCalls: 1,
      error: null,
      errorKind: null,
    });
    expect(reader.events.find((event) => event.type === 'tool_ended')).toMatchObject({ ok: false, terminal: null });
    expect(countOf(reader.events, 'text')).toBe(0);
  });

  test('a script that ignores interrupts and EOF mid-turn keeps running after interrupt() and close()', async () => {
    const { launch } = await setup();
    const session = await start(launch, {
      ignoreInterrupt: true,
      ignoreEofMidTurn: true,
      turns: [[{ do: 'sleep', ms: 30_000 }]],
    });
    const reader = record(session);
    await reader.waitFor((event) => event.type === 'turn_started');
    await session.interrupt({ cancelQueued: true });
    await session.close();
    await Bun.sleep(300);
    expect(await processIdentity(session.pid)).not.toBeNull();
    expect(countOf(reader.events, 'turn_ended')).toBe(0);
  });

  test('SIGTERM ends the agent with exit code 143, unless the script ignores it', async () => {
    const { launch } = await setup();
    const plain = await start(launch, { turns: [[{ do: 'sleep', ms: 30_000 }]] });
    await record(plain).waitFor((event) => event.type === 'turn_started');
    process.kill(-plain.pid, 'SIGTERM');
    expect(await plain.exited).toEqual({ code: 143, signal: null });

    const stubborn = await start(launch, { ignoreSigterm: true, turns: [[{ do: 'sleep', ms: 30_000 }]] });
    await record(stubborn).waitFor((event) => event.type === 'turn_started');
    process.kill(-stubborn.pid, 'SIGTERM');
    await Bun.sleep(300);
    expect(await processIdentity(stubborn.pid)).not.toBeNull();
    process.kill(-stubborn.pid, 'SIGKILL');
    expect(await stubborn.exited).toEqual({ code: null, signal: 'SIGKILL' });
  });

  test("a tool child that inherits the agent's pipes keeps its events open after it exits", async () => {
    const { launch } = await setup();
    const out = join(tempDir('agflow-fake-out-'), 'pid');
    const session = await start(launch, {
      turns: [
        [
          { do: 'tool', command: `echo $$ > '${out}'; exec sleep 30`, wait: false, inheritPipes: true },
          { do: 'exit', code: 0 },
        ],
      ],
    });
    let ended = false;
    void (async () => {
      for await (const _event of session.events);
      ended = true;
    })();
    expect(await session.exited).toEqual({ code: 0, signal: null });
    const pid = Number(await waitFile(out));
    killLater(pid);
    await Bun.sleep(200);
    expect(ended).toBe(false);
    process.kill(-pid, 'SIGKILL');
    const deadline = Date.now() + 5_000;
    while (!ended && Date.now() < deadline) await Bun.sleep(10);
    expect(ended).toBe(true);
  });

  test('close() ends an idle agent and an agent mid-turn', async () => {
    const { launch } = await setup();
    const idle = await start(launch, { turns: [] });
    const idleReader = record(idle);
    await idleReader.waitFor(turnEnded);
    await idle.close();
    expect(await idle.exited).toEqual({ code: 0, signal: null });

    const busy = await start(launch, { turns: [[{ do: 'sleep', ms: 30_000 }]] });
    const busyReader = record(busy);
    await busyReader.waitFor((event) => event.type === 'turn_started');
    await busy.close();
    expect(await busy.exited).toEqual({ code: 0, signal: null });
    expect(countOf(busyReader.events, 'turn_ended')).toBe(0);
  });

  test('a script that ignores EOF mid-turn finishes the turn before it exits, as Claude does', async () => {
    const { launch } = await setup();
    const session = await start(launch, {
      ignoreEofMidTurn: true,
      turns: [[{ do: 'sleep', ms: 300 }, { do: 'text', text: 'finished anyway' }]],
    });
    const reader = record(session);
    await reader.waitFor((event) => event.type === 'turn_started');
    await session.close();
    expect(await session.exited).toEqual({ code: 0, signal: null });
    expect(reader.types().slice(-2)).toEqual(['text', 'turn_ended']);
  });

  test('a signalled agent reports its signal; its stderr goes to the attempt log', async () => {
    const { launch } = await setup();
    const session = await start(launch, { turns: [[{ do: 'log', text: 'to stderr' }, { do: 'sleep', ms: 30_000 }]] });
    const reader = record(session);
    await reader.waitFor((event) => event.type === 'turn_started');
    await Bun.sleep(100);
    process.kill(-session.pid, 'SIGKILL');
    expect(await session.exited).toEqual({ code: null, signal: 'SIGKILL' });
    expect(readFileSync(launch.logFile, 'utf8')).toContain('to stderr');
  });
});

    const { launch } = await setup();
```

```ts
// The adapter interface (design 13, X-5). The Claude and Codex adapters implement it, and so does testkit's fake
// adapter. The runner core owns everything that is not vendor-specific; an adapter starts and drives one vendor's
// CLI and turns its output into AgentEvents.
import type { AgentRole, Approval, RunnerVendor, Vendor, VendorQuota } from '@agflow/core';
import type { RunnerConfig } from '../config';
import type { RunnerPaths } from '../paths';
import type { PermissionProfile } from '../profile';

/** How the runner runs agflow itself (`{ command, args }`, as the CLI's selfCommand gives it). */
export interface AgflowCommand {
  command: string;
  args: string[];
}

export interface PreflightResult {
  /** The runner adds models, ceilings, allowPaidUsage, preflightAt and degraded false. */
  facts: Pick<
    RunnerVendor,
    'vendor' | 'cliVersion' | 'ownerCliVersion' | 'ready' | 'problem' | 'accountId' | 'plan' | 'managedPolicy'
  >;
  quota: VendorQuota | null;
  /** Boundaries this laptop cannot enforce, merged with the runner's own into hello.profile.weakened. */
  weakened: string[];
}

export interface VendorAdapter {
  readonly vendor: Vendor;
  preflight(): Promise<PreflightResult>;
  start(launch: AgentLaunch): Promise<AgentSession>;
  /** The end of a session's transcript, read without a live session; null when there is none. */
  readTranscriptTail(input: { sessionRef: string; clone: string; maxChars: number }): Promise<string | null>;
  /** cleanup_attempt and retention. */
  deleteTranscript(input: { sessionRef: string; clone: string }): Promise<void>;
  /** Adds to an approval's detail (Codex: manifest diffs); without it the detail is reported as it came. */
  enrichApproval?(input: {
    clone: string;
    vault: string;
    startSha: string;
    request: { kind: Approval['kind']; summary: string; detail: Approval['detail'] };
  }): Promise<Approval['detail']>;
}

/**
 * One per vendor, in packages/runner/src/adapters/<vendor>/entry.ts; it returns null until that vendor's plan fills
 * it. The agflow command reaches adapters here, since preflight needs it outside any launch.
 */
export type AdapterFactory = (input: {
  config: RunnerConfig;
  paths: RunnerPaths;
  agflow: AgflowCommand;
}) => VendorAdapter | null;

export interface AgentLaunch {
  attemptId: string;
  role: AgentRole;
  /** Resolved by the runner. */
  model: string;
  /** The pin at start; the attempt's recorded version on every resume (design 7.4, X-13). */
  cliVersion: string;
  /** The real path of the clone; the agent's cwd. */
  clone: string;
  /** Claude's project configuration root; null for Codex. */
  baseCheckout: string | null;
  /** The clone's .codex/ equals the restore base's (design 9.2). */
  projectConfigVerified: boolean;
  /** CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR, or the Codex TMPDIR. */
  tmpDir: string;
  /** The agent environment (design 7.6). */
  env: Record<string, string>;
  /** `<agflow> mcp --vendor <v> --runner` with the bridge's own environment. */
  bridge: { command: string; args: string[]; env: Record<string, string> };
  profile: PermissionProfile;
  /** spec.brief plus "Your working directory: <clone>" (design 10). */
  brief: string;
  firstPrompt: string;
  resume: { sessionRef: string } | null;
  logFile: string;
  /** The runner records the process's pid, pgid and lstart; called before any of its output is read. */
  registerProcess(pid: number): void;
}

export interface AgentSession {
  readonly sessionRef: string;
  readonly pid: number;
  readonly events: AsyncIterable<AgentEvent>;
  send(message: { id: string; text: string; authority: 'person' | 'agent' | 'system' }): Promise<void>;
  interrupt(options?: { cancelQueued?: boolean }): Promise<void>;
  /** Gives whether a pending request took the answer. */
  answerApproval(approvalId: string, decision: 'approve' | 'decline', reason: string | null): Promise<boolean>;
  /** The vendor's own graceful end. */
  close(): Promise<void>;
  readonly exited: Promise<ExitInfo>;
}

/** The tools whose normal result ends or hands over the agent's work. */
export type TerminalTool = 'submit' | 'blocked' | 'impossible' | 'released' | 'handoff';

export type AgentEvent =
  | { type: 'started'; sessionRef: string; model: string; cliVersion: string; permissionMode: string | null }
  | { type: 'turn_started' }
  | {
      type: 'turn_ended';
      outcome: 'completed' | 'interrupted' | 'failed';
      toolCalls: number;
      error: string | null;
      errorKind: 'quota' | 'vendor' | 'auth' | 'context' | 'policy' | 'denials' | 'session_budget' | null;
    }
  | { type: 'tool_started'; toolId: string; name: string; input: string; command: string | null }
  | {
      type: 'tool_ended';
      toolId: string;
      ok: boolean;
      denied: boolean;
      /** Counted only on a normal result (design 10). */
      terminal: TerminalTool | null;
      /** The bridge answered the hub-unreachable text. */
      hubUnreachable: boolean;
    }
  | { type: 'text'; text: string }
  | { type: 'delivered'; id: string }
  | { type: 'acknowledged'; id: string }
  | { type: 'quota'; accountId: string | null; quota: VendorQuota }
  | {
      type: 'approval_request';
      approvalId: string;
      kind: Approval['kind'];
      summary: string;
      detail: Approval['detail'];
    }
  | { type: 'approval_void'; approvalId: string }
  | { type: 'waiting_approval'; waiting: boolean }
  | { type: 'compacted'; summary: string | null }
  | { type: 'context'; used: number }
  /** Reported as an attempt.activity note. */
  | { type: 'warning'; text: string };

export interface ExitInfo {
  code: number | null;
  signal: string | null;
}
```

```ts
// The fake adapter (design 15): a VendorAdapter whose agent is a real child process, fake-agent.ts run with Bun in
// its own process group, so runner tests exercise real signals, groups, pipes and git. The agent follows a script
// of turns and speaks JSON lines: AgentEvents on stdout, inputs on stdin. The basic fake keeps no transcript and
// raises no approvals.
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { appendFile, mkdir, mkdtemp, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { TEST_ACCOUNT_ID, type Vendor, type VendorQuota } from '@agflow/core';
import type {
  AgentEvent,
  AgentLaunch,
  AgentSession,
  ExitInfo,
  PreflightResult,
  TerminalTool,
  VendorAdapter,
} from '@agflow/runner';

/** The agent program; it runs with the Bun that runs the tests. */
export const FAKE_AGENT_PATH = join(import.meta.dir, 'fake-agent.ts');

/** One step of a turn. Every step but text, sleep, log and exit is a tool call. */
export type FakeStep =
  /** Writes a file under the clone, or deletes it (null). */
  | { do: 'write'; path: string; content: string | null }
  /** `git add -A` and `git commit` in the clone, with the agent's environment and so its git identity. */
  | { do: 'commit'; message: string }
  /**
   * A shell command run in its own process group in the clone, as a vendor CLI runs its tools. wait false reports
   * the tool done at once and leaves the command running, even after the agent exits. inheritPipes gives the command
   * the agent's stdout and stderr, so it keeps them open after the agent exits, as an escaped grandchild does.
   */
  | { do: 'tool'; command: string; wait?: boolean; inheritPipes?: boolean }
  /** A bridge tool that ends or hands over the work; the answer is scripted: ok by default. */
  | { do: 'terminal'; tool: TerminalTool; answer?: 'ok' | 'refused' | 'hub_unreachable' }
  | { do: 'text'; text: string }
  /** Interrupt cuts it short. */
  | { do: 'sleep'; ms: number }
  /** A line on stderr, which the adapter drains into the attempt log. */
  | { do: 'log'; text: string }
  /** Ends the process at once with this code. */
  | { do: 'exit'; code: number };

export interface FakeScript {
  /**
   * The turns in order: the first prompt starts the first, and each later input taken while idle starts the next.
   * Inputs that arrive mid-turn are taken at the next step boundary, as Claude folds them in. A turn past the end
   * of the list has no steps.
   */
  turns: FakeStep[][];
  /** Keep running the current turn when stdin ends mid-turn, and exit after it (Claude); by default EOF ends it. */
  ignoreEofMidTurn?: boolean;
  /** An interrupt neither ends the turn nor cuts its running step short; cancelQueued still drops queued inputs. */
  ignoreInterrupt?: boolean;
  /** SIGTERM is ignored; by default the agent exits 143 on it, as a SIGTERMed claude does. */
  ignoreSigterm?: boolean;
  /** Reported in started; 'acceptEdits' by default. */
  permissionMode?: string | null;
}

/** What the adapter hands the agent, in a file its one argument names. */
export interface FakeAgentConfig {
  script: FakeScript;
  sessionRef: string;
  model: string;
  cliVersion: string;
  /** null on a resume: the agent waits for a message. */
  firstPrompt: string | null;
}

/** A line on the agent's stdin. */
export type FakeAgentInput =
  | { t: 'message'; id: string; text: string; authority: 'person' | 'agent' | 'system' }
  | { t: 'interrupt'; cancelQueued: boolean };

export interface FakeAdapterOptions {
  /** 'claude' by default. */
  vendor?: Vendor;
  /** The version preflight reports; '0.0.0-fake' by default. */
  cliVersion?: string;
  /** What preflight reports over the defaults: ready, no problem, no account, no owner install. */
  facts?: Partial<Omit<PreflightResult['facts'], 'vendor' | 'cliVersion'>>;
  quota?: VendorQuota | null;
  /** Section 15.1: ready, problem and plan 'test mode', TEST_ACCOUNT_ID. */
  skipAuthChecks?: boolean;
  /** One script for every launch, or one per launch. */
  script: FakeScript | ((launch: AgentLaunch) => FakeScript);
}

export class FakeAdapter implements VendorAdapter {
  readonly vendor: Vendor;
  /** Every launch started, in order. */
  readonly launches: AgentLaunch[] = [];

  constructor(private readonly options: FakeAdapterOptions) {
    this.vendor = options.vendor ?? 'claude';
  }

  async preflight(): Promise<PreflightResult> {
    const base = {
      vendor: this.vendor,
      cliVersion: this.options.cliVersion ?? '0.0.0-fake',
      ownerCliVersion: null,
      ready: true,
      problem: null,
      accountId: null,
      plan: null,
      managedPolicy: false,
      ...this.options.facts,
    };
    const facts = this.options.skipAuthChecks
      ? { ...base, ready: true, problem: 'test mode', plan: 'test mode', accountId: TEST_ACCOUNT_ID }
      : base;
    return { facts, quota: this.options.quota ?? null, weakened: [] };
  }

  async start(launch: AgentLaunch): Promise<AgentSession> {
    const script = typeof this.options.script === 'function' ? this.options.script(launch) : this.options.script;
    const config: FakeAgentConfig = {
      script,
      sessionRef: launch.resume?.sessionRef ?? randomUUID(),
      model: launch.model,
      cliVersion: launch.cliVersion,
      firstPrompt: launch.resume ? null : launch.firstPrompt,
    };
    // The config travels in a file: a large script would pass the argument size limit (1 MiB on macOS).
    const configDir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'agflow-fake-agent-'));
    const configFile = join(configDir, 'config.json');
    await writeFile(configFile, JSON.stringify(config));
    // Bun would otherwise load a .env file and a bunfig.toml from the clone, so the repository's content would
    // change the agent's environment or run code in it before the script starts.
    const argv = [process.execPath, '--no-env-file', '--config=/dev/null', FAKE_AGENT_PATH, configFile];
    let proc: FakeProcess;
    try {
      proc = Bun.spawn(argv, {
        cwd: launch.clone,
        env: launch.env,
        detached: true,
        stdin: 'pipe',
        stdout: 'pipe',
        stderr: 'pipe',
      });
    } catch (error) {
      await rm(configDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
      throw error;
    }
    try {
      launch.registerProcess(proc.pid);
    } catch (error) {
      // Unregistered, nothing could ever stop it: it must not go on playing its script in the clone.
      try {
        process.kill(-proc.pid, 'SIGKILL');
      } catch {
        // Already gone.
      }
      await proc.exited;
      await rm(configDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
      throw error;
    }
    this.launches.push(launch);
    const removeConfig = () => rm(configDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
    return new FakeSession(proc, config.sessionRef, launch.logFile, removeConfig);
  }

  async readTranscriptTail(_input: { sessionRef: string; clone: string; maxChars: number }): Promise<string | null> {
    return null;
  }

  async deleteTranscript(_input: { sessionRef: string; clone: string }): Promise<void> {}
}

/** A single-consumer queue that an async iterator drains. */
class EventQueue implements AsyncIterable<AgentEvent> {
  private readonly items: AgentEvent[] = [];
  private waiting: ((result: IteratorResult<AgentEvent>) => void) | null = null;
  private ended = false;

  push(event: AgentEvent): void {
    const waiting = this.waiting;
    this.waiting = null;
    if (waiting) waiting({ value: event, done: false });
    else this.items.push(event);
  }

  end(): void {
    this.ended = true;
    const waiting = this.waiting;
    this.waiting = null;
    waiting?.({ value: undefined, done: true });
  }

  [Symbol.asyncIterator](): AsyncIterator<AgentEvent> {
    return {
      next: () => {
        const item = this.items.shift();
        if (item) return Promise.resolve({ value: item, done: false });
        if (this.ended) return Promise.resolve({ value: undefined, done: true });
        return new Promise((resolve) => {
          this.waiting = resolve;
        });
      },
    };
  }
}

type FakeProcess = Bun.Subprocess<'pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'>;

class FakeSession implements AgentSession {
  readonly pid: number;
  readonly events: EventQueue = new EventQueue();
  readonly exited: Promise<ExitInfo>;

  constructor(
    private readonly proc: FakeProcess,
    readonly sessionRef: string,
    logFile: string,
    cleanup: () => Promise<void>,
  ) {
    this.pid = proc.pid;
    this.exited = proc.exited.then(async () => {
      await cleanup();
      return { code: proc.exitCode, signal: proc.signalCode ?? null };
    });
    // Both pipes are read at once and to their end, whoever iterates the events, so the agent never blocks on them.
    void this.readEvents();
    void this.drainStderr(logFile);
  }

  async send(message: { id: string; text: string; authority: 'person' | 'agent' | 'system' }): Promise<void> {
    await this.write({ t: 'message', ...message });
  }

  async interrupt(options: { cancelQueued?: boolean } = {}): Promise<void> {
    await this.write({ t: 'interrupt', cancelQueued: options.cancelQueued ?? false });
  }

  async answerApproval(
    _approvalId: string,
    _decision: 'approve' | 'decline',
    _reason: string | null,
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    return false;
  }

  async close(): Promise<void> {
    try {
      await this.proc.stdin.end();
    } catch {
      // Already closed, or the agent is gone: either way its input has ended.
    }
  }

  private async write(input: FakeAgentInput): Promise<void> {
    if (this.proc.exitCode !== null || this.proc.signalCode !== null) throw new Error('the fake agent has exited');
    this.proc.stdin.write(`${JSON.stringify(input)}\n`);
    await this.proc.stdin.flush();
  }

  private async readEvents(): Promise<void> {
    const decoder = new TextDecoder();
    let buffered = '';
    const take = (line: string) => {
      if (line.trim() === '') return;
      try {
        this.events.push(JSON.parse(line) as AgentEvent);
      } catch {
        this.events.push({ type: 'warning', text: `unreadable fake agent output: ${line.slice(0, 200)}` });
      }
    };
    try {
      for await (const chunk of this.proc.stdout) {
        buffered += decoder.decode(chunk, { stream: true });
        const lines = buffered.split('\n');
        buffered = lines.pop() ?? '';
        for (const line of lines) take(line);
      }
      take(buffered + decoder.decode());
    } finally {
      this.events.end();
    }
  }

  private async drainStderr(logFile: string): Promise<void> {
    await mkdir(dirname(logFile), { recursive: true });
    for await (const chunk of this.proc.stderr) await appendFile(logFile, chunk);
  }
}
```

```ts
// The fake agent: the process FakeAdapter starts, in its own group with the agent environment and the clone as its
// cwd. It reads its FakeAgentConfig from the file its one argument names, plays its script (FakeScript) one turn per
// input, writes AgentEvents to stdout as JSON lines and reads FakeAgentInputs from stdin. Its tools are real: files,
// git with the agent's own environment, and shell commands in process groups of their own.
import { mkdirSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync, writeSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import type { AgentEvent, TerminalTool } from '@agflow/runner';
import type { FakeAgentConfig, FakeAgentInput, FakeStep } from './fake-adapter';

const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2] ?? '', 'utf8')) as FakeAgentConfig;
const { script } = config;

// A SIGTERMed claude exits 143, not by signal (design 7.4); a script may ignore the signal instead.
process.on('SIGTERM', () => {
  if (!script.ignoreSigterm) process.exit(143);
});

/** The bridge tool behind each terminal kind. */
const TERMINAL_TOOLS: Record<TerminalTool, string> = {
  submit: 'submit',
  blocked: 'declare_blocked',
  impossible: 'declare_impossible',
  released: 'release_task',
  handoff: 'write_handoff',
};

// Synchronous writes, so nothing is lost when a step exits the process right after.
function emit(event: AgentEvent): void {
  writeSync(1, `${JSON.stringify(event)}\n`);
}

interface Input {
  /** null for the first prompt, which the hub never sent. */
  id: string | null;
  text: string;
}

const queue: Input[] = [];
let stdinClosed = false;
let inTurn = false;
let interrupted = false;
/** Wakes the idle loop. */
let wake: (() => void) | null = null;
/** Cuts the running sleep or tool wait short. */
let abortStep: (() => void) | null = null;

function notify(): void {
  const waiting = wake;
  wake = null;
  waiting?.();
}

function receive(input: FakeAgentInput): void {
  if (input.t === 'message') {
    queue.push({ id: input.id, text: input.text });
    notify();
    return;
  }
  if (input.cancelQueued) queue.length = 0;
  if (inTurn && !script.ignoreInterrupt) {
    interrupted = true;
    abortStep?.();
  }
}

async function readStdin(): Promise<void> {
  const decoder = new TextDecoder();
  let buffered = '';
  for await (const chunk of Bun.stdin.stream()) {
    buffered += decoder.decode(chunk, { stream: true });
    const lines = buffered.split('\n');
    buffered = lines.pop() ?? '';
    for (const line of lines) {
      if (line.trim() !== '') receive(JSON.parse(line) as FakeAgentInput);
    }
  }
  stdinClosed = true;
  // Mid-turn EOF ends the process unless the script carries on like Claude; an idle agent ends in the loop.
  if (inTurn && !script.ignoreEofMidTurn) process.exit(0);
  notify();
}

/** The next input, or null once stdin has ended. */
async function nextInput(): Promise<Input | null> {
  for (;;) {
    const input = queue.shift();
    if (input) return input;
    if (stdinClosed) return null;
    await new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
      wake = resolve;
    });
  }
}

/** Waits for the promise, or gives onAbort at once when the turn is interrupted. */
function interruptible<T>(promise: Promise<T>, onAbort: T): Promise<T> {
  return new Promise<T>((resolve) => {
    abortStep = () => resolve(onAbort);
    promise.then(resolve);
  }).finally(() => {
    abortStep = null;
  });
}

let toolCount = 0;

async function tool(name: string, input: string, command: string | null, run: () => Promise<boolean>) {
  toolCount += 1;
  const toolId = `toolu_${toolCount}`;
  emit({ type: 'tool_started', toolId, name, input, command });
  const ok = await run();
  emit({ type: 'tool_ended', toolId, ok, denied: false, terminal: null, hubUnreachable: false });
}

async function exitsZero(argv: string[]): Promise<boolean> {
  const proc = Bun.spawn(argv, { stdin: 'ignore', stdout: 'ignore', stderr: 'ignore' });
  return (await proc.exited) === 0;
}

function quote(text: string): string {
  return `'${text.replace(/'/g, `'\\''`)}'`;
}

/** Runs one step; gives whether it was a tool call. */
async function runStep(step: FakeStep): Promise<boolean> {
  switch (step.do) {
    case 'write':
      await tool('Write', step.path, null, async () => {
        const target = join(process.cwd(), step.path);
        if (step.content === null) {
          rmSync(target, { force: true });
        } else {
          mkdirSync(dirname(target), { recursive: true });
          writeFileSync(target, step.content);
        }
        return true;
      });
      return true;
    case 'commit': {
      const command = `git add -A && git commit -q -m ${quote(step.message)}`;
      await tool('Bash', command, command, async () => {
        return (await exitsZero(['git', 'add', '-A'])) && exitsZero(['git', 'commit', '-q', '-m', step.message]);
      });
      return true;
    }
    case 'tool':
      await tool('Bash', step.command, step.command, async () => {
        // A group of its own, as vendor CLIs run their tools. One that inherits the agent's pipes holds them open
        // after the agent exits, as an escaped grandchild would.
        const output = step.inheritPipes ? 'inherit' : 'ignore';
        const child = Bun.spawn(['sh', '-c', step.command], {
          detached: true,
          stdin: 'ignore',
          stdout: output,
          stderr: output,
        });
        if (step.wait === false) {
          child.unref();
          return true;
        }
        return (await interruptible(child.exited, -1)) === 0;
      });
      return true;
    case 'terminal': {
      toolCount += 1;
      const toolId = `toolu_${toolCount}`;
      const answer = step.answer ?? 'ok';
      const name = `mcp__agflow__${TERMINAL_TOOLS[step.tool]}`;
      emit({ type: 'tool_started', toolId, name, input: '{}', command: null });
      emit({
        type: 'tool_ended',
        toolId,
        ok: answer === 'ok',
        denied: false,
        // Counted only on a normal result (design 10).
        terminal: answer === 'ok' ? step.tool : null,
        hubUnreachable: answer === 'hub_unreachable',
      });
      return true;
    }
    case 'text':
      emit({ type: 'text', text: step.text });
      return false;
    case 'sleep':
      await interruptible(Bun.sleep(step.ms), undefined);
      return false;
    case 'log':
      writeSync(2, `${step.text}\n`);
      return false;
    case 'exit':
      process.exit(step.code);
  }
}

let turnIndex = 0;

async function runTurn(first: Input): Promise<void> {
  inTurn = true;
  interrupted = false;
  const taken: string[] = [];
  const take = (input: Input) => {
    if (input.id === null) return;
    taken.push(input.id);
    emit({ type: 'delivered', id: input.id });
  };
  take(first);
  emit({ type: 'turn_started' });
  let toolCalls = 0;
  for (const step of script.turns[turnIndex] ?? []) {
    if (interrupted) break;
    for (let input = queue.shift(); input; input = queue.shift()) take(input);
    if (await runStep(step)) toolCalls += 1;
  }
  turnIndex += 1;
  emit({
    type: 'turn_ended',
    outcome: interrupted ? 'interrupted' : 'completed',
    toolCalls,
    error: null,
    errorKind: null,
  });
  for (const id of taken) emit({ type: 'acknowledged', id });
  inTurn = false;
  interrupted = false;
}

emit({
  type: 'started',
  sessionRef: config.sessionRef,
  model: config.model,
  cliVersion: config.cliVersion,
  permissionMode: script.permissionMode === undefined ? 'acceptEdits' : script.permissionMode,
});
if (config.firstPrompt !== null) queue.push({ id: null, text: config.firstPrompt });
void readStdin();
for (let input = await nextInput(); input; input = stdinClosed ? null : await nextInput()) {
  await runTurn(input);
}
process.exit(0);
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run the tests and see them pass**

Run: `bun test packages/testkit/test/fake-adapter.test.ts && bun test && bun run typecheck`
Expected: the task's tests pass; then the whole suite passes (`0 fail`) and `tsc` exits 0.

The fake agent runs Bun with `--config=/dev/null` and reads its script from a file in a fresh temporary directory, so a clone's `bunfig.toml` preload or `.env` never runs. SIGTERM exits 143 by default; `ignoreSigterm`, `ignoreInterrupt` and a tool's `inheritPipes` let the stop-ladder tests play stubborn agents. If `registerProcess` throws, the group gets SIGKILL and `start` rethrows; an adapter registers exactly one process per launch (X-50).

### Task 13: Attempt clones: task clones, lead clones and the lead fast-forward

Each attempt gets a standalone `git clone --shared --no-checkout` of the vault in `work/<project>/<attempt>` (design 7.3, 6.11), made with the local environment before the agent gets it: the task branch at the resolved start commit, origin pointing at the vault so the agent's fetches stay on the laptop, `.agflow/run/` excluded, and the start pin written. Lead clones are detached at main with no task branch. After hand-over the runner never runs git with the clone's `.git`: the clean check and the lead fast-forward go through the vault with `--work-tree` and a temporary index, and HEAD and refs are read as plain files.

```ts
describe('fastForwardLeadClone and HEAD', () => {
  const forward = (s: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof setup>>, clone: string) =>
    fastForwardLeadClone({ vault: s.vault, local: s.local, attemptId: 'lead-a1', clone });

  test('leaves a clone whose HEAD names a branch of the lead\'s own', async () => {
    const s = await setup();
    const { clone } = await leadClone(s);
    await commitFiles(s.repo.path, { branch: 'main', files: { 'src/app.ts': 'app v2\n' } });
    await s.fetch({ ref: 'refs/heads/main', sha: null });
    await gitIn(clone, ['switch', '--quiet', '-c', 'lead-notes']);
    expect(await forward(s, clone)).toEqual({ moved: false, reason: 'not_fast_forward', sha: s.repo.mainSha });
    expect(readFileSync(join(clone, '.git', 'HEAD'), 'utf8')).toBe('ref: refs/heads/lead-notes\n');
    expect(readFileSync(join(clone, 'src', 'app.ts'), 'utf8')).toBe('app\n');
  });

  test('leaves a clone detached at a commit the vault holds when main no longer descends from it', async () => {
    const s = await setup();
    const { clone } = await leadClone(s);
    const newer = await commitFiles(s.repo.path, { branch: 'main', files: { 'src/app.ts': 'app v2\n' } });
    await s.fetch({ ref: 'refs/heads/main', sha: null });
    expect((await forward(s, clone)).moved).toBe(true);
    // Origin's main is rewound to a sibling of the commit the clone is at.
    const sibling = await commitFiles(s.repo.path, {
      branch: 'sibling',
      from: s.repo.mainSha,
      files: { 'other.txt': 'other\n' },
    });
    await gitIn(s.repo.path, ['update-ref', 'refs/heads/main', sibling]);
    await s.fetch({ ref: 'refs/heads/main', sha: null });
    expect(await forward(s, clone)).toEqual({ moved: false, reason: 'not_fast_forward', sha: newer });
    expect(readFileSync(join(clone, '.git', 'HEAD'), 'utf8').trim()).toBe(newer);
  });

  test('finishes a move cut short after the files changed, before .git/HEAD and .git/index were written', async () => {
    const s = await setup();
    const { clone } = await leadClone(s);
    const newer = await commitFiles(s.repo.path, { branch: 'main', files: { 'src/app.ts': 'app v2\n' } });
    await s.fetch({ ref: 'refs/heads/main', sha: null });
    // The runner's own move, through the vault and a temporary index, as a crash right after it leaves it.
    const index = join(tempDir('agflow-index-'), 'index');
    const git = (args: string[]) =>
      runGit(s.local, [`--git-dir=${s.vault.path}`, `--work-tree=${clone}`, ...args], {
        cwd: clone,
        env: { GIT_INDEX_FILE: index },
      });
    await git(['read-tree', s.repo.mainSha]);
    await git(['update-index', '-q', '--refresh']);
    await git(['read-tree', '-m', '-u', s.repo.mainSha, newer]);
    expect(readFileSync(join(clone, 'src', 'app.ts'), 'utf8')).toBe('app v2\n');
    expect(readFileSync(join(clone, '.git', 'HEAD'), 'utf8').trim()).toBe(s.repo.mainSha);
    expect(await forward(s, clone)).toEqual({ moved: true, from: s.repo.mainSha, to: newer });
    expect(readFileSync(join(clone, '.git', 'HEAD'), 'utf8').trim()).toBe(newer);
    expect(await gitIn(clone, ['status', '--porcelain', '--untracked-files=all'])).toBe('');
    expect(await s.git(['rev-parse', localPinRefs('lead-a1').start])).toBe(newer);
  });
});

  });

    const path = join(tempDir('agflow-growing-'), 'HEAD');
    writeFileSync(path, 'abc\n');

    try {
      const { size } = await handle.stat();
      appendFileSync(path, 'x'.repeat(64 * 1024));
      await expect(readSized(handle, size, path)).rejects.toThrow(/changed while it was read/);
      expect(await readSized(handle, size + 64 * 1024, path)).toHaveLength(size + 64 * 1024);
    } finally {
      await handle.close();
    }
  });

  test('a link planted at .git/index is replaced, not written through', async () => {
    const s = await setup();
    const { clone } = await leadClone(s);
    const outside = join(tempDir('agflow-outside-'), 'precious');
    writeFileSync(outside, 'precious\n');
    rmSync(join(clone, '.git', 'index'));
    symlinkSync(outside, join(clone, '.git', 'index'));

    expect(result.moved).toBe(true);
    expect(readFileSync(outside, 'utf8')).toBe('precious\n');
    expect(lstatSync(join(clone, '.git', 'index')).isFile()).toBe(true);
    expect(await gitIn(clone, ['status', '--porcelain', '--untracked-files=all'])).toBe('');
  });
});
```

**File:** `packages/runner/test/planted-config.ts` (new)

```ts
// Planted git configuration for the tests of runner operations on an agent's clone (design 7.3). The plants are
// keys the local environment does not pin, so they stay silent only if the runner never runs git with the clone's
// own .git: a filter driver that the repository's committed .gitattributes names (PLANTED_ATTRIBUTES) and only the
// clone's .git/config defines. The pinned keys (core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath) are planted as well.
//
// Every planted program is a shell command, which git runs through sh: macOS checks each newly written executable
// on its first run, which takes about a second under load, so fresh scripts would make these tests slow and flaky.
// The hooks directory does hold fresh scripts, but they only run if the runner is wrong.
import { chmodSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, utimesSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { gitIn } from '@agflow/testkit';

/** A .gitattributes for the clone's repository: every file goes through the planted filter. */
export const PLANTED_ATTRIBUTES = '* filter=planted\n';

export interface PlantedConfig {
  /** Every planted program appends a line to it. */
  marker: string;
  /** Whether any planted program has run. */
  fired(): boolean;
  /**
   * Proves the plants live: git run in the clone fires the fsmonitor and the filter's clean command. file is a
   * tracked file of the clone.
   */
  proveLive(file: string): Promise<void>;
}

/** Shell-quoted, for a command git runs through sh. */
function quoted(path: string): string {
  return `'${path.replace(/'/g, `'\\''`)}'`;
}

/** A config value in double quotes, as git's config syntax reads it. */
function configString(value: string): string {
  return `"${value.replace(/\\/g, '\\\\').replace(/"/g, '\\"')}"`;
}

/**
 * Plants program-valued keys in the clone's .git/config: the filter driver, an fsmonitor command and a hooks
 * directory. dir is a runner-unrelated directory for the marker and the hooks.
 */
export function plantCloneConfig(clone: string, dir: string): PlantedConfig {
  const marker = join(dir, 'fired');
  const record = (what: string) => configString(`echo ${what} >> ${quoted(marker)}`);
  const hooks = join(dir, 'hooks');
  mkdirSync(hooks, { recursive: true });
  for (const hook of ['pre-commit', 'post-checkout', 'post-index-change', 'reference-transaction', 'post-merge']) {
    writeFileSync(join(hooks, hook), `#!/bin/sh\necho ${hook} >> ${quoted(marker)}\n`);
    chmodSync(join(hooks, hook), 0o755);
  }
  const config = join(clone, '.git', 'config');
  writeFileSync(
    config,
    [
      readFileSync(config, 'utf8').trimEnd(),
      '[core]',
      `\tfsmonitor = ${record('fsmonitor')}`,
      `\thooksPath = ${configString(hooks)}`,
      '[filter "planted"]',
      `\tclean = ${configString(`cat; echo clean >> ${quoted(marker)}`)}`,
      `\tsmudge = ${configString(`cat; echo smudge >> ${quoted(marker)}`)}`,
      '',
    ].join('\n'),
  );
  return {
    marker,
    fired: () => existsSync(marker),
    async proveLive(file: string) {
      // No optional locks: status then writes no index, so no fresh hook script runs.
      await gitIn(clone, ['--no-optional-locks', 'status']);
      await gitIn(clone, ['hash-object', file]);
      const lines = readFileSync(marker, 'utf8');
      if (!lines.includes('fsmonitor') || !lines.includes('clean')) {
        throw new Error(`the planted programs did not run: ${JSON.stringify(lines)}`);
      }
    },
  };
}

/** Moves a file's mtime forward, content unchanged, so any refresh of an index must hash it again. */
export function touchLater(path: string): void {
  const later = new Date(Date.now() + 60_000);
  utimesSync(path, later, later);
}
```

```ts
// Attempt clones (design 7.3, 6.11). Each attempt works in a standalone `git clone --shared --no-checkout` of the
// vault: it borrows the vault's objects, and its origin is the vault path, so the agent's fetches never leave the
// laptop. The runner makes the clone with the local environment before hand-over: the task branch checked out at
// the start commit (a lead's clone detached at main), .agflow/run/ excluded from the agent's git, and the start
// pinned in the vault. From hand-over on, the clone and its .git are the agent's and untrusted: the runner reads
// its refs as plain files and works on its files only through the vault, with --work-tree and a temporary index,
// writing .git/HEAD and .git/index back as files.
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { constants, existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { copyFile, type FileHandle, lstat, mkdir, mkdtemp, open, rename, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { basename, dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { type GitEnvironment, gitOk, RUN_DIR_EXCLUDE, runGit } from './run';
import type { Vault } from './vault';

const SHA = /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/;

/** The largest packed-refs file read; an agent can make it any size. */
const PACKED_REFS_MAX_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024;

export interface CloneTarget {
  vault: Vault;
  /** The local environment, localGitEnv(paths). */
  local: GitEnvironment;
  attemptId: string;
  /** paths.clone(project, attemptId). */
  clone: string;
}

export interface CloneResult {
  /** false when the clone already existed; it is never recreated. */
  created: boolean;
}

/** HEAD as the clone's files say: the branch it names, if any, and the commit it resolves to, if any. */
export interface CloneHead {
  ref: string | null;
  sha: string | null;
}

export type FastForwardResult =
  | { moved: true; from: string; to: string }
  | {
      moved: false;
      /** dirty: changed or untracked files; not_fast_forward: HEAD names a branch, or main does not descend from it. */
      reason: 'up_to_date' | 'dirty' | 'not_fast_forward';
      sha: string;
    };

/** A clone appears in its place only once it is complete, so its directory existing means it is there. */
export function cloneExists(clone: string): boolean {
  return existsSync(clone);
}

/** A task clone on its branch at the start commit. An existing clone is kept as it is. */
export function createTaskClone(target: CloneTarget & { branch: string; startSha: string }): Promise<CloneResult> {
  return create(target, target.startSha, ['--no-track', '-B', target.branch, target.startSha]);
}

/** A lead's clone, detached at main (startSha), with no task branch. An existing clone is kept as it is. */
export function createLeadClone(target: CloneTarget & { startSha: string }): Promise<CloneResult> {
  return create(target, target.startSha, ['--detach', target.startSha]);
}

async function create(target: CloneTarget, startSha: string, checkout: string[]): Promise<CloneResult> {
  const { vault, local, clone, attemptId } = target;
  if (!SHA.test(startSha)) throw new Error(`not a commit sha: ${JSON.stringify(startSha)}`);
  if (cloneExists(clone)) return { created: false };
  // Built beside its place and renamed into it, so a runner that dies halfway leaves no clone that looks complete.
  const building = join(dirname(clone), `.${basename(clone)}.creating`);
  await rm(building, { recursive: true, force: true });
  await mkdir(dirname(clone), { recursive: true });
  try {
    // No template: the clone gets no sample hooks and no info/ of git's own.
    await runGit(local, ['clone', '--quiet', '--shared', '--no-checkout', '--template=', vault.path, building]);
    const self = [`--git-dir=${join(building, '.git')}`, `--work-tree=${building}`];
    await runGit(local, [...self, 'checkout', '--quiet', ...checkout], { cwd: building });
    await mkdir(join(building, '.git', 'info'), { recursive: true });
    await writeFile(join(building, '.git', 'info', 'exclude'), '# Written by the agflow runner.\n/.agflow/run/\n');
    await vault.pin(attemptId, { start: startSha });
    await rename(building, clone);
  } catch (error) {
    await rm(building, { recursive: true, force: true });
    throw error;
  }
  return { created: true };
}

/** The clone's .git, which must be a real directory: a .git file or link could point the runner anywhere. */
async function gitDirOf(clone: string): Promise<string> {
  const gitDir = join(clone, '.git');
  const stat = await lstat(gitDir);
  if (!stat.isDirectory()) throw new Error(`${gitDir} is not a directory`);
  return gitDir;
}

/**
 * Reads an open file whose fstat gave size, refusing it when more arrives: the agent may append to a file while the
 * runner reads it, and reading to the end would let it pass any limit.
 */
export async function readSized(handle: FileHandle, size: number, path: string): Promise<string> {
  const buffer = Buffer.alloc(size + 1);
  let length = 0;
  while (length < buffer.length) {
    const { bytesRead } = await handle.read(buffer, length, buffer.length - length, length);
    if (bytesRead === 0) break;
    length += bytesRead;
  }
  if (length > size) throw new Error(`${path} changed while it was read`);
  return buffer.toString('utf8', 0, length);
}

/**
 * Reads a file under the clone's .git without following a symlink anywhere on the way. Gives null when it does not
 * exist.
 */
async function readGitFile(clone: string, relative: string, maxBytes: number): Promise<string | null> {
  let path = await gitDirOf(clone);
  const parts = relative.split('/');
  for (const part of parts.slice(0, -1)) {
    path = join(path, part);
    const stat = await lstat(path).catch(() => null);
    if (stat === null) return null;
    if (!stat.isDirectory()) throw new Error(`${path} is not a directory`);
  }
  path = join(path, parts.at(-1) as string);
  let handle: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof open>>;
  try {
    handle = await open(path, constants.O_RDONLY | constants.O_NOFOLLOW | constants.O_NONBLOCK);
  } catch (error) {
    const code = (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;
    if (code === 'ENOENT' || code === 'ENOTDIR') return null;
    if (code === 'ELOOP') throw new Error(`${path} is a symbolic link`);
    throw error;
  }
  try {
    const stat = await handle.stat();
    if (!stat.isFile()) throw new Error(`${path} is not a regular file`);
    if (stat.size > maxBytes) throw new Error(`${path} is larger than ${maxBytes} bytes`);
    return await readSized(handle, stat.size, path);
  } finally {
    await handle.close();
  }
}

/** A ref name the clone's files may hold: refs/..., with no empty, dot-leading or traversing component. */
function checkRefName(ref: string): void {
  const parts = ref.split('/');
  if (parts[0] !== 'refs' || parts.length < 2 || parts.some((part) => part === '' || part.startsWith('.'))) {
    throw new Error(`not a ref the runner reads: ${JSON.stringify(ref)}`);
  }
}

function commitSha(value: string, where: string): string {
  const sha = value.trim();
  if (!SHA.test(sha)) throw new Error(`${where} is not a commit sha: ${JSON.stringify(value.slice(0, 80))}`);
  return sha;
}

/**
 * The commit a ref of the clone names, read from its loose ref file or else from packed-refs, as plain files. Only
 * 40 hex is accepted, never a symbolic value. Gives null when the clone has no such ref.
 */
export async function readCloneRef(clone: string, ref: string): Promise<string | null> {
  checkRefName(ref);
  const loose = await readGitFile(clone, ref, 4096);
  if (loose !== null) return commitSha(loose, ref);
  const packed = await readGitFile(clone, 'packed-refs', PACKED_REFS_MAX_BYTES);
  if (packed === null) return null;
  for (const line of packed.split('\n')) {
    if (line.startsWith('#') || line.startsWith('^')) continue;
    const space = line.indexOf(' ');
    if (space > 0 && line.slice(space + 1).trimEnd() === ref) {
      return commitSha(line.slice(0, space), `${ref} in packed-refs`);
    }
  }
  return null;
}

/** The clone's HEAD, read as a file: a commit sha (detached), or `ref: <branch>` resolved through readCloneRef. */
export async function readCloneHead(clone: string): Promise<CloneHead> {
  const head = await readGitFile(clone, 'HEAD', 4096);
  if (head === null) throw new Error(`${clone} has no .git/HEAD`);
  const text = head.trim();
  if (text.startsWith('ref:')) {
    const ref = text.slice(4).trim();
    return { ref, sha: await readCloneRef(clone, ref) };
  }
  return { ref: null, sha: commitSha(text, 'HEAD') };
}

/** Runs fn with the path of a runner-owned temporary index, removed afterwards. */
async function withTempIndex<T>(fn: (index: string) => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  const dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'agflow-index-'));
  try {
    return await fn(join(dir, 'index'));
  } finally {
    await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

/** Local git on the vault, with the clone as its work tree and the temporary index. */
function worktreeGit(input: { vault: Vault; local: GitEnvironment; clone: string }, index: string) {
  return (args: string[]) =>
    runGit(input.local, [`--git-dir=${input.vault.path}`, `--work-tree=${input.clone}`, ...args], {
      cwd: input.clone,
      env: { GIT_INDEX_FILE: index },
      check: false,
    });
}

/**
 * Whether the work tree matches the commit the index was read from: no changed or deleted tracked file, and no
 * untracked file outside the ignore rules and the runner's exclusions.
 */
async function matchesIndex(git: ReturnType<typeof worktreeGit>): Promise<boolean> {
  // refresh records the files' stat data, hashing only what changed, and writes no object.
  if ((await git(['update-index', '-q', '--refresh'])).code !== 0) return false;
  // A gitlink is compared with the nested HEAD, read as a file: looking for changes inside the nested repository
  // would start git there, with that repository's config, which the agent wrote (its filter drivers, say). The flag
  // also overrides any submodule.<name>.ignore in an agent-written .gitmodules.
  if ((await git(['diff-files', '--quiet', '--ignore-submodules=dirty'])).code !== 0) return false;
  const untracked = await git(['ls-files', '-z', '--others', '--exclude-standard', '--', ':(top)', RUN_DIR_EXCLUDE]);
  return untracked.code === 0 && untracked.stdout === '';
}

/** Reads the commit into the temporary index and compares the work tree with it. */
async function matchesCommit(git: ReturnType<typeof worktreeGit>, sha: string): Promise<boolean> {
  return (await git(['read-tree', sha])).code === 0 && matchesIndex(git);
}

/**
 * Whether the clone's files equal its HEAD (read as a file), compared through the vault: no git runs with the
 * clone's .git. A HEAD the vault does not hold (commits not harvested yet) is not clean.
 */
export async function isWorktreeClean(input: { vault: Vault; local: GitEnvironment; clone: string }): Promise<boolean> {
  const head = await readCloneHead(input.clone);
  if (head.sha === null || !(await input.vault.hasCommit(head.sha))) return false;
  const sha = head.sha;
  return withTempIndex((index) => matchesCommit(worktreeGit(input, index), sha));
}

/**
 * Replaces a file in the clone's .git by renaming a new one over it, so a link planted in its place is replaced, not
 * written through. The new file has a random name and is created exclusively, so nothing planted at that name is
 * followed or stands in the way.
 */
async function replaceGitFile(gitDir: string, name: string, write: (path: string) => Promise<void>): Promise<void> {
  const fresh = join(gitDir, `${name}.agflow-${randomUUID()}`);
  try {
    await write(fresh);
    await rename(fresh, join(gitDir, name));
  } catch (error) {
    await rm(fresh, { force: true });
    throw error;
  }
}

/**
 * resume_attempt for a lead (design 7.3): moves a clean clone detached at an older main to the vault's main. The
 * files change through the vault with a two-tree read-tree; .git/index and .git/HEAD are then written as files and
 * the start pin moves along. A dirty clone, or one main does not fast-forward, is left as it is. A move that a crash
 * or a failure cut short after the files changed (files at main, HEAD and index still at the old commit) is
 * finished.
 */
export async function fastForwardLeadClone(target: CloneTarget): Promise<FastForwardResult> {
  const { vault, local, clone, attemptId } = target;
  const head = await readCloneHead(clone);
  if (head.sha === null) throw new Error(`the HEAD of ${clone} names no commit`);
  const from = head.sha;
  const main = (await vault.resolveStart({ ref: `refs/heads/${vault.mainBranch}`, sha: null })).sha;
  if (main === from) return { moved: false, reason: 'up_to_date', sha: from };
  const fastForward =
    head.ref === null &&
    (await vault.hasCommit(from)) &&
    (await gitOk(local, [`--git-dir=${vault.path}`, 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor', from, main]));
  if (!fastForward) return { moved: false, reason: 'not_fast_forward', sha: from };
  return withTempIndex(async (index): Promise<FastForwardResult> => {
    const git = worktreeGit(target, index);
    if (await matchesCommit(git, from)) {
      const moved = await git(['read-tree', '-m', '-u', from, main]);
      if (moved.code !== 0) throw new Error(`cannot move ${clone} to ${main}: ${moved.stderr.trim()}`);
    } else if (!(await matchesCommit(git, main))) {
      return { moved: false, reason: 'dirty', sha: from };
    }
    const gitDir = await gitDirOf(clone);
    await replaceGitFile(gitDir, 'index', (path) => copyFile(index, path, constants.COPYFILE_EXCL));
    await replaceGitFile(gitDir, 'HEAD', (path) => writeFile(path, `${main}\n`, { flag: 'wx' }));
    await vault.pin(attemptId, { start: main });
    return { moved: true, from, to: main };
  });
}
```

### Task 14: Harvest: refs read as files and a verified fetch through a quarantine

The first half of every harvest (design 7.3, steps 1-3) never runs git in the clone. It reads HEAD and the task branch as files (loose refs or packed-refs, 40-hex only), copies only regular loose-object and pack files, at most 200 MB, into a bare quarantine that borrows the vault's objects, and fetches the head into the attempt's head pin with `transfer.fsckObjects=true`, so a malformed object fails the harvest instead of entering the vault. A HEAD that names another branch also brings that tip, with a warning, and a broken clone fails the harvest, not the runner. The quarantine is always deleted.
