```ts
// Protected paths on the runner (design 7.3, X-16). The hub sends each attempt's restore set (AttemptSpec.restore):
// protected-class patterns with the task's exemptions applied. Paths are classified only with core's
// matchesProtectedPattern, case-insensitively, from git's -z output, and never with git pathspecs. Everything works
// through the vault with the local environment: restore checks files out into the clone with a temporary index and
// --work-tree, detection and strip read and build trees in the vault, and no git ever runs with the clone's .git.
// Restore, detection, strip and dependency preparation all use one base, resolveRestoreBase's.
import { lstat, mkdtemp, readdir, realpath, rm } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { basename, dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { type AttemptSpec, localPinRefs, matchesProtectedPattern } from '@agflow/core';
import { type GitEnvironment, RUN_DIR_EXCLUDE, runGit, WORKTREE_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS } from './run';
import { commitTree } from './snapshot';
import type { Vault } from './vault';

/** The vault, and the local environment its commands run with. */
export interface ProtectGit {
  vault: Vault;
  local: GitEnvironment;
}

/** A change between the base and a head to a path the restore set covers. */
export interface ProtectedChange {
  path: string;
  /** added: not in the base (strip removes it); modified or deleted: in the base (strip puts it back). */
  status: 'added' | 'modified' | 'deleted';
}

const SHA = /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/;
const NO_SHA = '0'.repeat(40);

/** The Claude CLI's untracked staging directory, whose contents are never a violation (X-28). */
const CC_WRITES = '.claude/.cc-writes/**';

/** Whether the restore set covers the path. */
function isProtected(path: string, patterns: readonly string[]): boolean {
  // Only paths inside the staging directory are exempt. git tracks no directories, so an entry at
  // .claude/.cc-writes itself is a file or a link planted in its place, and the pattern also covers a file standing
  // in for .claude, which both stay protected.
  const inStaging = path.split('/').filter(Boolean).length >= 3 && matchesProtectedPattern(path, CC_WRITES);
  if (inStaging) return false;
  return patterns.some((pattern) => matchesProtectedPattern(path, pattern));
}

/**
 * What restore never removes: the runner's own .agflow/run/, and the Claude CLI's staging directory while it is a
 * real directory, since a live CLI writes there. An entry above one of them is looked into instead of removed.
 */
const KEPT = ['.agflow/run', '.claude/.cc-writes'] as const;

function vaultGit(git: ProtectGit, args: string[], options: { input?: string; index?: string; check?: boolean } = {}) {
  return runGit(git.local, [`--git-dir=${git.vault.path}`, ...args], {
    input: options.input,
    env: options.index === undefined ? undefined : { GIT_INDEX_FILE: options.index },
    check: options.check,
  });
}

/** Runs fn with the path of a runner-owned temporary index, removed afterwards. */
async function withTempIndex<T>(fn: (index: string) => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  const dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'agflow-protect-'));
  try {
    return await fn(join(dir, 'index'));
  } finally {
    await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

/** Splits -z output into its entries. */
function entries(output: string): string[] {
  return output.split('\0').filter((entry) => entry !== '');
}

/** The best common ancestor of two commits in the vault; null when they share no history. */
export async function mergeBase(git: ProtectGit, a: string, b: string): Promise<string | null> {
  const result = await vaultGit(git, ['merge-base', a, b], { check: false });
  const sha = result.stdout.trim();
  return result.code === 0 && SHA.test(sha) ? sha : null;
}

/** The commit a ref names in the vault, or null. */
async function commitOf(git: ProtectGit, ref: string): Promise<string | null> {
  const result = await vaultGit(git, ['rev-parse', '--verify', '--quiet', `${ref}^{commit}`], { check: false });
  const sha = result.stdout.trim();
  return result.code === 0 && SHA.test(sha) ? sha : null;
}

/**
 * The one base of an attempt's protected paths (X-16): merge-base(restore.base, the start commit), what the branch
 * should contain, with restore.base (refs/heads/<main>) resolved in the vault after the pre-start fetch; the start
 * commit itself when restore.base is null. The start commit is the attempt's start pin, which the clone was made at
 * (and which a lead's fast-forward moves).
 */
export async function resolveRestoreBase(
  vault: Vault,
  spec: Pick<AttemptSpec, 'attemptId' | 'restore'>,
): Promise<string> {
  const git = { vault, local: vault.local };
  const pin = localPinRefs(spec.attemptId).start;
  const start = await commitOf(git, pin);
  if (start === null) throw new Error(`the vault has no start pin for ${spec.attemptId} (${pin})`);
  if (spec.restore.base === null) return start;
  const tip = await commitOf(git, spec.restore.base);
  if (tip === null) throw new Error(`the restore base ${spec.restore.base} is not in the vault`);
  const base = await mergeBase(git, tip, start);
  if (base === null) throw new Error(`${spec.restore.base} and the start ${start} share no history`);
  return base;
}

/**
 * The protected changes from base to head, from `diff --raw -z -M`: content, mode and type changes (a symlink
 * planted at a protected path included), additions, deletions, and both sides of a rename, so a rename out of a
 * protected directory counts as its deletion. Sorted by path.
 */
export async function detectProtected(
  git: ProtectGit,
  input: { base: string; head: string; paths: readonly string[] },
): Promise<ProtectedChange[]> {
  const raw = entries((await vaultGit(git, ['diff-tree', '-r', '-z', '--raw', '-M', input.base, input.head])).stdout);
  const changes = new Map<string, ProtectedChange['status']>();
  const note = (path: string, status: ProtectedChange['status']) => {
    if (isProtected(path, input.paths)) changes.set(path, status);
  };
  for (let i = 0; i < raw.length; i++) {
    // ":<old mode> <new mode> <old sha> <new sha> <status>", then the path, or both paths of a rename or copy.
    const status = (raw[i] ?? '').split(' ')[4] ?? '';
    const path = raw[++i] ?? '';
    if (status.startsWith('R') || status.startsWith('C')) {
      const to = raw[++i] ?? '';
      if (status.startsWith('R')) note(path, 'deleted');
      note(to, 'added');
    } else if (status === 'A') {
      note(path, 'added');
    } else if (status === 'D') {
      note(path, 'deleted');
    } else {
      note(path, 'modified');
    }
  }
  return [...changes]
    .map(([path, status]) => ({ path, status }))
    .sort((a, b) => (a.path < b.path ? -1 : a.path > b.path ? 1 : 0));
}

/**
 * Removes the shell's last argument from its working directory, once that directory is known to lie inside the
 * clone (the first argument, its real path). The working directory is pinned when the shell starts, and rm never
 * follows a link below it, so a parent swapped for a link at any moment redirects nothing.
 */
const REMOVE_SCRIPT = 'case "$(pwd -P)/" in "$1"/*) exec /bin/rm -rf -- "./$2";; *) exit 3;; esac';

/**
 * Removes a path in the clone, never through a link: the removal runs in the path's parent directory, which must
 * still be inside the clone when it does. Gives false when there is nothing to remove; throws when it cannot.
 */
export async function removeInClone(root: string, clone: string, path: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const target = join(clone, path);
  if ((await lstat(target).catch(() => null)) === null) return false;
  let code: number;
  try {
    const proc = Bun.spawn(['/bin/sh', '-c', REMOVE_SCRIPT, 'sh', root, basename(target)], {
      cwd: dirname(target),
      env: { PATH: '/usr/bin:/bin' },
      stdin: 'ignore',
      stdout: 'ignore',
      stderr: 'ignore',
    });
    code = await proc.exited;
  } catch (error) {
    throw new Error(`cannot remove ${path} from the clone: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : error}`);
  }
  if (code === 3) throw new Error(`${path} is no longer inside the clone`);
  if (code !== 0) throw new Error(`cannot remove ${path} from the clone (exit ${code})`);
  return true;
}

/**
 * Removes a protected entry git listed as untracked, keeping what KEPT names: an entry above a kept path is looked
 * into, and each protected entry in it removed, so a wholly untracked .claude/ or .agflow/ (an embedded repository,
 * or an ignored directory git lists as one entry) loses everything but the kept path. Adds what it removed.
 */
async function removeEntry(
  target: { root: string; clone: string; paths: readonly string[] },
  path: string,
  removed: string[],
): Promise<void> {
  const folded = path.toLowerCase();
  const kept = KEPT.find((keep) => keep === folded || keep.startsWith(`${folded}/`));
  if (kept !== undefined) {
    const stat = await lstat(join(target.clone, path)).catch(() => null);
    // A file or link where a directory belongs is removed whole; .agflow/run is the runner's, whatever it is.
    if (stat !== null && (stat.isDirectory() || folded === '.agflow/run')) {
      if (kept === folded) return;
      for (const name of await readdir(join(target.clone, path))) {
        await removeEntry(target, `${path}/${name}`, removed);
      }
      return;
    }
  }
  if (!isProtected(path, target.paths)) return;
  if (await removeInClone(target.root, target.clone, path)) removed.push(path);
}

/**
 * Restore (design 7.3), before every start, resume, dependency preparation and take-over: the clone's files under
 * the restore set become the base's. Base files that differ or are missing are checked out from the base through
 * the vault and a temporary index; files there that the base lacks are deleted, whether added by the branch or
 * untracked, and ignored ones too, since the agent writes the ignore rules. A wholly ignored directory (node_modules)
 * is one entry, which no pattern covers. Other work is left as it is, and the clone's .git is never touched. Every
 * git that reads the work tree is bounded (WORKTREE_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS): a restore that cannot finish fails.
 */
export async function restoreProtected(
  git: ProtectGit,
  input: { clone: string; base: string; paths: readonly string[]; timeoutMs?: number },
): Promise<{ restored: string[]; removed: string[] }> {
  const { clone } = input;
  const root = await realpath(clone);
  return withTempIndex(async (index) => {
    const tree = (args: string[], options: { input?: string; check?: boolean } = {}) =>
      runGit(git.local, [`--git-dir=${git.vault.path}`, `--work-tree=${clone}`, ...args], {
        cwd: clone,
        env: { GIT_INDEX_FILE: index },
        timeoutMs: input.timeoutMs ?? WORKTREE_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS,
        ...options,
      });
    const scope = ['--', ':(top)', RUN_DIR_EXCLUDE];
    await tree(['read-tree', input.base]);
    // Records the files' stat data, so diff-files lists only real changes; it fails when a file differs.
    await tree(['update-index', '-q', '--refresh'], { check: false });
    const diff = await tree(['diff-files', '-z', '--name-only', '--ignore-submodules=all', ...scope]);
    const differs = entries(diff.stdout);
    const others = await tree(['ls-files', '-z', '--others', '--exclude-standard', ...scope]);
    const ignored = await tree(['ls-files', '-z', '--others', '--ignored', '--exclude-standard', '--directory', ...scope]);
    const restored = differs.filter((path) => isProtected(path, input.paths)).sort();
    // A directory listed as one entry ends in a slash: one holding its own repository, or a wholly ignored one.
    const untracked = new Set([...entries(others.stdout), ...entries(ignored.stdout)].map((p) => p.replace(/\/+$/, '')));
    const removed: string[] = [];
    for (const path of [...untracked].sort()) await removeEntry({ root, clone, paths: input.paths }, path, removed);
    if (restored.length > 0) {
      // Git replaces a link or directory in a file's way and never writes through a link.
      await tree(['checkout-index', '-f', '-z', '--stdin'], { input: restored.map((path) => `${path}\0`).join('') });
    }
    return { restored, removed: removed.sort() };
  });
}

/**
 * Strip (design 7.3): a commit on head whose tree is head's with every protected change undone: changed and
 * deleted paths get the base's entry back, added ones are removed. Built in the vault with a temporary index, with
 * no checkout and no hooks; the clone is not involved. Gives head itself when nothing is protected.
 */
export async function stripProtected(
  git: ProtectGit,
  input: {
    base: string;
    head: string;
    paths: readonly string[];
    identity: { name: string; email: string };
    now?: Date;
  },
): Promise<{ sha: string; stripped: string[] }> {
  const changes = await detectProtected(git, input);
  if (changes.length === 0) return { sha: input.head, stripped: [] };
  // The base's entries, as "<mode> <type> <sha>\t<path>".
  const baseEntries = new Map<string, string>();
  for (const line of entries((await vaultGit(git, ['ls-tree', '-r', '-z', '--full-tree', input.base])).stdout)) {
    const tab = line.indexOf('\t');
    const [mode, , sha] = line.slice(0, tab).split(' ');
    baseEntries.set(line.slice(tab + 1), `${mode} ${sha}`);
  }
  // Removals first, so a base file can come back where the head has a link or a file in its directory's place.
  const removals = changes.filter((change) => change.status === 'added').map((change) => `0 ${NO_SHA}\t${change.path}`);
  const restores = changes.flatMap((change) => {
    const entry = change.status === 'added' ? undefined : baseEntries.get(change.path);
    return entry === undefined ? [] : [`${entry}\t${change.path}`];
  });
  const tree = await withTempIndex(async (index) => {
    await vaultGit(git, ['read-tree', input.head], { index });
    const info = [...removals, ...restores].map((line) => `${line}\0`).join('');
    await vaultGit(git, ['update-index', '-z', '--index-info'], { index, input: info });
    return (await vaultGit(git, ['write-tree'], { index })).stdout.trim();
  });
  const sha = await commitTree({
    vault: git.vault,
    local: git.local,
    tree,
    parent: input.head,
    message: 'agflow: protected paths reverted to the base',
    identity: input.identity,
    now: input.now ?? new Date(),
  });
  return { sha, stripped: changes.map((change) => change.path) };
}
```

### Task 17: Fenced pushes and late-work refs

Every push runs in the vault with the remote environment as `push --atomic --porcelain --no-verify` with one `--force-with-lease=<ref>:<exact sha>` per ref; never `--force`, a bare lease or a `+` refspec (design 7.3, 6.13). WIP pushes lease on the previous WIP sha, and late work goes to core's `lateWorkRef` with an empty lease, moving to the next n while one exists (X-18). A submission pushes the task branch and the WIP ref atomically; a stale branch lease is adopted with one retry, refused with `needs_merge` or refused with `branch_moved`, and network, server, auth and timeout failures are `remote`. `deleteRefsFenced` removes refs only at their expected sha, one at a time (design 6.18, X-39).

```ts
import { mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { lateWorkRef, wipRef } from '@agflow/core';
import { commitFiles, gitIn, originRepo } from '@agflow/testkit';
import { deleteRefsFenced, pushLateWork, pushRefs, pushSubmission, pushWip } from '../src/git/push';
import { ensureRunnerGitFiles, localGitEnv, remoteGitEnv, runGit } from '../src/git/run';
import { commitTree } from '../src/git/snapshot';
import { Vault } from '../src/git/vault';
import { runnerPaths } from '../src/paths';

// Every test here runs git or agent processes, which take several times as long on a machine loaded by other suites.
setDefaultTimeout(30_000);

const cleanups: (() => void | Promise<void>)[] = [];
afterEach(async () => {
  for (const cleanup of cleanups.splice(0).reverse()) await cleanup();
});

const PREFIX = 'refs/agflow/';
const PROJECT = 'demo-0123456789';
const BRANCH = 'agflow/T-4-tidy';
const BRANCH_REF = `refs/heads/${BRANCH}`;
const ATTEMPT = 'T-4-a1';
const WIP = wipRef(PREFIX, ATTEMPT);
const IDENTITY = { name: 'agflow runner', email: 'runner@agflow.invalid' };

function tempDir(prefix: string): string {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), prefix));
  cleanups.push(() => rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }));
  return dir;
}

async function setup() {
  const repo = await originRepo({ 'README.md': '# demo\n' });
  cleanups.push(() => repo.remove());
  const paths = runnerPaths(tempDir('agflow-push-'));
  ensureRunnerGitFiles(paths);
  const home = tempDir('agflow-owner-');
  const base = { ...process.env, HOME: home, XDG_CONFIG_HOME: undefined };
  const vault = new Vault({
    paths,
    project: PROJECT,
    repo: { url: repo.path, mainBranch: 'main' },
    remote: () => remoteGitEnv({ base }),
  });
  await vault.ensure();
  await vault.fetchForAttempt({ taskId: 'T-4', start: { ref: 'refs/heads/main', sha: null } }, PREFIX);
  const local = localGitEnv(paths);
  const remote = await remoteGitEnv({ base, gitDir: vault.path });
  // Every git the remote environment runs logs its argv here.
  const trace = join(tempDir('agflow-trace-'), 'trace');
  remote.env.GIT_TRACE = trace;
  const git = { vault, local, remote };
  let count = 0;
  /** A new commit in the vault on parent, with main's tree. */
  const commit = async (parent = repo.mainSha) => {
    count += 1;
    const tree = (await runGit(local, [`--git-dir=${vault.path}`, 'rev-parse', `${parent}^{tree}`])).stdout.trim();
    return commitTree({ vault, local, tree, parent, message: `work ${count}`, identity: IDENTITY, now: new Date() });
  };
  /** A ref on the origin, or null. */
  const origin = async (ref: string) =>
    (await gitIn(repo.path, ['rev-parse', '--verify', '--quiet', ref], { allowFailure: true })) || null;
  /** Points a ref on the origin at a commit the vault holds, as another machine's push would. */
  const setOrigin = async (ref: string, sha: string) =>
    runGit(remote, [`--git-dir=${vault.path}`, 'push', '--quiet', '--no-verify', 'origin', `+${sha}:${ref}`]);
  /** Points the vault's origin at a path that holds no repository. */
  const loseOrigin = () =>
    runGit(local, [`--git-dir=${vault.path}`, 'config', 'remote.origin.url', join(tempDir('agflow-gone-'), 'x')]);
  return { repo, vault, local, remote, git, commit, origin, setOrigin, loseOrigin, trace };
}

describe('pushWip', () => {

    expect(await pushWip({ ...s.git, ref: WIP, sha: c, previous: a })).toMatchObject({ ok: false, error: 'stale' });
    expect(await pushWip({ ...s.git, ref: WIP, sha: c, previous: null })).toMatchObject({ ok: false, error: 'stale' });
    expect(await s.origin(WIP)).toBe(b);
  });

  test('pushing the same sha again reports = and succeeds', async () => {
    const s = await setup();
    const a = await s.commit();
    await pushWip({ ...s.git, ref: WIP, sha: a, previous: null });
    // The lease is stale, but the ref already holds the commit: the retry of a push whose answer was lost.
    expect(await pushWip({ ...s.git, ref: WIP, sha: a, previous: null })).toEqual({
      ok: true,
      refs: [{ ref: WIP, status: 'up_to_date', detail: 'up to date' }],
    });
  });
});

describe('pushLateWork', () => {
  test('goes to the first late-work ref, then to the next free one', async () => {
    const s = await setup();
    const [a, b] = [await s.commit(), await s.commit()];
    const late = (sha: string) => pushLateWork({ ...s.git, wipRefPrefix: PREFIX, attemptId: ATTEMPT, sha });
    expect(await late(a)).toEqual({ ok: true, ref: lateWorkRef(PREFIX, ATTEMPT, 1), n: 1 });
    expect(await late(b)).toEqual({ ok: true, ref: lateWorkRef(PREFIX, ATTEMPT, 2), n: 2 });
    // A repeat of a push that landed finds its own ref.
    expect(await late(a)).toEqual({ ok: true, ref: lateWorkRef(PREFIX, ATTEMPT, 1), n: 1 });
    expect(await s.origin(lateWorkRef(PREFIX, ATTEMPT, 1))).toBe(a);
    expect(await s.origin(lateWorkRef(PREFIX, ATTEMPT, 2))).toBe(b);
  });
});

describe('pushSubmission', () => {
  const submission = (s: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof setup>>, sha: string, more: Record<string, unknown> = {}) =>
    pushSubmission({
      ...s.git,
      taskId: 'T-4',
      wipRefPrefix: PREFIX,
      branch: BRANCH,

      expectedBranchSha: null,
      previousWip: null,

  test('moves the task branch and the WIP ref together', async () => {
    const s = await setup();
    const a = await s.commit();
    expect(await submission(s, a)).toEqual({ ok: true, headSha: a, remoteHead: a, error: null, detail: null });
    expect(await s.origin(BRANCH_REF)).toBe(a);
    expect(await s.origin(WIP)).toBe(a);
    const b = await s.commit(a);
    expect(await submission(s, b, { expectedBranchSha: a, previousWip: a })).toMatchObject({ ok: true, headSha: b });
    expect(await s.origin(BRANCH_REF)).toBe(b);

  });

  test('adopts a remote head the submitted commit contains, with one retry', async () => {
    const s = await setup();

    await submission(s, a);
    const moved = await commitFiles(s.repo.path, { branch: BRANCH, files: { 'b.txt': 'b\n' } });
    await s.vault.refresh('T-4', [], PREFIX);
    const merged = await s.commit(moved);
    expect(await submission(s, merged, { expectedBranchSha: a, previousWip: a })).toEqual({

      headSha: merged,
      remoteHead: merged,
      error: null,
      detail: null,
    });
    expect(await s.origin(BRANCH_REF)).toBe(merged);
    expect(await s.origin(WIP)).toBe(merged);
  });

  test('adopts a remote head listed in adoptable', async () => {
    const s = await setup();
    const [other, mine] = [await s.commit(), await s.commit()];
    await s.setOrigin(BRANCH_REF, other);
    const outcome = await submission(s, mine, { expectedBranchSha: null, adoptable: [other.slice(0, 12)] });
    expect(outcome).toMatchObject({ ok: true, headSha: mine, remoteHead: mine });
    expect(await s.origin(BRANCH_REF)).toBe(mine);
  });

  test('a remote head on top of an adoptable sha gives needs_merge, any other gives branch_moved', async () => {
    const s = await setup();

    await submission(s, agentWork);
    const personal = await commitFiles(s.repo.path, { branch: BRANCH, files: { 'p.txt': 'person\n' } });
    const mine = await s.commit(agentWork);

      expectedBranchSha: agentWork,

    expect(needsMerge).toEqual({
      ok: false,
      headSha: mine,
      remoteHead: personal,
      error: 'needs_merge',
      detail: expect.stringContaining(`git fetch origin && git merge origin/${BRANCH}`),
    });
    expect(await s.origin(BRANCH_REF)).toBe(personal);
    expect(await s.origin(WIP)).toBe(agentWork);
    // The vault carries the remote head, so the agent's `git fetch origin && git merge` merges it.
    const vaultBranch = await runGit(s.local, [`--git-dir=${s.vault.path}`, 'rev-parse', '--verify', BRANCH_REF]);
    expect(vaultBranch.stdout.trim()).toBe(personal);
    const unrelated = await s.commit(s.repo.mainSha);
    await s.setOrigin(BRANCH_REF, unrelated);
    const moved = await submission(s, mine, {
      expectedBranchSha: agentWork,
      previousWip: agentWork,

    expect(moved).toMatchObject({ ok: false, headSha: mine, remoteHead: unrelated, error: 'branch_moved' });
    expect(await s.origin(BRANCH_REF)).toBe(unrelated);
    expect(await s.origin(WIP)).toBe(agentWork);
  });

  test('adopts a WIP ref whose push answer was lost', async () => {
    const s = await setup();

    const next = await s.commit(w);

      remoteHead: next,

      detail: null,

    expect(await s.origin(WIP)).toBe(next);
  });

  test('refuses a WIP ref at a commit this attempt did not push, and moves nothing', async () => {
    const s = await setup();
    const [foreign, mine] = [await s.commit(), await s.commit()];
    await s.setOrigin(WIP, foreign);
    const outcome = await submission(s, mine);
    expect(outcome).toMatchObject({ ok: false, headSha: mine, error: 'remote' });
    expect(outcome.detail).toContain(WIP);
    expect(await s.origin(WIP)).toBe(foreign);
    expect(await s.origin(BRANCH_REF)).toBeNull();
  });

  test('resolves an abbreviated expected branch sha from the remote', async () => {
    const s = await setup();
    const a = await s.commit();
    await submission(s, a);
    const b = await s.commit(a);
    const outcome = await submission(s, b, { expectedBranchSha: a.slice(0, 12), previousWip: a });
    expect(outcome).toEqual({ ok: true, headSha: b, remoteHead: b, error: null, detail: null });
    expect(await s.origin(BRANCH_REF)).toBe(b);
    expect(await s.origin(WIP)).toBe(b);
    // A rewritten branch: only the abbreviation's match with the remote head lets the lease through.
    const rewritten = await s.commit(s.repo.mainSha);
    const again = await submission(s, rewritten, { expectedBranchSha: b.slice(0, 12), previousWip: b });
    expect(again).toEqual({ ok: true, headSha: rewritten, remoteHead: rewritten, error: null, detail: null });
    expect(await s.origin(BRANCH_REF)).toBe(rewritten);
    expect(await s.origin(WIP)).toBe(rewritten);
  });

  test('a remote failure gives remote', async () => {
    const s = await setup();
    const a = await s.commit();
    await s.loseOrigin();
    expect(await submission(s, a)).toMatchObject({ ok: false, headSha: a, remoteHead: null, error: 'remote' });
  });
});

describe('deleteRefsFenced', () => {
  test('deletes a ref still at its expected sha and leaves one that moved', async () => {
    const s = await setup();
```

```ts
// Pushes (design 7.3, 6.13, 6.18). Every push runs in the vault with the remote environment, always
// `--atomic --porcelain --no-verify`, with `--force-with-lease=<ref>:<exact sha>` for each ref (empty to create it):
// never --force, a bare lease or a + refspec. A push that finds the ref already at its commit reports = and counts
// as success. WIP pushes lease on the attempt's previous WIP sha; late work goes to new refs beside the WIP ref; a
// submission moves the task branch and the WIP ref together and follows the stale-lease rules; fenced deletes
// remove refs only at the sha the hub recorded. Network, server, auth and timeout failures are all `remote`.
import { lateWorkRef, type SubmitError } from '@agflow/core';
import { type GitEnvironment, gitOk, runGit } from './run';
import type { Vault } from './vault';

export interface PushGit {
  vault: Vault;
  /** The local environment, for questions about the vault's commits. */
  local: GitEnvironment;
  /** The remote environment for the vault (remoteGitEnv with gitDir: the vault). */
  remote: GitEnvironment;
}

export interface RefUpdate {
  ref: string;
  /** The commit to push; null deletes the ref. */
  sha: string | null;
  /** The sha the ref must have on the remote; null: it must not exist. */
  expected: string | null;
}

export interface PushRefResult {
  ref: string;
  /**
   * ok: created, moved or deleted; up_to_date: already at the commit (=); stale: the lease failed; refused: rejected
   * by the remote, or left alone because another ref of the atomic push failed.
   */
  status: 'ok' | 'up_to_date' | 'stale' | 'refused';
  /** git's summary: "new reference", "stale info", "atomic push failed", "remote rejected (...)"... */
  detail: string;
}

export type PushResult =
  | { ok: true; refs: PushRefResult[] }
  | { ok: false; error: 'stale' | 'remote'; refs: PushRefResult[]; detail: string };

const SHA = /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/;

function requireSha(sha: string, what: string): string {
  if (!SHA.test(sha)) throw new Error(`${what} must be a full commit sha, not ${JSON.stringify(sha)}`);
  return sha;
}

/** The arguments of a push: every ref leased on its exact expected sha, every refspec without a +. */
export function pushArgs(updates: readonly RefUpdate[]): string[] {
  if (updates.length === 0) throw new Error('a push needs at least one ref');
  const leases = updates.map((update) => {
    const expected = update.expected === null ? '' : requireSha(update.expected, 'a lease');
    return `--force-with-lease=${update.ref}:${expected}`;
  });
  const refspecs = updates.map((update) =>
    update.sha === null ? `:${update.ref}` : `${requireSha(update.sha, 'a pushed commit')}:${update.ref}`,
  );
  return ['push', '--atomic', '--porcelain', '--no-verify', ...leases, 'origin', ...refspecs];
}

/** One porcelain line: "<flag>\t<from>:<to>\t<summary>", the summary "[word]", "[word] (reason)" or text. */
function parseLine(line: string): PushRefResult | null {
  const [flag, refspec, summary] = line.split('\t');
  if (flag === undefined || refspec === undefined || summary === undefined || flag.length !== 1) return null;
  const ref = refspec.slice(refspec.lastIndexOf(':') + 1);
  const reason = summary.match(/\(([^)]*)\)\s*$/)?.[1];
  const word = summary.match(/^\[([^\]]*)\]/)?.[1];
  const detail = reason ?? word ?? summary.trim();
  if (flag === '=') return { ref, status: 'up_to_date', detail };
  if (flag !== '!') return { ref, status: 'ok', detail };
  return { ref, status: reason === 'stale info' ? 'stale' : 'refused', detail };
}

/**
 * One atomic push of the updates. Gives ok when every ref was moved or was already at its commit; stale when a
 * lease failed (nothing moved); remote for everything else: an unreachable or refusing remote, a timeout.
 */
export async function pushRefs(input: PushGit & { updates: readonly RefUpdate[] }): Promise<PushResult> {
  const args = pushArgs(input.updates);
  const result = await runGit(input.remote, [`--git-dir=${input.vault.path}`, ...args], { check: false });
  const refs = result.stdout
    .split('\n')
    .map(parseLine)
    .filter((ref): ref is PushRefResult => ref !== null);
  const wanted = new Set(input.updates.map((update) => update.ref));
  const complete = refs.length === wanted.size && refs.every((ref) => wanted.has(ref.ref));
  const landed = refs.every((ref) => ref.status === 'ok' || ref.status === 'up_to_date');
  if (!result.timedOut && result.code === 0 && complete && landed) return { ok: true, refs };
  const stale = refs.find((ref) => ref.status === 'stale');
  if (stale && !result.timedOut) return { ok: false, error: 'stale', refs, detail: `${stale.ref}: stale info` };
  const refused = refs.find((ref) => ref.status === 'refused' && ref.detail !== 'atomic push failed');
  const detail = result.timedOut
    ? `the push timed out after ${input.remote.timeoutMs} ms`
    : refused
      ? `${refused.ref}: ${refused.detail}`
      : result.stderr.trim() || `git push exited with ${result.code}`;
  return { ok: false, error: 'remote', refs, detail };
}

/** The attempt's WIP ref to sha, leased on the previous WIP sha (null: the ref must not exist yet). */
export function pushWip(input: PushGit & { ref: string; sha: string; previous: string | null }): Promise<PushResult> {
  return pushRefs({ ...input, updates: [{ ref: input.ref, sha: input.sha, expected: input.previous }] });
}

/** The highest late-work number tried before giving up. */
const LATE_WORK_MAX = 1000;

export type LateWorkResult = { ok: true; ref: string; n: number } | { ok: false; error: 'remote'; detail: string };

/**
 * Late work and hand-backs: a new ref beside the WIP ref, lateWorkRef(prefix, attempt, n), created with an empty
 * lease from n = 1, moving to the next n while one exists. A ref already at sha is the landing of an earlier try.
 */
export async function pushLateWork(
  input: PushGit & { wipRefPrefix: string; attemptId: string; sha: string },
): Promise<LateWorkResult> {
  for (let n = 1; n <= LATE_WORK_MAX; n++) {
    const ref = lateWorkRef(input.wipRefPrefix, input.attemptId, n);
    const result = await pushRefs({ ...input, updates: [{ ref, sha: input.sha, expected: null }] });
    if (result.ok) return { ok: true, ref, n };
    if (result.error === 'remote') return { ok: false, error: 'remote', detail: result.detail };
  }
  return { ok: false, error: 'remote', detail: `late-work refs 1 to ${LATE_WORK_MAX} all exist` };
}

/** The remote's shas for the refs, read with ls-remote; a ref the remote lacks is absent from the map. */
async function lsRemote(git: PushGit, refs: string[]): Promise<Map<string, string>> {
  const result = await runGit(git.remote, [`--git-dir=${git.vault.path}`, 'ls-remote', 'origin', ...refs]);
  const heads = new Map<string, string>();
  for (const line of result.stdout.split('\n')) {
    const [sha, ref] = line.split('\t');
    // ls-remote matches patterns against the end of each name; only the exact names count.
    if (sha !== undefined && ref !== undefined && SHA.test(sha) && refs.includes(ref)) heads.set(ref, sha);
  }
  return heads;
}

export interface SubmitPushOutcome {
  ok: boolean;
  /** The submitted commit. */
  headSha: string;
  /** The task branch's head on the remote after the push: the submitted commit, the one that refused it, or null. */
  remoteHead: string | null;
  error: Extract<SubmitError, 'needs_merge' | 'branch_moved' | 'remote'> | null;
  detail: string | null;
}

export interface SubmissionInput extends PushGit {
  taskId: string;
  wipRefPrefix: string;
  /** The task branch, without refs/heads/. */
  branch: string;
  /** The attempt's WIP ref. */
  wipRef: string;
  /** The harvested commit to submit. */
  sha: string;
  /** push_submission.expectedBranchSha: the branch head the hub recorded, perhaps abbreviated; null: none. */
  expectedBranchSha: string | null;
  /** The attempt's previous WIP sha; null: none yet. */
  previousWip: string | null;
  /** push_submission.adoptable: shas the hub knows as agflow work for the task, perhaps abbreviated. */
  adoptable: readonly string[];
}

/**
 * push_submission's push (design 6.13): the task branch and the WIP ref to one commit, atomically. On a stale
 * branch lease it reads the remote head (and fetches it into the vault), then:
 * 1. a remote head the submitted commit contains, or one in adoptable, is adopted as the lease, with one retry;
 * 2. a remote head that descends from an adoptable sha (someone added commits on top of agflow work) refuses with
 *    needs_merge, which the agent fixes by merging the branch;
 * 3. any other head refuses with branch_moved.
 * The WIP ref belongs to the attempt: a remote value the commit contains or the hub lists is adopted the same way.
 * The remote branch never moves on a refusal.
 */
export async function pushSubmission(input: SubmissionInput): Promise<SubmitPushOutcome> {
  const { sha, branch } = input;
  requireSha(sha, 'a submitted commit');
  const branchRef = `refs/heads/${branch}`;
  const outcome = (error: SubmitPushOutcome['error'], remoteHead: string | null, detail: string | null) => ({
    ok: error === null,
    headSha: sha,
    remoteHead,
    error,
    detail,
  });
  const isAncestor = (ancestor: string, descendant: string) =>
    gitOk(input.local, [`--git-dir=${input.vault.path}`, 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor', ancestor, descendant]);
  // Recorded shas may be abbreviated (at least 7 hex).
  const known = input.adoptable.filter((entry) => /^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$/.test(entry));
  const matches = (head: string | null, recorded: string | null) =>
    head === recorded || (head !== null && recorded !== null && recorded.length >= 7 && head.startsWith(recorded));
  const adoptable = async (head: string) =>
    known.some((entry) => head.startsWith(entry)) || (await isAncestor(head, sha));

  let leases = { branch: input.expectedBranchSha, wip: input.previousWip };
  for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
    // A lease needs an exact sha: an abbreviated recorded head is resolved from the remote first.
    if (leases.branch === null || SHA.test(leases.branch)) {
      const updates = [
        { ref: branchRef, sha, expected: leases.branch },
        { ref: input.wipRef, sha, expected: leases.wip },
      ];
      const result = await pushRefs({ ...input, updates });
      if (result.ok) return outcome(null, sha, null);
      if (result.error === 'remote') return outcome('remote', null, result.detail);
    }
    let heads: Map<string, string>;
    try {
      heads = await lsRemote(input, [branchRef, input.wipRef]);
      await input.vault.refresh(input.taskId, [...heads.keys()], input.wipRefPrefix);
    } catch (error) {
      return outcome('remote', null, error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));
    }
    const remoteHead = heads.get(branchRef) ?? null;
    const remoteWip = heads.get(input.wipRef) ?? null;
    if (!matches(remoteHead, leases.branch)) {
      if (remoteHead === null) return outcome('branch_moved', null, `${branch} was deleted on the remote`);
      if (!(await adoptable(remoteHead))) {
        for (const entry of known) {
          if (await isAncestor(entry, remoteHead)) {
            const fix = `git fetch origin && git merge origin/${branch}`;
            return outcome('needs_merge', remoteHead, `${branch} has commits on top of agflow work; run \`${fix}\``);
          }
        }
        return outcome('branch_moved', remoteHead, `${branch} moved to ${remoteHead}, which is not agflow work`);
      }
    }
    // The WIP ref is the attempt's own: another value there is adopted on the same terms, never pushed over.
    if (!matches(remoteWip, leases.wip) && remoteWip !== null && !(await adoptable(remoteWip))) {
      return outcome('remote', remoteHead, `${input.wipRef} is at ${remoteWip}, which this attempt did not push`);
    }
    if (attempt === 1) return outcome('remote', remoteHead, `${branch} kept moving while it was pushed`);
    leases = { branch: remoteHead, wip: remoteWip };
  }
}

export interface DeleteRefResult {
  ref: string;
  /** deleted, or already gone; moved: left alone at remoteSha; failed: the remote could not be reached. */
  status: 'deleted' | 'gone' | 'moved' | 'failed';
  remoteSha: string | null;
  detail: string | null;
}

/** delete_refs (design 6.18): each ref is deleted only while it is still at its expected sha, one push each. */
export async function deleteRefsFenced(
  input: PushGit & { refs: readonly { ref: string; expectedSha: string }[] },
): Promise<DeleteRefResult[]> {
  const results: DeleteRefResult[] = [];
  for (const { ref, expectedSha } of input.refs) {
    const pushed = await pushRefs({ ...input, updates: [{ ref, sha: null, expected: expectedSha }] });
    if (pushed.ok) {
      results.push({ ref, status: 'deleted', remoteSha: null, detail: null });
    } else if (pushed.error === 'remote') {
      results.push({ ref, status: 'failed', remoteSha: null, detail: pushed.detail });
    } else {
      // A lease on a ref that does not exist fails as stale too.
      const heads = await lsRemote(input, [ref]).catch(() => null);
      if (heads === null) results.push({ ref, status: 'failed', remoteSha: null, detail: 'ls-remote failed' });
      else {
        const remoteSha = heads.get(ref) ?? null;
        results.push({ ref, status: remoteSha === null ? 'gone' : 'moved', remoteSha, detail: null });
      }
    }
  }
  return results;
}
```

### Task 18: The fake adapter: failures, quota, approvals and transcripts

The rest of the fake adapter's script (design 13, 7.4, 15; X-46 splits it from Task 12): turns that fail with each `errorKind`, quota events with an account id, context, compaction and warning events, and approvals as tool calls that raise `approval_request` and `waiting_approval`, wait for `answerApproval` and can be voided. An optional `enrichApproval` adds a detail field (X-9). Transcripts are JSON lines that `readTranscriptTail` and `deleteTranscript` read and remove without a session, and resuming a session that never ran a turn falls back to a fresh session, as the real CLIs do.

- Modify: `packages/testkit/src/fake-adapter.ts`

```ts
import { afterEach, describe, expect, setDefaultTimeout, test } from 'bun:test';
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import type { VendorQuota } from '@agflow/core';
import type { AgentEvent } from '@agflow/runner';
import { FakeAdapter, type FakeStep } from '../src/fake-adapter';
import { killLater, record, runCleanups, setup, start, tempDir, turnEnded } from './fake-helpers';

afterEach(runCleanups);

// Every test here runs git or agent processes, which take several times as long on a machine loaded by other suites.
setDefaultTimeout(30_000);

const ERROR_KINDS = ['quota', 'vendor', 'auth', 'context', 'policy', 'denials', 'session_budget'] as const;

const waitingFor = (approvalId: string) => (event: AgentEvent) =>
  event.type === 'approval_request' && event.approvalId === approvalId;

describe('scripted failures', () => {
  test('end the turn as failed with each errorKind', async () => {
    const { launch } = await setup();
    const session = await start(launch, {
      turns: ERROR_KINDS.map((kind): FakeStep[] => [
        { do: 'tool', command: 'true' },
        { do: 'fail', kind, error: `${kind} trouble` },
        { do: 'text', text: 'never said' },
      ]),
    });
    const reader = record(session);
    for (const [i, kind] of ERROR_KINDS.entries()) {
      if (i > 0) await session.send({ id: `m${i}`, text: 'go on', authority: 'system' });
      await reader.waitFor((event) => event.type === 'turn_ended' && event.errorKind === kind);
    }
    const ended = reader.events.filter((event) => event.type === 'turn_ended');
    expect(ended).toEqual(
      ERROR_KINDS.map((kind) => ({
        type: 'turn_ended',
        outcome: 'failed',
        toolCalls: 1,
        error: `${kind} trouble`,
        errorKind: kind,
      })),
    );
    expect(reader.events.some((event) => event.type === 'text')).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe('scripted reports', () => {
  test('quota, context, compaction and warning events appear as scripted', async () => {
    const { launch } = await setup();
    const quota: VendorQuota = {
      state: 'ok',
      resetsAt: 1_800_000_000_000,
      windows: { fiveHour: 0.97, weekly: 0.4 },
      paidUsage: 'in_use',
      updatedAt: 1_700_000_000_000,
    };
    const session = await start(launch, {
      turns: [
        [
          { do: 'quota', quota, accountId: 'acct-1' },
          { do: 'context', used: 0.82 },
          { do: 'compacted', summary: 'the story so far' },
          { do: 'warning', text: 'auto-compaction ran' },
          { do: 'quota', quota: { ...quota, state: 'exhausted', paidUsage: 'disabled' } },
        ],
      ],
    });
    const reader = record(session);
    await reader.waitFor(turnEnded);
    expect(reader.events.slice(2, -1)).toEqual([
      { type: 'quota', accountId: 'acct-1', quota },
      { type: 'context', used: 0.82 },
      { type: 'compacted', summary: 'the story so far' },
      { type: 'warning', text: 'auto-compaction ran' },
      { type: 'quota', accountId: null, quota: { ...quota, state: 'exhausted', paidUsage: 'disabled' } },
    ]);
  });
});

describe('scripted approvals', () => {
  test('raise approval_request and waiting_approval, and the tool follows the answer', async () => {
    const { launch } = await setup();
    const session = await start(launch, {
      turns: [
        [
          {
            do: 'approval',
            approvalId: 'A-1',
            kind: 'command',
            summary: 'run the deploy script',
            detail: { command: './deploy.sh', cwd: launch.clone },
          },
          { do: 'approval', approvalId: 'A-2', kind: 'file_change', summary: 'edit the lockfile' },
          { do: 'text', text: 'done' },
        ],
      ],
    });
    const reader = record(session);
    await reader.waitFor(waitingFor('A-1'));
    expect(await session.answerApproval('A-404', 'approve', null)).toBe(false);
    expect(await session.answerApproval('A-1', 'approve', null)).toBe(true);
    expect(await session.answerApproval('A-1', 'approve', null)).toBe(false);
    await reader.waitFor(waitingFor('A-2'));
    expect(await session.answerApproval('A-2', 'decline', 'not now')).toBe(true);
    await reader.waitFor(turnEnded);
    expect(reader.events.slice(1)).toEqual([
      { type: 'turn_started' },
      { type: 'tool_started', toolId: 'toolu_1', name: 'Bash', input: 'run the deploy script', command: './deploy.sh' },
      {
        type: 'approval_request',
        approvalId: 'A-1',
        kind: 'command',
        summary: 'run the deploy script',
        detail: { command: './deploy.sh', cwd: launch.clone },
      },
      { type: 'waiting_approval', waiting: true },
      { type: 'waiting_approval', waiting: false },
      { type: 'tool_ended', toolId: 'toolu_1', ok: true, denied: false, terminal: null, hubUnreachable: false },
      { type: 'tool_started', toolId: 'toolu_2', name: 'Edit', input: 'edit the lockfile', command: null },
      { type: 'approval_request', approvalId: 'A-2', kind: 'file_change', summary: 'edit the lockfile', detail: {} },
      { type: 'waiting_approval', waiting: true },
      { type: 'waiting_approval', waiting: false },
      { type: 'tool_ended', toolId: 'toolu_2', ok: false, denied: true, terminal: null, hubUnreachable: false },
      { type: 'text', text: 'done' },
      { type: 'turn_ended', outcome: 'completed', toolCalls: 2, error: null, errorKind: null },
    ]);
  });

  test('a voided request ends the wait; answering it afterwards is refused', async () => {
    const { launch } = await setup();
    const session = await start(launch, {
      turns: [
        [
          { do: 'approval', approvalId: 'A-1', kind: 'other', summary: 'open the network', voidAfterMs: 100 },
          { do: 'approval', approvalId: 'A-2', kind: 'command', summary: 'rm -rf build' },
        ],
      ],
    });
    const reader = record(session);
    await reader.waitFor((event) => event.type === 'approval_void');
    expect(await session.answerApproval('A-1', 'approve', null)).toBe(false);
    await reader.waitFor(waitingFor('A-2'));
    // An interrupt voids the request it is waiting on.
    await session.interrupt();
    const ended = await reader.waitFor(turnEnded);
    expect(ended).toMatchObject({ outcome: 'interrupted', toolCalls: 2 });
    expect(await session.answerApproval('A-2', 'approve', null)).toBe(false);
    const flow = reader.events.flatMap((event) =>
      event.type === 'approval_void'
        ? [`void ${event.approvalId}`]
        : event.type === 'waiting_approval'
          ? [`waiting ${event.waiting}`]
          : event.type === 'tool_ended'
            ? [`tool ${event.ok} ${event.denied}`]
            : [],
    );
    expect(flow).toEqual([
      'waiting true',
      'void A-1',
      'waiting false',
      'tool false false',
      'waiting true',
      'void A-2',
      'waiting false',
      'tool false false',
    ]);
  });

  test('enrichApproval, when configured, adds its detail field; otherwise the adapter has none', async () => {
    const request = { kind: 'command' as const, summary: 'npm install', detail: { command: 'npm install' } };
    const input = { clone: '/tmp/clone', vault: '/tmp/vault', startSha: 'a'.repeat(40), request };
    expect(new FakeAdapter({ script: { turns: [] } }).enrichApproval).toBeUndefined();
    const adapter = new FakeAdapter({ script: { turns: [] }, enrichDetail: { manifestDiff: '+ left-pad' } });
    expect(await adapter.enrichApproval?.(input)).toEqual({ command: 'npm install', manifestDiff: '+ left-pad' });
  });
});

describe('transcripts', () => {
  test('readTranscriptTail reads the last assistant turns without a session; deleteTranscript drops them', async () => {
    const { launch, clone } = await setup();
    const transcriptDir = tempDir('agflow-fake-transcripts-');
    const adapter = new FakeAdapter({
      transcriptDir,
      script: {
        turns: [
          [{ do: 'text', text: 'first answer' }],
          [
            { do: 'text', text: 'second answer' },
            { do: 'text', text: 'and more' },
          ],
        ],
      },
    });
    const session = await adapter.start(launch);
    killLater(session.pid);
    const reader = record(session);
    await reader.waitFor(turnEnded);
    await session.send({ id: 'm1', text: 'continue', authority: 'person' });
    await reader.waitFor((event) => event.type === 'acknowledged');
    await session.close();
    await session.exited;
    const later = new FakeAdapter({ transcriptDir, script: { turns: [] } });
    const ref = { sessionRef: session.sessionRef, clone };
    const full = 'first answer\n\nsecond answer\nand more';
    expect(await later.readTranscriptTail({ ...ref, maxChars: 1_000 })).toBe(full);
    expect(await later.readTranscriptTail({ ...ref, maxChars: 12 })).toBe(full.slice(-12));
    expect(await later.readTranscriptTail({ sessionRef: 'never-ran', clone, maxChars: 100 })).toBeNull();
    await later.deleteTranscript(ref);
    expect(await later.readTranscriptTail({ ...ref, maxChars: 1_000 })).toBeNull();
    expect(existsSync(join(transcriptDir, `${session.sessionRef}.jsonl`))).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe('resume', () => {
  test('a session that ran a turn is resumed; one that never did starts fresh with a new sessionRef', async () => {
    const { launch } = await setup();
    const transcriptDir = tempDir('agflow-fake-transcripts-');
    const adapter = new FakeAdapter({
      transcriptDir,
      script: (current) =>
        current.resume ? { turns: [[{ do: 'text', text: 'resumed' }]] } : { turns: [[{ do: 'text', text: 'fresh' }]] },
    });
    const first = await adapter.start(launch);
    killLater(first.pid);
    await record(first).waitFor(turnEnded);
    await first.close();
    await first.exited;

    const resumed = await adapter.start({ ...launch, resume: { sessionRef: first.sessionRef } });
    killLater(resumed.pid);
    expect(resumed.sessionRef).toBe(first.sessionRef);
    const resumedReader = record(resumed);
    await resumedReader.waitFor((event) => event.type === 'started');
    await Bun.sleep(100);
    expect(resumedReader.events.map((event) => event.type)).toEqual(['started']);
    await resumed.close();
    await resumed.exited;

    const unborn = await adapter.start({ ...launch, resume: { sessionRef: 'never-ran-a-turn' } });
    killLater(unborn.pid);
    expect(unborn.sessionRef).not.toBe('never-ran-a-turn');
    expect(unborn.sessionRef).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/);
    const unbornReader = record(unborn);
    await unbornReader.waitFor(turnEnded);
    expect(unbornReader.events[0]).toMatchObject({ type: 'started', sessionRef: unborn.sessionRef });
    // A fresh session: the first prompt starts a turn at once, with the script of a new launch.
    expect(unbornReader.events.find((event) => event.type === 'text')).toEqual({ type: 'text', text: 'fresh' });
  });
});
```

```ts
// Helpers for the fake adapter's tests: a clone with its run directory and a launch for it, sessions started from
// a script and killed at the end of the test, and a recorder of their events.
import { appendFileSync, existsSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import {
  type AgentEvent,
  type AgentLaunch,
  type AgentSession,
  agentGitEnv,
  removeAgentTools,
  standardProfile,
  writeRunDir,
} from '@agflow/runner';
import { FakeAdapter, type FakeAdapterOptions, type FakeScript } from '../src/fake-adapter';
import { gitIn, originRepo } from '../src/git-fixtures';

const cleanups: (() => void)[] = [];

/** Runs every cleanup a test registered, newest first; each test file calls it from afterEach. */
export function runCleanups(): void {
  for (const cleanup of cleanups.splice(0).reverse()) cleanup();
}

export function tempDir(prefix: string): string {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), prefix));
  cleanups.push(() => rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }));
  return dir;
}

/** Kills a process group at the end of the test, whatever state it is in. */
export function killLater(pgid: number): void {
  cleanups.push(() => {
    try {
      process.kill(-pgid, 'SIGKILL');
    } catch {
      // Already gone.
    }
  });
}

export const IDENTITY = { name: 'Agent Smith', email: 'agent@agflow.invalid' };

/** A clone on its task branch with the agent's .agflow/run/, and a launch for it. */
export async function setup(overrides: Partial<AgentLaunch> = {}): Promise<{ launch: AgentLaunch; clone: string }> {
  const origin = await originRepo({ 'README.md': '# demo\n' });
  cleanups.push(() => origin.remove());
  const clone = join(tempDir('agflow-fake-clone-'), 'T-4-a1');
  await gitIn(tmpdir(), ['clone', '--quiet', origin.path, clone]);
  await gitIn(clone, ['checkout', '--quiet', '-b', 'agflow/T-4-tidy']);
  const tools = join(tempDir('agflow-fake-tools-'), 'T-4-a1');
  cleanups.push(() => removeAgentTools(tools));
  const runDir = writeRunDir({ clone, tools, taskPack: '# T-4\n', brief: 'brief', identity: IDENTITY });
  // As the runner's clones do, so the agent's `git add -A` leaves .agflow/run/ out.
  appendFileSync(join(clone, '.git', 'info', 'exclude'), '/.agflow/run/\n');
  const env = { PATH: process.env.PATH ?? '/usr/bin:/bin', HOME: tempDir('agflow-fake-home-'), ...agentGitEnv(runDir) };
  const launch: AgentLaunch = {
    attemptId: 'T-4-a1',
    role: 'worker',
    model: 'fake-model',
    cliVersion: '9.9.9',
    clone,
    baseCheckout: null,
    projectConfigVerified: true,
    tmpDir: runDir.tmp,
    env,
    bridge: { command: '/bin/false', args: [], env: {} },
    profile: standardProfile,
    brief: 'brief',
    firstPrompt: 'start working',
    resume: null,
    logFile: join(tempDir('agflow-fake-logs-'), 'T-4-a1.log'),
    registerProcess: () => {},
    ...overrides,
  };
  return { launch, clone };
}

export async function start(
  launch: AgentLaunch,
  script: FakeScript,
  options: Omit<FakeAdapterOptions, 'script'> = {},
): Promise<AgentSession> {
  const session = await new FakeAdapter({ ...options, script }).start(launch);
  killLater(session.pid);
  return session;
}

/** Reads every event of a session in the background. */
export function record(session: AgentSession) {
  const events: AgentEvent[] = [];
  void (async () => {
    for await (const event of session.events) events.push(event);
  })();
  return {
    events,
    types: () =>
      events.map((event) =>
        event.type === 'delivered' || event.type === 'acknowledged' ? `${event.type} ${event.id}` : event.type,
      ),
    async waitFor(check: (event: AgentEvent) => boolean, timeoutMs = 15_000): Promise<AgentEvent> {
      const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
      for (;;) {
        const found = events.find(check);
        if (found) return found;
        if (Date.now() > deadline) throw new Error(`no such event in ${JSON.stringify(events)}`);
        await Bun.sleep(5);
      }
    },
  };
}

export const turnEnded = (event: AgentEvent) => event.type === 'turn_ended';
export const countOf = (events: AgentEvent[], type: AgentEvent['type']) =>
  events.filter((event) => event.type === type).length;

export async function waitFile(path: string): Promise<string> {
  const deadline = Date.now() + 5_000;
  while (!existsSync(path) || readFileSync(path, 'utf8').trim() === '') {
    if (Date.now() > deadline) throw new Error(`${path} never appeared`);
    await Bun.sleep(10);
  }
  return readFileSync(path, 'utf8').trim();
}
```

### Task 19: The stop ladder

Design 7.4's stop ladder is one function every stop uses: the protocol interrupt with up to `stopInterrupt` for the turn to end, the vendor's close with up to `stopClose`, SIGTERM to every recorded group with up to `stopKill`, then SIGKILL and a sweep of the processes in the clone. Each signal checks the group's recorded identity, and `groups()` is read again at each step, so a group found during the stop still dies. `stoppedBy` (core's `STOPPED_BY`) records the step during whose wait the agent exited, so a CLI that exits 143 on SIGTERM still counts as requested. `killAndSweep` runs the last two steps alone, for exits the runner did not request (X-15).

**Files:**
- Modify: `packages/runner/src/index.ts`
- Modify: `packages/runner/src/processes.ts`
- Create: `packages/runner/src/stop-ladder.ts`
- Test: `packages/runner/test/stop-ladder.test.ts`

**File:** `packages/runner/test/stop-ladder.test.ts` (new)

```ts
import { afterEach, describe, expect, setDefaultTimeout, test } from 'bun:test';
import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync, symlinkSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { FakeAdapter, type FakeScript } from '@agflow/testkit';
import type { AgentEvent, AgentSession, ExitInfo } from '../src/adapters/types';
import { DescendantTracker, listProcesses, type ProcessIdentity, processIdentity } from '../src/processes';
import { standardProfile } from '../src/profile';
import { killAndSweep, runStopLadder } from '../src/stop-ladder';
import { requireLsofOnMacOS } from './prerequisites';

// Every test here runs git or agent processes, which take several times as long on a machine loaded by other suites.
setDefaultTimeout(30_000);

const cleanups: (() => void)[] = [];
afterEach(() => {
  for (const cleanup of cleanups.splice(0).reverse()) cleanup();
});

function tempDir(prefix: string): string {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), prefix));
  cleanups.push(() => rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }));
  return dir;
}

function killLater(pgid: number): void {
  cleanups.push(() => {
    try {
      process.kill(-pgid, 'SIGKILL');
    } catch {
      // Already gone.
    }
  });
}

const TIMINGS = { stopInterrupt: 400, stopClose: 400, stopKill: 400 };

async function until(check: () => Promise<boolean> | boolean, timeoutMs = 15_000): Promise<void> {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  while (!(await check())) {
    if (Date.now() > deadline) throw new Error('timed out waiting for a condition');
    await Bun.sleep(20);
  }
}

/** True once the process is gone or only a zombie waiting to be reaped. */
async function gone(pid: number): Promise<boolean> {
  const row = (await listProcesses([pid])).find((candidate) => candidate.pid === pid);
  return row === undefined || row.stat.startsWith('Z');
}

/** A pid a tool wrote, once the file holds a whole line. */
async function pidFrom(file: string): Promise<number> {
  let text = '';
  await until(() => {
    try {
      text = readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
    } catch {
      return false;
    }
    return text.endsWith('\n');
  });
  return Number(text.trim());
}

/** Follows a session's events as the controller does: whether a turn runs, and a wait for its end. */
function follow(session: AgentSession) {
  const events: AgentEvent[] = [];
  let inTurn = false;
  const waiters: (() => void)[] = [];
  void (async () => {
    for await (const event of session.events) {
      events.push(event);
      if (event.type === 'turn_started') inTurn = true;
      if (event.type === 'turn_ended') {
        inTurn = false;
        for (const waiter of waiters.splice(0)) waiter();
      }
    }
  })();
  return {
    events,
    turnEnded: () => (inTurn ? new Promise<void>((resolve) => waiters.push(resolve)) : Promise.resolve()),
    started: () => until(() => inTurn),
  };
}

/** A fake agent in a clone directory, started as the runner starts agents, with its recorded identity. */
async function startAgent(script: FakeScript) {
  const dir = tempDir('agflow-ladder-');
  const clone = join(dir, 'T-4-a1');
  mkdirSync(clone);
  const adapter = new FakeAdapter({ script, transcriptDir: join(dir, 'transcripts') });
  const session = await adapter.start({
    attemptId: 'T-4-a1',
    role: 'worker',
    model: 'fake-model',
    cliVersion: '9.9.9',
    clone,
    baseCheckout: null,
    projectConfigVerified: true,
    tmpDir: dir,
    env: { PATH: process.env.PATH ?? '/usr/bin:/bin', HOME: dir },
    bridge: { command: '/bin/false', args: [], env: {} },
    profile: standardProfile,
    brief: 'brief',
    firstPrompt: 'start working',
    resume: null,
    logFile: join(dir, 'T-4-a1.log'),
    registerProcess: (pid) => killLater(pid),
  });
  const identity = (await processIdentity(session.pid)) as ProcessIdentity;
  return { dir, clone, session, identity, turns: follow(session) };
}

const LONG_SLEEP = { do: 'sleep', ms: 30_000 } as const;

describe('runStopLadder', () => {
  test('close, SIGTERM and SIGKILL each end the agent that ignores the step before', async () => {
    const polite = await startAgent({ turns: [[LONG_SLEEP]] });
    await polite.turns.started();
    const closed = await runStopLadder({
      session: polite.session,
      turnEnded: polite.turns.turnEnded,
      groups: async () => [polite.identity],
      clone: polite.clone,
      timings: TIMINGS,
    });
    expect(closed).toMatchObject({ stoppedBy: 'close', exit: { code: 0, signal: null } });
    expect(polite.turns.events.some((event) => event.type === 'turn_ended' && event.outcome === 'interrupted')).toBe(
      true,
    );

    const stubborn = await startAgent({ turns: [[LONG_SLEEP]], ignoreInterrupt: true, ignoreEofMidTurn: true });
    await stubborn.turns.started();
    const terminated = await runStopLadder({
      session: stubborn.session,
      turnEnded: stubborn.turns.turnEnded,
      groups: async () => [stubborn.identity],
      clone: stubborn.clone,
      timings: TIMINGS,
    });
    // A SIGTERMed claude exits 143, not by signal; stoppedBy says it was asked to.
    expect(terminated).toMatchObject({ stoppedBy: 'sigterm', exit: { code: 143, signal: null } });

    const deaf = await startAgent({
      turns: [[LONG_SLEEP]],
      ignoreInterrupt: true,
      ignoreEofMidTurn: true,
      ignoreSigterm: true,
    });
    await deaf.turns.started();
    const killed = await runStopLadder({
      session: deaf.session,
      turnEnded: deaf.turns.turnEnded,
      groups: async () => [deaf.identity],
      clone: deaf.clone,
      timings: TIMINGS,
    });
    expect(killed).toMatchObject({ stoppedBy: 'sigkill', exit: { signal: 'SIGKILL' } });
    expect(killed.killed).toContain(deaf.identity.pgid);
  }, 60_000);

  test('the interrupt cancels queued input, so a message sent mid-turn starts no second turn', async () => {
    const agent = await startAgent({ turns: [[LONG_SLEEP], [LONG_SLEEP]], ignoreEofMidTurn: true });
    await agent.turns.started();
    await agent.session.send({ id: '41', text: 'one more thing', authority: 'person' });
    const result = await runStopLadder({
      session: agent.session,
      turnEnded: agent.turns.turnEnded,
      groups: async () => [agent.identity],
      clone: agent.clone,
      timings: TIMINGS,
    });
    expect(result.stoppedBy).toBe('close');
    expect(agent.turns.events.filter((event) => event.type === 'turn_started')).toHaveLength(1);
  }, 60_000);

  test('an agent that exits on the interrupt was stopped by interrupt, and is never closed', async () => {
    let exit!: (info: ExitInfo) => void;
    let closes = 0;
    const session = {
      exited: new Promise<ExitInfo>((resolve) => {
        exit = resolve;
      }),
      interrupt: async () => exit({ code: 0, signal: null }),
      close: async () => {
        closes += 1;
      },
    };
    const result = await runStopLadder({
      session,
      // The turn's end is never seen: the exit alone settles the step.
      turnEnded: () => new Promise<void>(() => {}),
      groups: async () => [],
      clone: null,
      timings: TIMINGS,
    });
    expect(result).toEqual({
      stoppedBy: 'interrupt',
      exit: { code: 0, signal: null },
      killed: [],
      swept: [],
      sweepSkipped: null,
    });
    expect(closes).toBe(0);
  });

  test('a close that never returns does not hold the ladder: SIGTERM and SIGKILL still follow in bounds', async () => {
    const agent = await startAgent({
      turns: [[LONG_SLEEP]],
      ignoreInterrupt: true,
      ignoreEofMidTurn: true,
      ignoreSigterm: true,
    });
    await agent.turns.started();
    const began = performance.now();
    const result = await runStopLadder({
      session: {
        interrupt: (options) => agent.session.interrupt(options),
        // Like an adapter whose close waits for the CLI to exit.
        close: () => new Promise<void>(() => {}),
        exited: agent.session.exited,
      },
      turnEnded: agent.turns.turnEnded,
      groups: async () => [agent.identity],
      clone: agent.clone,
      timings: TIMINGS,
    });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ stoppedBy: 'sigkill', exit: { signal: 'SIGKILL' } });
    expect(performance.now() - began).toBeLessThan(TIMINGS.stopInterrupt + TIMINGS.stopClose + TIMINGS.stopKill + 2_500);
  }, 60_000);

  test('an agent that already exited was stopped by none', async () => {
    const agent = await startAgent({ turns: [[{ do: 'exit', code: 3 }]] });
    await agent.session.exited;
    const result = await runStopLadder({
      session: agent.session,
      turnEnded: agent.turns.turnEnded,
      groups: async () => [agent.identity],
      clone: agent.clone,
      timings: TIMINGS,
    });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ stoppedBy: 'none', exit: { code: 3 } });
  });

  test.skipIf(process.platform !== 'darwin')(
    'a tool group dies with the agent, and a detached process left in the clone is swept (the runner supports darwin-arm64 only; design 7.1)',
    async () => {
      requireLsofOnMacOS();
      const outside = tempDir('agflow-ladder-outside-');
      const toolPid = join(outside, 'tool.pid');
      const leftPid = join(outside, 'left.pid');
      const scripted = await startAgent({
        turns: [
          [
            // Its own group, working outside the clone: only the group kill reaches it.
            { do: 'tool', command: `cd / && echo $$ > '${toolPid}' && exec sleep 30`, wait: false },
            // Left behind in the clone by a shell that has exited: only the sweep finds it.
            { do: 'tool', command: `sleep 30 >/dev/null 2>&1 & echo $! > '${leftPid}'` },
            LONG_SLEEP,
          ],
        ],
      });
      const tool = await pidFrom(toolPid);
      const left = await pidFrom(leftPid);
      killLater(tool);
      cleanups.push(() => {
        try {
          process.kill(left, 'SIGKILL');
        } catch {
          // Already gone.
        }
      });
      const tracker = new DescendantTracker();
      await tracker.snapshot([scripted.identity]);
      expect(tracker.groups().map((group) => group.pgid)).toContain(tool);
      const result = await runStopLadder({
        session: scripted.session,
        turnEnded: scripted.turns.turnEnded,
        groups: async () => {
          await tracker.snapshot([scripted.identity]);
          return tracker.groups();
        },
        clone: scripted.clone,
        timings: TIMINGS,
      });
      expect(result.stoppedBy).toBe('close');
      expect(result.killed).toContain(tool);
      expect(result.swept).toContain(left);
      await until(() => gone(tool));
      await until(() => gone(left));
    },
    60_000,
  );

  test('a recorded group whose leader identity changed is not signalled', async () => {
    const elsewhere = tempDir('agflow-ladder-elsewhere-');
    const bystander = Bun.spawn(['sh', '-c', 'exec sleep 30'], {
      cwd: elsewhere,
      detached: true,
      stdin: 'ignore',
      stdout: 'ignore',
      stderr: 'ignore',
    });
    killLater(bystander.pid);
    const real = (await processIdentity(bystander.pid)) as ProcessIdentity;
    const reused = { ...real, lstart: 'Thu Jan  1 00:00:00 1970' };
    const agent = await startAgent({
      turns: [[LONG_SLEEP]],
      ignoreInterrupt: true,
      ignoreEofMidTurn: true,
      ignoreSigterm: true,
    });
    await agent.turns.started();
    const result = await runStopLadder({
      session: agent.session,
      turnEnded: agent.turns.turnEnded,
      groups: async () => [agent.identity, reused],
      clone: agent.clone,
      timings: TIMINGS,
    });
    expect(result.stoppedBy).toBe('sigkill');
    expect(result.killed).not.toContain(real.pgid);
    expect(await processIdentity(bystander.pid)).toEqual(real);
  }, 60_000);

  test.skipIf(process.platform !== 'darwin')(
    'returns within its bounds while an escaped grandchild holds the pipes open (the runner supports darwin-arm64 only; design 7.1)',
    async () => {
      requireLsofOnMacOS();
      const agent = await startAgent({
        turns: [[{ do: 'tool', command: 'exec sleep 30', wait: false, inheritPipes: true }, LONG_SLEEP]],
        ignoreInterrupt: true,
        ignoreEofMidTurn: true,
        ignoreSigterm: true,
      });
      await until(() => agent.turns.events.some((event) => event.type === 'tool_ended'));
      const began = performance.now();
      const result = await runStopLadder({
        session: agent.session,
        turnEnded: agent.turns.turnEnded,
        groups: async () => [agent.identity],
        clone: agent.clone,
        timings: TIMINGS,
      });
      const elapsed = performance.now() - began;
      expect(result.stoppedBy).toBe('sigkill');
      // Three steps of 400 ms, the bounded wait for the killed agent, and the sweep.
      expect(elapsed).toBeLessThan(TIMINGS.stopInterrupt + TIMINGS.stopClose + TIMINGS.stopKill + 2_500);
      expect(result.swept.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    },
    60_000,
  );
});

describe('killAndSweep', () => {
  test.skipIf(process.platform !== 'darwin')(

    async () => {

    const real = (await processIdentity(bystander.pid)) as ProcessIdentity;
    const clone = join(tempDir('agflow-ladder-link-'), 'T-4-a1');
    symlinkSync(home, clone);
    const result = await killAndSweep({ groups: async () => [], clone });
    expect(result).toEqual({ killed: [], swept: [], sweepSkipped: 'the clone path is not a directory' });
    expect(await processIdentity(bystander.pid)).toEqual(real);

    // A sweep that cannot run, such as one of a clone path too wide to sweep, is reported, not thrown.
    const wide = await killAndSweep({ groups: async () => [], clone: '/usr' });
    expect(wide.sweepSkipped).toMatch(/^the sweep failed: refusing to sweep/);
    expect(await processIdentity(bystander.pid)).toEqual(real);
  }, 60_000);
});
```

```ts
// The stop ladder (design 7.4, 8.4, 9.4): one function every stop uses. Each step waits a bounded time for the agent
// to exit and records what ended it in stoppedBy, core's STOPPED_BY: a SIGTERMed claude exits 143, not by signal,
// and exit code 0 does not mean a clean finish, so stoppedBy, not the exit, says whether the runner asked. Whatever
// step ends the agent, the recorded groups are then SIGKILLed and the clone is swept, so no tool outlives a stop.
// Every group kill checks the leader's identity first, because macOS PIDs wrap. Nothing waits on the agent's pipes,
// nor on the vendor's close: an escaped grandchild that inherited them, or a close that never returns, must not hold
// a stop. The sweep never follows the clone path's last component, which the agent can replace with a link.
import { lstat } from 'node:fs/promises';
import type { StoppedBy } from '@agflow/core';
import type { AgentSession, ExitInfo } from './adapters/types';
import type { RunnerTimings } from './config';
import { boundedWait, killGroup, type ProcessIdentity, sweepCloneProcesses } from './processes';

/** How long a SIGKILLed agent's exit is waited for: the kill is immediate, but its exit report may not be. */
export const EXIT_AFTER_KILL_MS = 1_000;

export interface KillAndSweepInput {
  /**
   * The groups to signal, read at each step so a group recorded meanwhile is included: the attempt's recorded
   * groups and those its descendant snapshots found.
   */
  groups(): Promise<readonly ProcessIdentity[]>;
  /** The clone whose processes are swept; null sweeps nothing. */
  clone: string | null;
}

export interface KillAndSweepResult {
  /** The groups SIGKILLed: those whose leader identity still matched. */
  killed: number[];
  /** The processes the sweep killed. */
  swept: number[];
  /** Why no sweep ran: a missing lsof, a clone path that is not a directory, or a sweep that failed. */
  sweepSkipped: string | null;
}

export interface StopLadderInput extends KillAndSweepInput {
  session: Pick<AgentSession, 'interrupt' | 'close' | 'exited'>;
  /** Resolves once no turn is running; the caller reads the session's events. */
  turnEnded(): Promise<void>;
  timings: Pick<RunnerTimings, 'stopInterrupt' | 'stopClose' | 'stopKill'>;
}

export interface StopLadderResult extends KillAndSweepResult {
  stoppedBy: StoppedBy;
  /** null when the agent's exit was not reported within the last bound. */
  exit: ExitInfo | null;
}

/** Signals every group whose leader identity still matches; gives the pgids signalled. */
async function signalGroups(groups: readonly ProcessIdentity[], name: NodeJS.Signals): Promise<number[]> {
  const signalled: number[] = [];
  for (const group of groups) {
    if (signalled.includes(group.pgid)) continue;
    if (await killGroup(group, name)) signalled.push(group.pgid);
  }
  return signalled;
}

/**
 * Ladder steps 3 and 4 alone: SIGKILL every group that passes the identity check, then sweep the clone. Exits the
 * runner did not request run this before the final harvest, so no orphaned tool writes during or after it (X-15).
 */
export async function killAndSweep(input: KillAndSweepInput): Promise<KillAndSweepResult> {
  const killed = await signalGroups(await input.groups(), 'SIGKILL');
  if (input.clone === null) return { killed, swept: [], sweepSkipped: null };
  // A link or a file the agent put in the clone's place is not swept: through it the sweep would kill the owner's
  // processes wherever it points.
  const stat = await lstat(input.clone).catch(() => null);
  if (stat !== null && !stat.isDirectory()) {
    return { killed, swept: [], sweepSkipped: 'the clone path is not a directory' };
  }
  try {
    const sweep = await sweepCloneProcesses(input.clone);
    return { killed, swept: sweep.killed, sweepSkipped: sweep.skipped };
  } catch (error) {
    // The agent is gone either way; a sweep that cannot run must not fail its stop or its exit.
    const detail = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
    return { killed, swept: [], sweepSkipped: `the sweep failed: ${detail}` };
  }
}

/** Runs a request to the agent, which may already be gone; it never fails the stop. */
async function ask(request: () => Promise<void>): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await request();
  } catch {
    // The agent's input is closed or the agent has exited: the next step's wait tells.
  }
}

/**
 * Stops an agent: the protocol interrupt, up to stopInterrupt for the turn to end; the vendor's own close, up to
 * stopClose for the exit; SIGTERM to every recorded group, up to stopKill; then SIGKILL to every recorded group and
 * a sweep of the clone. Returns within the sum of those bounds, EXIT_AFTER_KILL_MS and the sweep.
 */
export async function runStopLadder(input: StopLadderInput): Promise<StopLadderResult> {
  const { session, timings } = input;
  const finish = async (stoppedBy: StoppedBy, exit: ExitInfo | null): Promise<StopLadderResult> => ({
    stoppedBy,
    exit,
    ...(await killAndSweep(input)),
  });
  const exitWithin = async (ms: number, also?: Promise<unknown>) => {
    const waited = await boundedWait(also ? Promise.race([session.exited, also]) : session.exited, ms);
    if (!waited.done) return null;
    // Only the exit itself, not the end of the turn, settles the step.
    const exited = await boundedWait(session.exited, 0);
    return exited.done ? exited.value : null;
  };

  const already = await boundedWait(session.exited, 0);
  if (already.done) return finish('none', already.value);

  // 1. The interrupt, cancelling queued input so no message or continuation starts a turn.
  const turnOver = (async () => {
    await ask(() => session.interrupt({ cancelQueued: true }));
    await ask(() => input.turnEnded());
  })();
  const interrupted = await exitWithin(timings.stopInterrupt, turnOver);
  if (interrupted) return finish('interrupt', interrupted);

  // 2. The vendor's own close: stdin EOF ends app-server and its commands, and an idle claude. The close itself is
  // not waited for, only the exit: a close that never returns must not keep the ladder from SIGTERM.
  void ask(() => session.close());
  const closed = await exitWithin(timings.stopClose);
  if (closed) return finish('close', closed);

  // 3. SIGTERM to every recorded group, then SIGKILL.
  await signalGroups(await input.groups(), 'SIGTERM');
  const terminated = await exitWithin(timings.stopKill);
  if (terminated) return finish('sigterm', terminated);
  const result = await finish('sigkill', null);
  const killed = await boundedWait(session.exited, EXIT_AFTER_KILL_MS);
  return { ...result, exit: killed.done ? killed.value : null };
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run the tests and see them pass**

Run: `bun test packages/runner/test/stop-ladder.test.ts && bun test && bun run typecheck`
Expected: on macOS, 10 pass, 0 fail, no skips across 1 file (30 expect() calls); then the whole suite passes (`0 fail`) and `tsc` exits 0.

Every exit ends with `killAndSweep`, so a tool group that outlived a polite close still dies. `close()` is not awaited; only the exit is, bounded by `stopClose`. In production, an invalid clone directory or unavailable `lsof` yields a skipped-sweep reason. The three macOS sweep cases call `requireLsofOnMacOS` before creating fixtures, so a missing prerequisite fails those tests. macOS must execute every clone-sweep, orphan-cleanup and hand-back security assertion. Missing lsof on macOS fails with a prerequisite diagnostic. Keep portable cases enabled on Linux; macOS-only cases use test.skipIf(process.platform !== 'darwin') with the reason ‘the runner supports darwin-arm64 only; design 7.1’. Never omit individual safety assertions or return early because lsof is missing on macOS.

### Task 20: Stall facts

A `FactsTracker` per attempt produces design 6.8's `AttemptFacts` on the awake clock (design 7.5): phase, event age, the tool in flight with its cap from core's `capForCommand` (X-18), file and commit ages from watches on the clone, turns, turns without progress from a diff fingerprint, repeated calls, continuations, vendor-error time, `activeMs` and context use. `activeMs` counts only the phases `starting` and `turn` (X-35). The controller drives the phase; the tracker never infers it.
