```ts
    expect(userTexts(f, 'T-4-a1')[1]).toBe(handoffPrompt('the runner is stopping'));
    expect(exitsOf(f, 'T-5-a1')[0]?.data).toMatchObject({ cause: 'runner_stop', handoffWritten: false });
    expect(userTexts(f, 'T-5-a1')).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(exitsOf(f, 'T-6-a1')[0]?.data).toMatchObject({ cause: 'suspend', handoffWritten: false });
    expect(f.store.get('T-6-a1')?.state).toBe('suspended');
    expect(f.store.get('T-5-a1')?.state).toBe('stopped');
  });

  test('a stop after the process already exited reports nothing twice; a stale fence is refused', async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture();
    const controller = await started(f);
    expect(await controller.stop({ ...STOP, fence: { epoch: 1, counter: 0 } })).toEqual({
      ok: false,
      error: 'stale_fence',
    });
    process.kill(-(controller.session?.pid as number), 'SIGKILL');
    await waitFor(() => exitsOf(f).length === 1);
    await controller.settled();
    expect(await controller.stop(STOP)).toEqual({ ok: false, error: 'not_running' });
    expect(await controller.hold({ fence: FENCE })).toEqual({ ok: false, error: 'not_running' });
    expect(await controller.stopForRunner('runner_stop', { handoff: true })).toEqual({ ok: false, error: 'not_running' });
    expect(exitsOf(f)).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  test("an exit is dealt with while an escaped process still holds the agent's pipes", async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({
      script: {
        turns: [[{ do: 'tool', command: 'exec sleep 30', wait: false, inheritPipes: true }, { do: 'exit', code: 0 }]],
      },
    });
    const controller = f.controller();
    await controller.start(f.spec());
    const began = performance.now();
    await waitFor(() => exitsOf(f).length === 1, 10_000);
    expect(performance.now() - began).toBeLessThan(8_000);
    expect(exitsOf(f)[0]?.data).toMatchObject({ code: 0, stoppedBy: 'none' });
  }, 60_000);

  test('an agent that exits by itself during the stop is reported once', async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({
      config: { timings: { stopInterrupt: 10_000 } },
      // The second input releases the scripted exit, only once the ladder enters its interrupt step.
      script: { turns: [[], [{ do: 'exit', code: 3 }]] },
    });
    const controller = f.controller();
    await controller.start(f.spec());
    await waitFor(() => f.events('attempt.activity').some((event) => event.data.summary.startsWith('turn completed')));
    const session = controller.session!;
    session.interrupt = async (options) => {
      expect(options).toEqual({ cancelQueued: true });
      await session.send({ id: 'exit-during-stop', text: 'release the exit', authority: 'system' });
      // EOF and exited are independent signals. Keep the interrupt pending until the exit promise settles,
      // so an earlier EOF cannot advance the ladder to close while the fake adapter removes its script file.
      await session.exited;

    expect(await controller.stop({ ...STOP, handoff: false })).toMatchObject({ ok: true, stoppedBy: 'interrupt' });
    await controller.settled();
    expect(exitsOf(f)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(exitsOf(f)[0]?.data).toMatchObject({ code: 3, stoppedBy: 'interrupt' });
  });
});
```

**File:** `packages/runner/src/attempt/stop.ts` (new)

```ts
// Stops of a live agent (design 6.8, Replacement steps 1-3; 6.13, Hold; 6.4, the runner's own stops; 7.1). Every
// stop prepares the agent, then runs the stop ladder (stop-ladder.ts), and the controller's exit work follows:
// - stop_attempt: when interruptFirst is set or a tool is in flight, the turn is interrupted, queued input dropped,
//   and its end waited for (up to stopInterrupt); with handoff, a handoff note is asked for as its own turn and
//   waited for up to the hub's handoff time, until write_handoff, the end of the turn that took the prompt (its
//   acknowledged event), or the agent's end. A prompt sent while a turn still runs waits for that turn to end, and
//   is then taken as the next one. A note written before the stop arrived does not count: the stop asks again.
//   Every call to the agent is bounded too, so an agent whose control channel no longer answers reaches the ladder.
// - hold_attempt: no further continuation; the running turn may end by itself (up to hold), so the agent sees its
//   submit's result; then the ladder, with no handoff turn. Clone and session stay, as after every stop.
// - The runner's own stops (X-41): runner_stop with a handoff turn (agflow runner stop and uninstall) or without one
//   (the disk and battery guards), and suspend without one (SIGTERM), each reported as attempt.exited.cause.
// The runner removes a clone and its session only on cleanup_attempt, so keepClone needs nothing of a stop: the
// hub sends it so that a stopped-and-held attempt keeps its clone for a person's take-over.
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import type { ExitCause, StoppedBy } from '@agflow/core';
import type { AgentEvent, AgentSession } from '../adapters/types';
import { boundedWait } from '../processes';

/** The reason a runner's own stop gives in its handoff prompt. */
export const RUNNER_STOP_REASON = 'the runner is stopping';

export interface StopOptions {
  /** Ask for a handoff note as its own turn before the ladder (design 6.8). */
  handoff: boolean;
  /** Interrupt the running turn first, even with no tool in flight (stuck tools, quiet agents, loops). */
  interruptFirst: boolean;
  /** Why the attempt stops, as the hub or the runner words it; the handoff prompt quotes it. */
  reason: string;
  /** attempt.exited.cause: the runner's own stops; null for the hub's. */
  cause: ExitCause | null;
}

/** What a stop did: the step that ended the agent and the seq of its attempt.exited, or why nothing was stopped. */
export type StopOutcome =
  | { ok: true; stoppedBy: StoppedBy; exitedSeq: number }
  | { ok: false; error: 'stale_fence' | 'not_running' };

/** The handoff turn's prompt: the hub's or the runner's reason, then what the note must hold. */
export function handoffPrompt(reason: string): string {
  return (
    `agflow is stopping this attempt: ${reason}. Do not start new work. Call write_handoff now with a handoff note ` +
    'for whoever continues: what you did, what is left, what you were about to do next, and anything that surprised ' +
    'you. Your uncommitted work is saved for them.'
  );
}

/**
 * A live agent's turns as stops and holds follow them: whether a turn runs, and waits for events to come. The
 * controller feeds it every event after the pump has handled it, and ends it when the agent's events end, which
 * settles every wait.
 */
export class TurnWatch {
  private running = false;
  private ended = false;
  private readonly waiters = new Set<{ match: (event: AgentEvent) => boolean; resolve: () => void }>();

  /** Whether a turn is running. */
  get inTurn(): boolean {
    return this.running;
  }

  observe(event: AgentEvent): void {
    if (event.type === 'turn_started') this.running = true;
    if (event.type === 'turn_ended') this.running = false;
    for (const waiter of [...this.waiters]) {
      if (!waiter.match(event)) continue;
      this.waiters.delete(waiter);
      waiter.resolve();
    }
  }

  /** The agent's events have ended: no turn runs, and every wait is over. */
  end(): void {
    this.ended = true;
    this.running = false;
    for (const waiter of this.waiters) waiter.resolve();
    this.waiters.clear();
  }

  /** Resolves on the next event that matches, or when the events end. */
  until(match: (event: AgentEvent) => boolean): Promise<void> {
    if (this.ended) return Promise.resolve();
    return new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
      this.waiters.add({ match, resolve });
    });
  }

  /** Resolves once no turn runs. */
  turnEnded(): Promise<void> {
    return this.running ? this.until((event) => event.type === 'turn_ended') : Promise.resolve();
  }
}

export interface PrepareStopInput {
  session: Pick<AgentSession, 'interrupt' | 'send'>;
  watch: TurnWatch;
  /** Whether a tool call is in flight now. */
  toolInFlight(): boolean;
  /** Whether the agent has written a handoff note since the stop arrived. */
  handoffWritten(): boolean;
  options: Pick<StopOptions, 'handoff' | 'interruptFirst' | 'reason'>;
  /** Ms the interrupt and the interrupted turn's end are waited for: stopInterrupt. */
  interruptMs: number;
  /** Ms the handoff note is waited for, the prompt's send included: the hub's handoffMs. */
  handoffMs: number;
}

/**
 * Steps 1 and 2 of a replacement (design 6.8): the interrupt when a tool is in flight or interruptFirst is set,
 * then the handoff turn. Every wait is bounded; an agent that is gone, or does not answer, only ends them early.
 */
export async function prepareForStop(input: PrepareStopInput): Promise<void> {
  const { session, watch, options } = input;
  if (watch.inTurn && (options.interruptFirst || input.toolInFlight())) {
    // Queued input is dropped, so no message or continuation starts another turn first.
    const interrupted = session.interrupt({ cancelQueued: true }).catch(() => {});
    await boundedWait(Promise.all([interrupted, watch.turnEnded()]), input.interruptMs);
  }
  if (!options.handoff || input.handoffWritten()) return;
  const deadline = performance.now() + input.handoffMs;
  const remaining = () => Math.max(0, deadline - performance.now());
  const id = randomUUID();
  const written = watch.until((event) => event.type === 'tool_ended' && event.terminal === 'handoff');
  // The prompt's own turn: the one that took it ends with its acknowledged event, whether it ran next or the
  // running turn folded the prompt in at a tool boundary.
  const answered = watch.until((event) => event.type === 'acknowledged' && event.id === id);
  const sent = await boundedWait(
    session.send({ id, text: handoffPrompt(options.reason), authority: 'system' }).then(
      () => true,
      () => false,
    ),
    remaining(),
  );
  // The agent is gone, or does not take input: the ladder finds it so.
  if (!sent.done || !sent.value) return;
  await boundedWait(Promise.race([written, answered]), remaining());
}
```

### Task 28: The attempt controller: continuation, vendor errors, quota waits and the outage nudge

Runner-side turn policy (design 6.8, 6.10, 7.1). A worker whose turn completed with no terminal tool and no stop or hold within `continuationWait` gets a continuation listing its acceptance ids: never after a failed or interrupted turn, never for leads, and with the link down only after the next welcome; each turn that ended because of an outage gets one 'the agflow hub is reachable again' message after the next welcome (X-38). Vendor errors retry with doubling backoff in phase `vendor_error`. A limit hit, or paid usage while `allowPaidUsage` is off, interrupts the turn, sets `quota_wait` and reports `attempt.quota`; the turn resumes at `resetsAt`, or every `quotaUnknown`, with `attempt.quota` state `ok` (X-14). The wait ends only once the runner's clock reaches its end: its timer is armed for at most 2^31 - 1 ms, and armed again while time is left, so neither a far reset nor a timer that fires early ends it. Auth, context, policy, denials and session-budget outcomes become `attempt.vendor_outcome` (X-31). The two `quotaUnknown` timestamp assertions allow 1 ms of Bun timer/`Date.now()` rounding; production still checks the exact deadline and re-arms an early timer.

```ts
import { afterEach, describe, expect, jest, setDefaultTimeout, test } from 'bun:test';
import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import {
  type AttemptPhase,
  type AttemptSpec,
  TEST_ACCOUNT_ID,
  VENDOR_OUTCOME_KINDS,
  type VendorQuota,
} from '@agflow/core';
import type { FakeScript, FakeStep, TranscriptLine } from '@agflow/testkit';
import type { PumpEvent } from '../src/attempt/pump';
import {
  continuationPrompt,
  OUTAGE_NUDGE,
  QUOTA_RESUME_PROMPT,
  TurnPolicy,
  vendorRetryDelay,
  vendorRetryPrompt,
} from '../src/attempt/turns';
import { DEFAULT_TIMINGS } from '../src/config';
import { noopLogger } from '../src/log';
import {
  cleanupRunnerFixtures,
  createRunnerFixture as createFixture,
  FIXTURE_PROJECT,
  type RunnerFixture,
  type RunnerFixtureOptions,
  waitFor,
} from './fixture';

afterEach(cleanupRunnerFixtures);

// Every test here runs git or agent processes, which take several times as long on a machine loaded by other suites.
setDefaultTimeout(30_000);

/** The fixture, with a continuationWait of 100 ms unless the options give one. */
function createRunnerFixture(options: RunnerFixtureOptions = {}): Promise<RunnerFixture> {
  const timings = { continuationWait: 100, ...options.config?.timings };
  return createFixture({ ...options, config: { ...options.config, timings } });
}

const PROMPT = 'Start working on T-4.';
const LONG_SLEEP = { do: 'sleep', ms: 30_000 } as const;
const DAY_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1_000;
const SUBMIT = { do: 'terminal', tool: 'submit' } as const;

/** A worker spec of task T-<n>, attempt a1. */
function specOf(f: RunnerFixture, n: number, overrides: Partial<AttemptSpec> = {}): AttemptSpec {
  return f.spec({
    attemptId: `T-${n}-a1`,
    taskId: `T-${n}`,
    branch: `agflow/T-${n}-x`,
    wipRef: `refs/agflow/T-${n}/a1`,
    ...overrides,
  });
}

/** A script per attempt, by the number of its task. */
function scripts(byTask: Record<number, FakeScript>) {
  return (launch: { attemptId: string }): FakeScript => {
    const n = Number(launch.attemptId.match(/\d+/)?.[0]);
    const script = byTask[n];
    if (!script) throw new Error(`no script for ${launch.attemptId}`);
    return script;
  };
}

/** The user lines of the attempt's fake transcript so far. */
function userTexts(f: RunnerFixture, attemptId: string): string[] {
  const spawned = f.events('attempt.spawned').filter((event) => event.attemptId === attemptId);
  const sessionRef = spawned.at(-1)?.data.sessionRef;
  if (sessionRef === undefined) return [];
  const file = join(f.paths.clone(FIXTURE_PROJECT, attemptId), '.agflow', 'run', 'fake-transcripts', `${sessionRef}.jsonl`);
  if (!existsSync(file)) return [];
  return readFileSync(file, 'utf8')
    .split('\n')
    .filter((line) => line !== '')
    .map((line) => JSON.parse(line) as TranscriptLine)
    .filter((line) => line.role === 'user')
    .map((line) => line.text);
}

/**
 * Records, while it runs, when each user line of the attempt's transcript appeared (Date.now, as events' at): the
 * moments the agent took the runner's messages. stop(count) waits until count lines were seen, then stops.
 */
function watchUserTexts(f: RunnerFixture, attemptId: string): { times: number[]; stop(count: number): Promise<void> } {
  const times: number[] = [];
  const timer = setInterval(() => {
    const count = userTexts(f, attemptId).length;
    while (times.length < count) times.push(Date.now());
  }, 5);
  return {
    times,
    stop: async (count) => {
      await waitFor(() => times.length >= count);
      clearInterval(timer);
    },
  };
}

/** Turns ended so far: each ends with one turn or vendor_error activity. */
const turnsEnded = (f: RunnerFixture, attemptId: string) =>
  f.events('attempt.activity').filter(
    (event) => event.attemptId === attemptId && (event.data.kind === 'turn' || event.data.kind === 'vendor_error'),
  ).length;

const quotaOf = (overrides: Partial<VendorQuota>): VendorQuota => ({
  state: 'ok',
  resetsAt: null,
  windows: { fiveHour: 0.5, weekly: 0.2 },
  paidUsage: 'disabled',
  updatedAt: Date.now(),
  ...overrides,
});

describe('AttemptController: continuation', () => {
  test('a completed worker turn without a terminal tool gets one continuation listing the acceptance ids', async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({ script: { turns: [[], [SUBMIT]] } });
    const controller = f.controller();
    await controller.start(f.spec({ acceptanceIds: ['A1', 'A2'] }));
    await waitFor(() => turnsEnded(f, 'T-4-a1') === 2);
    await Bun.sleep(400);
    expect(userTexts(f, 'T-4-a1')).toEqual([PROMPT, continuationPrompt(['A1', 'A2'])]);
    expect(controller.facts()?.continuations).toBe(1);
    expect(continuationPrompt(['A1', 'A2'])).toContain('A1, A2');
  });

  test('no continuation after a failed or interrupted turn, a terminal tool, a hold or stop in the wait, or a lead', async () => {
    const terminal = (tool: 'submit' | 'blocked' | 'impossible' | 'released', answer?: 'refused') => ({
      turns: [[{ do: 'terminal' as const, tool, ...(answer ? { answer } : {}) }], [SUBMIT]],
    });
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({
      config: { timings: { continuationWait: 1_000 } },
      script: scripts({
        1: { turns: [[{ do: 'fail', kind: 'policy' }]] },
        2: { turns: [[LONG_SLEEP]] },
        3: terminal('submit'),
        4: terminal('blocked'),
        5: terminal('impossible'),
        6: terminal('released'),
        7: { turns: [[]] },
        8: { turns: [[]] },
        9: { turns: [[]] },
        10: terminal('submit', 'refused'),
      }),
    });
    const fence = { epoch: 1, counter: 1 };
    let interrupted: ReturnType<RunnerFixture['controller']> | null = null;
    for (const n of [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10]) {
      const controller = f.controller(`T-${n}-a1`);
      if (n === 2) interrupted = controller;
      await controller.start(specOf(f, n));
    }
    await f.controller('lead-a9').start(f.spec({ attemptId: 'lead-a9', taskId: null, role: 'lead', branch: null, wipRef: null }));
    await waitFor(() => interrupted?.phase === 'turn');
    expect(await interrupted?.interrupt({ fence })).toEqual({ ok: true });
    // A hold and a stop that arrive within continuationWait of the turn's end, and wait on the queue behind other
    // work past it: their arrival alone keeps the continuation back.
    const held = f.controller('T-7-a1');
    const stopped = f.controller('T-8-a1');
    await Promise.all([held.start(specOf(f, 7)), stopped.start(specOf(f, 8))]);
    await waitFor(() => turnsEnded(f, 'T-7-a1') === 1 && turnsEnded(f, 'T-8-a1') === 1);
    let release = () => {};
    const gate = new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
      release = resolve;
    });
    void f.queue.run('T-7-a1', () => gate);
    void f.queue.run('T-8-a1', () => gate);
    const holding = held.hold({ fence });
    const stopping = stopped.stop({ fence, reason: 'stopped', handoff: false, interruptFirst: false, keepClone: false });
    await Bun.sleep(1_500);
    expect(userTexts(f, 'T-7-a1')).toEqual([PROMPT]);
    expect(userTexts(f, 'T-8-a1')).toEqual([PROMPT]);
    release();
    expect(await holding).toMatchObject({ ok: true });
    expect(await stopping).toMatchObject({ ok: true });
    await waitFor(() => turnsEnded(f, 'T-10-a1') === 2, 8_000);
    await Bun.sleep(1_500);
    for (const n of [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]) expect([n, userTexts(f, `T-${n}-a1`)]).toEqual([n, [PROMPT]]);
    expect(userTexts(f, 'lead-a9')).toEqual([PROMPT]);
    // A refused submit is no terminal tool.
    expect(userTexts(f, 'T-10-a1')).toEqual([PROMPT, continuationPrompt(['A1'])]);
  }, 60_000);
});

describe('AttemptController: outages', () => {
  test('no continuation while the link is down or after a hub-unreachable answer; one nudge after the welcome', async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({
      script: scripts({
        1: { turns: [[], [SUBMIT]] },
        2: { turns: [[{ do: 'terminal', tool: 'submit', answer: 'hub_unreachable' }], [SUBMIT]] },
        3: { turns: [[LONG_SLEEP], [SUBMIT]] },
      }),
    });
    const down = f.controller('T-1-a1');
    const unreachable = f.controller('T-2-a1');
    const interrupted = f.controller('T-3-a1');
    f.link.up = false;
    await down.start(specOf(f, 1));
    await waitFor(() => turnsEnded(f, 'T-1-a1') === 1);
    await unreachable.start(specOf(f, 2));
    await interrupted.start(specOf(f, 3));
    await waitFor(() => turnsEnded(f, 'T-2-a1') === 1 && interrupted.phase === 'turn');
    // needs_login: the runner interrupts the turn and marks it for the nudge.
    await interrupted.interrupt({ outage: true });
    await waitFor(() => turnsEnded(f, 'T-3-a1') === 1);
    await Bun.sleep(300);
    for (const attemptId of ['T-1-a1', 'T-2-a1', 'T-3-a1']) expect(userTexts(f, attemptId)).toEqual([PROMPT]);
    f.link.up = true;
    for (const controller of [down, unreachable, interrupted]) await controller.onWelcome();
    for (const controller of [down, unreachable, interrupted]) await controller.onWelcome();
    await waitFor(() => [1, 2, 3].every((n) => turnsEnded(f, `T-${n}-a1`) === 2));
    await Bun.sleep(300);
    // The continuation that fell due while the link was down goes after the welcome; the others get the nudge.
    expect(userTexts(f, 'T-1-a1')).toEqual([PROMPT, continuationPrompt(['A1'])]);
    expect(userTexts(f, 'T-2-a1')).toEqual([PROMPT, OUTAGE_NUDGE]);
    expect(userTexts(f, 'T-3-a1')).toEqual([PROMPT, OUTAGE_NUDGE]);
    expect(OUTAGE_NUDGE).toBe('the agflow hub is reachable again; retry the tool that failed');
  });

  test('with the link up, a hub-unreachable answer gets one nudge when its turn ends and no continuation', async () => {
    const unreachable = { do: 'terminal', tool: 'submit', answer: 'hub_unreachable' } as const;
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({ script: { turns: [[unreachable], [unreachable], [SUBMIT]] } });
    const controller = f.controller();
    await controller.start(f.spec());
    await waitFor(() => turnsEnded(f, 'T-4-a1') === 2);
    // The second failure gets no second nudge before a welcome: a hub that keeps failing is no loop.
    await Bun.sleep(3 * 100 + 200);
    expect(userTexts(f, 'T-4-a1')).toEqual([PROMPT, OUTAGE_NUDGE]);
    await controller.onWelcome();
    await waitFor(() => turnsEnded(f, 'T-4-a1') === 3);
    await Bun.sleep(300);
    expect(userTexts(f, 'T-4-a1')).toEqual([PROMPT, OUTAGE_NUDGE, OUTAGE_NUDGE]);
  });

  test('a welcome that arrives while the marked turn still runs gives the nudge when that turn ends', async () => {
    const unreachable = { do: 'terminal', tool: 'submit', answer: 'hub_unreachable' } as const;
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({ script: { turns: [[unreachable, { do: 'sleep', ms: 600 }], [SUBMIT]] } });
    const controller = f.controller();
    f.link.up = false;
    await controller.start(f.spec());
    await waitFor(() => controller.phase === 'turn');
    await Bun.sleep(150);
    // The link as the policy reads it stays down: only the welcome says the hub is back.
    await controller.onWelcome();
    await waitFor(() => turnsEnded(f, 'T-4-a1') === 2);
    await Bun.sleep(300);
    expect(userTexts(f, 'T-4-a1')).toEqual([PROMPT, OUTAGE_NUDGE]);
  });
});

describe('AttemptController: vendor errors', () => {
  test('a vendor error sets vendor_error and retries with a doubling delay, outside every budget', async () => {
    const call = { do: 'tool', command: 'true' } as const;
    const failed: FakeStep[] = [call, { do: 'fail', kind: 'vendor', error: 'overloaded' }];
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({
      config: { timings: { vendorErrorBackoff: { base: 150, cap: 1_000 } } },
      script: { turns: [failed, failed, [call, LONG_SLEEP]] },
    });
    const controller = f.controller();
    await controller.start(f.spec());
    const taken = watchUserTexts(f, 'T-4-a1');
    await waitFor(() => controller.phase === 'vendor_error');
    await waitFor(() => userTexts(f, 'T-4-a1').length === 3 && controller.phase === 'turn', 5_000);
    await taken.stop(3);
    const retries = f.logger.entries.filter((entry) => entry.message.startsWith('the vendor failed the turn'));
    expect(retries.map((entry) => entry.fields.delayMs)).toEqual([150, 300]);
    // The waits themselves: from each failed turn's end to the agent taking the retry.
    const failedAt = f.events('attempt.activity')
      .filter((event) => event.data.kind === 'vendor_error')
      .map((event) => event.at);
    expect((taken.times[1] as number) - (failedAt[0] as number)).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(150);
    expect((taken.times[2] as number) - (failedAt[1] as number)).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(300);
    expect(userTexts(f, 'T-4-a1')).toEqual([PROMPT, vendorRetryPrompt('claude'), vendorRetryPrompt('claude')]);
    await waitFor(() => controller.facts()?.repeatedCalls === 1);
    expect(controller.facts()).toMatchObject({ continuations: 0, turnsWithoutProgress: 0, repeatedCalls: 1 });
    expect(f.events('attempt.activity').filter((event) => event.data.kind === 'vendor_error')).toHaveLength(2);
    // The defaults: 30 s, doubling, up to 10 minutes.
    expect([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 9].map((n) => vendorRetryDelay(n, DEFAULT_TIMINGS))).toEqual([
      30_000, 60_000, 120_000, 240_000, 480_000, 600_000, 600_000,
    ]);
  });
});

describe('AttemptController: quota', () => {
  test('a limit hit interrupts the turn, waits in quota_wait and resumes at resetsAt with attempt.quota ok', async () => {
    let resetsAt = 0;
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({
      script: () => {
        resetsAt = Date.now() + 1_200;
        const quota = quotaOf({ state: 'exhausted', resetsAt, windows: { fiveHour: 1, weekly: 0.4 } });
        return { turns: [[{ do: 'quota', quota, accountId: TEST_ACCOUNT_ID }, LONG_SLEEP], [SUBMIT]] };
      },
    });
    const controller = f.controller();
    await controller.start(f.spec());
    await waitFor(() => controller.phase === 'quota_wait');
    const [exhausted] = await waitFor(() => f.events('attempt.quota').length === 1 && f.events('attempt.quota'));
    expect(exhausted?.data).toMatchObject({ vendor: 'claude', accountId: TEST_ACCOUNT_ID, quota: { state: 'exhausted', resetsAt } });
    expect(controller.facts()?.phase).toBe('quota_wait');
    // The interrupted turn's end comes from the agent after the interrupt, so its note may follow the quota report.
    await waitFor(() => f.events('attempt.activity').some((event) => event.data.summary === 'turn interrupted'));
    await waitFor(() => turnsEnded(f, 'T-4-a1') === 2, 5_000);
    expect(Date.now()).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(resetsAt);
    const reports = f.events('attempt.quota');
    expect(reports.map((event) => event.data.quota.state)).toEqual(['exhausted', 'ok']);
    expect(reports[1]?.data.accountId).toBe(TEST_ACCOUNT_ID);
    expect(userTexts(f, 'T-4-a1')).toEqual([PROMPT, QUOTA_RESUME_PROMPT]);

  test('with an unknown reset the turn is retried every quotaUnknown', async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({

    const controller = f.controller();

    await waitFor(() => turnsEnded(f, 'T-4-a1') === 3, 20_000);
    await waitFor(() => userTexts(f, 'T-4-a1').length === 3);
    // Bun timers can fire 1 ms early against Date.now() (also seen on Linux). Allow that rounding in the
    // outbox timestamps; TurnPolicy.armWait itself re-arms an early timer against its own clock.
    const quotaAt = f.events('attempt.quota').map((event) => event.at);

    expect(reports.map((data) => [data.quota.state, data.quota.resetsAt, data.accountId])).toEqual([

    const controller = f.controller();
    await controller.start(f.spec());
    await waitFor(() => f.events('attempt.quota').length > 0 && turnsEnded(f, 'T-4-a1') > 0);
    await Bun.sleep(500);
    expect(f.events('attempt.quota').map((event) => [event.data.quota.state, event.data.quota.resetsAt])).toEqual([
      ['exhausted', resetsAt],
    ]);
    expect(controller.phase).toBe('quota_wait');
    expect(userTexts(f, 'T-4-a1')).toEqual([PROMPT]);
  });

  test('the wait of a far reset is armed again until the reset passes, then ends with the resume prompt', () => {
    jest.useFakeTimers();
    try {
      const reports: PumpEvent[] = [];
      const phases: AttemptPhase[] = [];
      const sent: string[] = [];
      const policy = new TurnPolicy({
        attemptId: 'T-4-a1',
        spec: () => ({ role: 'worker', vendor: 'claude', acceptanceIds: ['A1'] }),
        session: {
          send: async (message) => {
            sent.push(message.text);
          },
          interrupt: async () => {},
        },
        inTurn: () => false,
        stopping: () => false,
        linkUp: () => true,
        allowPaidUsage: () => false,
        timings: () => ({ ...DEFAULT_TIMINGS, quotaUnknown: 1_000 }),
        setPhase: (phase) => phases.push(phase),
        report: (event) => reports.push(event),
        continuationSent: () => {},
        logger: noopLogger,
      });
      const resetsAt = Date.now() + 30 * DAY_MS;
      const quota = quotaOf({ state: 'exhausted', resetsAt, updatedAt: Date.now() });
      policy.observe({ type: 'quota', accountId: TEST_ACCOUNT_ID, quota });
      const states = () => reports.flatMap((event) => (event.type === 'attempt.quota' ? [event.data.quota.state] : []));
      expect(states()).toEqual(['exhausted']);
      // Past the longest delay a timer takes, and on to a minute before the reset: the wait goes on.
      jest.advanceTimersByTime(2 ** 31);
      jest.advanceTimersByTime(resetsAt - Date.now() - 60_000);
      expect(states()).toEqual(['exhausted']);
      expect(phases).toEqual(['quota_wait']);
      expect(sent).toEqual([]);
      jest.advanceTimersByTime(60_000);
      expect(states()).toEqual(['exhausted', 'ok']);
      expect(phases).toEqual(['quota_wait', 'idle']);
      expect(sent).toEqual([QUOTA_RESUME_PROMPT]);
      policy.close();
    } finally {
      jest.useRealTimers();
    }
  });

  test('a wait of quotaUnknown never ends early by the runner clock, though its timer fires early', () => {
    jest.useFakeTimers();
    try {
      const reports: PumpEvent[] = [];
      // The runner's clock against the timers': a timer that fires early finds less time gone than it waited.
      let lag = 0;
      const policy = new TurnPolicy({
        attemptId: 'T-4-a1',
        spec: () => ({ role: 'worker', vendor: 'claude', acceptanceIds: ['A1'] }),
        session: { send: async () => {}, interrupt: async () => {} },
        inTurn: () => false,
        stopping: () => false,
        linkUp: () => true,
        allowPaidUsage: () => false,
        timings: () => ({ ...DEFAULT_TIMINGS, quotaUnknown: 1_000 }),
        setPhase: () => {},
        report: (event) => reports.push(event),
        continuationSent: () => {},
        logger: noopLogger,
        now: () => Date.now() - lag,
      });
      policy.observe({ type: 'quota', accountId: TEST_ACCOUNT_ID, quota: quotaOf({ state: 'exhausted', resetsAt: null }) });
      const states = () => reports.flatMap((event) => (event.type === 'attempt.quota' ? [event.data.quota.state] : []));
      lag = 5;
      jest.advanceTimersByTime(1_000);
      expect(states()).toEqual(['exhausted']);
      jest.advanceTimersByTime(5);
      expect(states()).toEqual(['exhausted', 'ok']);
      policy.close();
    } finally {
      jest.useRealTimers();
    }
  });

  test('the wait holds when the hit turn completes anyway, with no continuation and the account left alone', async () => {
    const paid = quotaOf({ paidUsage: 'in_use', resetsAt: Date.now() + 60_000 });
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({
      config: { allowPaidUsage: { claude: false, codex: false } },
      // The interrupt loses the race: the turn completes after the hit.
      script: { turns: [[{ do: 'quota', quota: paid, accountId: TEST_ACCOUNT_ID }]], ignoreInterrupt: true },
    });
    const controller = f.controller();
    await controller.start(f.spec());
    await waitFor(() => turnsEnded(f, 'T-4-a1') === 1);
    await Bun.sleep(600);
    expect(controller.phase).toBe('quota_wait');
    expect(userTexts(f, 'T-4-a1')).toEqual([PROMPT]);
    // Paid usage in use is this runner's refusal, not the account's exhaustion.
    expect(f.events('attempt.quota').map((event) => [event.data.quota.state, event.data.accountId])).toEqual([
      ['exhausted', null],
    ]);
  });

  test('a delivery during a paid-usage wait is interrupted and the wait goes on', async () => {
    const paid = quotaOf({ paidUsage: 'in_use', resetsAt: Date.now() + 60_000 });
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({
      config: { allowPaidUsage: { claude: false, codex: false } },
      script: { turns: [[{ do: 'quota', quota: paid }, LONG_SLEEP], [LONG_SLEEP]] },
    });
    const controller = f.controller();
    await controller.start(f.spec());
    await waitFor(() => controller.phase === 'quota_wait' && turnsEnded(f, 'T-4-a1') === 1);
    const message = { messageId: 7, authority: 'person' as const, text: 'how is it going?' };
    expect(await controller.deliver({ fence: { epoch: 1, counter: 1 }, messages: [message], more: 0 })).toEqual({ ok: true });
    await waitFor(() => turnsEnded(f, 'T-4-a1') === 2);
    await Bun.sleep(400);
    expect(controller.phase).toBe('quota_wait');
    const summaries = f.events('attempt.activity').map((event) => event.data.summary);
    expect(summaries.filter((summary) => summary === 'turn interrupted')).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(userTexts(f, 'T-4-a1')).toEqual([PROMPT, message.text]);
    expect(f.events('attempt.quota')).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  test('paid usage in use is a limit hit while allowPaidUsage is false for the vendor, for both vendors', async () => {
    const paid = quotaOf({ paidUsage: 'in_use', resetsAt: Date.now() + 60_000 });
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({
      config: { allowPaidUsage: { claude: false, codex: true } },
      script: { turns: [[{ do: 'quota', quota: paid }, { do: 'sleep', ms: 500 }]] },
    });
    const run = async (n: number, vendor: 'claude' | 'codex') => {
      const controller = f.controller(`T-${n}-a1`);
      await controller.start(specOf(f, n, { vendor }));
      await waitFor(() => turnsEnded(f, `T-${n}-a1`) === 1);
      return controller;
    };
    const claudeHit = await run(1, 'claude');
    const codexAllowed = await run(2, 'codex');
    f.config.allowPaidUsage = { claude: true, codex: false };
    const claudeAllowed = await run(3, 'claude');
    const codexHit = await run(4, 'codex');
    const hits = f.events('attempt.quota').map((event) => [event.attemptId, event.data.vendor, event.data.quota.state]);
    expect(hits).toEqual([
      ['T-1-a1', 'claude', 'exhausted'],
      ['T-4-a1', 'codex', 'exhausted'],
    ]);
    expect([claudeHit.phase, codexHit.phase]).toEqual(['quota_wait', 'quota_wait']);
    expect([claudeAllowed.phase, codexAllowed.phase]).not.toContain('quota_wait');
    const summaries = (attemptId: string) =>
      f.events('attempt.activity').filter((event) => event.attemptId === attemptId).map((event) => event.data.summary);
    expect(summaries('T-1-a1')).toContain('turn interrupted');
    expect(summaries('T-3-a1')).toContain('turn completed with 0 tool calls');
  });
});

describe('AttemptController: vendor outcomes', () => {
  test('auth, context, policy, denials and session_budget outcomes are reported with their detail', async () => {
    const byTask: Record<number, FakeScript> = {};
    VENDOR_OUTCOME_KINDS.forEach((kind, index) => {
      byTask[index + 1] = { turns: [[{ do: 'fail', kind, error: `the ${kind} detail` }]] };
    });
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({ script: scripts(byTask) });
    for (const [index] of VENDOR_OUTCOME_KINDS.entries()) await f.controller(`T-${index + 1}-a1`).start(specOf(f, index + 1));
    await waitFor(() => f.events('attempt.vendor_outcome').length === VENDOR_OUTCOME_KINDS.length);
    const outcomes = f.events('attempt.vendor_outcome').map((event) => [event.attemptId, event.data]);
    expect(outcomes).toEqual(
      VENDOR_OUTCOME_KINDS.map((kind, index) => [`T-${index + 1}-a1`, { kind, detail: `the ${kind} detail` }]),
    );
    await Bun.sleep(300);
    for (const [index] of VENDOR_OUTCOME_KINDS.entries()) expect(userTexts(f, `T-${index + 1}-a1`)).toEqual([PROMPT]);
  }, 60_000);
});
```

**File:** `packages/runner/src/attempt/turns.ts` (new)

```ts
// The runner's turn policy (design 6.8, 6.10, 7.1), one per live agent. It reads the agent's events after the pump
// and decides what the runner sends on its own:
// - Continuation: a worker whose turn completed normally, with no successful submit, declare_blocked,
//   declare_impossible or release_task, gets a continuation prompt listing the task's acceptance ids once
//   continuationWait has passed with no hold or stop arriving and no new turn. Never after a failed or interrupted
//   turn, for leads, or after a tool answered "hub unreachable". One due while the link is down waits for the next
//   welcome.
// - The outage nudge (X-38): an attempt whose turn ended because of an outage (a hub-unreachable answer, or the
//   runner's own interrupt in needs_login) gets one "the agflow hub is reachable again; retry the tool that failed"
//   once the hub is back: at the next welcome, or as soon as the turn ends when the link is up by then or a welcome
//   came during the turn. It is the only message after an outage, once per welcome.
// - Vendor errors: phase vendor_error, and the turn retried after a delay that doubles from 30 s to 10 minutes; such
//   turns count toward no continuation, no-progress or loop (the facts leave them out).
// - Quota (X-14): a limit hit, or paid usage in use while allowPaidUsage is false for the vendor, interrupts the
//   turn, sets quota_wait and reports attempt.quota; at resetsAt, however far ahead, or every quotaUnknown when the
//   reset is unknown or already past, the wait ends, attempt.quota reports state ok and the turn resumes. Until then
//   the wait holds: nothing is sent, and a turn that starts (a delivery's) is interrupted. A hit that is only paid
//   usage is reported with no account, since the account itself is not exhausted and allowPaidUsage is per runner.
// - Other vendor outcomes (auth, context, policy, denials, session_budget) are reported as attempt.vendor_outcome.
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import {
  type AttemptPhase,
  type AttemptSpec,
  VENDOR_OUTCOME_KINDS,
  type VendorOutcomeKind,
  type VendorQuota,
} from '@agflow/core';
import type { AgentEvent, AgentSession, TerminalTool } from '../adapters/types';
import { doublingDelay } from '../backoff';
import type { RunnerTimings } from '../config';
import type { Logger } from '../log';
import { clip, LONG_TEXT_MAX, type PumpEvent } from './pump';

/** The one message after an outage (X-38). */
export const OUTAGE_NUDGE = 'the agflow hub is reachable again; retry the tool that failed';

/** What resumes a turn once the usage limit has reset. */
export const QUOTA_RESUME_PROMPT = 'The usage limit has reset. Continue where you stopped.';

/** The longest delay a timer takes (2^31 - 1 ms, about 24.8 days): a longer one fires at once. */
const MAX_TIMER_MS = 2 ** 31 - 1;

/** The terminal tools whose success ends continuations: the handoff note does not. */
const ENDING_TOOLS: readonly TerminalTool[] = ['submit', 'blocked', 'impossible', 'released'];

/** The continuation prompt (design 6.8), naming the task's acceptance criteria. */
export function continuationPrompt(acceptanceIds: readonly string[]): string {
  const criteria =
    acceptanceIds.length === 0 ? 'its acceptance criteria' : `acceptance criteria ${acceptanceIds.join(', ')}`;
  return (
    `Continue working on your task until ${criteria} hold. Then call submit; if you cannot finish it, call ` +
    'declare_blocked or declare_impossible, or release_task to give it back.'
  );
}

/** The retry after a turn the vendor failed. */
export function vendorRetryPrompt(vendor: AttemptSpec['vendor']): string {
  return `Your last turn failed with an error from ${vendor}. Continue where you stopped.`;
}

/** The delay before vendor-error retry number attempt (from 0): 30 s doubling to 10 minutes by default. */
export function vendorRetryDelay(attempt: number, timings: Pick<RunnerTimings, 'vendorErrorBackoff'>): number {
  return doublingDelay(attempt, timings.vendorErrorBackoff);
}

/** A limit hit: an exhausted window, or paid usage in use where the owner does not allow it (design 6.10). */
export function isLimitHit(quota: VendorQuota, allowPaidUsage: boolean): boolean {
  return quota.state === 'exhausted' || (quota.paidUsage === 'in_use' && !allowPaidUsage);
}

export interface TurnPolicyOptions {
  attemptId: string;
  /** The attempt's spec as of its last start or resume: role, vendor and acceptance ids. */
  spec(): Pick<AttemptSpec, 'role' | 'vendor' | 'acceptanceIds'>;
  session: Pick<AgentSession, 'send' | 'interrupt'>;
  /** Whether a turn runs now. */
  inTurn(): boolean;
  /** A stop or hold arrived: nothing more is sent. */
  stopping(): boolean;
  /** Whether the link to the hub is up. */
  linkUp(): boolean;
  /** runner.json's allowPaidUsage for the attempt's vendor, as it is now. */
  allowPaidUsage(): boolean;
  timings(): Pick<RunnerTimings, 'continuationWait' | 'vendorErrorBackoff' | 'quotaUnknown'>;
  setPhase(phase: AttemptPhase): void;
  report(event: PumpEvent): void;
  /** Counts a continuation in the facts. */
  continuationSent(): void;
  logger: Logger;
  /** Date.now by default: resetsAt is epoch ms. */
  now?: () => number;
}

/** A limit hit the attempt waits on, and the account its reports name. */
interface QuotaWait {
  quota: VendorQuota;
  /** null for a hit that is only paid usage. */
  accountId: string | null;
}

export class TurnPolicy {
  private readonly options: TurnPolicyOptions;
  /** A continuation, a vendor-error retry or the outage nudge. */
  private timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
  /** The end of a quota wait; a new turn does not cancel it. */
  private quotaTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
  /** A submit, declare_blocked, declare_impossible or release_task succeeded: no continuation ever follows. */
  private ended = false;
  /** A tool of the running turn answered "hub unreachable". */
  private unreachable = false;
  /** A welcome arrived since that answer: the hub is back before the turn ends. */
  private returned = false;
  /** A turn ended because of an outage: the next welcome sends the nudge. */
  private outage = false;
  /** The nudge went out since the last welcome: a hub that fails again waits for the next one. */
  private nudged = false;
  /** A continuation fell due while the link was down: the next welcome sends it. */
  private owed = false;
  private vendorErrors = 0;
  /** The wait of a limit hit; null when not waiting. */
  private waiting: QuotaWait | null = null;
  private lastQuota: { accountId: string | null; quota: VendorQuota } | null = null;
  private closed = false;

  constructor(options: TurnPolicyOptions) {
    this.options = options;
  }

  /** Every agent event, after the pump has handled it; nothing once the process is gone. */
  observe(event: AgentEvent): void {
    if (this.closed) return;
    switch (event.type) {
      case 'turn_started':
        // Whatever was scheduled, a turn runs now; only a quota wait goes on.
        this.cancel();
        this.unreachable = false;
        this.returned = false;
        this.owed = false;
        if (this.waiting !== null) this.interruptInWait();
        return;
      case 'tool_ended':
        if (event.hubUnreachable) {
          this.unreachable = true;
          this.returned = false;
        }
        if (event.terminal !== null && ENDING_TOOLS.includes(event.terminal)) this.ended = true;
        return;
      case 'quota':
        this.lastQuota = { accountId: event.accountId, quota: event.quota };
        if (isLimitHit(event.quota, this.options.allowPaidUsage())) this.limitHit(this.lastQuota);
        return;
      case 'turn_ended':
        this.turnEnded(event);
        return;
      default:
        return;
    }
  }

  /** The runner's own interrupt in needs_login: the turn ended because of the outage (X-38). */
  async interruptForOutage(): Promise<void> {
    if (!this.options.inTurn()) return;
    this.outage = true;
    this.cancel();
    await this.options.session.interrupt();
  }

  /**
   * After each welcome: the one nudge, for an attempt whose turn ended because of the outage, or the continuation
   * that fell due while the link was down. A turn still running after a hub-unreachable answer gets its nudge when it
   * ends.
   */
  async onWelcome(): Promise<void> {
    if (this.closed) return;
    this.nudged = false;
    if (this.unreachable) this.returned = true;
    if (this.options.stopping()) return;
    if (this.outage) {
      this.outage = false;
      this.owed = false;
      this.nudged = true;
      await this.send(OUTAGE_NUDGE, 'the outage nudge');
      return;
    }
    if (this.owed) {
      this.owed = false;
      await this.sendContinuation();
    }
  }

  /** The agent's process is gone: nothing more is scheduled. */
  close(): void {
    this.closed = true;
    this.cancel();
    if (this.quotaTimer !== null) clearTimeout(this.quotaTimer);
    this.quotaTimer = null;
  }

  private turnEnded(event: Extract<AgentEvent, { type: 'turn_ended' }>): void {
    const outage = this.unreachable;
    this.unreachable = false;
    if (this.waiting !== null) {
      // The limit still holds, however the turn ended: no continuation and no retry until the wait ends.
      if (outage) this.outage = true;
      this.options.setPhase('quota_wait');
      return;
    }
    if (outage) this.outageEnded();
    if (event.outcome === 'completed') {
      this.vendorErrors = 0;
      if (!outage) this.continueLater();
      return;
    }
    if (event.outcome !== 'failed') return;
    if (event.errorKind === 'vendor') {
      this.vendorError(event.error);
    } else if (event.errorKind === 'quota') {
      this.limitHit(this.quotaAtLimit());
    } else if (event.errorKind !== null && (VENDOR_OUTCOME_KINDS as readonly string[]).includes(event.errorKind)) {
      const kind = event.errorKind as VendorOutcomeKind;
      const detail = event.error === null ? null : clip(event.error, LONG_TEXT_MAX);
      this.options.report({ type: 'attempt.vendor_outcome', data: { kind, detail } });
    }
  }

  /**
   * A turn ended because a tool could not reach the hub. When the hub is back already (the link is up, or a welcome
   * came during the turn), the nudge goes at once, once per welcome; otherwise the next welcome sends it.
   */
  private outageEnded(): void {
    const back = this.returned || this.options.linkUp();
    this.returned = false;
    if (!back || this.nudged) {
      this.outage = true;
      return;
    }
    this.nudged = true;
    this.schedule(0, async () => {
      await this.send(OUTAGE_NUDGE, 'the outage nudge');
    });
  }

  /**
   * What a turn that failed at its limit reports: the last quota report when it was a hit whose reset is still
   * ahead, else the reset unknown.
   */
  private quotaAtLimit(): { accountId: string | null; quota: VendorQuota } {
    const last = this.lastQuota;
    if (last !== null && isLimitHit(last.quota, this.options.allowPaidUsage()) && !this.resetPassed(last.quota)) {
      return last;
    }
    const windows = last?.quota.windows ?? { fiveHour: null, weekly: null };
    const paidUsage = last?.quota.paidUsage ?? 'unknown';
    return {
      accountId: last?.accountId ?? null,
      quota: { state: 'exhausted', resetsAt: null, windows, paidUsage, updatedAt: this.now() },
    };
  }

  /** Whether a report's reset time has come: the limit outlasted it, so the reset is unknown now. */
  private resetPassed(quota: VendorQuota): boolean {
    return quota.resetsAt !== null && quota.resetsAt <= this.now();
  }

  /** A worker's continuation, once continuationWait has passed with no hold, stop or new turn. */
  private continueLater(): void {
    const { spec, timings } = this.options;
    if (spec().role !== 'worker' || this.ended || this.outage) return;
    this.schedule(timings().continuationWait, async () => {
      if (this.ended || this.outage || this.options.inTurn()) return;
      if (!this.options.linkUp()) {
        this.owed = true;
        return;
      }
      await this.sendContinuation();
    });
  }

  private async sendContinuation(): Promise<void> {
    if (this.ended || this.options.inTurn()) return;
    const prompt = continuationPrompt(this.options.spec().acceptanceIds);
    if (await this.send(prompt, 'a continuation')) this.options.continuationSent();
  }

  private vendorError(error: string | null): void {
    this.options.setPhase('vendor_error');
    const delayMs = vendorRetryDelay(this.vendorErrors, this.options.timings());
    this.vendorErrors += 1;
    const { attemptId, logger } = this.options;
    logger.warn('the vendor failed the turn; retrying', { attemptId, delayMs, error });
    this.schedule(delayMs, async () => {
      if (this.options.inTurn()) return;
      await this.send(vendorRetryPrompt(this.options.spec().vendor), 'a vendor-error retry');
    });
  }

  /**
   * A limit hit: the turn is interrupted, quota_wait set and the wait reported, until the reset; a reset unknown or
   * already past is waited for quotaUnknown.
   */
  private limitHit(hit: { accountId: string | null; quota: VendorQuota }): void {
    if (this.waiting !== null) return;
    this.cancel();
    // Only an exhausted window is the account's: paid usage in use is this runner's refusal (allowPaidUsage).
    const wait: QuotaWait = { quota: hit.quota, accountId: hit.quota.state === 'exhausted' ? hit.accountId : null };
    this.waiting = wait;
    this.options.setPhase('quota_wait');
    const { vendor } = this.options.spec();
    // Paid usage in use counts as exhausted, so the hub moves the attempt to quota_wait too.
    const quota: VendorQuota = { ...hit.quota, state: 'exhausted' };
    this.options.report({ type: 'attempt.quota', data: { vendor, accountId: wait.accountId, quota } });
    if (this.options.inTurn()) this.interruptInWait();
    this.armWait(wait);
  }

  /**
   * The timer of a wait: at resetsAt, or quotaUnknown from now when the reset is unknown or already past. The wait
   * ends only once the runner's clock has passed that time: a reset further ahead than the longest timer (a monthly
   * window) is reached in steps of it, and a timer that fires early is armed again for what is left.
   */
  private armWait(wait: QuotaWait, until?: number): void {
    const { resetsAt } = wait.quota;
    const now = this.now();
    const end = until ?? (resetsAt !== null && resetsAt > now ? resetsAt : now + this.options.timings().quotaUnknown);
    this.quotaTimer = setTimeout(() => {
      this.quotaTimer = null;
      if (this.closed || this.options.stopping() || this.waiting !== wait) return;
      if (end > this.now()) {
        this.armWait(wait, end);
        return;
      }
      this.endWait(wait).catch((error) => {
        this.options.logger.error('the turn policy failed', { attemptId: this.options.attemptId, error: String(error) });
      });
    }, Math.min(Math.max(end - now, 0), MAX_TIMER_MS));
    this.quotaTimer.unref?.();
  }

  /** The wait is over: attempt.quota ok, and the turn resumes unless one runs already. */
  private async endWait(wait: QuotaWait): Promise<void> {
    if (this.waiting !== wait) return;
    this.waiting = null;
    const { vendor } = this.options.spec();
    const ok: VendorQuota = { ...wait.quota, state: 'ok', updatedAt: this.now() };
    this.options.report({ type: 'attempt.quota', data: { vendor, accountId: wait.accountId, quota: ok } });
    if (this.options.inTurn()) {
      this.options.setPhase('turn');
      return;
    }
    this.options.setPhase('idle');
    await this.send(QUOTA_RESUME_PROMPT, 'the resume after a quota wait');
  }

  /**
   * A turn runs while the limit holds (the hit's own turn, or one a delivery started): it is interrupted, so it uses
   * no exhausted or paid quota. A stop's handoff turn is left to run.
   */
  private interruptInWait(): void {
    if (this.options.stopping()) return;
    this.options.session.interrupt().catch((error) => {
      this.options.logger.warn('cannot interrupt a turn at its limit', {
        attemptId: this.options.attemptId,
        error: String(error),
      });
    });
  }

  private schedule(ms: number, run: () => Promise<void>): void {
    this.cancel();
    if (this.closed) return;
    this.timer = setTimeout(() => {
      this.timer = null;
      if (this.closed || this.options.stopping()) return;
      run().catch((error) => {
        this.options.logger.error('the turn policy failed', { attemptId: this.options.attemptId, error: String(error) });
      });
    }, ms);
    this.timer.unref?.();
  }

  private cancel(): void {
    if (this.timer !== null) clearTimeout(this.timer);
    this.timer = null;
  }

  /** Sends a system message of the runner's; gives whether the agent took it. */
  private async send(text: string, what: string): Promise<boolean> {
    try {
      await this.options.session.send({ id: randomUUID(), text, authority: 'system' });
      return true;
    } catch (error) {
      this.options.logger.warn(`cannot send ${what}`, { attemptId: this.options.attemptId, error: String(error) });
      return false;
    }
  }

  private now(): number {
    return (this.options.now ?? Date.now)();
  }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run the tests and see them pass**

Run: `bun test packages/runner/test/controller-turns.test.ts packages/runner/test/controller-stop.test.ts && bun test && bun run typecheck`
Expected: the task's tests pass; then the whole suite passes (`0 fail`) and `tsc` exits 0.

Bun clamps a timer delay over 2^31 - 1 ms (about 24.8 days) to 1 ms, so a timer without a cap and re-arming would end a monthly wait, or testkit's recorded limit hit with its 2030 reset, at once and loop. A timer may also fire up to 1 ms early by the wall clock. `controller-turns.test.ts` covers the cap with a controller test whose reset is 30 days ahead and a `TurnPolicy` unit test with `jest.useFakeTimers()` past 2^31 ms, and the early timer with a unit test whose runner clock lags the timers. A quota wait has its own timer that a new turn does not cancel, and a reset at or before now waits `quotaUnknown`. The limit-hit test reads the phase at once and then waits for the 'turn interrupted' note, which the agent's turn end may bring after the quota report. The fixture's default `continuationWait` is 60 s, so agents in other tests stay idle. Only those two timestamp assertions allow the 1 ms rounding.

### Task 29: The attempt controller: resume

`resume_attempt` brings a new fence and token (design 6.3, 6.4, 7.4). A live process is first stopped without a handoff turn while the old fence is still current, because a bridge's token cannot change in place. The controller then rewrites task.md, restores protected paths, fast-forwards a clean lead clone to the vault's main, recomputes `projectConfigVerified` (X-5), prepares a worker's dependencies (X-40), resumes the session in the same clone with the attempt's recorded CLI version (X-13), reports `attempt.spawned`, and sends the prompt and the carried messages. A session that never ran a turn starts fresh and reports its new session ref (X-50); any other failure pushes the clone's work under the new fence and reports `attempt.failed_to_start`. An older fence is refused. After stopping the old process, reset `finalizedAt` with the resumed spec, fence and starting state before `resumeAdmitted` begins work; failed resumes leave it null.

```ts
import { afterEach, describe, expect, setDefaultTimeout, test } from 'bun:test';
import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import type { Fence, InjectedMessage } from '@agflow/core';
import { commitFiles, FakeAdapter, type TranscriptLine } from '@agflow/testkit';
import type { VendorAdapter } from '../src/adapters/types';
import { handoffPrompt } from '../src/attempt/stop';
import { readCloneHead } from '../src/git/clone';
import type { DependencyPreparer } from '../src/seams';
import {
  cleanupRunnerFixtures,
  createRunnerFixture,
  FIXTURE_PROJECT,
  fixtureAgentToken,
  type RunnerFixture,
  waitFor,
} from './fixture';

afterEach(cleanupRunnerFixtures);

// Every test here runs git or agent processes, which take several times as long on a machine loaded by other suites.
setDefaultTimeout(30_000);

const OLD: Fence = { epoch: 1, counter: 1 };
const NEW: Fence = { epoch: 1, counter: 2 };
const NEW_TOKEN = fixtureAgentToken('T-4-a1 resumed');
const FILES = { 'README.md': '# demo\n', 'src/app.ts': 'app\n', '.claude/settings.json': '{"permissions":{}}\n' };

/** A resume_attempt for T-4-a1 with the new fence and token. */
function resumeCommand(f: RunnerFixture, overrides: Partial<Parameters<ReturnType<RunnerFixture['controller']>['resume']>[0]> = {}) {
  return {
    fence: NEW,
    agentToken: NEW_TOKEN,
    prompt: 'Review feedback: rename the helper.',
    messages: [{ messageId: 12, authority: 'person', text: 'also fix the typo' }] as InjectedMessage[],
    taskPack: '# T-4 Tidy the app, round 2\n',
    restore: f.spec().restore,
    acceptanceIds: ['A1', 'A2'],
    ...overrides,
  };
}

/** The user lines of the session's fake transcript. */
function userTexts(f: RunnerFixture, sessionRef: string, attemptId = 'T-4-a1'): string[] {
  const file = join(f.paths.clone(FIXTURE_PROJECT, attemptId), '.agflow', 'run', 'fake-transcripts', `${sessionRef}.jsonl`);
  if (!existsSync(file)) return [];
  return readFileSync(file, 'utf8')
    .split('\n')
    .filter((line) => line !== '')
    .map((line) => JSON.parse(line) as TranscriptLine)
    .filter((line) => line.role === 'user')
    .map((line) => line.text);
}

const fenceOf = (event: ReturnType<RunnerFixture['events']>[number]) => ('fence' in event ? event.fence : null);

const spawnedOf = (f: RunnerFixture, attemptId = 'T-4-a1') =>
  f.events('attempt.spawned').filter((event) => event.attemptId === attemptId);

/** Starts T-4-a1 and stops it after its first turn, with no handoff. */
async function startedAndStopped(f: RunnerFixture, spec = f.spec()) {
  const controller = f.controller(spec.attemptId);
  expect(await controller.start(spec)).toEqual({ started: true });
  await waitFor(() => f.events('attempt.activity').some((event) => event.attemptId === spec.attemptId));
  const stop = { fence: OLD, reason: 'paused', handoff: false, interruptFirst: false, keepClone: true };
  expect(await controller.stop(stop)).toMatchObject({ ok: true });
  return controller;
}

describe('AttemptController: resume', () => {
  test('resume resets finalization before preparing work, even if preparation fails', async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture();
    await startedAndStopped(f);
    f.store.update('T-4-a1', { finalizedAt: 123 });
    const seen: (number | null)[] = [];
    const opened: (number | null)[] = [];
    const fetchForAttempt = f.vault.fetchForAttempt.bind(f.vault);
    f.vault.fetchForAttempt = async (attempt, wipRefPrefix) => {
      opened.push(f.store.get('T-4-a1')!.finalizedAt);
      await fetchForAttempt(attempt, wipRefPrefix);
    };
    const controller = f.controller('T-4-a1', {
      preparer: { available: true, prepare: async () => {
        seen.push(f.store.get('T-4-a1')!.finalizedAt);
        return { ran: true, ok: false, error: 'preparation failed', logTail: null };
      } },
    });
    expect(await controller.resume(resumeCommand(f))).toMatchObject({ resumed: false });
    expect(opened).toEqual([null]);
    expect(seen).toEqual([null]);
    expect(f.store.get('T-4-a1')?.finalizedAt).toBeNull();
  });

    expect(readFileSync(join(clone, '.claude', 'settings.json'), 'utf8')).toBe(FILES['.claude/settings.json']);

    await startedAndStopped(f);

    const spawned = await waitFor(() => spawnedOf(f)[1]);

  test('a resume restores agent config a dependency preparation wrote, then verifies the project config', async () => {

    resumed = true;

  test("a resumed successor reports no second first_output, unless its session started fresh", async () => {

    await waitFor(() => existsSync(join(f.paths.clone(FIXTURE_PROJECT, 'T-4-a1'), 'more.txt')));
    expect(await controller.pushWip()).toMatchObject({ status: 'pushed' });
    const wips = f.events('attempt.wip');
    expect(wips.at(-1)?.fence).toEqual(NEW);
    const resumed = spawnedOf(f)[1]?.seq ?? 0;
    expect(f.events().filter((event) => event.seq > resumed && fenceOf(event)?.counter === 1)).toEqual([]);
  });
```

**File:** `packages/runner/src/attempt/resume.ts` (new)

```ts
// resume_attempt (design 6.3, 6.4, 7.3, 7.4). A resume carries a new fence and token, and the task pack, restore
// set and acceptance ids the hub recomputed. The controller first stops a live process with the stop ladder and the
// final push, without a handoff turn, because a bridge's token cannot change in place. It then prepares the clone the
// attempt already has, as a start does but without making one: task.md rewritten, protected paths restored at the
// restore base, a lead's clean clone fast-forwarded to the vault's main, a worker's dependencies prepared, the
// project config verified. The session resumes in that clone with the CLI version recorded for the attempt (X-13);
// a session that never ran a turn starts fresh, as the adapter falls back. attempt.spawned (startSha null) follows,
// then the prompt and the carried messages, each bounded so an agent that takes no input never holds the queue.
// attempt.first_output is reported once per attempt: a resumed session reports none, unless the adapter started a
// fresh one after all. A failure is harvested and pushed and reported as attempt.failed_to_start; a command with an
// older fence than the attempt's is refused.
import { type AttemptSpec, localPinRefs, type RunnerCommand } from '@agflow/core';
import type { StoredAttemptSpec } from '../attempt-store';
import { cloneExists, fastForwardLeadClone } from '../git/clone';
import { type CloneStep, commitOf, realClonePath } from './workspace';

/** What resume_attempt carries for the controller. */
export type ResumeInput = Omit<Extract<RunnerCommand, { kind: 'resume_attempt' }>, 'kind' | 'attemptId'>;

/** What a resume did: the session resumed (or started fresh), or why not; a failure was also reported. */
export type ResumeOutcome = { resumed: true } | { resumed: false; error: string };

/**
 * How long the resume prompt and its messages may take to reach the agent. One that takes no input meanwhile is left
 * to its exit or the hub's stall rules, and the attempt's queue goes on.
 */
export const RESUME_SEND_MS = 30_000;

/** The reason a resume gives the stop of the live process before it. */
export const RESUME_STOP_REASON = 'the attempt resumes';

/** A resume's spec: the recorded one with the command's fence, token, task pack, restore set and acceptance ids. */
export function resumedSpec(recorded: StoredAttemptSpec, command: ResumeInput): AttemptSpec {
  return {
    ...recorded,
    fence: command.fence,
    agentToken: command.agentToken,
    taskPack: command.taskPack ?? recorded.taskPack,
    restore: command.restore,
    acceptanceIds: command.acceptanceIds,
  };
}

/**
 * A resume's clone step: the clone the attempt has, never a new one. A lead's clean clone detached at an older main
 * moves to the vault's main first, which moves its start pin too; a dirty one stays. Gives the start pin.
 */
export const reopenClone: CloneStep = async (deps, spec, path) => {
  const { vault, local } = deps;
  if (!cloneExists(path)) throw new Error(`the clone of ${spec.attemptId} is gone`);
  if (spec.role === 'lead') {
    await fastForwardLeadClone({ vault, local, attemptId: spec.attemptId, clone: await realClonePath(path) });
  }
  const startSha = await commitOf(vault, local, localPinRefs(spec.attemptId).start);
  if (startSha === null) throw new Error(`the vault has no start pin for ${spec.attemptId}`);
  return { created: false, startSha };
};
```

The first-turn script handles coalesced input; fresh-fallback output remains buffered before consumer attachment, even across exit. `resume_attempt` does not call `RunnerHealth.admit`; M2c's disk and battery guards stop such a resume at their next evaluation. Respecting battery holds during resume admission remains deferred.

### Task 30: The attempt controller: submissions

`push_submission` pushes only to the attempt's own task branch, checked with core's `isTaskBranch` (X-18); any other branch reports `attempt.violation` phase `submit` and pushes nothing (design 6.13). The controller harvests the clone and refuses with `dirty` for uncommitted changes and `protected_paths` for protected ones, with a detail that tells the agent to merge main when main changed the path; then it pushes the task branch and the WIP ref atomically under the stale-lease rules. Remote failures retry with doubling backoff until a stop or hold arrives (`interrupted`) or `submitRetry` passes (`remote`) (X-33). The outcome is `attempt.submitted`, repeated in the command result.

```ts
describe('pushSubmissionWithRetries', () => {
  const failure: SubmitPushOutcome = { ok: false, headSha: 'h', remoteHead: null, error: 'remote', detail: 'down' };

  /** A fake clock: each sleep is recorded and passes at once, unless sleeps never end. */
  function clock(options: { endless?: boolean } = {}) {
    let at = 0;
    const waits: number[] = [];
    return {
      waits,
      now: () => at,
      sleep: (ms: number) => {
        waits.push(ms);
        if (options.endless) return new Promise<void>(() => {});
        at += ms;
        return Promise.resolve();
      },
    };
  }

  const base = { interrupted: () => false, stopArrived: () => new Promise<void>(() => {}), onRetry: () => {} };

  test('waits 1 s doubling to a minute, the last wait shortened to the budget', async () => {
    const fake = clock();
    let tries = 0;
    const outcome = await pushSubmissionWithRetries({
      ...base,
      ...fake,
      budgetMs: 200_000,
      push: async () => {
        tries += 1;
        return failure;
      },
    });
    expect(outcome).toBe(failure);
    expect(fake.waits).toEqual([1_000, 2_000, 4_000, 8_000, 16_000, 32_000, 60_000, 60_000, 17_000]);
    expect(tries).toBe(10);
  });

  test('a refusal, or a remote outcome that cannot clear, is never retried', async () => {
    for (const [result, retryable] of [
      [{ ...failure, error: 'needs_merge' }, true],
      [failure, false],
    ] as const) {
      const fake = clock();
      let tries = 0;
      const outcome = await pushSubmissionWithRetries({
        ...base,
        ...fake,
        budgetMs: 60_000,
        retryable: () => retryable,
        push: async () => {
          tries += 1;
          return result;
        },
      });
      expect([outcome, tries, fake.waits]).toEqual([result, 1, []]);
    }
  });

  test('a stop during a wait or a try gives interrupted at once', async () => {
    let arrive = () => {};
    let stops = 0;
    const fake = clock({ endless: true });
    const waiting = pushSubmissionWithRetries({
      ...fake,
      budgetMs: 60_000,
      interrupted: () => stops > 0,
      stopArrived: () => new Promise<void>((resolve) => (arrive = resolve)),
      onRetry: () => {},
      push: async () => failure,
    });
    await Bun.sleep(10);
    stops += 1;
    arrive();
    expect(await waiting).toBe('interrupted');

    const during = clock();
    let tries = 0;
    let arrived = false;
    const outcome = await pushSubmissionWithRetries({
      ...base,
      ...during,
      budgetMs: 60_000,
      interrupted: () => arrived,
      push: async () => {
        tries += 1;
        arrived = true;
        return failure;
      },
    });
    expect([outcome, tries, during.waits]).toEqual(['interrupted', 1, []]);
  });
});
```

```ts
// push_submission (design 6.13, X-18, X-33). The runner pushes only to the task's own branch: the one
// AttemptSpec.branch names, in the task's namespace (core's isTaskBranch); any other is refused and reported as
// attempt.violation phase submit, and nothing is pushed. The clone is harvested; uncommitted changes (files over
// 10 MB the snapshot left out included) refuse the submission with dirty, protected changes with protected_paths,
// whose detail tells the agent to merge main when main has changed those paths, rather than revert them. Protected
// changes are judged against the submission base: the restore base, or, once the branch has merged a newer main,
// that merge's base on main, so a branch that followed the advice carries main's own versions and passes as it is.
// The task branch and the WIP ref then move together under the stale-lease rules (pushSubmission). Remote failures
// are retried with a doubling delay until submitRetry passes (remote) or a stop or hold for the attempt arrives
// (interrupted); a refusal that cannot clear (the attempt was fenced, ended or exited) ends the retries at once. The
// outcome is the outbox event attempt.submitted, and the command result repeats it.
import { type AttemptSpec, isTaskBranch, type RunnerEvent } from '@agflow/core';
import { doublingDelay } from '../backoff';
import { mergeBase } from '../git/protect';
import type { SubmitPushOutcome } from '../git/push';
import { type GitEnvironment, runGit } from '../git/run';
import type { Vault } from '../git/vault';
import { clipViolationPaths } from './workspace';

/** attempt.submitted's data: the outcome of one push_submission. */
export type SubmittedData = Extract<RunnerEvent, { type: 'attempt.submitted' }>['data'];

/** What push_submission carries for the controller. */
export interface SubmitCommand {
  fence: AttemptSpec['fence'];
  submissionId: string;
  branch: string;
  expectedBranchSha: string | null;
  adoptable: string[];
}

/**
 * What a push_submission did: an outcome, reported as attempt.submitted; or a refusal with no outcome: a fence that
 * is not the attempt's, or a branch that is not its own (reported as a violation).
 */
export type SubmitResult =
  | { ok: true; outcome: SubmittedData }
  | { ok: false; error: 'stale_fence' | 'branch_refused' };

/** The waits between tries of a submission push: 1 s, doubling to a minute, while submitRetry lasts. */
export const SUBMIT_RETRY_DELAY = { base: 1_000, cap: 60_000 } as const;

/** Whether a push_submission names the attempt's own branch: AttemptSpec.branch, in the task's namespace (X-18). */
export function isOwnBranch(spec: Pick<AttemptSpec, 'taskId' | 'branch'>, branch: string): boolean {
  return spec.taskId !== null && spec.branch === branch && isTaskBranch(spec.taskId, branch);
}

/** A list of paths for a detail, clipped as violations are. */
function listed(paths: readonly string[]): string {
  return clipViolationPaths(paths).join(', ');
}

/** dirty's detail: the paths with uncommitted changes, files over 10 MB the snapshot left out included. */
export function dirtyDetail(paths: readonly string[]): string {
  return (
    `the clone has uncommitted changes: ${listed(paths)}. Commit them, or remove what does not belong in the ` +
    'submission, then submit again.'
  );
}

/**
 * The base a submission's protected paths are judged against. A branch that merged main since the restore base
 * carries main's versions as of that merge: merge-base(the vault's main, head), when it descends from the restore
 * base. Otherwise the restore base. Either is a commit of main, which agents cannot write, so only main's own versions
 * of protected paths pass.
 */
export async function submissionBase(input: {
  vault: Vault;
  local: GitEnvironment;
  restoreBase: string;
  head: string;
}): Promise<string> {
  const { vault, local, restoreBase, head } = input;
  const merged = await mergeBase({ vault, local }, `refs/heads/${vault.mainBranch}`, head);
  if (merged === null || merged === restoreBase) return restoreBase;
  const args = [`--git-dir=${vault.path}`, 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor', restoreBase, merged];
  const descends = await runGit(local, args, { check: false });
  return descends.code === 0 ? merged : restoreBase;
}

/**
 * protected_paths' detail: the paths, and how to fix them. A path whose version on the vault's main differs from the
 * submission base changed on main since, so the agent merges main rather than revert it.
 */
export async function protectedDetail(input: {
  vault: Vault;
  local: GitEnvironment;
  base: string;
  paths: readonly string[];
}): Promise<string> {
  const { vault, local, base, paths } = input;
  const main = vault.mainBranch;
  const range = [base, `refs/heads/${main}`];
  const diff = await runGit(local, [`--git-dir=${vault.path}`, 'diff-tree', '-r', '-z', '--name-only', ...range], {
    check: false,
  });
  const changedOnMain = new Set(diff.code === 0 ? diff.stdout.split('\0').filter((path) => path !== '') : []);
  const newer = paths.filter((path) => changedOnMain.has(path));
  const intro = `the branch changes protected paths, which agents may not change: ${listed(paths)}.`;
  if (newer.length > 0) {
    return (
      `${intro} ${main} has changed ${listed(newer)} since your branch started: merge it rather than reverting them ` +
      `(\`git fetch origin && git merge origin/${main}\`), then submit again.`
    );
  }
  return `${intro} Revert them to the versions your branch started from, commit, and submit again.`;
}

export interface SubmitPushRetryInput {
  /** One try: the push, or why it may not run now (a remote outcome). */
  push(): Promise<SubmitPushOutcome>;
  /** submitRetry. */
  budgetMs: number;
  /** Whether a stop or hold for the attempt arrived since the submission began. */
  interrupted(): boolean;
  /** Resolves when a stop or hold arrives, so a wait ends at once. */
  stopArrived(): Promise<void>;
  /** Called before each wait. */
  onRetry(outcome: SubmitPushOutcome, delayMs: number): void;
  /** Whether a remote outcome may clear on a later try; every remote outcome by default. */
  retryable?(outcome: SubmitPushOutcome): boolean;
  /** Bun.sleep by default. */
  sleep?: (ms: number) => Promise<void>;
  /** Date.now by default. */
  now?: () => number;
}

/**
 * Runs the push until it lands or is refused, retrying remote failures with SUBMIT_RETRY_DELAY until budgetMs has
 * passed, the last try at its end. Gives the last outcome, or 'interrupted' once a stop or hold arrived: before a
 * try, after a failed one, or during a wait.
 */
export async function pushSubmissionWithRetries(
  input: SubmitPushRetryInput,
): Promise<SubmitPushOutcome | 'interrupted'> {
  const sleep = input.sleep ?? ((ms: number) => Bun.sleep(ms));
  const now = input.now ?? Date.now;
  const retryable = input.retryable ?? (() => true);
  const deadline = now() + input.budgetMs;
  for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
    if (input.interrupted()) return 'interrupted';
    const outcome = await input.push();
    if (outcome.error !== 'remote' || !retryable(outcome)) return outcome;
    if (input.interrupted()) return 'interrupted';
    const remaining = deadline - now();
    if (remaining <= 0) return outcome;
    const delayMs = Math.min(doublingDelay(attempt, SUBMIT_RETRY_DELAY), remaining);
    input.onRetry(outcome, delayMs);
    await Promise.race([sleep(delayMs), input.stopArrived()]);
  }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run the tests and see them pass**

Run: `bun test packages/runner/test/controller-submit.test.ts packages/runner/test/controller-resume.test.ts && bun test && bun run typecheck`
Expected: the task's tests pass; then the whole suite passes (`0 fail`) and `tsc` exits 0.

Protected paths are judged against a submission base: the merge base of the vault's main and the head when it descends from the restore base, else the restore base, so a branch that merged main is not refused for main's own protected files. `dirty` also covers files over 10 MB that the snapshot skipped. Retries wait 1 s, doubling to 60 s; only link-gate refusals and remote failures are retried, and a fenced, ended or exited attempt ends at once. The resume tests also exercise submissions; the unresolved missing-event failure is described in Known behaviour 10.

### Task 31: The attempt controller: take-over

`prepare_takeover` hands an agent's work to a person (design 6.12, 8.4, 9.4): interrupt and handoff, the stop, the final harvest and WIP push, the restore of protected paths, and a new `.git` that the runner builds, a shared clone of the vault with HEAD and the task branch at the harvested head. The agent's `.git`, and every nested `.git` in the clone, moves to `runner/forensics/<attempt>/` and is inspected; program-valued config, hooks, `commondir`, `gitdir` and extra alternates are reported as `attempt.violation` phase `takeover`. The runner builds both commands (X-5, X-10): the local one with its pinned binary of the attempt's recorded CLI version and its vendor home, and the anywhere one with core's `takeoverAnywhereCommand`. It reports `attempt.taken_over` and no `attempt.exited`. Live take-over uses the shared finalization ordering; stopped take-over resets completion before reharvesting and records outcome and pending work before marking completion.
