import { afterEach, expect, setDefaultTimeout, test } from 'bun:test';
import { existsSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import type { AttemptRecord } from '../src/attempt-store';
import { runGit } from '../src/git/run';
import { cleanupRunnerFixtures, createRunnerFixture, FIXTURE_PROJECT, waitFor } from './fixture';

setDefaultTimeout(30_000);
afterEach(cleanupRunnerFixtures);

// Take-over is the last lifecycle added by Task 31; exercise the shared finalization contract through every caller.
for (const mode of ['exit', 'stop', 'suspend', 'takeover', 'stopped takeover'] as const) {
  for (const failure of ['none', 'push', 'harvest'] as const) {
    test(`${mode}: records the ${failure} outcome before finalization`, async () => {
      const f = await createRunnerFixture({
        config: { timings: { finalPush: 1, lateRetry: { base: 60_000, cap: 60_000 } } },
        script: { turns: [
          [{ do: 'write', path: 'work.txt', content: 'unpublished\n' }, { do: 'sleep', ms: 30_000 }],
          [{ do: 'terminal', tool: 'handoff' }],
        ] },
      });
      const controller = f.controller();
      await controller.start(f.spec());
      const clone = f.paths.clone(FIXTURE_PROJECT, 'T-4-a1');
      await waitFor(() => existsSync(join(clone, 'work.txt')) && controller.phase === 'turn');
      expect(f.store.get('T-4-a1')?.finalizedAt).toBeNull();
      const stop = { fence: f.spec().fence, handoff: false, interruptFirst: false, keepClone: true, reason: 'done' };
      if (mode === 'stopped takeover') await controller.stop(stop);
      if (failure === 'push') {
        await runGit(f.local, [`--git-dir=${f.vault.path}`, 'config', 'remote.origin.url', join(f.home, 'missing-origin')]);
        // A stopped take-over harvest must differ from the already pushed tree.
        writeFileSync(join(clone, 'later.txt'), 'new work\n');
      }
      if (failure === 'harvest') rmSync(join(clone, '.git'), { recursive: true, force: true });
      const beforeMarkers: AttemptRecord[] = [];
      const update = f.store.update.bind(f.store);
      f.store.update = (id, patch) => {
        if (patch.finalizedAt != null) beforeMarkers.push(f.store.get(id)!);
        return update(id, patch);
      };
      if (mode === 'exit') {
        await controller.session!.close();
        await controller.settled();
      } else if (mode === 'stop') await controller.stop(stop);
      else if (mode === 'suspend') await controller.stopForRunner('suspend', { handoff: false });
      else await controller.prepareTakeover({ fence: f.spec().fence, person: 'alice' });
      expect(beforeMarkers).toHaveLength(1);
      const before = beforeMarkers[0]!;
      expect(before.finalizedAt).toBeNull();
      expect(before.state).toBe(mode === 'suspend' ? 'suspended' : 'stopped');
      expect(before.pushError).toEqual(failure === 'none' ? null : expect.any(String));
      expect(before.lateWorkSha).toEqual(failure === 'push' ? expect.any(String) : null);
      const record = f.store.get('T-4-a1')!;
      expect(record.finalizedAt).toEqual(expect.any(Number));
      expect(record.pushError).toBe(before.pushError);
      expect(record.lateWorkSha).toBe(before.lateWorkSha);
    });
  }
}

for (const field of ['pushError', 'lateWorkSha'] as const) {
  test(`a failed ${field} write never claims finalization completed`, async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({
      config: { timings: { finalPush: 1, lateRetry: { base: 60_000, cap: 60_000 } } },
      script: { turns: [[{ do: 'write', path: 'work.txt', content: 'kept\n' }, { do: 'sleep', ms: 30_000 }]] },
    });
    const controller = f.controller();
    await controller.start(f.spec());
    await waitFor(() => existsSync(join(f.paths.clone(FIXTURE_PROJECT, 'T-4-a1'), 'work.txt')));
    await runGit(f.local, [`--git-dir=${f.vault.path}`, 'config', 'remote.origin.url', join(f.home, 'missing-origin')]);
    const update = f.store.update.bind(f.store);
    let refused = false;
    f.store.update = (id, patch) => {
      if (patch[field] != null) {
        refused = true;

      }

      expect(refused).toBe(true);
      expect(f.store.get('T-4-a1')?.finalizedAt).toBeNull();
    } finally {

  ],
};

/** main's files: the fixture's, and a people-only file the agent edits. */
const FILES = { 'README.md': '# demo\n', 'src/app.ts': 'app\n', '.github/workflows/ci.yml': 'ci: main\n' };

const cloneOf = (f: RunnerFixture, attemptId = 'T-4-a1') => f.paths.clone(FIXTURE_PROJECT, attemptId);

/** git status --porcelain's lines, sorted, without the leading space gitIn's trim takes from the first. */
const statusLines = (status: string) => status.split('\n').map((line) => line.trim()).sort();

const takeoverViolations = (f: RunnerFixture) =>
  f.events('attempt.violation').filter((event) => event.data.phase === 'takeover');

const sessionOf = (f: RunnerFixture, attemptId = 'T-4-a1') => f.store.get(attemptId)?.sessionRef as string;

/** Starts the attempt and waits until its agent has done the first turn's work. */
async function startWorking(f: RunnerFixture, attemptId = 'T-4-a1', overrides = {}) {
  const controller = f.controller(attemptId);
  await controller.start(f.spec({ attemptId, ...overrides }));
  await waitFor(() => existsSync(join(cloneOf(f, attemptId), 'README.md')) && f.events('attempt.spawned').length > 0);
  // ci.yml is the turn's last write: a stop that comes sooner (a SIGKILL under load) would find the turn half done.
  const ci = join(cloneOf(f, attemptId), '.github', 'workflows', 'ci.yml');
  await waitFor(() => controller.phase === 'turn' && existsSync(ci) && readFileSync(ci, 'utf8') === 'ci: the agent\n');
  return controller;
}

describe('AttemptController: take-over', () => {
  test("the person's git is on the task branch at the harvested head, with the uncommitted work as changes", async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({ files: FILES, script: WORKING });
    const controller = await startWorking(f);
    const outcome = await controller.prepareTakeover({ fence: FENCE, person: 'alice' });
    expect(outcome).toMatchObject({ ok: true });
    const [taken] = f.events('attempt.taken_over');
    const wipSha = taken?.data.wipSha as string;
    expect(wipSha).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{40}$/);
    expect(await gitIn(f.origin.path, ['rev-parse', WIP])).toBe(wipSha);
    const clone = cloneOf(f);
    expect(await gitIn(clone, ['symbolic-ref', 'HEAD'])).toBe(`refs/heads/${BRANCH}`);
    // The harvested head, under the WIP's snapshot commit and the commit that strips its protected changes.
    const head = await gitIn(clone, ['rev-parse', 'HEAD']);
    expect(await gitIn(f.origin.path, ['log', '-1', '--format=%s', head])).toBe('committed work');
    expect(await gitIn(f.origin.path, ['rev-list', '--count', `${head}..${wipSha}`])).toBe('2');
    const status = await gitIn(clone, ['status', '--porcelain=v1', '--untracked-files=all']);
    expect(statusLines(status)).toEqual(['?? uncommitted.txt', 'M README.md']);
    expect(existsSync(join(clone, '.envrc'))).toBe(false);
    expect(readFileSync(join(clone, '.github', 'workflows', 'ci.yml'), 'utf8')).toBe('ci: main\n');
    expect(existsSync(join(f.paths.forensics('T-4-a1'), 'git', 'HEAD'))).toBe(true);
    // The agent's .git is the one the runner made: nothing in it is reported.
    expect(takeoverViolations(f)).toEqual([]);
    // The agent was asked for its handoff note before it stopped.
    const transcript = readFileSync(join(clone, '.agflow', 'run', 'fake-transcripts', `${sessionOf(f)}.jsonl`), 'utf8');
    const prompts = transcript
      .split('\n')
      .filter((line) => line !== '')
      .map((line) => JSON.parse(line) as TranscriptLine)
      .filter((line) => line.role === 'user')
      .map((line) => line.text);
    expect(prompts).toEqual(['Start working on T-4.', handoffPrompt(TAKEOVER_STOP_REASON)]);
    expect(f.events('attempt.exited')).toEqual([]);
    expect(f.fakes.claude?.launches).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(controller.session).toBeNull();
    await controller.settled();
    expect(f.events('attempt.exited')).toEqual([]);
    expect(f.store.processes('T-4-a1')).toEqual([]);
  }, 60_000);

  test('an agent .git with program-valued config, a hook, a commondir and an extra alternate is reported', async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({ files: FILES, script: WORKING });
    const controller = await startWorking(f);
    const gitDir = join(cloneOf(f), '.git');
    writeFileSync(
      join(gitDir, 'config'),
      `${await Bun.file(join(gitDir, 'config')).text()}[core]\n\thooksPath = .git/hooks\n\talternateRefsCommand = id\n` +
        '[alias]\n\tst = !sh -c id\n\tco = checkout\n[filter "x"]\n\tclean = cat\n[trailer "sign"]\n\tcmd = id\n' +
        '[submodule "lib"]\n\tupdate = !sh -c id\n[submodule "ok"]\n\tupdate = rebase\n[extensions]\n\tworktreeConfig = true\n',
    );
    // With extensions.worktreeConfig, git reads config.worktree too, and each linked worktree's own.
    writeFileSync(join(gitDir, 'config.worktree'), '[core]\n\tfsmonitor = id\n[gpg "ssh"]\n\tdefaultKeyCommand = id\n');
    mkdirSync(join(gitDir, 'worktrees', 'w1'), { recursive: true });
    writeFileSync(join(gitDir, 'worktrees', 'w1', 'config.worktree'), '[core]\n\tsshCommand = id\n');
    mkdirSync(join(gitDir, 'hooks'), { recursive: true });
    writeFileSync(join(gitDir, 'hooks', 'pre-commit'), '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n', { mode: 0o755 });
    writeFileSync(join(gitDir, 'commondir'), '.\n');
    const other = join(f.home, 'other.git');
    await gitIn(f.home, ['init', '--quiet', '--bare', other]);
    const alternates = join(gitDir, 'objects', 'info', 'alternates');
    writeFileSync(alternates, `${await Bun.file(alternates).text()}${join(other, 'objects')}\n`);
    expect(await controller.prepareTakeover({ fence: FENCE, person: 'alice' })).toMatchObject({ ok: true });
    const violations = takeoverViolations(f);
    expect(violations.map((event) => event.data.paths)).toEqual([
      [
        '.git/config:core.hookspath',
        '.git/config:core.alternaterefscommand',
        '.git/config:alias.st',
        '.git/config:filter.x.clean',
        '.git/config:trailer.sign.cmd',
        '.git/config:submodule.lib.update',
        '.git/config.worktree:core.fsmonitor',
        '.git/config.worktree:gpg.ssh.defaultkeycommand',
        '.git/worktrees/w1/config.worktree:core.sshcommand',
        '.git/hooks/pre-commit',
        '.git/commondir',
        '.git/objects/info/alternates',
      ],
    ]);
    const [taken] = f.events('attempt.taken_over');
    expect(violations[0]?.seq).toBeLessThan(taken?.seq as number);
    expect(taken?.data.error).toBeNull();
  }, 60_000);

  test('a .git/hooks the runner cannot read is reported, and the take-over still goes through', async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({ files: FILES, script: WORKING });
    const controller = await startWorking(f);
    const hooks = join(cloneOf(f), '.git', 'hooks');
    mkdirSync(hooks, { recursive: true });
    chmodSync(hooks, 0o000);
    try {
      expect(await controller.prepareTakeover({ fence: FENCE, person: 'alice' })).toMatchObject({ ok: true });
    } finally {
      for (const dir of [hooks, join(f.paths.forensics('T-4-a1'), 'git', 'hooks')]) {
        if (existsSync(dir)) chmodSync(dir, 0o700);
      }
    }
    expect(takeoverViolations(f).map((event) => event.data.paths)).toEqual([['.git/hooks']]);
    const [taken] = f.events('attempt.taken_over');
    expect(taken?.data.error).toBeNull();
    expect(taken?.data.commands.local).toContain('--resume');
  }, 60_000);

  test("a nested .git the agent made is moved aside, so the person's git never runs its program", async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({ files: FILES, script: WORKING });
    const controller = await startWorking(f);
    const clone = cloneOf(f);
    const marker = join(f.home, 'fsmonitor-ran');
    // A nested repository, committed as a gitlink, whose fsmonitor git runs when status recurses into it.
    const sub = join(clone, 'sub');
    await gitIn(clone, ['init', '--quiet', 'sub']);
    await gitIn(sub, ['commit', '--quiet', '--allow-empty', '-m', 'nested']);
    const subHead = await gitIn(sub, ['rev-parse', 'HEAD']);
    await gitIn(clone, ['update-index', '--add', '--cacheinfo', `160000,${subHead},sub`]);
    await gitIn(clone, ['commit', '--quiet', '-m', 'a gitlink']);
    await gitIn(sub, ['config', 'core.fsmonitor', `touch '${marker}'; true`]);
    // A link named .git deeper down, and one inside the run directory, which the walk does not skip.
    mkdirSync(join(clone, 'deep', 'er'), { recursive: true });
    symlinkSync(join(f.home, 'elsewhere'), join(clone, 'deep', 'er', '.git'));
    mkdirSync(join(clone, '.agflow', 'run', 'x'), { recursive: true });
    writeFileSync(join(clone, '.agflow', 'run', 'x', '.git'), 'gitdir: /elsewhere\n');
    expect(await controller.prepareTakeover({ fence: FENCE, person: 'alice' })).toMatchObject({ ok: true });
    expect(existsSync(marker)).toBe(false);
    expect(await gitIn(clone, ['ls-files', '--stage', 'sub'])).toBe(`160000 ${subHead} 0\tsub`);
    for (const nested of ['sub/.git', 'deep/er/.git', '.agflow/run/x/.git']) {
      expect(lstatSync(join(clone, nested), { throwIfNoEntry: false })).toBeUndefined();
      // Kept for forensics under its path in the clone.
      expect(lstatSync(join(f.paths.forensics('T-4-a1'), 'nested', '1', nested), { throwIfNoEntry: false })).toBeDefined();
    }
    // The person's own git, with nothing of theirs configured, runs nothing the agent planted.
    await gitIn(clone, ['status']);
    await gitIn(clone, ['status', '--ignore-submodules=none']);
    expect(existsSync(marker)).toBe(false);
    const [violation] = takeoverViolations(f).map((event) => event.data.paths);
    expect(violation).toEqual(
      expect.arrayContaining(['.agflow/run/x/.git', 'deep/er/.git', 'sub/.git', 'sub/.git/config:core.fsmonitor']),
    );
    expect(f.events('attempt.taken_over')[0]?.data.error).toBeNull();
  }, 60_000);

  test('attempt.taken_over carries the local resume command of the pinned CLI, the anywhere command and the wipSha', async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({ files: FILES, script: WORKING });
    const claude = await startWorking(f);
    const codex = await startWorking(f, 'T-5-a1', {
      taskId: 'T-5',
      vendor: 'codex',
      branch: 'agflow/T-5-other',
      wipRef: 'refs/agflow/T-5/a1',
    });
    expect(await claude.prepareTakeover({ fence: FENCE, person: 'alice' })).toMatchObject({ ok: true });
    expect(await codex.prepareTakeover({ fence: FENCE, person: 'bob' })).toMatchObject({ ok: true });
    const taken = f.events('attempt.taken_over');
    const of = (attemptId: string) => taken.find((event) => event.attemptId === attemptId);
    const homes = vendorHomes(f.config, f.paths);
    const claudeBinary = join(f.paths.runner, 'vendor', 'claude', fixtureCliVersion('claude'), 'claude');
    const codexBinary = join(f.paths.runner, 'vendor', 'codex', fixtureCliVersion('codex'), 'bin', 'codex');
    expect(of('T-4-a1')?.data).toEqual({
      commands: {
        local: `cd ${realpathSync(cloneOf(f))} && CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=${homes.claude} ${claudeBinary} --resume ${sessionOf(f)}`,
        anywhere: takeoverAnywhereCommand({
          ref: WIP,
          branch: BRANCH,
          takeoverRef: takeoverRef(FIXTURE_WIP_PREFIX, 'T-4', 'alice'),
        }),
      },
      wipSha: await gitIn(f.origin.path, ['rev-parse', WIP]),
      error: null,
    });
    expect(of('T-5-a1')?.data.commands).toEqual({
      local: `cd ${realpathSync(cloneOf(f, 'T-5-a1'))} && CODEX_HOME=${homes.codex} ${codexBinary} resume --no-daemon ${sessionOf(f, 'T-5-a1')}`,
      anywhere: takeoverAnywhereCommand({
        ref: 'refs/agflow/T-5/a1',
        branch: 'agflow/T-5-other',
        takeoverRef: takeoverRef(FIXTURE_WIP_PREFIX, 'T-5', 'bob'),
      }),
    });
    expect(f.events('attempt.exited')).toEqual([]);
  }, 30_000);

  test('a failure after the agent stopped still reports attempt.taken_over, with local null and the error', async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({ files: FILES, script: WORKING });
    const controller = await startWorking(f);
    // The agent left a .git the harvest refuses: a file, not a directory.
    const gitDir = join(cloneOf(f), '.git');
    rmSync(gitDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
    writeFileSync(gitDir, 'gitdir: /somewhere/else\n');
    expect(await controller.prepareTakeover({ fence: FENCE, person: 'alice' })).toMatchObject({ ok: true });
    const [taken] = f.events('attempt.taken_over');
    expect(taken?.data).toMatchObject({ commands: { local: null }, wipSha: null });
    expect(taken?.data.commands.anywhere).toContain(`git fetch origin ${WIP}`);
    expect(taken?.data.error).toContain('is not a directory');
    expect(f.events('attempt.exited')).toEqual([]);
    expect(controller.session).toBeNull();
  }, 60_000);

  test('a prepare_takeover resent after a restart, with the agent gone, continues from the harvest', async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({ files: FILES, script: WORKING });
    const before = await startWorking(f);
    // The runner dies: its agent is killed at the next start, and a new controller knows only the record.
    process.kill(-(before.session?.pid as number), 'SIGKILL');
    await waitFor(() => f.events('attempt.exited').length > 0);
    await before.settled();
    const exited = f.events('attempt.exited').length;
    const after = f.controller('T-4-a1');
    expect(await after.prepareTakeover({ fence: { epoch: 1, counter: 2 }, person: 'alice' })).toEqual({
      ok: false,
      error: 'stale_fence',
    });
    expect(await after.prepareTakeover({ fence: FENCE, person: 'alice' })).toMatchObject({ ok: true });
    const [taken] = f.events('attempt.taken_over');
    expect(taken?.data.error).toBeNull();
    expect(taken?.data.commands.local).toContain('--resume');
    const clone = cloneOf(f);
    expect(await gitIn(clone, ['symbolic-ref', 'HEAD'])).toBe(`refs/heads/${BRANCH}`);
    const status = await gitIn(clone, ['status', '--porcelain=v1', '--untracked-files=all']);
    expect(statusLines(status)).toEqual(['?? uncommitted.txt', 'M README.md']);
    expect(takeoverViolations(f)).toEqual([]);
    expect(f.events('attempt.exited')).toHaveLength(exited);
  }, 60_000);
});

describe('takeoverCommands', () => {
  const base = {
    wipRefPrefix: FIXTURE_WIP_PREFIX,
    taskId: 'T-4',
    wipRef: WIP,
    branch: BRANCH,
    person: 'alice',
  };
  const local = {
    vendor: 'claude' as const,
    cliVersion: '2.1.0',
    sessionRef: 'session-1',
    clone: '/w/clone',
    runnerDir: '/r',
    home: '/h/claude',
  };
  const anywhere = takeoverAnywhereCommand({
    ref: WIP,
    branch: BRANCH,
    takeoverRef: takeoverRef(FIXTURE_WIP_PREFIX, 'T-4', 'alice'),
  });

  test('builds the Claude and Codex resume commands and the anywhere command', () => {
    expect(takeoverCommands({ ...base, local })).toEqual({
      local: 'cd /w/clone && CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/h/claude /r/vendor/claude/2.1.0/claude --resume session-1',
      anywhere,
    });
    const codex = { ...local, vendor: 'codex' as const, sessionRef: 'thread-1', home: '/h/codex' };
    expect(takeoverCommands({ ...base, local: codex }).local).toBe(
      'cd /w/clone && CODEX_HOME=/h/codex /r/vendor/codex/2.1.0/bin/codex resume --no-daemon thread-1',
    );
  });

  test('gives local null without a session or a clone handed over, and anywhere still', () => {
    expect(takeoverCommands({ ...base, local: { ...local, sessionRef: null } })).toEqual({ local: null, anywhere });
    expect(takeoverCommands({ ...base, local: null })).toEqual({ local: null, anywhere });
  });

  test('quotes paths a shell would split, and a shell reads them back intact', () => {
    const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'agflow-takeover-cmd-'));
    try {
      const clone = join(root, "the person's clone");
      const runnerDir = join(root, 'runner dir');
      const home = join(root, "home $HOME 'x'");
      mkdirSync(clone, { recursive: true });
      // A stand-in for the pinned CLI that prints where it ran and what it was given.
      const binary = join(runnerDir, vendorBinary('claude', local.cliVersion));
      mkdirSync(dirname(binary), { recursive: true });
      writeFileSync(binary, '#!/bin/sh\nprintf "%s\\n" "$PWD" "$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR" "$@"\n', { mode: 0o755 });
      const command = takeoverLocalCommand({ ...local, clone, runnerDir, home, sessionRef: "s 1'" });
      expect(command).toStartWith(`cd '${root}/the person'\\''s clone' && `);
      const ran = Bun.spawnSync(['sh', '-c', command as string], { stdout: 'pipe', stderr: 'pipe' });
      expect(ran.stderr.toString()).toBe('');
      expect(ran.stdout.toString().split('\n')).toEqual([clone, home, '--resume', "s 1'", '']);
    } finally {
      rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true });
    }
  });
});

```ts
// prepare_takeover (design 6.12, 8.4, 9.4). The controller stops the agent with a handoff turn, harvests and pushes
// its WIP, and then hands the clone to a person: the protected paths restored, and the agent's .git replaced wholesale
// by one the runner builds, a fresh `clone --shared` of the vault with HEAD and the task branch at the harvested head
// and the index rebuilt, so `git status` shows the uncommitted work as changes. The agent's .git moves to
// runner/forensics/<attempt>/, out of every later harvest's reach, and is inspected there: program-valued config,
// hooks, commondir or gitdir files and extra alternates are reported as attempt.violation phase takeover. Every other
// .git the agent left in the work tree goes there too, under its path in the clone, since the person's git would
// recurse into it (a committed gitlink makes it a submodule) and run whatever its config names. The runner
// core builds both commands of attempt.taken_over (X-5): the local one runs the runner's pinned binary of the
// attempt's own CLI version (X-13) with its vendor home; the anywhere one is core's takeoverAnywhereCommand.
import { constants } from 'node:fs';
import { chmod, lstat, mkdir, open, readdir, realpath, rename, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { basename, dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { takeoverAnywhereCommand, takeoverRef, type Vendor } from '@agflow/core';
import { readSized } from '../git/clone';
import { type GitEnvironment, runGit } from '../git/run';
import type { Vault } from '../git/vault';
import { vendorBinary } from '../vendor/pins';

/** The reason the take-over's handoff turn quotes. */
export const TAKEOVER_STOP_REASON = 'a person takes the task over';

/** What prepare_takeover gives: attempt.taken_over's seq, or why nothing was taken over. */
export type TakeoverOutcome = { ok: true; takenOverSeq: number } | { ok: false; error: 'stale_fence' | 'not_running' };

const SAFE_SHELL_WORD = /^[A-Za-z0-9_\/.:=@%+,-]+$/;

/** A word a POSIX shell reads back as it is: left bare when safe, single-quoted otherwise. */
export function shellWord(word: string): string {
  return SAFE_SHELL_WORD.test(word) ? word : `'${word.replace(/'/g, `'\\''`)}'`;
}

export interface LocalCommandInput {
  vendor: Vendor;
  /** The CLI version the attempt started with (X-13). */
  cliVersion: string;
  /** The session or thread to resume; null when the agent never started one. */
  sessionRef: string | null;
  /** The clone's real path. */
  clone: string;
  /** RunnerPaths.runner, under which the pinned binaries live. */
  runnerDir: string;
  /** The vendor's home as the agents had it: vendorHomes(config, paths)[vendor]. */
  home: string;
}

export interface TakeoverCommandsInput {
  /** What the local command resumes; null when the clone was not handed over. */
  local: LocalCommandInput | null;
  wipRefPrefix: string;
  taskId: string;
  /** The attempt's WIP ref, which the anywhere command fetches. */
  wipRef: string;
  branch: string;
  /** The person's login, which names their take-over ref. */
  person: string;
}

/**
 * The take-over command on the runner's laptop (design 6.12): the pinned binary of the attempt's own CLI version
 * resuming its session in the clone, with the runner's vendor home. Null without a session to resume.
 */
export function takeoverLocalCommand(input: LocalCommandInput): string | null {
  if (input.sessionRef === null) return null;
  const binary = shellWord(join(input.runnerDir, vendorBinary(input.vendor, input.cliVersion)));
  const session = shellWord(input.sessionRef);
  const resume =
    input.vendor === 'claude'
      ? `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=${shellWord(input.home)} ${binary} --resume ${session}`
      : `CODEX_HOME=${shellWord(input.home)} ${binary} resume --no-daemon ${session}`;
  return `cd ${shellWord(input.clone)} && ${resume}`;
}

/**
 * attempt.taken_over's commands: the local one (null when the clone was not handed over or has no session), and
 * anywhere, the fetch of the WIP ref onto the task branch and the push to the person's take-over ref, as core builds
 * it for the hub too.
 */
export function takeoverCommands(input: TakeoverCommandsInput): { local: string | null; anywhere: string } {
  const anywhere = takeoverAnywhereCommand({
    ref: input.wipRef,
    branch: input.branch,
    takeoverRef: takeoverRef(input.wipRefPrefix, input.taskId, input.person),
  });
  return { local: input.local === null ? null : takeoverLocalCommand(input.local), anywhere };
}

/** Where the next of an attempt's moved-aside git directories goes: git, then git-2, git-3 and so on. */
async function forensicsTarget(forensics: string): Promise<string> {
  await mkdir(forensics, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
  for (let n = 1; ; n++) {
    const target = join(forensics, n === 1 ? 'git' : `git-${n}`);
    if ((await lstat(target).catch(() => null)) === null) return target;
  }
}

/**
 * Replaces <clone>/.git with a git directory the runner builds: a `clone --shared --no-checkout` of the vault, with
 * HEAD on the task branch at head and the index read from it, and .agflow/run/ excluded. The old .git, whatever it
 * is, moves to the next free place under forensics. Gives where it went; null when the clone had none.
 */
export async function replaceGitDir(input: {
  vault: Vault;
  local: GitEnvironment;
  clone: string;
  branch: string;
  head: string;
  forensics: string;
}): Promise<string | null> {
  const { vault, local, clone, branch, head } = input;
  // Built beside the clone, never inside it, so nothing of the agent's can reach the new directory first.
  const building = join(dirname(clone), `.${basename(clone)}.takeover`);
  await rm(building, { recursive: true, force: true });
  try {
    await runGit(local, ['clone', '--quiet', '--shared', '--no-checkout', '--template=', vault.path, building]);
    const gitDir = join(building, '.git');
    const git = (args: string[]) => runGit(local, [`--git-dir=${gitDir}`, ...args]);
    await git(['update-ref', `refs/heads/${branch}`, head]);
    await git(['symbolic-ref', 'HEAD', `refs/heads/${branch}`]);
    await git(['read-tree', head]);
    await mkdir(join(gitDir, 'info'), { recursive: true });
    await writeFile(join(gitDir, 'info', 'exclude'), '# Written by the agflow runner.\n/.agflow/run/\n');
    const old = join(clone, '.git');
    let moved: string | null = null;
    if ((await lstat(old).catch(() => null)) !== null) {
      moved = await forensicsTarget(input.forensics);
      await rename(old, moved);
    }
    await rename(gitDir, old);
    return moved;
  } finally {
    await rm(building, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

/**
 * Moves every .git the agent left in the clone's work tree, other than the clone's own, whatever it is (a directory,
 * a file or a link), to forensics/nested/<n>/<its path in the clone>, n counting take-overs. The walk never follows
 * a link and skips nothing else, .agflow/run included; a directory the agent made unreadable is made readable first.
 * Gives the moved entries' paths in the clone and where each went, in path order.
 */
export async function moveNestedGitDirs(input: {
  clone: string;
  forensics: string;
}): Promise<{ path: string; moved: string }[]> {
  const { clone } = input;
  const found: string[] = [];
  const pending = [''];
  while (pending.length > 0) {
    const dir = pending.pop() as string;
    const full = dir === '' ? clone : join(clone, dir);
    const entries = await readdir(full, { withFileTypes: true }).catch(async () => {
      await chmod(full, 0o700);
      return readdir(full, { withFileTypes: true });
    });
    for (const entry of entries) {
      const path = dir === '' ? entry.name : `${dir}/${entry.name}`;
      // The clone's own .git is replaced as a whole.
      if (path === '.git') continue;
      if (entry.name === '.git') found.push(path);
      else if (entry.isDirectory()) pending.push(path);
    }
  }
  if (found.length === 0) return [];
  const nested = join(input.forensics, 'nested');
  await mkdir(nested, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
  let target = '';
  for (let n = 1; ; n++) {
    target = join(nested, String(n));
    if ((await lstat(target).catch(() => null)) === null) break;
  }
  const moved: { path: string; moved: string }[] = [];
  for (const path of found.sort()) {
    const to = join(target, path);
    await mkdir(dirname(to), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
    await rename(join(clone, path), to);
    moved.push({ path, moved: to });
  }
  return moved;
}

/** The config keys whose values git runs as programs or reads as other configuration, lower-cased as git lists them. */
const PROGRAM_KEYS = new Set([
  'core.hookspath',
  'core.alternaterefscommand',
  'gpg.ssh.defaultkeycommand',
  'core.sshcommand',
  'core.editor',
  'core.pager',
  'core.askpass',
  'core.gitproxy',
  'core.worktree',
  'sequence.editor',
  'diff.external',
  'gpg.program',
  'credential.helper',
  'interactive.difffilter',
  'uploadpack.packobjectshook',
  'web.browser',
  'include.path',
]);

const PROGRAM_KEY_PATTERNS = [
  /^includeif\..+\.path$/,
  /^filter\..+\.(clean|smudge|process)$/,
  /^diff\..+\.(textconv|command)$/,
  /^merge\..+\.driver$/,
  /^credential\..+\.helper$/,
  /^gpg\..+\.program$/,
  /^remote\..+\.(uploadpack|receivepack|vcs)$/,
  /^(difftool|mergetool|man|browser)\..+\.(cmd|path)$/,
  /^pager\..+$/,
  /^trailer\..+\.(cmd|command)$/,
  /^sendemail\..*cmd$/,
  /^tar\..+\.command$/,
];

/** Whether git would run a config entry's value, or read another file through it. */
function isProgramValued(key: string, value: string): boolean {
  if (PROGRAM_KEYS.has(key) || PROGRAM_KEY_PATTERNS.some((pattern) => pattern.test(key))) return true;
  // fsmonitor is a boolean for git's own daemon, and a program otherwise.
  if (key === 'core.fsmonitor') return !/^(true|false|yes|no|on|off|1|0)?$/i.test(value.trim());
  // An alias or a submodule's update mode that starts with ! is a shell command.
  const shell = value.trimStart().startsWith('!');
  return shell && (key.startsWith('alias.') || /^submodule\..+\.update$/.test(key));
}

/** A small file of the moved .git, read without following a link; null when it is absent. */
async function readSmallFile(path: string, maxBytes: number): Promise<string | null> {
  let handle: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof open>>;
  try {
    handle = await open(path, constants.O_RDONLY | constants.O_NOFOLLOW | constants.O_NONBLOCK);
  } catch (error) {
    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'ENOENT') return null;
    throw error;
  }
  try {
    const stat = await handle.stat();
    if (!stat.isFile() || stat.size > maxBytes) throw new Error(`${path} is not a small regular file`);
    return await readSized(handle, stat.size, path);
  } finally {
    await handle.close();
  }
}

/**
 * Lists one config file of a moved .git, its includes not followed, adding each program-valued key to found as
 * `<label>:<key>`; a file that is not a regular one, or that git cannot list, is reported as label.
 */
async function inspectConfigFile(local: GitEnvironment, file: string, label: string, found: string[]): Promise<void> {
  const stat = await lstat(file).catch(() => null);
  if (stat === null) return;
  if (!stat.isFile()) {
    found.push(label);
    return;
  }
  // --no-includes: the listing itself must not read the files the agent pointed at.
  const listed = await runGit(local, ['config', '--file', file, '--no-includes', '--list', '-z'], { check: false });
  if (listed.code !== 0) found.push(label);
  for (const entry of listed.stdout.split('\0')) {
    if (entry === '') continue;
    const newline = entry.indexOf('\n');
    const key = newline < 0 ? entry : entry.slice(0, newline);
    const value = newline < 0 ? '' : entry.slice(newline + 1);
    if (isProgramValued(key, value)) found.push(`${label}:${key}`);
  }
}

/**
 * What an agent's moved .git held that the runner never planted, as paths relative to the clone, label (`.git`, or a
 * nested one's path) standing for the directory: program-valued config keys (`.git/config:<key>`, and those of
 * config.worktree and each worktrees/<name>/config.worktree, which git reads with extensions.worktreeConfig), hooks,
 * commondir and gitdir files, and alternates other than the vault's objects. Anything that is a link, or that cannot
 * be read as the runner expects, is reported as it stands.
 */
export async function inspectAgentGitDir(input: {
  gitDir: string;
  local: GitEnvironment;
  vault: Vault;
  label?: string;
}): Promise<string[]> {
  const { gitDir, local } = input;
  const label = input.label ?? '.git';
  const found: string[] = [];
  const top = await lstat(gitDir);
  if (!top.isDirectory()) return [label];
  await inspectConfigFile(local, join(gitDir, 'config'), `${label}/config`, found);
  await inspectConfigFile(local, join(gitDir, 'config.worktree'), `${label}/config.worktree`, found);
  const worktrees = join(gitDir, 'worktrees');
  const worktreesStat = await lstat(worktrees).catch(() => null);
  if (worktreesStat !== null && !worktreesStat.isDirectory()) found.push(`${label}/worktrees`);
  else if (worktreesStat !== null) {
    const names = await readdir(worktrees).catch(() => null);
    if (names === null) found.push(`${label}/worktrees`);
    for (const name of (names ?? []).sort()) {
      const file = join(worktrees, name, 'config.worktree');
      await inspectConfigFile(local, file, `${label}/worktrees/${name}/config.worktree`, found);
    }
  }
  const hooks = join(gitDir, 'hooks');
  const hooksStat = await lstat(hooks).catch(() => null);
  if (hooksStat !== null && !hooksStat.isDirectory()) found.push(`${label}/hooks`);
  else if (hooksStat !== null) {
    // The runner makes clones with no template: whatever is here, the agent put here. git never runs a .sample, and
    // a directory the runner cannot read is suspect in itself.
    const names = await readdir(hooks).catch(() => null);
    if (names === null) found.push(`${label}/hooks`);
    for (const name of (names ?? []).sort()) {
      if (!name.endsWith('.sample')) found.push(`${label}/hooks/${name}`);
    }
  }
  for (const name of ['commondir', 'gitdir']) {
    if ((await lstat(join(gitDir, name)).catch(() => null)) !== null) found.push(`${label}/${name}`);
  }
  const alternates = join(gitDir, 'objects', 'info', 'alternates');
  let lines: string[] = [];
  try {
    lines = ((await readSmallFile(alternates, 64 * 1024)) ?? '').split('\n');
  } catch {
    found.push(`${label}/objects/info/alternates`);
  }
  const vaultObjects = new Set([join(input.vault.path, 'objects')]);
  vaultObjects.add(await realpath(join(input.vault.path, 'objects')).catch(() => join(input.vault.path, 'objects')));
  const extra = lines.map((line) => line.trim()).filter((line) => line !== '' && !line.startsWith('#'));
  if (extra.some((line) => !vaultObjects.has(line))) found.push(`${label}/objects/info/alternates`);
  return found;
}
```

A failure after the stop still reports `attempt.taken_over`, with `local` null and the error. A `prepare_takeover` resent after a restart starts again at the harvest. The tests wait for phase `turn` and the turn's last write before they take over; otherwise the handoff prompt can queue behind a turn the stop has not seen start, and be dropped. A take-over's final work that leaves work for a late-work ref is also recorded as `lateWorkSha`, before `attempt.taken_over`, and uses the same durable retry contract as an exit.

### Task 32: The attempt controller: cleanup and transcripts

`cleanup_attempt` (design 6.4, 7.8) stops a live process first. Before it deletes anything, it pushes the late work still pending (the record's `lateWorkSha`, the exit's own harvest, which the vault holds even when the clone is gone), then saves the clone's work not yet on the origin, each to a new late-work ref with `attempt.late_work`. It uploads the transcript tail, deletes the vendor transcript, removes the clone, the pins, the private tmp directory, the tools directory, the quarantine and the forensics directory, and releases the base checkout. The record stays with `endedAt` set and no clone, which drops it from hello's list. A late push that fails keeps the clone and answers the command with the error, and the work it could not push becomes pending late work, retried until it lands, since the hub never sends a failed cleanup again. `upload_transcript` posts the tail without a live session. Successful work resolution clears `pushError` before removal; failed harvest or push resolution preserves the unresolved error.

**File:** `packages/runner/src/attempt/cleanup.ts` (new)

```ts
// cleanup_attempt and upload_transcript (design 6.4 Cleanup, 6.3, 7.8). A cleanup first stops a live process with the
// stop ladder (an accept or reject during a hold), then pushes the late work still pending (AttemptRecord.lateWorkSha)
// and saves the clone's work that is not yet on the origin to a new late-work ref, each reported as attempt.late_work,
// before anything is deleted: a late push that fails keeps the clone and answers the command with the reason. Then
// the transcript tail is uploaded, and the clone, the attempt's vault pins, its private /tmp/agf/<id> directory, its
// tools, quarantine and forensics directories and the vendor's transcript are removed, and the base checkout
// released. The record stays, with endedAt, the clone forgotten, so hello no longer lists the attempt (isCleanedUp).
// upload_transcript posts the tail of an attempt with no live session, for attempts the hub ended lost.
import { chmod, lstat, readdir, rm } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import type { AttemptRecord } from '../attempt-store';

/** The reason a cleanup gives the stop of a process still alive. */
export const CLEANUP_STOP_REASON = 'the attempt is cleaned up';

/** What cleanup_attempt gives: done, or why the clone was kept (a late push that failed, say). */
export type CleanupOutcome = { ok: true } | { ok: false; error: string };

/** Whether cleanup_attempt has run for the record: hello no longer lists such an attempt. */
export function isCleanedUp(record: Pick<AttemptRecord, 'clone' | 'endedAt'>): boolean {
  return record.clone === null && record.endedAt !== null;
}

/** Makes every directory under dir writable again, never following a link, so its entries can be removed. */
async function makeWritable(dir: string): Promise<void> {
  await chmod(dir, 0o700).catch(() => {});
  const entries = await readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true }).catch(() => []);
  for (const entry of entries) {
    if (entry.isDirectory()) await makeWritable(join(dir, entry.name));
  }
}

/**
 * Removes a file tree the agent wrote, links as links. Directories it made read-only are made writable first, so
 * nothing is left behind; a path that does not exist is no error.
 */
export async function removeTree(path: string): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await rm(path, { recursive: true, force: true });
  } catch (error) {
    const code = (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;
    if (code !== 'EACCES' && code !== 'EPERM' && code !== 'ENOTEMPTY') throw error;
    const stat = await lstat(path).catch(() => null);
    if (stat?.isDirectory()) await makeWritable(path);
    await rm(path, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run the tests and see them pass**

Run: `bun test packages/runner/test/controller-cleanup.test.ts && bun test && bun run typecheck`
Expected: the task's tests pass; then the whole suite passes (`0 fail`) and `tsc` exits 0.

'Not yet on the origin' is decided by tree, since every snapshot makes a new commit. A pending sha the vault no longer holds is dropped from the record: nothing is left to push. When the origin's refs cannot be read, the clone's work is pushed unchecked, so at worst a late-work ref holds a tree twice. The cleanup marks the attempt ended first, so `endedAt` is set even when a later step fails. Read-only directories are made writable before removal, and links are never followed.

Clear pushError when a successful harvest proves the work matches the start tree or a WIP/late-work tree on origin (successful late-work pushes already clear it). Clear before file removal so a later removal failure cannot retain it. Failed harvest, origin lookup or push preserve unresolved errors. The existing policy of removing an unharvestable clone with a note is kept and is not work resolution. Tests: stale-error clearing for unchanged work, preservation after harvest/push failure, clearing after successful retry.

### Task 33: The attempt controller: hand-back

`hand_back` with the clone source returns a person's work to the task (design 6.12). It stops the runner-home Codex daemon with the runner's codex binary (errors ignored), and refuses while a process runs in the clone with `{ ok: false, error: 'process_running' }`, the pids and an `attempt.activity` note (X-37). Otherwise it harvests and strips the person's work like a WIP (violations report phase `wip`, X-3), pushes it to a new late-work ref, reports `attempt.handed_back` and cleans the attempt up. The person's work holds the agent's, so the push settles the agent's pending late work (`lateWorkCount` updated, `lateWorkSha` and `pushError` null in one update before reporting and cleanup), whatever the cleanup does. A ref source, which protocol-1 hubs never send, only fetches the ref into the vault and answers ok, with no event (X-2).

import { afterEach, describe, expect, setDefaultTimeout, test } from 'bun:test';
import { chmodSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { lateWorkRef, takeoverRef } from '@agflow/core';
import { commitFiles, type FakeScript, gitIn } from '@agflow/testkit';
import { isCleanedUp } from '../src/attempt/cleanup';
import { vendorHomes } from '../src/config';
import { vendorBinary } from '../src/vendor/pins';
import {
  cleanupRunnerFixtures,
  createRunnerFixture,
  FIXTURE_PROJECT,
  FIXTURE_WIP_PREFIX,
  fixtureCliVersion,
  type RunnerFixture,
  waitFor,
} from './fixture';
import { requireLsofOnMacOS } from './prerequisites';

afterEach(cleanupRunnerFixtures);

// Every test here runs git or agent processes, which take several times as long on a machine loaded by other suites.
setDefaultTimeout(30_000);

const FENCE = { epoch: 1, counter: 1 };
const CLONE = { kind: 'clone' } as const;

const WORKING: FakeScript = {
  turns: [
    [
      { do: 'write', path: 'work.txt', content: 'work\n' },
      { do: 'sleep', ms: 20_000 },
    ],
    [{ do: 'terminal', tool: 'handoff' }],
  ],
};

const cloneOf = (f: RunnerFixture) => f.paths.clone(FIXTURE_PROJECT, 'T-4-a1');

/** Starts T-4-a1 and takes it over, as a person in the browser would. */
async function takenOver(f: RunnerFixture) {
  const controller = f.controller();
  await controller.start(f.spec());
  await waitFor(() => existsSync(join(cloneOf(f), 'work.txt')) && controller.phase === 'turn');
  expect(await controller.prepareTakeover({ fence: FENCE, person: 'alice' })).toMatchObject({ ok: true });
  return controller;
}

/** A stand-in for the runner's pinned codex that records how it was run, then fails. */
function fakeCodex(f: RunnerFixture): string {
  const binary = join(f.paths.runner, vendorBinary('codex', fixtureCliVersion('codex')));
  const record = join(f.home, 'codex-ran.txt');
  mkdirSync(dirname(binary), { recursive: true });
  writeFileSync(binary, `#!/bin/sh\necho "$CODEX_HOME $*" >> '${record}'\nexit 3\n`);
  chmodSync(binary, 0o755);
  return record;
}

```ts
// hand_back (design 6.12 Hand back, 7.3 Late work, X-37, X-2). With the clone source, the runner first stops the
// runner-home Codex daemon a person's `codex resume` may have left (errors ignored), and refuses while any process
// still runs in the clone: { ok: false, error: 'process_running' } with the pids, and an attempt.activity note, so
// the person can end it and hand back again; when it cannot look (no lsof), it refuses too. Otherwise it harvests
// the clone, the person's commits and uncommitted work, strips and checks it like a WIP (violations report phase
// wip), pushes it to a new late-work ref, reports attempt.handed_back and cleans the attempt up. A ref source, which
// protocol-1 hubs never send, only fetches the ref into the vault and answers ok, with no event.
import { boundedWait } from '../processes';

/** How long the Codex daemon's stop may take before it is killed. */
export const DAEMON_STOP_MS = 10_000;

export type HandBackSource = { kind: 'clone' } | { kind: 'ref'; ref: string; sha: string };

/**
 * What hand_back gives: the late-work ref the clone's work went to (null for a ref source); a process still in the
 * clone, with its pids; or why the hand-back failed, with the clone kept.
 */
export type HandBackOutcome =
  | { ok: true; handedBack: { ref: string; sha: string } | null }
  | { ok: false; error: 'process_running'; pids: number[] }
  | { ok: false; error: string };

/** The activity note of a hand-back refused for processes still running in the clone. */
export function processRunningNote(pids: readonly number[]): string {
  return `hand-back refused: processes still run in the clone (pids ${pids.join(', ')}); end them and hand back again`;
}

/**
 * Stops the Codex daemon of the runner's Codex home: `CODEX_HOME=<home> <codex> app-server daemon stop`, bounded by
 * DAEMON_STOP_MS. Whatever happens, a missing binary or a failed stop, is no error: there may be no daemon at all.
 */
export async function stopCodexDaemon(input: {
  binary: string;
  home: string;
  /** The rest of the environment: the runner's captured PATH and the codex-user HOME. */
  env: Record<string, string>;
  timeoutMs?: number;
}): Promise<void> {
  let proc: Bun.Subprocess;
  try {
    proc = Bun.spawn([input.binary, 'app-server', 'daemon', 'stop'], {
      env: { ...input.env, CODEX_HOME: input.home },
      stdin: 'ignore',
      stdout: 'ignore',
      stderr: 'ignore',
    });
  } catch {
    return;
  }
  const exited = await boundedWait(proc.exited, input.timeoutMs ?? DAEMON_STOP_MS);
  if (!exited.done) proc.kill('SIGKILL');
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run the tests and see them pass**

Run: `bun test packages/runner/test/controller-handback.test.ts && bun test && bun run typecheck`
Expected: on macOS, 7 pass, 0 fail, no skips across 1 file (49 expect() calls); then the whole suite passes (`0 fail`) and `tsc` exits 0.

When `lsof` cannot run, the hand-back is refused and the clone kept, with a note. macOS must execute every clone-sweep, orphan-cleanup and hand-back security assertion. Missing lsof on macOS fails with a prerequisite diagnostic. Keep portable cases enabled on Linux; macOS-only cases use test.skipIf(process.platform !== 'darwin') with the reason ‘the runner supports darwin-arm64 only; design 7.1’. Never omit individual safety assertions or return early because lsof is missing on macOS. After a hand-back the cleanup does not push the agent's pending late work: the hand-back ref already carries the person's continuation of it. `findCloneProcesses` is split out of `sweepCloneProcesses`, with no change in behaviour.

A successful clone hand-back updates lateWorkCount, lateWorkSha = null and pushError = null together before attempt.handed_back and cleanup. Failed harvest/push preserves the error. Regression: reject a hand-back push first, then allow it and force cleanup removal failure: hand-back succeeds, pending work and pushError are cleared, the cleanup failure is logged. Ref-source behaviour unchanged. The macOS cases call `requireLsofOnMacOS` before fixture creation; its error names PATH and `/usr/sbin`.

      cliVersion: '1.0.0',
      ownerCliVersion: null,
      ready: true,
      problem: 'test mode',
      accountId: TEST_ACCOUNT_ID,
      plan: 'test mode',
      managedPolicy: false,
      ...fields,
    },
    quota: QUOTA,
    weakened,
  };
}

describe('createAdapters', () => {
  test("lists each vendor's entry, and an entry gives null or its own vendor's adapter", () => {
    const { config, paths } = setup();
    expect(ADAPTER_FACTORIES).toEqual([claudeAdapterFactory, codexAdapterFactory]);
    expect(createAdapters(config, paths, { agflow: AGFLOW, factories: [() => null, () => null] })).toEqual([]);
    // Holds before and after M2d and M2e fill the entries.
    expect(claudeAdapterFactory({ config, paths, agflow: AGFLOW })?.vendor ?? 'claude').toBe('claude');
    expect(codexAdapterFactory({ config, paths, agflow: AGFLOW })?.vendor ?? 'codex').toBe('codex');
  });

  test('refuses two adapters of one vendor', () => {
    const { config, paths } = setup();
    const factory = (): AdapterFactory => () =>
      new FakeAdapter({ vendor: 'claude', skipAuthChecks: true, script: { turns: [[]] } });
    expect(() => createAdapters(config, paths, { agflow: AGFLOW, factories: [factory(), factory()] })).toThrow(
      'two adapters for claude',
    );
  });

  test('passes the config, the paths and the agflow command to each factory, and keeps what they return', () => {
    const { config, paths } = setup();
    const fake = new FakeAdapter({ vendor: 'codex', skipAuthChecks: true, script: { turns: [[]] } });
    const seen: Parameters<AdapterFactory>[0][] = [];
    const stub: AdapterFactory = (input) => {
      seen.push(input);
      return fake;
    };
    const none: AdapterFactory = () => null;
    expect(createAdapters(config, paths, { agflow: AGFLOW, factories: [none, stub] })).toEqual([fake]);
    expect(seen).toEqual([{ config, paths, agflow: AGFLOW }]);
  });
});

    ).toBe(false);

    const auto = setup({ profile: 'auto' }).config;
    const standard = setup().config;
    const nameOf = (config: typeof auto, weakened: string[]) =>
      vendorReport({

        preflights: [preflight('claude', {}, weakened), preflight('codex')],
        at: 1,
        preparer: skipDependencyPreparer,
      }).profile.name;
    expect(nameOf(auto, ['auto'])).toBe('auto');
    expect(nameOf(auto, ['/tmp/claude'])).toBe('standard');
    expect(nameOf(standard, ['auto'])).toBe('standard');
  });

```ts
// The adapter registry (design 13, X-6). Each vendor has an entry file, adapters/<vendor>/entry.ts, exporting an
// AdapterFactory; createAdapters asks each one and keeps what it returns. The entries return null until M2d and M2e
// fill them, and they fill only their own entry file, never this one. `agflow runner start`'s host calls
// createAdapters unless its caller injects adapters.
import type { RunnerConfig } from '../config';
import type { RunnerPaths } from '../paths';
import { claudeAdapterFactory } from './claude/entry';
import { codexAdapterFactory } from './codex/entry';
import type { AdapterFactory, AgflowCommand, VendorAdapter } from './types';

/** Every vendor's entry, in the order adapters are listed. */
export const ADAPTER_FACTORIES: readonly AdapterFactory[] = [claudeAdapterFactory, codexAdapterFactory];

/**
 * The adapters whose entries return one, given the runner's settings, its layout and how it runs agflow. Two for
 * one vendor throw: the runtime keys adapters by vendor, and hello would list the vendor twice.
 */
export function createAdapters(
  config: RunnerConfig,
  paths: RunnerPaths,
  options: { agflow: AgflowCommand; factories?: readonly AdapterFactory[] },
): VendorAdapter[] {
  const factories = options.factories ?? ADAPTER_FACTORIES;
  const adapters = factories.flatMap((factory) => factory({ config, paths, agflow: options.agflow }) ?? []);
  const seen = new Set<VendorAdapter['vendor']>();
  for (const adapter of adapters) {
    if (seen.has(adapter.vendor)) throw new Error(`two adapters for ${adapter.vendor}`);
    seen.add(adapter.vendor);
  }
  return adapters;
}
```

**File:** `packages/runner/src/vendors.ts` (new)

```ts
// What hello and runner.vendors say about the runner's vendors (design 6.3, 13, X-5). Each adapter's preflight gives
// its facts, its quota and the boundaries it cannot enforce; vendorReport adds what runner.json says (models,
// ceilings, allowPaidUsage), when the preflight ran, and degraded false, which only the hub's vendor holds change. A
// quota report without an account id is left out (X-21). The profile is 'auto' only when runner.json asks for it and
// an adapter reports the auto profile as weakened, so it is in force (X-29); otherwise 'standard'. Its weakened list
// merges the runner's own with every adapter's, without duplicates.
import type { AccountQuotaReport, ProfileSummary, RunnerVendor } from '@agflow/core';
import type { PreflightResult } from './adapters/types';
import type { RunnerConfig } from './config';
import type { DependencyPreparer } from './seams';

/** What hello carries about the vendors, and runner.vendors after each preflight. */
export interface VendorReport {
  vendors: RunnerVendor[];
  quota: AccountQuotaReport[];
  profile: ProfileSummary;
}

export interface VendorReportInput {
  config: Pick<RunnerConfig, 'models' | 'ceilings' | 'allowPaidUsage' | 'profile'>;
  /** The adapters' preflights, one per vendor. */
  preflights: readonly PreflightResult[];
  /** When the preflights ran, epoch ms. */
  at: number;
  preparer: Pick<DependencyPreparer, 'available'>;
  /** The runner's own boundaries it cannot enforce, merged with the adapters'. */
  weakened?: readonly string[];
}

export function vendorReport(input: VendorReportInput): VendorReport {
  const { config, preflights } = input;
  const vendors = preflights.map(
    ({ facts }): RunnerVendor => ({
      ...facts,
      models: { ...config.models[facts.vendor] },
      ceilings: { ...config.ceilings[facts.vendor] },
      allowPaidUsage: config.allowPaidUsage[facts.vendor],
      degraded: false,
      preflightAt: input.at,
    }),
  );
  const quota = preflights.flatMap(({ facts, quota }): AccountQuotaReport[] =>
    quota !== null && facts.accountId !== null ? [{ vendor: facts.vendor, accountId: facts.accountId, quota }] : [],
  );
  const weakened = [...new Set([...(input.weakened ?? []), ...preflights.flatMap((result) => result.weakened)])];
  const auto = config.profile === 'auto' && preflights.some((result) => result.weakened.includes('auto'));
  return {
    vendors,
    quota,
    profile: { name: auto ? 'auto' : 'standard', weakened, dependencyPrep: input.preparer.available },
  };
}
```

### Task 35: The command executor

The command executor turns hub commands into controller work (design 6.3). It journals each valid command as running and then done, so a resend joins the first run or gets its stored result; lifecycle and git commands of one attempt run on its serial queue, live commands act at once, and unknown or invalid commands answer `unsupported`. It applies `welcome.stop` before any command (X-36), handles the 17 kinds (X-2) and the runner-level commands, and after a restart runs again the journal rows of the restartable kinds and answers the rest `interrupted`. `update_settings` runs through the new `SettingsSync` (`settings-sync.ts`), the runner side of design 6.3's settings sync (X-12): a local edit is in flight until an echo answers it and the snapshot reaches that echo's version, and runner.json holds the snapshot with the edits in flight laid over it. The answers live in the runner.db meta key `settingsEchoed` with the echo's version. Each hello starts a new lineage of commands, so an echo taken before it answers nothing and waits for the hub's resend; an echo that fails or would skip a version waits and is retried locally; and a probe settles the edits the hub refused (see Decisions).

import { afterEach, describe, expect, setDefaultTimeout, spyOn, test } from 'bun:test';
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { COMMAND_MIN_PROTOCOL, type RunnerCommand, RunnerCommandSchema, type Vendor } from '@agflow/core';
import { gitIn } from '@agflow/testkit';
import type { PreflightResult } from '../src/adapters/types';
import type { AttemptController, ControllerDeps } from '../src/attempt/controller';
import { saveRunnerConfig } from '../src/config';
import { CommandExecutor, RESTARTABLE_COMMANDS } from '../src/executor';
import { Journal } from '../src/journal';
import type { CommandMessage, WelcomeMessage } from '../src/link';
import { Outbox } from '../src/outbox';
import type { PrepareInput } from '../src/seams';
import { vendorReport } from '../src/vendors';
import {
  cleanupRunnerFixtures,
  createRunnerFixture,
  FIXTURE_PROJECT,
  FIXTURE_WIP_PREFIX,
  type RunnerFixture,
  waitFor,
} from './fixture';

// Every test here runs git or agent processes, which take several times as long on a machine loaded by other suites.
setDefaultTimeout(30_000);

const liveControllers: AttemptController[] = [];
afterEach(async () => {
  // Close fake sessions first, so an assertion failure does not leave an idle child waiting on stdin.
  for (const controller of liveControllers.splice(0)) await controller.session?.close();
  await cleanupRunnerFixtures();
});

const FENCE = { epoch: 1, counter: 1 };
const STOP = {
  kind: 'stop_attempt',
  attemptId: 'T-4-a1',
  fence: FENCE,
  cause: 'stop',
  reason: 'stopped by a person',
  handoff: false,
  interruptFirst: false,
  keepClone: true,
} as const;

function message(command: RunnerCommand, seq = 1): CommandMessage {
  return { t: 'command', id: `1-R-1-${seq}`, seq, command };
}

function welcome(stop: WelcomeMessage['stop']): WelcomeMessage {
  return {
    t: 'welcome',
    runnerId: 'R-1',
    hubEpoch: 1,
    hubTime: Date.now(),
    ackedSeq: 0,
    wipRefPrefix: FIXTURE_WIP_PREFIX,
    stop,
    timings: { heartbeatMs: 15_000, deadLinkMs: 45_000, handoffMs: 2_000, wipGraceMs: 300_000 },
  };
}

/** Timers a test fires by hand. */
function manualTimers() {
  const set: { run: () => void; ms: number; done: boolean }[] = [];
  const waiting = () => set.filter((timer) => !timer.done);
  return {
    setTimeout: (run: () => void, ms: number) => {
      const timer = { run, ms, done: false };
      set.push(timer);
      return timer;
    },
    clearTimeout: (handle: unknown) => {
      (handle as { done: boolean }).done = true;
    },
    /** The timers set and neither fired nor cleared, oldest first. */
    waiting,
    /** Fires the oldest waiting timer. */
    fire: () => {
      const timer = waiting()[0];
      if (timer === undefined) throw new Error('no timer is waiting');
      timer.done = true;
      timer.run();
    },
  };
}

/** The runtime wiring. */
function executor(f: RunnerFixture, overrides: Partial<ControllerDeps> = {}) {
  const journal = new Journal(f.db);
  const controllers = new Map<string, AttemptController>();
  const controller = (id: string) => {
    let value = controllers.get(id);
    if (!value) {
      value = f.controller(id, overrides);
      controllers.set(id, value);
      liveControllers.push(value);
    }
    return value;
  };
  const deps = f.deps(overrides);
  // Each vendor's last preflight, as the runtime keeps them.
  const preflights = new Map<Vendor, { result: PreflightResult; at: number }>();
  const options = {
    journal,
    controller,
    known: (id: string) => controllers.has(id) || f.store.get(id) !== null,
    config: () => f.config,
    // As the runtime does: config() gives the new settings even when the write fails.
    saveConfig: (config: RunnerFixture['config']) => {
      f.config = config;
      saveRunnerConfig(f.paths.config, config);
    },
    outbox: f.outbox,
    vault: f.vault,
    local: f.local,
    remote: deps.remote,
    wipRefPrefix: () => FIXTURE_WIP_PREFIX,
    adapters: f.adapters,
    preflighted: (result: PreflightResult) => preflights.set(result.facts.vendor, { result, at: Date.now() }),
    vendors: () => {
      const each = [...preflights.values()].map(({ result, at }) =>
        vendorReport({ config: f.config, preflights: [result], at, preparer: deps.preparer }),
      );
      return { vendors: each.flatMap((report) => report.vendors), quota: each.flatMap((report) => report.quota) };
    },
    logger: f.logger,
  };
  return { run: new CommandExecutor(options), journal, controller, options, preflights };
}

function commands(f: RunnerFixture): RunnerCommand[] {
  const attemptId = 'T-4-a1';
  return [
    { kind: 'start_attempt', attempt: f.spec() },
    {
      kind: 'resume_attempt',
      attemptId,
      fence: FENCE,
      agentToken: f.spec().agentToken,
      prompt: 'resume',
      messages: [],
      taskPack: null,
      restore: f.spec().restore,
      acceptanceIds: [],
    },
    STOP,
    { kind: 'hold_attempt', attemptId, fence: FENCE },
    { kind: 'deliver', attemptId, fence: FENCE, messages: [], more: 0 },
    { kind: 'interrupt', attemptId, fence: FENCE },
    { kind: 'decide_approval', attemptId, fence: FENCE, approvalId: randomUUID(), decision: 'approve', reason: null },
    {
      kind: 'push_submission',
      attemptId,
      fence: FENCE,
      submissionId: 'S-1',
      branch: 'agflow/T-4-tidy',
      expectedBranchSha: null,
      adoptable: [],
    },
    { kind: 'prepare_takeover', attemptId, fence: FENCE, person: 'owner' },
    { kind: 'hand_back', attemptId, source: { kind: 'clone' } },
    { kind: 'cleanup_attempt', attemptId },
    { kind: 'upload_transcript', attemptId },
    { kind: 'prepare_dependencies', attemptId, fence: FENCE, requestId: '1-R-1-99' },
    { kind: 'refresh_vault', taskId: 'T-4', refs: [] },
    { kind: 'delete_refs', refs: [] },
    { kind: 'update_settings', settings: { capacity: 3 }, version: 1 },
    { kind: 'preflight', vendor: 'claude' },
  ];
}

/** Dispatch probes, leaving process, git and preparation behavior to the integration tests below. */
function probes(controller: AttemptController) {
  return {
    start_attempt: spyOn(controller, 'start').mockResolvedValue({ started: true }),
    resume_attempt: spyOn(controller, 'resume').mockResolvedValue({ resumed: true }),
    stop_attempt: spyOn(controller, 'stop').mockResolvedValue({ ok: true, stoppedBy: 'none', exitedSeq: 1 }),
    hold_attempt: spyOn(controller, 'hold').mockResolvedValue({ ok: true, stoppedBy: 'none', exitedSeq: 1 }),
    deliver: spyOn(controller, 'deliver').mockResolvedValue({ ok: true }),
    interrupt: spyOn(controller, 'interrupt').mockResolvedValue({ ok: true }),
    decide_approval: spyOn(controller, 'decideApproval').mockResolvedValue({ applied: false }),
    push_submission: spyOn(controller, 'submit').mockResolvedValue({
      ok: true,
      outcome: { submissionId: 'S-1', ok: true, headSha: 'a'.repeat(40), remoteHead: null, error: null, detail: null },
    }),
    prepare_takeover: spyOn(controller, 'prepareTakeover').mockResolvedValue({ ok: true, takenOverSeq: 1 }),
    hand_back: spyOn(controller, 'handBack').mockResolvedValue({ ok: true, handedBack: null }),
    cleanup_attempt: spyOn(controller, 'cleanup').mockResolvedValue({ ok: true }),
    upload_transcript: spyOn(controller, 'uploadTranscript').mockResolvedValue({ uploaded: false }),
    prepare_dependencies: spyOn(controller, 'prepareRequested').mockResolvedValue({
      ok: true,
      prepared: { requestId: '1-R-1-13', ok: true, error: null, logTail: null },
    }),
  };
}

describe('CommandExecutor', () => {
  test('journals before execution, joins a running resend by id or key, and returns the stored result', async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture();
    const x = executor(f);
    const entered = Promise.withResolvers<void>();
    const release = Promise.withResolvers<void>();
    const controller = x.controller('T-4-a1');
    const original = controller.start.bind(controller);
    const start = spyOn(controller, 'start').mockImplementation(async (spec) => {
      expect(x.journal.get('1-R-1-1')?.state).toBe('running');
      expect(JSON.stringify(x.journal.get('1-R-1-1'))).not.toContain(spec.agentToken);
      entered.resolve();
      await release.promise;
      return original(spec);
    });
    const command = { kind: 'start_attempt', attempt: f.spec() } as const;
    const first = x.run.onCommand(message(command));
    await entered.promise;
    const duplicate = x.run.onCommand(message(command));
    const newId = x.run.onCommand(message(command, 2));
    expect(start).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    release.resolve();
    const result = { ok: true, data: { started: true } };
    expect(await Promise.all([first, duplicate, newId])).toEqual([result, result, result]);
    expect(x.journal.get('1-R-1-1')).toMatchObject({ state: 'done', result });
    expect(await x.run.onCommand(message(command, 3))).toEqual(result);
    expect(start).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  }, 60_000);

  test('start, stop and submission keep seq order; delivery and approval bypass a handoff stop', async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({
      script: {
        turns: [
          [],

            { do: 'terminal', tool: 'handoff' },
          ],
        ],
      },
      config: { timings: { submitRetry: 1 } },
    });
    const x = executor(f);
    await x.run.onCommand(message({ kind: 'start_attempt', attempt: f.spec() }));
    await waitFor(() => x.controller('T-4-a1').phase === 'idle');
    let stopped = false;
    const stopping = x.run.onCommand(message({ ...STOP, handoff: true }, 2)).then((result) => {
      stopped = true;
      return result;
    });
    const submitting = x.run.onCommand(message(commands(f).find((c) => c.kind === 'push_submission')!, 3));
    const approval = await waitFor(() => f.events('approval.requested')[0]);
    expect(f.events('attempt.submitted')).toHaveLength(0);

  test('pause lets in-flight work finish and resumes held commands in order', async () => {

    await Promise.all([second, third]);

    x.run.resume();

  });

  test('an update_settings echo sends no local edit again that the outbox carries still', async () => {

    f.outbox.ack(f.outbox.epoch, f.outbox.lastSeq());

      capacity: 7,
      draining: true,
      keepAwake,
      confirmedSettings: { capacity: 7, draining: true, keepAwake, version: base + 3 },
    });
  });

  test('an echo cut short before runner.json took it leaves its edit in flight; run again, it marks no second edit', async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture();
    const x = executor(f);
    const outbox = new Outbox(f.db, { confirmedVersion: () => f.config.confirmedSettings.version });
    const journal = new Journal(f.db);
    const base = f.config.confirmedSettings.version;
    const append = (draining: boolean) =>
      outbox.append({ type: 'runner.settings', data: { settings: { draining }, baseVersion: base } }).seq;
    // A drain, an undrain and a drain again, all acknowledged; runner.json holds the last.
    const seqs = [append(true), append(false), append(true)];
    outbox.ack(outbox.epoch, outbox.lastSeq());
    f.config.draining = true;
    // What a kill between the mark and runner.json's write leaves: the row running, the mark, the old snapshot.
    const command: RunnerCommand = { kind: 'update_settings', settings: { draining: true }, version: base + 1 };
    journal.begin('1-R-1-9', 9, command);
    expect(outbox.markSettingsEcho({ draining: true }, base + 1).answered?.seq).toBe(seqs[0]);
    expect(outbox.settingsInFlight().map((event) => event.seq)).toEqual(seqs);
    // The next start runs the row again when the hub sends it again.
    const run = new CommandExecutor({ ...x.options, outbox, journal });
    await run.recover();
    expect(journal.get('1-R-1-9')?.state).toBe('running');
    expect(await run.onCommand({ t: 'command', id: '1-R-1-9', seq: 9, command })).toEqual({ ok: true });
    expect(journal.get('1-R-1-9')).toMatchObject({ state: 'done', result: { ok: true } });
    expect(f.config).toMatchObject({ draining: true, confirmedSettings: { draining: true, version: base + 1 } });
    expect(f.db.meta('settingsEchoed')).toEqual([{ seq: seqs[0], version: base + 1 }]);
    expect(outbox.settingsInFlight().map((event) => event.seq)).toEqual(seqs.slice(1));
    expect(f.events('runner.settings')).toHaveLength(3);
  });

  test('a failed run of an echo runs again shortly on its own, and the echoes after it wait for it, not for a reconnect', async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture();
    const timers = manualTimers();
    const run = new CommandExecutor({ ...executor(f).options, timers });
    const journal = new Journal(f.db);
    const echo = (edit: { capacity?: number; draining?: boolean; keepAwake?: 'off' }, version: number) =>
      run.onCommand(message({ kind: 'update_settings', settings: edit, version }, version));
    const base = f.config.confirmedSettings.version;
    const fail = () => {
      throw new Error('database is locked');
    };
    // The owner's capacity edit fails once; the drain and keepAwake edits after it would each skip a version.
    const mark = spyOn(f.outbox, 'markSettingsEcho').mockImplementationOnce(fail);
    const results = [
      echo({ capacity: 3 }, base + 1),
      echo({ draining: true }, base + 2),
      echo({ keepAwake: 'off' }, base + 3),
    ];
    await waitFor(() => timers.waiting().length === 1);
    expect(timers.waiting()[0]?.ms).toBe(1_000);
    expect(f.config.confirmedSettings.version).toBe(base);
    expect(journal.get(`1-R-1-${base + 1}`)?.state).toBe('running');
    // The link stays up: the retry runs them all, in version order, and each gets its result.
    timers.fire();
    expect(await Promise.all(results)).toEqual([{ ok: true }, { ok: true }, { ok: true }]);
    expect(f.config).toMatchObject({
      capacity: 3,
      draining: true,
      keepAwake: 'off',
      confirmedSettings: { capacity: 3, draining: true, keepAwake: 'off', version: base + 3 },
    });
    expect(journal.running()).toEqual([]);
    // A failure that lasts: each retry waits twice as long as the one before.
    mark.mockImplementation(fail);
    const stuck = echo({ capacity: 4 }, base + 4);
    await waitFor(() => timers.waiting().length === 1);
    timers.fire();
    await waitFor(() => timers.waiting().length === 1);
    expect(timers.waiting()[0]?.ms).toBe(2_000);
    // A hello leaves it to the hub's resend after the welcome, and ends the retries.
    run.helloSent();
    expect(await stuck).toBeNull();
    expect(timers.waiting()).toEqual([]);
    expect(journal.get(`1-R-1-${base + 4}`)?.state).toBe('running');
    mark.mockRestore();
    expect(await echo({ capacity: 4 }, base + 4)).toEqual({ ok: true });
    expect(f.config).toMatchObject({ capacity: 4, confirmedSettings: { version: base + 4 } });
  });
