```ts
    const echo = (edit: Record<string, unknown>, version: number, id = version) =>
      x.run.onCommand(message({ kind: 'update_settings', settings: edit, version }, id));
    // Runs once every runner command taken before it has run.
    const barrier = () => x.run.onCommand(message({ kind: 'preflight', vendor: 'claude' }, 1_000));
    const base = f.config.confirmedSettings.version;
    const { version: _version, ...snapshot } = f.config.confirmedSettings;
    // A keepAwake edit, sent and acknowledged. The hub applied it after an owner's edit whose echo never came.
    f.config.keepAwake = 'always';
    const edit = f.outbox.append({
      type: 'runner.settings',
      data: { settings: { keepAwake: 'always' }, baseVersion: base },
    });
    f.outbox.ack(f.outbox.epoch, edit.seq);
    // Then an owner's PATCH that names every field, but one vendor's ceiling and the other's paid usage only: it is
    // not the hub's whole settings, so it skips no version either.
    const low = { fiveHour: 0.5, weekly: 0.6 };
    const patch = {
      capacity: 4,
      keepAwake: 'always',
      draining: true,
      ceilings: { codex: low },
      allowPaidUsage: { claude: true },
    };
    const waiting = [echo({ capacity: 3 }, base + 2), echo({ keepAwake: 'always' }, base + 3), echo(patch, base + 4)];
    await barrier();
    expect(x.journal.get(`1-R-1-${base + 2}`)?.state).toBe('running');
    expect(f.config).toMatchObject({ capacity: 2, keepAwake: 'always', confirmedSettings: { version: base } });
    expect(f.outbox.settingsInFlight().map((event) => event.seq)).toEqual([edit.seq]);
    // The link drops: the hello leaves them unanswered, for the hub to send again after its welcome.
    x.run.helloSent();
    expect(await Promise.all(waiting)).toEqual([null, null, null]);
    // That hello reported the older version: the hub sends them again, then all of its settings, which apply past the
    // gap; the echoes they cover only mark the edit they answer.
    const resent = [echo({ capacity: 3 }, base + 2), echo({ keepAwake: 'always' }, base + 3), echo(patch, base + 4)];
    const whole = {
      capacity: 4,
      keepAwake: 'always',
      draining: true,
      ceilings: { ...snapshot.ceilings, codex: low },
      allowPaidUsage: { ...snapshot.allowPaidUsage, claude: true },
    };
    expect(await echo(whole, base + 4, 100)).toEqual({ ok: true });
    expect(await Promise.all(resent)).toEqual([{ ok: true }, { ok: true }, { ok: true }]);
    expect(f.outbox.settingsInFlight()).toEqual([]);
    expect(f.config).toMatchObject({ ...whole, confirmedSettings: { ...whole, version: base + 4 } });
    // The next echo applies as usual, and nothing was sent again.
    expect(await echo({ capacity: 5 }, base + 5)).toEqual({ ok: true });
    expect(f.config).toMatchObject({ capacity: 5, confirmedSettings: { capacity: 5, version: base + 5 } });
    expect(settings()).toEqual([{ keepAwake: 'always' }]);
  });

  test('an update_settings taken before the latest hello is left unanswered, unless the hub sends it again after that hello', async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture();
    const x = executor(f);
    const update = (settings: { capacity?: number; draining?: boolean }, version: number): RunnerCommand => ({
      kind: 'update_settings',
      settings,
      version,
    });
    const base = f.config.confirmedSettings.version;
    // Two echoes wait behind a pause. The link drops, and the next hello goes to a hub restored from a backup that has
    // the first and not the second; run before its welcome, they would move the snapshot past what that hello said.
    x.run.pause();
    const kept = x.run.onCommand(message(update({ capacity: 3 }, base + 1), 1));
    const lost = x.run.onCommand(message(update({ draining: true }, base + 2), 2));
    x.run.helloSent();
    // That hello reported the version before both: the restored hub sends the first again, then all of its settings.
    const resent = x.run.onCommand(message(update({ capacity: 3 }, base + 1), 1));
    const { version: _version, ...snapshot } = f.config.confirmedSettings;
    const whole = x.run.onCommand({
      t: 'command',
      id: '2-R-1-1',
      seq: 1,
      command: { kind: 'update_settings', settings: { ...snapshot, capacity: 3 }, version: base + 1 },
    });
    x.run.resume();
    expect(await kept).toEqual({ ok: true });
    expect(await resent).toEqual({ ok: true });
    expect(await lost).toBeNull();
    expect(x.journal.get('1-R-1-2')?.state).toBe('running');
    expect(await whole).toEqual({ ok: true });
    expect(f.config).toMatchObject({
      capacity: 3,
      draining: false,
      confirmedSettings: { capacity: 3, draining: false, version: base + 1 },
    });
  });

  test("a reconnect to the same hub loses no echo: its resend joins one still queued, and runs one the hello left unanswered", async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture();
    const x = executor(f);
    const update = (settings: { capacity?: number; draining?: boolean }, version: number): RunnerCommand => ({
      kind: 'update_settings',
      settings,
      version,
    });
    const base = f.config.confirmedSettings.version;
    // A long preflight holds the runner's queue, with two echoes behind it.
    const gate = Promise.withResolvers<void>();
    const adapter = f.adapters.get('claude')!;
    const preflight = adapter.preflight.bind(adapter);
    spyOn(adapter, 'preflight').mockImplementationOnce(async () => {
      await gate.promise;
      return preflight();
    });
    const held = x.run.onCommand(message({ kind: 'preflight', vendor: 'claude' }, 1));
    const first = x.run.onCommand(message(update({ capacity: 3 }, base + 1), 2));
    const second = x.run.onCommand(message(update({ draining: true }, base + 2), 3));
    // The link drops and says hello again. After the welcome, the hub's resend of the first comes while it waits.
    x.run.helloSent();
    const resent = x.run.onCommand(message(update({ capacity: 3 }, base + 1), 2));
    gate.resolve();
    expect((await held)?.ok).toBe(true);
    expect(await first).toEqual({ ok: true });
    expect(await resent).toEqual({ ok: true });
    // The second ran before its resend came: it answered nothing, and its resend runs it from the journal.
    expect(await second).toBeNull();
    expect(x.journal.get('1-R-1-3')?.state).toBe('running');
    expect(await x.run.onCommand(message(update({ draining: true }, base + 2), 3))).toEqual({ ok: true });
    expect(f.config).toMatchObject({
      capacity: 3,
      draining: true,
      confirmedSettings: { capacity: 3, draining: true, version: base + 2 },
    });
  });

  test('settingsAcknowledged sends a probe for an acknowledged edit no echo answered, once the commands before it ran', async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture();
    const x = executor(f);
    const settings = () => f.events('runner.settings').map((event) => event.data.settings);
    const echo = (edit: { capacity?: number; draining?: boolean }, version: number) =>
      x.run.onCommand(message({ kind: 'update_settings', settings: edit, version }, version));
    const ack = () => f.outbox.ack(f.outbox.epoch, f.outbox.lastSeq());
    const base = f.config.confirmedSettings.version;
    const capacity = f.config.capacity;
    // A drain whose echo came before its ack, as M2a sends them, and waits behind a pause: no probe.
    f.config.draining = true;
    f.outbox.append({ type: 'runner.settings', data: { settings: { draining: true }, baseVersion: base } });
    x.run.pause();
    const echoed = echo({ draining: true }, base + 1);
    ack();
    const checked = x.run.settingsAcknowledged({ welcome: false });
    x.run.resume();
    await Promise.all([echoed, checked]);
    expect(settings()).toEqual([{ draining: true }]);
    // A capacity edit the hub acknowledged and never echoed: a probe follows.
    f.config.capacity = capacity + 1;
    f.outbox.append({ type: 'runner.settings', data: { settings: { capacity: capacity + 1 }, baseVersion: base + 1 } });
    ack();
    await x.run.settingsAcknowledged({ welcome: false });
    expect(settings()).toEqual([{ draining: true }, { capacity: capacity + 1 }, {}]);
    // None more while that probe waits for its acknowledgement, or once acknowledged, for its echo; one at a welcome.
    await x.run.settingsAcknowledged({ welcome: true });
    ack();
    await x.run.settingsAcknowledged({ welcome: false });
    expect(settings()).toHaveLength(3);
    await x.run.settingsAcknowledged({ welcome: true });
    await x.run.settingsAcknowledged({ welcome: true });
    expect(settings()).toEqual([{ draining: true }, { capacity: capacity + 1 }, {}, {}]);
    // The first probe's echo: the capacity edit was refused. Nothing is left to probe for.
    ack();
    expect((await echo({}, base + 2))?.ok).toBe(true);
    expect(f.config.capacity).toBe(capacity);
    await x.run.settingsAcknowledged({ welcome: true });
    expect(settings()).toHaveLength(4);
  });

    expect(f.events('attempt.prepared').at(-1)?.data).toMatchObject({

    await x.run.onCommand(message({ ...STOP, attemptId: 'lead-a1' }, 10));

    expect(f.events('attempt.prepared').at(-1)?.data).toMatchObject({

  test('restart re-runs exactly the ten idempotent handlers, update_settings once the hub sends it again, and interrupts the other seven, without tokens', async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture();
    const x = executor(f);
    const handlers = probes(x.controller('T-4-a1'));
    const refresh = spyOn(f.vault, 'refresh');
    const preflight = spyOn(f.adapters.get('claude')!, 'preflight');
    const remote = spyOn(x.options, 'remote');
    const save = spyOn(x.options, 'saveConfig');
    const all = commands(f);
    for (const [i, command] of all.entries()) x.journal.begin(`1-R-1-${i + 1}`, i + 1, command);
    expect(JSON.stringify(x.journal.running())).not.toContain(f.spec().agentToken);
    const restarted = new CommandExecutor(x.options);
    await restarted.recover();
    const restartable: RunnerCommand['kind'][] = [
      'push_submission',
      'prepare_takeover',
      'hand_back',
      'cleanup_attempt',
      'upload_transcript',
      'refresh_vault',
      'delete_refs',
      'update_settings',
      'preflight',
      'prepare_dependencies',
    ];
    expect([...RESTARTABLE_COMMANDS].sort()).toEqual(restartable.sort());
    // A hub restored without it would never send it again: it waits for the hub, and runs then.
    const settings = all.findIndex((command) => command.kind === 'update_settings');
    expect(x.journal.get(`1-R-1-${settings + 1}`)?.state).toBe('running');
    expect(save).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(0);
    expect(await restarted.onCommand(message(all[settings]!, settings + 1))).toEqual({ ok: true });
    for (const [i, command] of all.entries()) {
      const entry = x.journal.get(`1-R-1-${i + 1}`)!;
      expect(entry.state).toBe('done');
      if (restartable.includes(command.kind)) expect(entry.result?.ok).toBe(true);
      else expect(entry.result).toEqual({ ok: false, error: 'interrupted' });
      if (command.kind in handlers)
        expect(handlers[command.kind as keyof typeof handlers]).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(
          restartable.includes(command.kind) ? 1 : 0,
        );
      expect(await restarted.onCommand(message(command, i + 1))).toEqual(entry.result!);
    }
    expect(refresh).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(preflight).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(remote).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(save).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(x.journal.running()).toEqual([]);
  });
});
```

```diff
+/**
+ * The snapshot with runner.settings edits laid over it in order: what the hub holds once it has applied them. Of the
+ * per-vendor records an edit replaces only the vendors it names.
+ */
+export function settingsAfterEdits(snapshot: RunnerSettings, edits: readonly SettingsEdits[]): RunnerSettings {
+  const result = structuredClone(snapshot);
+  for (const edit of edits) {
+    for (const field of SCALAR_FIELDS) {
+      if (edit[field] !== undefined) Object.assign(result, { [field]: edit[field] });
+    }
+    for (const field of VENDOR_FIELDS) {
+      const given = edit[field];
+      if (given !== undefined) Object.assign(result, { [field]: { ...result[field], ...structuredClone(given) } });
+    }
+  }
+  return result;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Whether settings are the hub's whole settings, as hello's echoes carry them, which set the snapshot whatever came
+ * before: every field named, and in each per-vendor record every vendor the snapshot's record holds. The hub's records
+ * hold every vendor the runner's snapshot does (it stored what the runner reported, and merges vendor by vendor), and
+ * an owner's PATCH that names every field but not those vendors is an edit like any other.
+ */
+export function isWholeSettings(settings: SettingsEdits, snapshot: RunnerSettings): boolean {
+  if (![...SCALAR_FIELDS, ...VENDOR_FIELDS].every((field) => settings[field] !== undefined)) return false;
+  return VENDOR_FIELDS.every((field) => {
+    const given: Partial<Record<Vendor, unknown>> = settings[field] ?? {};
+    return VENDORS.every((vendor) => snapshot[field][vendor] === undefined || given[vendor] !== undefined);
+  });
```

```ts
// The command executor (design 6.3, "Commands"; 6.4; 6.18; 7.7). It turns the hub's commands into controller and
// runner work:
// - Journal: each command is validated with core's RunnerCommandSchema, recorded as running before it executes and as
//   done with its result after. A resend while it runs joins the first execution (by id, or by design 6.3's
//   idempotency keys); a resend when done gets the stored result. An unknown or invalid command answers unsupported
//   and is never journaled; a command for an attempt this runner has no record of answers unknown_attempt.
// - Ordering: an attempt's lifecycle and git commands go to its controller, whose serial queue runs them in arrival
//   order, which is the hub's seq order; deliver, interrupt and decide_approval act on the live session at once.
//   Different attempts run concurrently; the runner's own commands (refresh_vault, preflight, delete_refs,
//   update_settings) run one at a time.
// - welcome.stop is applied before any command that follows the welcome: each attempt named there is marked ended at
//   once, a live process is stopped without a handoff turn (its new work goes to a late-work ref), and later commands
//   for it answer attempt_ended, except those that outlive an attempt: cleanup_attempt, upload_transcript and
//   hand_back (X-36).
// - pause() holds new commands until resume(), which runs them in order; work already dispatched goes on (X-7).
// - After a restart, journal rows left running are run again when their handler is idempotent (RESTARTABLE_COMMANDS)
//   and answered interrupted otherwise. start_attempt and resume_attempt are never re-run: the journal keeps no agent
//   token, and the hub resends them with a fresh one. update_settings runs again when the hub sends it again.
// - update_settings (X-12): each hello starts a new lineage, and one taken before the latest hello answers nothing,
//   its row left running for the hub to send it again after the welcome; a hub restored from a backup sends only the
//   ones it still has. One that fails, or would skip a version (SettingsSync.echo), waits: a failed one runs again
//   after a short backoff, and each that waits runs, in version order, once the ones before it have; the next hello
//   leaves those still waiting unanswered. One whose journal row cannot be written is taken again after the backoff;
//   any other command answers that failure.
import { type RunnerCommand, type RunnerCommandKind, RunnerCommandSchema, type Vendor } from '@agflow/core';
import type { PreflightResult, VendorAdapter } from './adapters/types';
import type { AttemptController } from './attempt/controller';
import { type ClockSource, systemClock } from './clock';
import type { RunnerConfig } from './config';
import { deleteRefsFenced } from './git/push';
import type { GitEnvironment } from './git/run';
import type { Vault } from './git/vault';
import type { CommandResult, Journal, JournaledCommand, JournalEntry } from './journal';
import type { CommandMessage, WelcomeMessage } from './link';
import type { Logger } from './log';
import type { Outbox } from './outbox';
import { SerialQueue } from './queue';
import { SettingsSync } from './settings-sync';
import type { VendorReport } from './vendors';

/** The commands whose handlers are idempotent, so a row a previous run left running is run again (design 6.3). */
export const RESTARTABLE_COMMANDS: ReadonlySet<RunnerCommandKind> = new Set<RunnerCommandKind>([
  'push_submission',
  'prepare_takeover',
  'hand_back',
  'cleanup_attempt',
  'upload_transcript',
  'refresh_vault',
  'delete_refs',
  'update_settings',
  'preflight',
  'prepare_dependencies',
]);

/** The commands that outlive their attempt: the hub keeps them when it ends one, and the runner runs them then too. */
const OUTLIVE_ATTEMPT: ReadonlySet<RunnerCommandKind> = new Set<RunnerCommandKind>([
  'cleanup_attempt',
  'upload_transcript',
  'hand_back',
]);

export interface CommandExecutorOptions {
  journal: Journal;
  /** The attempt's controller, made when there is none yet (a new start, or a record left by a previous run). */
  controller(attemptId: string): AttemptController;
  /** Whether the runner knows the attempt: it has a controller or a record in runner.db. */
  known(attemptId: string): boolean;
  config(): RunnerConfig;
  /** Writes runner.json and makes config() give the new settings. */
  saveConfig(config: RunnerConfig): void;
  outbox: Outbox;
  vault: Vault;
  local: GitEnvironment;
  /** The remote environment of the vault's pushes. */
  remote(): Promise<GitEnvironment>;
  wipRefPrefix(): string;
  adapters: ReadonlyMap<Vendor, VendorAdapter>;
  /** Told each preflight a preflight command ran, so the runner's vendor readiness follows it. */
  preflighted?(result: PreflightResult): void;
  /**
   * What runner.vendors carries after a preflight command: every vendor's latest preflight, the new one included,
   * each with its own preflightAt. The hub replaces the runner's whole vendor list with it (design 6.3).
   */
  vendors(): Pick<VendorReport, 'vendors' | 'quota'>;
  logger: Logger;
  /** The timers of the settings retries; the system's by default. */
  timers?: Pick<ClockSource, 'setTimeout' | 'clearTimeout'>;
}

/** The wait before an update_settings that failed runs again; it doubles at each failure, up to the cap. */
const SETTINGS_RETRY_MS = 1_000;
const SETTINGS_RETRY_CAP_MS = 60_000;

function describe(error: unknown): string {
  return error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
}

/** When a command came: the lineage of the hub that sent it, and the outbox's newest seq then. */
interface Sighting {
  lineage: number;
  outboxSeq: number;
}

/** A command executing now. */
interface Execution {
  result: Promise<CommandResult | null>;
  /** The lineage that sent it last: a resend from a restored hub joins the execution, and makes it current. */
  lineage: number;
  /** The outbox's newest seq when it first came (Journal.begin): an echo answers no edit made after that. */
  outboxSeq: number;
}

/** An update_settings left waiting (X-12): its result comes once it runs, or null at the next hello. */
interface Waits {
  waits: Promise<CommandResult | null>;
}

/** An update_settings whose journal row could not be written, to be taken again as it came, or as a resend made it. */
interface Retake {
  timer: unknown;
  seen: Sighting;
  resolve(result: CommandResult | null): void;
}

/** One update_settings waiting, as it came. */
interface Waiting {
  command: Extract<RunnerCommand, { kind: 'update_settings' }>;
  execution: Execution;
  resolve(result: CommandResult | null): void;
}

/** The attempt a command is about, if any. */
function attemptOf(command: RunnerCommand | JournaledCommand): string | null {
  if (command.kind === 'start_attempt') return command.attempt.attemptId;
  return 'attemptId' in command ? command.attemptId : null;
}

/**
 * A controller's outcome as a command result: a refusal (ok, started or resumed false, with an error) answers ok
 * false with its error; anything else is the result's data.
 */
function resultOf(outcome: object): CommandResult {
  const refused =
    ('ok' in outcome && outcome.ok === false) ||
    ('started' in outcome && outcome.started === false) ||
    ('resumed' in outcome && outcome.resumed === false);
  if (refused && 'error' in outcome && typeof outcome.error === 'string') return { ok: false, error: outcome.error };
  return { ok: true, data: outcome };
}

/** A result that repeats an outcome the outbox reports too: ok as the outcome's, with its error and all of it. */
function outcomeResult(outcome: { ok: boolean; error: string | null }): CommandResult {
  return outcome.ok || outcome.error === null
    ? { ok: outcome.ok, data: outcome }
    : { ok: false, error: outcome.error, data: outcome };
}

export class CommandExecutor {
  /** Each command executing now, by its first id. */
  private readonly active = new Map<string, Execution>();
  /** The attempts welcome.stop named. */
  private readonly ended = new Set<string>();
  /** Commands that arrived while paused, in order. */
  private readonly held: (() => void)[] = [];
  /** The runner's own commands, one at a time. */
  private readonly runnerQueue = new SerialQueue();
  private paused = false;
  /** Each hello starts a new lineage: an update_settings taken before the latest one answers nothing (X-12). */
  private lineage = 0;
  /** The update_settings of this lineage that failed or would skip a version, by command id, as they came. */
  private readonly waiting = new Map<string, Waiting>();
  private readonly timers: Pick<ClockSource, 'setTimeout' | 'clearTimeout'>;
  private retryTimer: unknown = null;
  private retryMs = SETTINGS_RETRY_MS;
  /** The update_settings whose journal row could not be written, each taken again when its timer fires, by id. */
  private readonly retakes = new Map<string, Retake>();
  private closed = false;
  /** Settings sync (X-12): update_settings runs its echoes here, and the runtime shares it. */
  readonly settings: SettingsSync;

  constructor(private readonly options: CommandExecutorOptions) {
    const { outbox, logger } = options;
    this.timers = options.timers ?? systemClock;
    this.settings = new SettingsSync({
      config: () => options.config(),
      saveConfig: (next) => options.saveConfig(next),
      outbox,
      logger,
    });
  }

  /** Holds new commands until resume(); commands already dispatched go on. */
  pause(): void {
    this.paused = true;
  }

  /** Runs the held commands in their arrival order, and every new one at once again. */
  resume(): void {
    this.paused = false;
    for (const run of this.held.splice(0)) {
      try {
        run();
      } catch (error) {
        this.options.logger.error('a held command failed', { error: describe(error) });
      }
    }
  }

  /**
   * Each hello, as the link builds it, starts a new lineage (X-12). An update_settings taken before it answers nothing
   * when it runs, and those waiting answer nothing now: the hub sends them again after the welcome, if it still has
   * them. Run between this hello and its welcome, one from a hub that a restore replaced would move the snapshot past
   * the version this hello reports, which the restored hub reconciles against.
   */
  helloSent(): void {
    this.lineage += 1;
    this.stopWaiting();
  }

  /** The runner closes: no retry runs any more, and what waits answers nothing. */
  close(): void {
    this.closed = true;
    this.stopWaiting();
  }

  /**
   * Each welcome, before any command that follows it. welcome.stop: every named attempt is marked ended at once, then
   * each live process is stopped. Resolves once those stops are done.
   */
  async onWelcome(welcome: Pick<WelcomeMessage, 'stop'>): Promise<void> {
    const { controller, known, logger } = this.options;
    const stopping: { attemptId: string; reason: string }[] = [];
    for (const { attemptId, reason } of welcome.stop) {
      this.ended.add(attemptId);
      if (!known(attemptId)) continue;
      controller(attemptId).markEnded();
      stopping.push({ attemptId, reason });
    }
    await Promise.all(
      stopping.map(async ({ attemptId, reason }) => {
        try {
          await controller(attemptId).stopEnded(reason);
        } catch (error) {
          logger.error('cannot stop an attempt the hub ended', { attemptId, error: describe(error) });
        }
      }),
    );
  }

  /**
   * LinkHandlers.onCommand: journals the command and runs it, or answers it from the journal; null answers nothing
   * (update_settings, X-12).
   */
  onCommand(message: CommandMessage): Promise<CommandResult | null> {
    return this.take(message, { lineage: this.lineage, outboxSeq: this.options.outbox.lastSeq() });
  }

  /**
   * Journals the command and runs it, or answers it from the journal. Never throws: a journal that cannot be written
   * (a full disk, say) takes an update_settings again after the backoff, so the echoes after it wait for it rather
   * than for a reconnect, and answers any other command with the failure.
   */
  private take(message: CommandMessage, seen: Sighting): Promise<CommandResult | null> {
    try {
      return this.takeNow(message, seen);
    } catch (error) {
      if (RunnerCommandSchema.safeParse(message.command).data?.kind !== 'update_settings') return Promise.reject(error);
      return this.retake(message, seen, error);
    }
  }

  private takeNow(message: CommandMessage, seen: Sighting): Promise<CommandResult | null> {
    const parsed = RunnerCommandSchema.safeParse(message.command);
    if (!parsed.success) return Promise.resolve({ ok: false, error: 'unsupported' });
    const command = parsed.data;
    const begun = this.options.journal.begin(message.id, message.seq, command, seen.outboxSeq);
    if (begun.state === 'done') return Promise.resolve(begun.result);
    if (begun.state === 'running') {
      const active = this.active.get(begun.commandId);
      if (active) {
        active.lineage = Math.max(active.lineage, seen.lineage);
        return active.result;
      }
      // Left running by a previous run, not recovered yet, or left unanswered.
      const entry = this.options.journal.get(begun.commandId);
      if (entry === null) return Promise.resolve({ ok: false, error: 'interrupted' });
      return this.replay(entry, seen.lineage);
    }
    if (this.refusedAsEnded(command)) {
      const result: CommandResult = { ok: false, error: 'attempt_ended' };
      this.options.journal.finish(message.id, result);
      return Promise.resolve(result);
    }
    return this.schedule(message.id, command, seen);
  }

  /**
   * After a restart, once the first welcome's stop list is applied: the rows a previous run left running. An
   * update_settings waits for the hub to send it again, which it does after each welcome while the command is
   * pending; a hub restored from a backup without it never does, so an echo of settings the restore lost is never
   * applied (X-12).
   */
  async recover(): Promise<void> {
    const entries = this.options.journal.running().filter((entry) => entry.kind !== 'update_settings');
    await Promise.all(
      entries.map((entry) => this.active.get(entry.commandId)?.result ?? this.replay(entry, this.lineage)),
    );
  }

  /**
   * After an acknowledgement, and after each welcome: once every runner command received before it has run (held
   * ones included, so a pause holds this too), an acknowledged settings edit still unanswered gets a probe
   * (SettingsSync.probeUnanswered). Resolves once that check ran.
   */
  settingsAcknowledged(options: { welcome: boolean }): Promise<void> {
    const checked = Promise.withResolvers<void>();
    const check = () => {
      this.runnerQueue
        .run('runner', async () => this.settings.probeUnanswered(options))
        .catch((error) => this.options.logger.error('cannot check the settings edits', { error: describe(error) }))
        .then(checked.resolve);
    };
    if (this.paused) this.held.push(check);
    else check();
    return checked.promise;
  }

  /** Whether welcome.stop ended the command's attempt and the command does not outlive it. */
  private refusedAsEnded(command: RunnerCommand): boolean {
    const attemptId = attemptOf(command);
    return attemptId !== null && this.ended.has(attemptId) && !OUTLIVE_ATTEMPT.has(command.kind);
  }

  /**
   * A journal row left running: run again when its handler is idempotent, answered interrupted otherwise. It keeps
   * the outbox position it first came at.
   */
  private replay(entry: JournalEntry, lineage: number): Promise<CommandResult | null> {
    const { commandId, command } = entry;
    const parsed = RESTARTABLE_COMMANDS.has(command.kind) ? RunnerCommandSchema.safeParse(command) : null;
    if (parsed === null || !parsed.success) {
      const result: CommandResult = { ok: false, error: parsed === null ? 'interrupted' : 'unsupported' };
      this.options.journal.finish(commandId, result);
      return Promise.resolve(result);
    }
    const outboxSeq = entry.outboxSeq ?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER;
    return this.schedule(commandId, parsed.data, { lineage, outboxSeq });
  }

  /**
   * Runs the command now, or when the executor resumes; its result is journaled, then given. A command that answers
   * nothing leaves its row running.
   */
  private schedule(commandId: string, command: RunnerCommand, seen: Sighting): Promise<CommandResult | null> {
    const result = Promise.withResolvers<CommandResult | null>();
    const execution: Execution = { result: result.promise, ...seen };
    this.active.set(commandId, execution);
    const run = () => {
      this.execute(commandId, command, execution)
        // An update_settings left waiting gives its result once it runs (X-12).
        .then((done) => (done !== null && 'waits' in done ? done.waits : done))
        .catch((error): CommandResult => {
          const fields = { commandId, kind: command.kind, error: describe(error) };
          this.options.logger.error('a command failed', fields);
          return { ok: false, error: describe(error) };
        })
        .then((done) => {
          if (done !== null) this.options.journal.finish(commandId, done);
          return done;
        })
        // Gone before the result is given: a resend after an unanswered run runs it again.
        .finally(() => this.active.delete(commandId))
        .then(result.resolve, result.reject);
    };
    if (this.paused) this.held.push(run);
    else run();
    return result.promise;
  }

  /**
   * One command's work. An attempt's command reaches its controller with no await before it, so the controller's
   * queue takes it in arrival order.
   */
  private async execute(
    commandId: string,
    command: RunnerCommand,
    execution: Execution,
  ): Promise<CommandResult | Waits | null> {
    const attemptId = attemptOf(command);
    if (attemptId === null) {
      return this.runnerQueue.run('runner', () => this.runnerCommand(commandId, command, execution));
    }
    // A command held by a pause meets a welcome.stop that came meanwhile.
    if (this.refusedAsEnded(command)) return { ok: false, error: 'attempt_ended' };
    if (command.kind !== 'start_attempt' && !this.options.known(attemptId)) {
      return { ok: false, error: 'unknown_attempt' };
    }
    const controller = this.options.controller(attemptId);
    switch (command.kind) {
      case 'start_attempt':
        return resultOf(await controller.start(command.attempt));
      case 'resume_attempt':
        return resultOf(await controller.resume(command));
      case 'stop_attempt':
        return resultOf(await controller.stop(command));
      case 'hold_attempt':
        return resultOf(await controller.hold(command));
      case 'deliver':
        return resultOf(await controller.deliver(command));
      case 'interrupt':
        return resultOf(await controller.interrupt(command));
      case 'decide_approval':
        return resultOf(await controller.decideApproval(command));
      case 'push_submission': {
        const submitted = await controller.submit(command);
        return submitted.ok ? outcomeResult(submitted.outcome) : resultOf(submitted);
      }
      case 'prepare_takeover':
        return resultOf(await controller.prepareTakeover(command));
      case 'hand_back': {
        const handed = await controller.handBack(command);
        if (handed.ok) return { ok: true, data: handed };
        // process_running names the pids the person must end, as data: { pids } (X-37); the hub reads nothing else.
        return 'pids' in handed
          ? { ok: false, error: handed.error, data: { pids: handed.pids } }
          : { ok: false, error: handed.error };
      }
      case 'cleanup_attempt':
        return resultOf(await controller.cleanup());
      case 'upload_transcript':
        return resultOf(await controller.uploadTranscript());
      case 'prepare_dependencies': {
        // The command id is the request's id (X-40), which the hub returned to the agent.
        const requested = await controller.prepareRequested({ fence: command.fence, requestId: commandId });
        return requested.ok ? outcomeResult(requested.prepared) : resultOf(requested);
      }
      default:
        return { ok: false, error: 'unsupported' };
    }
  }

  /** The runner's own commands. */
  private async runnerCommand(
    commandId: string,
    command: RunnerCommand,
    execution: Execution,
  ): Promise<CommandResult | Waits | null> {
    const { vault, outbox } = this.options;
    switch (command.kind) {
      case 'refresh_vault':
        // A late-work ref the hub tells the current holder to merge: fetched before the agent asks for it.
        await vault.refresh(command.taskId, command.refs, this.options.wipRefPrefix());
        return { ok: true };
      case 'preflight': {
        const adapter = this.options.adapters.get(command.vendor);
        if (!adapter) return { ok: false, error: `no ${command.vendor} adapter on this runner` };
        // Run first: an optional call would skip its argument, the preflight itself, without the callback.
        const result = await adapter.preflight();
        this.options.preflighted?.(result);
        const { vendors, quota } = this.options.vendors();
        outbox.append({ type: 'runner.vendors', data: { vendors, quota } });
        return { ok: true };
      }
      case 'delete_refs': {
        // Each ref is deleted only at the sha the hub recorded; one that moved or is gone is reported as it is.
        const results = await deleteRefsFenced({
          vault,
          local: this.options.local,
          remote: await this.options.remote(),
          refs: command.refs,
        });
        const failed = results.find((result) => result.status === 'failed');
        return failed ? { ok: false, error: 'remote', data: results } : { ok: true, data: results };
      }
      case 'update_settings':
        return this.settingsEcho(commandId, command, execution);
      default:
        return { ok: false, error: 'unsupported' };
    }
  }

  /**
   * update_settings: the echo becomes the snapshot, and runner.json the snapshot with the edits still in flight
   * (SettingsSync.echo, X-12). One taken before the latest hello answers nothing: its version may be one a restored hub
   * hands out again with other settings, and the hub sends it again after the welcome, if it still has it. One that
   * fails, or would skip a version, waits (runWaiting), so a failure stalls no later echo until a reconnect.
   */
  private settingsEcho(
    commandId: string,
    command: Extract<RunnerCommand, { kind: 'update_settings' }>,
    execution: Execution,
  ): CommandResult | Waits | null {
    if (this.closed) return null;
    if (execution.lineage < this.lineage) {
      this.options.logger.warn('left unanswered an update_settings from before the last hello', {
        version: command.version,
      });
      return null;
    }
    if (this.runEcho(command, execution) === 'ran') {
      this.runWaiting();
      return { ok: true };
    }
    const waits = Promise.withResolvers<CommandResult | null>();
    this.waiting.set(commandId, { command, execution, resolve: waits.resolve });
    return { waits: waits.promise };
  }

  /** One echo's run: ran, waits (it would skip a version), or failed, which arms a retry. */
  private runEcho(
    command: Extract<RunnerCommand, { kind: 'update_settings' }>,
    execution: Execution,
  ): 'ran' | 'waits' | 'failed' {
    try {
      if (!this.settings.echo(command, execution.outboxSeq)) return 'waits';
      this.retryMs = SETTINGS_RETRY_MS;
      return 'ran';
    } catch (error) {
      const fields = { version: command.version, error: describe(error), retryMs: this.retryMs };
      this.options.logger.error('an update_settings failed; it runs again shortly', fields);
      this.retryLater();
      return 'failed';
    }
  }

  /**
   * The waiting update_settings, in version order, each run again until none can run: after an echo ran, and when a
   * retry comes. A failure stops the round; the retry after it starts again.
   */
  private runWaiting(): void {
    for (let ran = true; ran && this.waiting.size > 0; ) {
      ran = false;
      const waiting = [...this.waiting].sort(([, a], [, b]) => a.command.version - b.command.version);
      for (const [commandId, entry] of waiting) {
        const outcome = this.runEcho(entry.command, entry.execution);
        if (outcome === 'failed') return;
        if (outcome === 'waits') continue;
        this.waiting.delete(commandId);
        entry.resolve({ ok: true });
        ran = true;
      }
    }
  }

  /** Runs the waiting update_settings again after the backoff, on the runner's queue. */
  private retryLater(): void {
    if (this.retryTimer !== null || this.closed) return;
    const ms = this.retryMs;
    this.retryMs = Math.min(ms * 2, SETTINGS_RETRY_CAP_MS);
    this.retryTimer = this.timers.setTimeout(() => {
      this.retryTimer = null;
      this.runnerQueue
        .run('runner', async () => this.runWaiting())
        .catch((error) => {
          this.options.logger.error('cannot run the settings echoes again', { error: describe(error) });
        });
    }, ms);
  }

  /**
   * An update_settings whose journal row could not be written, taken again (with where it first came) after the
   * settings backoff; its result is the one taken then. The next hello or close() answers it nothing.
   */
  private retake(message: CommandMessage, seen: Sighting, error: unknown): Promise<CommandResult | null> {
    if (this.closed) return Promise.resolve(null);
    const ms = this.retryMs;
    this.retryMs = Math.min(ms * 2, SETTINGS_RETRY_CAP_MS);
    this.options.logger.error('cannot journal an update_settings; it is taken again shortly', {
      commandId: message.id,
      error: describe(error),
      retryMs: ms,
    });
    // A command the hub sent once is taken once: a resend while one waits shares its wait, and makes it current, as a
    // resend that joins an execution does; it keeps where it first came.
    const earlier = this.retakes.get(message.id);
    if (earlier !== undefined) {
      earlier.seen = { ...earlier.seen, lineage: Math.max(earlier.seen.lineage, seen.lineage) };
      const shared = Promise.withResolvers<CommandResult | null>();
      const resolve = earlier.resolve;
      earlier.resolve = (result) => {
        resolve(result);
        shared.resolve(result);
      };
      return shared.promise;
    }
    const taken = Promise.withResolvers<CommandResult | null>();
    const retake: Retake = {
      timer: this.timers.setTimeout(() => {
        if (this.retakes.get(message.id) !== retake) return;
        this.retakes.delete(message.id);
        this.take(message, retake.seen).then(retake.resolve, () => retake.resolve(null));
      }, ms),
      seen,
      resolve: taken.resolve,
    };
    this.retakes.set(message.id, retake);
    return taken.promise;
  }

  /**
   * Ends the retries; what waits answers nothing, its journal row left running (or never written) for the hub to send
   * it again.
   */
  private stopWaiting(): void {
    if (this.retryTimer !== null) this.timers.clearTimeout(this.retryTimer);
    this.retryTimer = null;
    this.retryMs = SETTINGS_RETRY_MS;
    const waiting = [...this.waiting.values()];
    this.waiting.clear();
    for (const entry of waiting) entry.resolve(null);
    const retakes = [...this.retakes.values()];
    this.retakes.clear();
    for (const retake of retakes) {
      this.timers.clearTimeout(retake.timer);
      retake.resolve(null);
    }
  }
}
```

**File:** `packages/runner/src/settings-sync.ts` (new)

```ts
// Settings sync on the runner (design 6.3, "Settings sync"; X-12). runner.json holds the settings and the snapshot
// the hub confirmed last; local edits go out as runner.settings, which the hub applies in seq order whatever their
// base, each at a new version, and echoes verbatim with update_settings, as it echoes the owner's edits.
// - In flight: a runner.settings is in flight until an echo answers it (Outbox.markSettingsEcho) and runner.json's
//   snapshot has that echo's version. runner.json holds the snapshot with the edits in flight laid over it (the
//   view), so a local edit back to an earlier value differs from it and is sent.
// - An echo becomes the snapshot. runner.json takes the new view, but where it differs from the view before the echo
//   (an edit made by other means), which is kept and sent again. An echo answers only edits made before it came.
// - Versions: the snapshot moves one version at a time, or to the hub's whole settings; an echo that would skip a
//   version waits for the ones before it (CommandExecutor), and one the snapshot already covers only marks. A failed
//   write of runner.json leaves the echo in the settings the runner holds.
// - Refusals: the hub acknowledges an edit it refuses and never echoes it. A probe (isSettingsProbe) settles which
//   acknowledged edits will get no echo: at its echo, every older edit still unanswered was refused, and runner.json
//   falls back to the hub's value for it. Nothing is ever sent again for a refused edit.
import type { RunnerSettings } from '@agflow/core';
import {
  applySettingsEcho,
  isWholeSettings,
  type RunnerConfig,
  type SettingsEdits,
  settingsAfterEdits,
} from './config';
import type { Logger } from './log';
import { isSettingsProbe, type Outbox, type SettingsEvent } from './outbox';

export interface SettingsSyncOptions {
  config(): RunnerConfig;
  /**
   * Makes config() give the new settings, then writes runner.json. config() gives them even when the write throws:
   * the runner goes on with what it holds, and the next write that succeeds brings runner.json up to it.
   */
  saveConfig(config: RunnerConfig): void;
  outbox: Outbox;
  logger: Logger;
}

const settingsOfEvents = (events: readonly SettingsEvent[]) => events.map((event) => event.data.settings);

function describe(error: unknown): string {
  return error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
}

export class SettingsSync {
  constructor(private readonly options: SettingsSyncOptions) {}

  /** The confirmed snapshot with the edits in flight laid over it: what the hub holds once it has applied them. */
  view(config: RunnerConfig = this.options.config()): RunnerSettings {
    const inFlight = this.options.outbox.settingsInFlight(config.confirmedSettings.version);
    return settingsAfterEdits(config.confirmedSettings, settingsOfEvents(inFlight));
  }

  /**
   * An update_settings echo, run one at a time in arrival order; gives false when it waits. It may answer the edits up
   * to arrivedAfter, the outbox's newest seq when it came (Outbox.markSettingsEcho).
   * - The snapshot moves one version at a time: an echo of the snapshot's version + 1 becomes it. One further ahead
   *   waits, changing nothing: a version before it has not run here yet, and the executor runs it again once that one
   *   has (CommandExecutor). One at or below the snapshot's version (the same command run again, or one that the hub's
   *   whole settings covered) only marks the edit it answers, and the snapshot stays. The hub's whole settings
   *   (hello's echoes, isWholeSettings) become the snapshot at any version not below it.
   * - The marks go first, at the echo's version, and count once the snapshot has that version: a run cut short leaves
   *   the edits in flight, and runs again when the hub sends the command again, without marking more.
   * - When runner.json's write fails, the runner holds the new settings all the same (SettingsSyncOptions.saveConfig);
   *   should it stop before a write succeeds, its next hello reports the older version and the hub sends its whole
   *   settings.
   */
  echo(update: { settings: SettingsEdits; version: number }, arrivedAfter = Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER): boolean {
    const { outbox, logger } = this.options;
    const config = this.options.config();
    const current = config.confirmedSettings.version;
    const whole = isWholeSettings(update.settings, config.confirmedSettings);
    if (!whole && update.version > current + 1) {
      logger.warn('an update_settings skips a version; it waits for the ones before it', {
        version: update.version,
        snapshot: current,
      });
      return false;
    }
    const stale = whole ? update.version < current : update.version <= current;
    const before = settingsOfEvents(outbox.settingsInFlight(current));
    const { refused } = outbox.markSettingsEcho(update.settings, update.version, arrivedAfter);
    const echo = stale ? { settings: {}, version: current } : update;
    const after = settingsOfEvents(outbox.settingsInFlight(echo.version));
    const { config: next, pending } = applySettingsEcho(config, echo, { before, after });
    this.save(next);
    for (const event of refused) {
      logger.warn("the hub refused a settings edit; runner.json takes the hub's settings", {
        seq: event.seq,
        settings: event.data.settings,
      });
    }
    if (Object.keys(pending).length > 0) {
      outbox.append({ type: 'runner.settings', data: { settings: pending, baseVersion: echo.version } });
    }
    return true;
  }

  /** saveConfig, with a failed write logged; the runner goes on with the settings config() gives. */
  private save(config: RunnerConfig): void {
    try {
      this.options.saveConfig(config);
    } catch (error) {
      this.options.logger.error('cannot write runner.json; the runner goes on with the settings it holds', {
        error: describe(error),
      });
      return;
    }
    this.options.outbox.settingsSaved(config.confirmedSettings.version);
  }

  /**
   * Sends a probe when the hub has acknowledged a settings edit no echo has answered, once the commands that came
   * before the acknowledgement have run (CommandExecutor.settingsAcknowledged). The hub had applied or refused it,
   * and M2a sends an applied edit's echo before the ack of the events message that carried it, so after an ack only a
   * refused edit is left; at a welcome the echoes the hub still holds come after it, and a probe for one of those
   * costs one version. None goes while a probe newer than the edits still waits for its acknowledgement; nor while
   * one the hub acknowledged waits for its echo, except at a welcome, so a refused probe is followed by one probe per
   * welcome at most.
   */
  probeUnanswered(options: { welcome: boolean }): void {
    const { outbox } = this.options;
    const acked = outbox.ackedSeq();
    const unanswered = outbox.settingsUnanswered();
    const waiting = unanswered.filter((event) => !isSettingsProbe(event) && event.seq <= acked).at(-1);
    if (waiting === undefined) return;
    const probes = unanswered.filter((event) => isSettingsProbe(event) && event.seq > waiting.seq);
    if (probes.some((probe) => probe.seq > acked)) return;
    if (probes.length > 0 && !options.welcome) return;
    const baseVersion = this.options.config().confirmedSettings.version;
    outbox.append({ type: 'runner.settings', data: { settings: {}, baseVersion } });
  }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run the tests and see them pass**

Run: `bun test packages/runner/test/executor.test.ts packages/runner/test/config.test.ts packages/runner/test/db.test.ts && bun test && bun run typecheck`
Expected: the task's tests pass; then the whole suite passes (`0 fail`) and `tsc` exits 0.

The Outbox holds the bookkeeping: `settingsInFlight(confirmedVersion?)`, `markSettingsEcho(settings, version, arrivedAfter?)`, which answers the oldest unanswered edit with the same settings among those appended before the echo arrived (the journal's `outboxSeq`), `settingsUnanswered`, `settingsSaved` (the runner.db meta key `settingsSavedVersion`), `onAck`, and probes (`isSettingsProbe`, a `runner.settings` with no fields). A mark counts once runner.json's snapshot has its version, and an echo run again marks nothing more. `pruneAcked` and `pruneBefore` keep every edit still in flight, keep no probe, and drop the marks of what they delete; without a `confirmedVersion` option an Outbox counts marks up to `settingsSavedVersion`, so M2c's `new Outbox(db)` needs no change. `config.ts` gains `settingsAfterEdits`, `applySettingsEcho(config, echo, { before, after })` and `isWholeSettings(settings, snapshot)`: settings are whole only when they name every field and every vendor the snapshot's per-vendor records hold. The settings retries use the `CommandExecutorOptions.timers` seam: 1 s, doubling to 60 s. `helloSent()` and `close()` answer every waiting echo null. An `update_settings` whose journal row cannot be written is taken again after the backoff; any other such command rejects, and the link answers `ok: false`. A `hand_back` refused with `process_running` answers `{ ok: false, error: 'process_running', data: { pids } }`; any other refusal has no data. After `welcome.stop`, new commands for that attempt answer `attempt_ended`, except `cleanup_attempt`, `upload_transcript` and `hand_back`. A preflight with no `preflighted` callback still runs the adapter's preflight. An edit still in flight is not sent again, only a field changed by other means (refinement 61). Stateful echo handling lives in `SettingsSync`; `config.ts` retains the pure functions `settingsOf`, `localSettingsEdits`, `settingsAfterEdits`, `applySettingsEcho` and `isWholeSettings`. A failed `update_settings` journal write keeps its place and promise pending through settings backoff. `CommandExecutorOptions.vendors()` is required and there is no `preparer` option. Older-lineage `update_settings` rows stay running until `Journal.pruneBefore` removes them; M2c's 14-day prune bounds retention.

### Task 36: Startup recovery

Before its first hello the runner settles what a previous run left (design 7.4). `killRegisteredGroups` kills recorded groups whose identity still matches and sweeps every recorded clone, also where the leader is gone; M2c's uninstall reuses it (X-7). `recoverOnStart` records starting, running and idle attempts as stopped and keeps suspended ones suspended. `liveAttemptsForHello` lists the attempts hello reports, with design 6.3's states (X-36): an ended attempt stays `stopped` while its clone exists, and live controllers on a reconnect report `running`, or `idle` for a lead between turns. Recovery never sets `finalizedAt`: stopped process state is not evidence that final work was recorded.

```ts
import { requireLsofOnMacOS } from './prerequisites';

// Every test here runs git or agent processes, which take several times as long on a machine loaded by other suites.

const children: ReturnType<typeof Bun.spawn>[] = [];
const controllers: AttemptController[] = [];
afterEach(async () => {
  for (const child of children.splice(0)) {
    child.kill('SIGKILL');
    await child.exited;
  }
  for (const controller of controllers.splice(0)) await controller.session?.close();
  await cleanupRunnerFixtures();

/** A real group leader with its own cwd, without invoking any vendor CLI. */
async function childIn(clone: string) {
  mkdirSync(clone, { recursive: true });
  const child = Bun.spawn([process.execPath, '-e', 'setInterval(() => {}, 1000)'], {
    detached: true,
    cwd: clone,
    stdin: 'ignore',
    stdout: 'ignore',
    stderr: 'ignore',
  });
  children.push(child);
  // Wait for the child to enter its event loop before the clone sweep.
  let identity: ProcessIdentity | null = null;
  for (let tries = 0; tries < 100 && identity === null; tries++) {
    identity = await processIdentity(child.pid);
    if (identity === null) await Bun.sleep(10);
  }
  expect(identity).not.toBeNull();
  return { child, identity: identity! };
}

function record(f: RunnerFixture, n: number, state: LocalAttemptState, clone: string | null) {
  const attemptId = `T-${n}-a1`;

    clone,
    tmpDir: null,
    cliVersion: null,
  });
  return f.store.update(attemptId, { state, sessionRef: state === 'starting' ? null : `session-${n}` });
}
```

```ts
// Startup recovery (design 7.4, "Runner start"; 6.3, hello.attempts; X-36). Before the first hello the runner
// settles what a previous run left: every registered group whose leader is still the process the registry recorded
// (pid, pgid and lstart) is killed, and every recorded clone swept, so no agent or escaped tool of a dead runner keeps
// writing; a pid that now belongs to another process is not signalled. The registry is then cleared, and the attempts
// that had a process are recorded as stopped; suspended ones stay suspended, so the hub resumes them as such. No
// agent is resumed here: the hub decides that from hello. killRegisteredGroups is exported for M2c's uninstall (X-7).
//
// hello lists every attempt whose start or resume the runner recorded, as LiveAttempt entries with design 6.3's
// states: starting before attempt.spawned, running while its process lives (a worker, or a lead in a turn), idle for
// a lead's process between wake-ups, stopped with no process, suspended after a suspend. An ended attempt stays listed
// as stopped while its clone waits for cleanup_attempt; once cleaned up it is left out.
import type { LiveAttempt } from '@agflow/core';
import type { AttemptController } from './attempt/controller';
import type { AttemptStore, ProcessRecord } from './attempt-store';
import { cloneExists } from './git/clone';
import { type Logger, noopLogger } from './log';
import { killAndSweep } from './stop-ladder';

/**
 * Kills the registered groups whose leader is still the recorded process, then sweeps each recorded clone once, also
 * when its leader is gone or its pid now belongs to another process, and clears the registry. Gives the groups it
 * killed.
 */
export async function killRegisteredGroups(store: AttemptStore, logger: Logger = noopLogger): Promise<ProcessRecord[]> {
  const groups = store.processes();
  const byClone = new Map<string | null, ProcessRecord[]>();
  // Every recorded clone is swept: a leader that is gone, or whose pid was reused, may have left escaped tools
  // writing there. Only the group kill checks the leader's identity, as killGroup does for every group signal.
  for (const group of groups) byClone.set(group.clone, [...(byClone.get(group.clone) ?? []), group]);
  const killed: ProcessRecord[] = [];
  for (const [clone, recorded] of byClone) {
    const result = await killAndSweep({ groups: async () => recorded, clone });
    killed.push(...recorded.filter((group) => result.killed.includes(group.pgid)));
    if (result.sweepSkipped !== null) logger.warn('cannot sweep a recorded clone', { clone, why: result.sweepSkipped });
  }
  // What is left of them is dead or someone else's; the next start records its own groups.
  for (const group of groups) store.forgetProcess(group.attemptId, group.pgid);
  return killed;
}

/** Settles what a previous run left, before the first hello: its processes killed, its live attempts stopped. */
export async function recoverOnStart(store: AttemptStore, logger: Logger = noopLogger): Promise<void> {
  const killed = await killRegisteredGroups(store, logger);
  if (killed.length > 0) {
    const attempts = [...new Set(killed.map((group) => group.attemptId))];
    logger.info('killed the agents a previous run left', { attempts });
  }
  for (const record of store.list()) {
    if (record.state === 'starting' || record.state === 'running' || record.state === 'idle') {
      store.update(record.attemptId, { state: 'stopped' });
    }
  }
}

/**
 * hello.attempts: every recorded attempt as a LiveAttempt, except ended ones whose clone is gone. The runtime gives
 * its controllers, whose live processes tell running from a lead idle between wake-ups on a reconnect.
 */
export function liveAttemptsForHello(
  store: AttemptStore,
  controllers: ReadonlyMap<string, Pick<AttemptController, 'phase' | 'session'>> = new Map(),
): LiveAttempt[] {
  return store.list().flatMap((record): LiveAttempt[] => {
    const clone = record.clone !== null && cloneExists(record.clone);
    if ((record.endedAt !== null || record.state === 'ended') && !clone) return [];
    const controller = controllers.get(record.attemptId);
    let state: LiveAttempt['state'] = record.state === 'ended' ? 'stopped' : record.state;
    if (controller?.session) {
      const between = record.spec.role === 'lead' && controller.phase === 'idle';
      if (record.state !== 'starting') state = between ? 'idle' : 'running';
    } else if (controller?.phase === 'starting' || controller?.phase === 'preparing') {
      // A start or resume under way, with no process yet.
      state = 'starting';
    }
    return [{ attemptId: record.attemptId, fence: record.fence, state, sessionRef: record.sessionRef, clone }];
  });
}
```

### Task 37: The runner runtime: composition, hello, welcome and heartbeats

`createRunner(options)` composes the runner (design 6.3, 13): runner.json, runner.db, the awake clock, the link, the executor, the controllers, and what the caller passes in (adapters, seams, credentials provider, agflow command, logger, and `cliVersion`, the CLI version of new attempts, this platform's pin by default). It runs startup recovery first, reads the project's name and repo from `GET /api/status` (cached in runner.db with the hub URL), preflights every adapter, and says hello with the confirmed settings, vendor reports, git readiness, health state, outbox positions (X-1) and recovered attempts; each hello starts a new lineage in the executor. On each welcome it stores `wipRefPrefix` and the hub epoch, hands the welcome to the executor, settles the previous run's journal rows and resumes its pending late work after the first one, sends the hand edits made while it was down, and probes for refused edits (X-12). A welcome of another hub epoch is a restored hub's: the runner records the events it holds, then the new epoch, and says hello again at once, before it runs or sends anything. Heartbeats carry every live attempt's facts, starting and preparing ones included, and the health seam's report. Failures of ordinary welcome writes are logged and handling continues; failed restore bookkeeping drops the link with normal backoff and returns before commands or replay, leaving the epoch unrecorded for the next welcome to retry.
