### Task 39: Planted git configuration never runs

The security tests of design 7.3 and 15 plant every program-valued git key by three routes: directly in `.git/config`, through `include.path`, and in `config.worktree`, with hooks and a `.gitattributes` filter. Three portable cases prove the plants are live, then exercise submission, WIP harvest/snapshot/detection/strip and take-over without firing them. Three separate macOS cases repeat that path and complete a clone hand-back after requiring lsof. A seventh, portable case proves the agent's git never offers the owner's or system's credentials. No case returns early when lsof is missing.

**Files:**
- Test: `packages/runner/test/security-git.test.ts`

- [ ] **Step 1: Make the change**

**File:** `packages/runner/test/security-git.test.ts` (new)

```ts
// Design 7.3's planted-config test and section 15's credential-free agent git. An agent owns its clone's .git, so it
// can name a program in any key git runs: directly in .git/config, through include.path, or in config.worktree with
// extensions.worktreeConfig. The runner never runs git with that directory, so none of them may run during any of its
// operations on the clone: harvest, snapshot, detection, restore, a WIP push, a submission push, a take-over and a
// hand-back. Each test first proves the plants live, by running git in the clone as the agent would. The agent's own
// git may run what it planted, but never reaches a credential helper outside the clone.
import { afterEach, describe, expect, setDefaultTimeout, test } from 'bun:test';
import { appendFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { lateWorkRef } from '@agflow/core';
import { type FakeScript, gitIn } from '@agflow/testkit';
import { buildAgentEnv } from '../src/env';
import {
  cleanupRunnerFixtures,
  createRunnerFixture,
  FIXTURE_PROJECT,
  FIXTURE_WIP_PREFIX,
  type RunnerFixture,
  waitFor,
} from './fixture';
import { requireLsofOnMacOS } from './prerequisites';

afterEach(cleanupRunnerFixtures);

// Every test here runs git or agent processes, which take several times as long on a machine loaded by other suites.
setDefaultTimeout(30_000);

const FENCE = { epoch: 1, counter: 1 };
const BRANCH = 'agflow/T-4-tidy';
const WIP = 'refs/agflow/T-4/a1';

/**
 * main's files: every file goes through the planted clean and smudge filter, and .proc files through a process one.
 * Only an uncommitted .proc file is written: git runs the process filter as a protocol peer, and the planted one
 * would fail the agent's own git in the clone.
 */
const FILES = {
  'README.md': '# demo\n',
  'src/app.ts': 'app\n',
  '.gitattributes': '* filter=planted\n*.proc filter=byprocess\n',
};

/** The agent's work, all committed, in a turn that stays live; then the handoff turn a take-over asks for. */
const SCRIPT: FakeScript = {
  turns: [
    [
      { do: 'write', path: 'src/app.ts', content: 'tidy\n' },
      { do: 'commit', message: 'tidy the app' },
      { do: 'sleep', ms: 60_000 },
    ],
    [{ do: 'terminal', tool: 'handoff' }],
  ],
};

const METHODS = ['directly', 'through include.path', 'in config.worktree'] as const;
type Method = (typeof METHODS)[number];

/** The hooks planted both in .git/hooks and in the core.hooksPath directory. */
const HOOKS = ['pre-commit', 'post-checkout', 'reference-transaction', 'pre-push', 'post-index-change', 'post-merge'];

/** Shell-quoted, for a command git runs through sh. */
function quoted(path: string): string {
  return `'${path.replace(/'/g, `'\\''`)}'`;
}

/** A config value in double quotes, as git's config syntax reads it. */
function configString(value: string): string {
  return `"${value.replace(/\\/g, '\\\\').replace(/"/g, '\\"')}"`;
}

interface Planted {
  /** The keys and hooks that ran, one per line, in order. */
  fired(): string[];
  /** Forgets what ran so far. */
  reset(): void;
}

/**
 * Plants every program-valued key in a .git directory by the given method, and hooks in its hooks directory and in
 * the one core.hooksPath names. Every planted program is a shell command that appends its key to a marker file in
 * dir, outside the clone.
 */
function plant(gitDir: string, dir: string, method: Method): Planted {
  mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
  const marker = join(dir, 'fired');
  const record = (key: string) => configString(`echo ${key} >> ${quoted(marker)}`);
  const hooksPath = join(dir, 'hooks');
  for (const hooks of [hooksPath, join(gitDir, 'hooks')]) {
    mkdirSync(hooks, { recursive: true });
    for (const hook of HOOKS) {
      writeFileSync(join(hooks, hook), `#!/bin/sh\necho hook ${hook} >> ${quoted(marker)}\n`, { mode: 0o755 });
    }
  }
  const keys = [
    '[core]',
    `\thooksPath = ${configString(hooksPath)}`,
    `\tfsmonitor = ${record('core.fsmonitor')}`,
    `\tsshCommand = ${record('core.sshCommand')}`,
    `\tpager = ${record('core.pager')}`,
    `\teditor = ${record('core.editor')}`,
    `\taskPass = ${record('core.askPass')}`,
    '[credential]',
    `\thelper = ${configString(`!echo credential.helper >> ${quoted(marker)}; echo username=agent; echo password=x`)}`,
    // What the agent's gitconfig forbids, a repository's config allows again.
    '[protocol]',
    '\tallow = always',
    '[diff]',
    `\texternal = ${record('diff.external')}`,
    '[sequence]',
    `\teditor = ${record('sequence.editor')}`,
    '[gpg]',
    `\tprogram = ${record('gpg.program')}`,
    // So a commit or tag made with this config would call gpg.program.
    '[commit]',
    '\tgpgSign = true',
    '[tag]',
    '\tgpgSign = true',
    '[filter "planted"]',
    `\tclean = ${configString(`cat; echo filter.planted.clean >> ${quoted(marker)}`)}`,
    `\tsmudge = ${configString(`cat; echo filter.planted.smudge >> ${quoted(marker)}`)}`,
    '[filter "byprocess"]',
    `\tprocess = ${record('filter.byprocess.process')}`,
    '[uploadpack]',
    `\tpackObjectsHook = ${record('uploadpack.packObjectsHook')}`,
    '',
  ].join('\n');
  const config = join(gitDir, 'config');
  if (method === 'directly') {
    appendFileSync(config, keys);
  } else if (method === 'through include.path') {
    const included = join(dir, 'planted.inc');
    writeFileSync(included, keys);
    appendFileSync(config, `[include]\n\tpath = ${configString(included)}\n`);
  } else {
    writeFileSync(join(gitDir, 'config.worktree'), keys);
    appendFileSync(config, '[extensions]\n\tworktreeConfig = true\n');
  }
  return {
    fired: () => (existsSync(marker) ? readFileSync(marker, 'utf8').split('\n').filter((line) => line !== '') : []),
    reset: () => rmSync(marker, { force: true }),
  };
}

/** Proves the plants live: the agent's git in the clone runs the fsmonitor, the hooks and both filters. */
async function proveLive(clone: string, planted: Planted): Promise<void> {
  // No optional locks: status then writes no index, so no hook runs before the runner's operations. None of these
  // commands changes the clone.
  await gitIn(clone, ['--no-optional-locks', 'status']);
  await gitIn(clone, ['hash-object', 'src/app.ts']);
  await gitIn(clone, ['hook', 'run', 'pre-commit']);
  await gitIn(clone, ['cat-file', '--filters', 'HEAD:src/app.ts']);
  const fired = planted.fired().join('\n');
  expect(fired).toContain('core.fsmonitor');
  expect(fired).toContain('filter.planted.clean');
  expect(fired).toContain('hook pre-commit');
  expect(fired).toContain('filter.planted.smudge');
  planted.reset();
}

const cloneOf = (f: RunnerFixture) => f.paths.clone(FIXTURE_PROJECT, 'T-4-a1');

/** Starts T-4-a1 and waits until its agent has committed its work and is in its long turn. */
async function startCommitted(f: RunnerFixture) {
  const controller = f.controller();
  await controller.start(f.spec());
  const clone = cloneOf(f);
  await waitFor(() => controller.phase === 'turn');
  for (;;) {
    if ((await gitIn(clone, ['log', '-1', '--format=%s'])) === 'tidy the app') return controller;
    await Bun.sleep(50);
  }
}

describe('planted git configuration', () => {
  for (const method of METHODS) {
    async function throughTakeover() {
      const f = await createRunnerFixture({ files: FILES, script: SCRIPT });
      const controller = await startCommitted(f);
      const clone = cloneOf(f);
      const head = await gitIn(clone, ['rev-parse', 'HEAD']);
      const planted = plant(join(clone, '.git'), join(f.home, 'planted'), method);
      await proveLive(clone, planted);

      // A submission push: the clone is clean, its work committed.
      const submitted = await controller.submit({
        fence: FENCE,
        submissionId: 'S-1',
        branch: BRANCH,
        expectedBranchSha: null,
        adoptable: [],
      });
      expect(submitted).toMatchObject({ ok: true, outcome: { ok: true, headSha: head } });
      expect(await gitIn(f.origin.path, ['rev-parse', `refs/heads/${BRANCH}`])).toBe(head);

      // Uncommitted work and a protected change: the harvest, the snapshot, the detection that strips it, a WIP push.
      writeFileSync(join(clone, 'src', 'app.ts'), 'tidier\n');
      writeFileSync(join(clone, 'notes.proc'), 'notes\n');
      writeFileSync(join(clone, '.envrc'), 'export X=1\n');
      expect(await controller.pushWip()).toMatchObject({ status: 'pushed', ref: WIP });
      expect(await gitIn(f.origin.path, ['show', `${WIP}:src/app.ts`])).toBe('tidier');
      expect(await gitIn(f.origin.path, ['show', `${WIP}:notes.proc`])).toBe('notes');
      expect(f.events('attempt.violation').map((event) => event.data)).toEqual([{ phase: 'wip', paths: ['.envrc'] }]);

      // A take-over: the stop, the final harvest and push, the restore that removes .envrc, and a new .git.
      expect(await controller.prepareTakeover({ fence: FENCE, person: 'alice' })).toMatchObject({ ok: true });
      expect(f.events('attempt.taken_over')[0]?.data.error).toBeNull();
      expect(existsSync(join(clone, '.envrc'))).toBe(false);
      expect(planted.fired()).toEqual([]);
      return { f, controller, clone, planted };
    }

    test(`keys planted ${method} never run in harvest, snapshot, detection, restore, WIP, submission and take-over`, async () => {
      await throughTakeover();
    }, 60_000);

    test.skipIf(process.platform !== 'darwin')(
      `keys planted ${method} never run in hand-back (the runner supports darwin-arm64 only; design 7.1)`,
      async () => {
        requireLsofOnMacOS();
        const { f, controller, clone, planted } = await throughTakeover();

        // The person's .git, planted the same way: the hand-back harvests it, pushes it and removes the clone.
        const again = plant(join(clone, '.git'), join(f.home, 'planted-again'), method);
        writeFileSync(join(clone, 'src', 'app.ts'), 'by a person\n');
        await proveLive(clone, again);
        expect(await controller.handBack({ source: { kind: 'clone' } })).toMatchObject({ ok: true });
        const late = lateWorkRef(FIXTURE_WIP_PREFIX, 'T-4-a1', 1);
        expect(await gitIn(f.origin.path, ['show', `${late}:src/app.ts`])).toBe('by a person');
        expect(existsSync(clone)).toBe(false);
        expect(planted.fired()).toEqual([]);
        expect(again.fired()).toEqual([]);
      },
      60_000,
    );
  }

  test("the agent's git, with a planted credential.helper and protocols allowed again, never reaches another helper", async () => {
    const f = await createRunnerFixture({ files: FILES, script: SCRIPT });
    await startCommitted(f);
    const clone = cloneOf(f);
    // The owner's own git configuration names a helper too, which the agent's git must never reach.
    const owner = join(f.home, 'owner');
    const ownerMarker = join(owner, 'helper-ran');
    mkdirSync(owner, { recursive: true });
    writeFileSync(
      join(owner, '.gitconfig'),
      `[credential]\n\thelper = ${configString(`!echo owner >> ${quoted(ownerMarker)}; echo password=secret`)}\n`,
    );
    const record = f.store.get('T-4-a1');
    const tools = f.paths.agentTools(FIXTURE_PROJECT, 'T-4-a1');
    const env = buildAgentEnv({
      vendor: 'claude',
      spec: f.spec(),
      clone,
      tools,
      tmpDir: record?.tmpDir ?? null,
      config: f.config,
      paths: f.paths,
      base: { HOME: owner, USER: process.env.USER },
    });
    // A remote that asks for a login, as a git host does, and records what it is offered.
    const offered: (string | null)[] = [];
    const server = Bun.serve({
      hostname: '127.0.0.1',
      port: 0,
      fetch: (request) => {
        offered.push(request.headers.get('authorization'));
        return new Response('login required', { status: 401, headers: { 'WWW-Authenticate': 'Basic realm="git"' } });
      },
    });
    const url = `http://127.0.0.1:${server.port}/acme/demo.git`;
    const agentGit = async (args: string[]) => {
      const run = Bun.spawn(['git', ...args], { cwd: clone, env, stdin: 'ignore', stdout: 'pipe', stderr: 'pipe' });
      const [stdout, stderr, code] = await Promise.all([
        new Response(run.stdout).text(),
        new Response(run.stderr).text(),
        run.exited,
      ]);
      return { stdout, stderr, code };
    };
    try {
      // As the runner left the clone, the agent's git uses no network protocol.
      const refused = await agentGit(['ls-remote', url]);
      expect(refused.code).not.toBe(0);
      expect(refused.stderr).toContain("transport 'http' not allowed");
      expect(offered).toEqual([]);

      const dir = join(f.home, 'planted');
      for (const method of METHODS) plant(join(clone, '.git'), join(dir, method), method);
      for (const args of [['ls-remote', url], ['push', url, 'HEAD:refs/heads/main']]) {
        const result = await agentGit(args);
        expect(result.code).not.toBe(0);
      }
      // The agent's own helpers answered, and nothing else: the owner's never ran, and no other secret was sent.
      const sent = offered.flatMap((authorization) =>
        authorization === null ? [] : [Buffer.from(authorization.replace(/^Basic /, ''), 'base64').toString()],
      );
      expect(sent.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
      for (const credentials of sent) expect(credentials).toMatch(/^agent:x/);
      expect(existsSync(ownerMarker)).toBe(false);

      // Every helper the agent's git sees is the clone's own, or the empty one of the agent's gitconfig: no global,
      // XDG or system helper (Apple git's osxkeychain, say).
      expect(env.GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL).toBe(join(tools, 'gitconfig'));
      const helpers = await agentGit(['config', '--show-scope', '--show-origin', '--get-all', 'credential.helper']);
      const lines = helpers.stdout.split('\n').filter((line) => line !== '');
      const outside = lines.filter((line) => !line.startsWith('local\t') && !line.startsWith('worktree\t'));
      expect(outside).toEqual([`global\tfile:${env.GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL}\t`]);
      expect(lines.filter((line) => line.includes('echo username=agent'))).toHaveLength(METHODS.length);
    } finally {
      server.stop(true);
    }
  }, 30_000);
});
```

### Task 40: The runner against the in-process hub

The runner meets M2a's hub for the first time (design 1, 6.3, 6.4, 6.13, 15). `test/hub-fixture.ts` serves the hub in process for every runner-side suite (X-26): `startTestHub` runs `startHub` on 127.0.0.1, port 0, over a fake-clock test context with `TEST_HUB_TIMINGS`, the scheduler `manual` and no database lock, gives the owner a CLI session, and re-exports `startRunnerAttempt`, `mintAgentToken` and `addRunnerAttempt`. The integration test runs one hub and one runner with the fake adapter and a local bare origin: registration, placement, WIP, a two-phase submission, a hold, acceptance and cleanup; a killed agent whose successor starts from its final WIP; and a runner restart that replays its outbox without duplicates.
```ts
// The in-process hub every runner-side suite shares (design 13, 15; X-26): M2a's startHub on 127.0.0.1 and a free
// port, over a fake-clock test context with an in-memory database, test-mode timings, the scheduler created stopped
// ('manual') and no database lock. The test ticks the scheduler itself; nothing starts an attempt behind its back.
// The runner's owner gets a CLI session, as `agflow login` gives one. M2c, M2d and M2e reuse it.
import type { Credentials } from '@agflow/core';
import { createSession } from '@agflow/hub/src/auth';
import {
  HUB_RUNNER_DEFAULTS,
  type HubConfig,
  type HubContext,
  stopGraceFor,
  tx,
  wipGraceFor,
} from '@agflow/hub/src/context';
import { storeRunnerLeads } from '@agflow/hub/src/project';
import type { Scheduler, TickResult } from '@agflow/hub/src/scheduler';
import { type HubServer, startHub } from '@agflow/hub/src/server';
import { createTestContext, markHubAlive, type TestClock } from '@agflow/hub/test/helpers';

export { startRunnerAttempt } from '@agflow/hub/src/attempts';
export { mintAgentToken } from '@agflow/hub/src/auth';
export { addRunnerAttempt } from '@agflow/hub/test/helpers';

/**
 * Section 12's defaults with the hub's test mode on and the intervals a runner hears in welcome shortened, so that a
 * runner under test heartbeats every second and finds a dead link within seconds.
 */
export const TEST_HUB_TIMINGS: Partial<HubConfig> = {
  ...HUB_RUNNER_DEFAULTS,
  testMode: true,
  heartbeatMs: 1_000,
  deadLinkMs: 5_000,
  handoffMs: 5_000,
  stopGraceMs: stopGraceFor(5_000),
};

export interface TestHubOptions {
  /**
   * The hub's configuration over TEST_HUB_TIMINGS: the project's repo (a local bare origin), for one. As the hub's
   * loadConfig does, stopGraceMs and wipGraceMs follow handoffMs and runnerLeaseMs unless set here too, and the owner
   * is always among allowedUsers.
   */
  config?: Partial<HubConfig>;
  /** The runner's owner, who gets the CLI session: alice by default. */
  owner?: string;
  /** Whether the scheduler starts runner leads; off by default, since a lead would take a runner slot every tick. */
  runnerLeads?: boolean;
  /**
   * The hub's housekeeping timers (dead links, sign-ins, delivery flushes): off by default, as the fake clock does
   * not move on its own.
   */
  timers?: boolean;
}

export interface TestHub {
  /** The served origin: the runner link, the API and AttemptSpec.hubUrl. */
  url: string;
  ctx: HubContext;
  clock: TestClock;
  server: HubServer;
  scheduler: Scheduler;
  owner: string;
  /** The owner's CLI session token. */
  token: string;
  /** The credentials a runner of the owner's signs in with. */
  credentials: Credentials;
  /**
   * One scheduler tick now. The hub is marked alive first, as its timer would have ticked every tickMs, so a fake
   * clock moved further than that opens no recovery window (design 6.14).
   */
  tick(): TickResult;
  /** Closes the runner links and the port, and the database. */
  stop(): Promise<void>;
}

/** Serves M2a's hub in this process for a runner under test. */
export function startTestHub(options: TestHubOptions = {}): TestHub {
  const owner = options.owner ?? 'alice';
  const given = options.config ?? {};
  const config: Partial<HubConfig> = {
    ...TEST_HUB_TIMINGS,
    ...given,
    allowedUsers: [...new Set([...(given.allowedUsers ?? ['alice', 'bob']), owner])],
  };
  // The derived settings follow their base, as loadConfig keeps them (X-11).
  config.stopGraceMs = given.stopGraceMs ?? stopGraceFor(config.handoffMs ?? HUB_RUNNER_DEFAULTS.handoffMs);
  config.wipGraceMs = given.wipGraceMs ?? wipGraceFor(config.runnerLeaseMs ?? HUB_RUNNER_DEFAULTS.runnerLeaseMs);
  const { ctx, clock } = createTestContext(config);
  // In a transaction of its own, as its callers run it.
  tx(ctx, () => storeRunnerLeads(ctx, options.runnerLeads ?? false));
  // Before the port opens, so that a failure here leaves nothing serving.
  const token = createSession(ctx, owner, 'cli');
  const server = startHub(ctx, {
    port: 0,
    hostname: '127.0.0.1',
    scheduler: 'manual',
    dbLock: false,
    timers: options.timers ?? false,
  });
  // The port is known only now: starts tell runners and agents this URL.
  ctx.config.publicUrl = server.url;
  const scheduler = server.scheduler;
  if (scheduler === null) throw new Error('startHub made no scheduler');
  let stopped = false;
  return {
    url: server.url,
    ctx,
    clock,
    server,
    scheduler,
    owner,
    token,
    credentials: { hubUrl: server.url, token, user: owner },
    tick() {
      markHubAlive(ctx);
      return scheduler.tick();
    },
    async stop() {
      if (stopped) return;
      stopped = true;
      await server.stop({ closeDatabase: true });
    },
  };
}
```

```ts
// The runner against M2a's hub (design 1 exit criterion 1, 6.3, 6.4, 6.13, 15): one in-process hub, one runner with
// the fake adapter and a local bare origin, over the real link. The hub places the work, the fake agent commits and
// submits with its own agent token, and the runner pushes, holds, cleans up, recovers a killed agent's work and
// replays its outbox after a restart, all through the protocol both sides implement.
import { afterEach, describe, expect, setDefaultTimeout, test } from 'bun:test';
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import type { HubStatus } from '@agflow/core';
import { attemptLog, getAttempt } from '@agflow/hub/src/attempt-store';
import { HUB_RUNNER_DEFAULTS } from '@agflow/hub/src/context';
import { getRunner } from '@agflow/hub/src/runners';
import { getTask, listTaskNotes } from '@agflow/hub/src/task-store';
import { acceptTask, createTasks } from '@agflow/hub/src/tasks';
import { addRunner, newTask } from '@agflow/hub/test/helpers';
import { FakeAdapter, type FakeScript, gitIn, type OriginRepo, originRepo } from '@agflow/testkit';
import { AttemptStore } from '../src/attempt-store';
import { loadRunnerConfig, RunnerConfigSchema, saveRunnerConfig } from '../src/config';
import { openRunnerDb, type RunnerDb } from '../src/db';
import type { CredentialsProvider, WelcomeMessage } from '../src/link';
import { memoryLogger } from '../src/log';
import { Outbox } from '../src/outbox';
import { projectKey, type RunnerPaths, runnerPaths } from '../src/paths';
import { killGroup, processIdentity } from '../src/processes';
import { removeAgentTools } from '../src/run-dir';
import { createRunner, type RunnerEvents, type RunnerHandle } from '../src/runner';
import { FIXTURE_AGFLOW, fixtureCliVersion, waitFor } from './fixture';
import { startTestHub, type TestHub } from './hub-fixture';
import { afterThisTest, cleanupRunnerSetups, tempDir } from './runner-setup';

afterEach(cleanupRunnerSetups);

// Each test runs a hub, a runner, git and agent processes, which take several times as long on a loaded machine.
setDefaultTimeout(60_000);

const PROJECT = 'demo';

/** The agent's scripts, by attempt id or task id; a launch of any other attempt does nothing. */
type Scripts = Record<string, FakeScript>;

interface Setup {
  hub: TestHub;
  origin: OriginRepo;
  paths: RunnerPaths;
  /** The vault's project key: the hub's URL and the project's name. */
  project: string;
  /** Starts a runner on the home; closed after the test. A second start is a restart. */
  start(options?: StartOptions): Promise<RunnerHandle>;
  /** The runner.db of the last start. */
  db(): RunnerDb;
}

interface StartOptions {
  /** The hub's credentials by default. */
  credentials?: CredentialsProvider;
  events?: RunnerEvents;
}

/** A hub serving a local bare origin, and a runner home whose fake agents play the scripts. */
async function setup(scripts: Scripts): Promise<Setup> {
  const origin = await originRepo({ 'README.md': '# demo\n', 'src/app.ts': 'app\n' });
  afterThisTest(() => origin.remove());
  const hub = startTestHub({ config: { projectName: PROJECT, projectRepo: origin.path } });
  afterThisTest(() => hub.stop());
  const paths = runnerPaths(tempDir('agflow-runner-home-'));
  // The attempts' tools directories are read-only: they must be made writable before the home can go.
  afterThisTest(() => {
    if (!existsSync(paths.vaults)) return;
    for (const entry of readdirSync(paths.vaults).filter((name) => name.endsWith('.agent'))) {
      for (const attempt of readdirSync(join(paths.vaults, entry))) removeAgentTools(join(paths.vaults, entry, attempt));
    }
  });
  mkdirSync(dirname(paths.db), { recursive: true });
  // Short, as Claude's private temporary directories must be.
  const tmpRoot = mkdtempSync('/tmp/ag');
  afterThisTest(() => rmSync(tmpRoot, { recursive: true, force: true }));
  const config = RunnerConfigSchema.parse({
    runnerKey: 'rk_integration',
    machineId: 'MACHINE-1',
    name: 'laptop',
    test: { skipAuthChecks: true, allowShortTimings: true },
  });
  // A resumed session does nothing more: its script played in the session it resumes.
  const script = (launch: { attemptId: string; resume: unknown }): FakeScript =>
    (launch.resume === null &&
      (scripts[launch.attemptId] ?? scripts[launch.attemptId.replace(/-a\d+$/, '')])) || { turns: [[]] };
  let lastDb: RunnerDb | null = null;
  const start = async (options: StartOptions = {}) => {
    // A restart reads the runner.json the previous run left, its local edits and confirmed snapshot included.
    const restart = lastDb !== null;
    if (!restart) saveRunnerConfig(paths.config, config);
    const db = openRunnerDb(paths.db);
    lastDb = db;
    const runner = await createRunner({
      paths,
      config: restart ? loadRunnerConfig(paths.config) : config,
      db,
      credentials: options.credentials ?? (() => ({ ...hub.credentials })),
      events: options.events,
      adapters: (['claude', 'codex'] as const).map((vendor) => new FakeAdapter({ vendor, skipAuthChecks: true, script })),
      agflow: FIXTURE_AGFLOW,
      // The darwin-arm64 pins, so the fake agents start where no CLI is pinned (CI's linux-x64).
      cliVersion: fixtureCliVersion,
      logger: memoryLogger(),
      tmpRoot,
    });
    afterThisTest(async () => {
      // Whatever agent the test left running goes before the files do.
      for (const group of new AttemptStore(db).processes()) await killGroup(group, 'SIGKILL');
      await runner.close();
      db.close();
    });
    return runner;
  };
  const db = () => {
    if (lastDb === null) throw new Error('no runner started yet');
    return lastDb;
  };
  return { hub, origin, paths, project: projectKey(hub.url, PROJECT), start, db };
}

/** Starts the runner and waits until the hub has it online. */
async function online(s: Setup): Promise<RunnerHandle> {
  const runner = await s.start();
  await waitFor(() => runner.status().link === 'online');
  return runner;
}

/** Creates a ready task by alice; returns its id. */
function readyTask(hub: TestHub, title: string): string {
  const [task] = createTasks(hub.ctx, [newTask({ title })], 'user:alice');
  if (!task) throw new Error('no task created');
  return task.id;
}

/**
 * The fake agent's submit, as the bridge sends it: POST /api/tasks/:id/submit with its own agent token from the agent
 * environment. curl -f fails the tool on any answer but a success.
 */
function submitStep(taskId: string): FakeScript['turns'][number][number] {
  const body = JSON.stringify({ summary: 'Tidied the app', evidence: ['src/app.ts reads well'] });
  const command =
    `curl -sf -X POST "$AGFLOW_HUB_URL/api/tasks/${taskId}/submit" -H "authorization: Bearer $AGFLOW_AGENT_TOKEN" ` +
    `-H 'content-type: application/json' --data '${body}'`;
  return { do: 'tool', command };
}

/** The hub's acknowledged position in the runner's outbox. */
function hubAckedSeq(hub: TestHub, runnerId: string, outboxEpoch: string): number {
  const row = hub.ctx.db
    .query('SELECT acked_seq FROM runner_inbox WHERE runner_id = $runnerId AND outbox_epoch = $outboxEpoch')
    .get({ runnerId, outboxEpoch }) as { acked_seq: number } | null;
  return row?.acked_seq ?? 0;
}

/** How many hub events of the type the hub recorded. */
function hubEvents(hub: TestHub, type: string): number {
  const row = hub.ctx.db.query('SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM events WHERE type = $type').get({ type }) as {
    count: number;
  };
  return row.count;
}

/** How many entries of the attempt's hub log begin with the text. */
function logged(hub: TestHub, attemptId: string, text: string): number {
  return attemptLog(hub.ctx, attemptId).filter((entry) => entry.summary.startsWith(text)).length;
}

/** The commit a ref names on the origin; null when it does not exist. */
async function originSha(origin: OriginRepo, ref: string): Promise<string | null> {
  const sha = await gitIn(origin.path, ['rev-parse', '--verify', '--quiet', `${ref}^{commit}`], { allowFailure: true });
  return sha === '' ? null : sha;
}

describe('startTestHub', () => {
  test('a hub events transaction failure closes with 1011 and the runner replays from the acknowledged position', async () => {
    const s = await setup({});
    const welcomes: WelcomeMessage[] = [];
    const closes: number[] = [];
    const runner = await s.start({
      events: {
        welcome: (welcome) => welcomes.push(welcome),
        link: (_state, detail) => {
          if (detail.code !== null) closes.push(detail.code);
        },
      },
    });
    await waitFor(() => runner.status().link === 'online');
    const runnerId = runner.status().runnerId as string;
    const box = new Outbox(s.db());
    const first = (await runner.changeSettings({ capacity: 3 })) as number;
    expect(await runner.waitAcked(first, 5_000)).toBe(true);
    await waitFor(() => loadRunnerConfig(s.paths.config).confirmedSettings.version === getRunner(s.hub.ctx, runnerId).settingsVersion);
    const version = getRunner(s.hub.ctx, runnerId).settingsVersion;
    const acked = box.ackedSeq();
    s.hub.ctx.db.run(`CREATE TRIGGER fail_events BEFORE UPDATE ON runner_inbox WHEN NEW.acked_seq > ${acked}
      BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'scripted full disk'); END`);
    const failed = (await runner.changeSettings({ draining: true })) as number;
    await waitFor(() => closes.includes(1011));
    expect(box.ackedSeq()).toBe(acked);
    expect(getRunner(s.hub.ctx, runnerId)).toMatchObject({ draining: false, settingsVersion: version });
    s.hub.ctx.db.run('DROP TRIGGER fail_events');
    expect(await runner.waitAcked(failed, 10_000)).toBe(true);
    await waitFor(() => getRunner(s.hub.ctx, runnerId).draining);
    expect(welcomes.slice(1).some((welcome) => welcome.ackedSeq === acked)).toBe(true);
    expect(getRunner(s.hub.ctx, runnerId).settingsVersion).toBe(version + 1);
    expect(runner.status().link).toBe('online');
  });

  test('serves the runner gateway and the API on one port, ticks only when the test runs the scheduler, and stops cleanly without a pid file', async () => {
    const origin = await originRepo({ 'README.md': '# demo\n' });
    afterThisTest(() => origin.remove());

    afterThisTest(() => hub.stop());
    expect(hub.url).toMatch(/^http:\/\/127\.0\.0\.1:\d+$/);
    expect(hub.ctx.config.publicUrl).toBe(hub.url);
    expect(hub.credentials).toEqual({ hubUrl: hub.url, token: hub.token, user: 'alice' });
    // The API, with the owner's CLI session.
    const status = await fetch(`${hub.url}/api/status`, { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${hub.token}` } });
    expect(status.status).toBe(200);
    const { project } = (await status.json()) as HubStatus;
    expect(project).toMatchObject({ name: PROJECT, repo: origin.path, runnerLeads: false });
    // The runner link on the same port: a WebSocket upgrade with the same session.
    const socket = new WebSocket(`${hub.url.replace('http', 'ws')}/api/runner/ws`, {
      headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${hub.token}` },
    });
    await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
      socket.addEventListener('open', () => resolve());
      socket.addEventListener('error', () => reject(new Error('the runner link did not open')));
    });
    socket.close();
    // The scheduler is created stopped: with a runner online, a ready task still waits past the debounce of a started
    // scheduler's tick on task.created, until the test ticks.

    hub.clock.advance(10 * hub.ctx.config.tickMs);

    const defaults = startTestHub();

describe('the runner against the hub', () => {
  test("the runner registers through hello; a scheduler tick places a ready task on it; the fake agent commits and leaves uncommitted work; a WIP push updates the task's work position on the hub", async () => {
    const s = await setup({
      'T-1': {
        turns: [
          [
            { do: 'write', path: 'src/app.ts', content: 'app, tidied\n' },
            { do: 'commit', message: 'Tidy the app' },
            { do: 'write', path: 'notes.txt', content: 'not committed yet\n' },
          ],
        ],
      },
    });
    const runner = await online(s);
    const runnerId = runner.status().runnerId as string;
    expect(runnerId).toMatch(/^R-\d+$/);
    const taskId = readyTask(s.hub, 'Tidy the app');
    const [started] = s.hub.tick().started;
    expect(started).toMatchObject({ taskId, runnerId, vendor: 'claude' });
    const attemptId = started?.id as string;
    await waitFor(() => getAttempt(s.hub.ctx, attemptId).status === 'running');
    await waitFor(() => runner.status().attempts.find((a) => a.attemptId === attemptId)?.phase === 'idle');
    const wipRef = getAttempt(s.hub.ctx, attemptId).wipRef as string;
    const [pushed] = await runner.pushWipNow();
    expect(pushed).toEqual({ attemptId, outcome: { status: 'pushed', ref: wipRef, sha: expect.any(String) } });
    const wipSha = await originSha(s.origin, wipRef);
    expect(wipSha).toBe(pushed?.outcome.status === 'pushed' ? pushed.outcome.sha : null);
    await waitFor(() => getTask(s.hub.ctx, taskId).workSha === wipSha);
    expect(getTask(s.hub.ctx, taskId)).toMatchObject({ status: 'claimed', workRef: wipRef, workSha: wipSha });
    // The WIP holds the commit and the uncommitted file.
    expect(await gitIn(s.origin.path, ['show', `${wipSha}:src/app.ts`])).toBe('app, tidied');
    expect(await gitIn(s.origin.path, ['show', `${wipSha}:notes.txt`])).toBe('not committed yet');
  });

  test('the fake agent submits with its agent token; the runner pushes the task branch; the hub records the submission and holds the attempt, and the runner stops the process; accepting the task cleans the clone up', async () => {
    const s = await setup({

        turns: [

    // The submission lands: the task is submitted at the pushed head, and the attempt holds.
    const submitted = await waitFor(() => {
      const task = getTask(s.hub.ctx, taskId);
      return task.status === 'submitted' && task;
    });
    const head = submitted.submission?.headSha as string;
    expect(submitted.submission).toMatchObject({ summary: 'Tidied the app', evidence: ['src/app.ts reads well'] });
    expect(await originSha(s.origin, `refs/heads/${submitted.branch}`)).toBe(head);
    expect(await gitIn(s.origin.path, ['show', `${head}:src/app.ts`])).toBe('app, tidied');
    expect(submitted).toMatchObject({ workRef: `refs/heads/${submitted.branch}`, workSha: head });
    expect(getAttempt(s.hub.ctx, attemptId)).toMatchObject({ status: 'holding', submittedSha: head });
    // The hold stops the agent; the clone stays for review.
    await waitFor(() => {
      const attempt = runner.status().attempts.find((entry) => entry.attemptId === attemptId);
      return attempt?.phase === null && attempt.process === null;
    });
    expect(existsSync(clone)).toBe(true);
    // Accepting ends the attempt, and its cleanup removes the clone.
    acceptTask(s.hub.ctx, taskId, 'user:alice');
    expect(getAttempt(s.hub.ctx, attemptId).status).toBe('ended');
    await waitFor(() => !existsSync(clone));
    await waitFor(() => runner.status().attempts.every((entry) => entry.attemptId !== attemptId));
  });

  test("a second task's agent group is SIGKILLed mid-turn: the hub ends the attempt crashed with the final WIP as the work position, and the successor's clone starts at that commit with the uncommitted file present", async () => {
    const s = await setup({
      'T-1': { turns: [[{ do: 'sleep', ms: 60_000 }]] },
      'T-2-a1': {
        turns: [
          [
            { do: 'write', path: 'src/app.ts', content: 'app, half done\n' },
            { do: 'commit', message: 'Start on the app' },
            { do: 'write', path: 'notes.txt', content: 'not committed yet\n' },
            { do: 'sleep', ms: 60_000 },
          ],
        ],
      },
    });
    const runner = await online(s);
    const first = readyTask(s.hub, 'Something else');
    const second = readyTask(s.hub, 'Finish the app');
    const started = s.hub.tick().started;
    expect(started.map((attempt) => attempt.taskId)).toEqual([first, second]);
    const attemptId = started[1]?.id as string;
    const clone = s.paths.clone(s.project, attemptId);
    await waitFor(() => existsSync(join(clone, 'notes.txt')));
    const agent = await waitFor(() => runner.status().attempts.find((entry) => entry.attemptId === attemptId)?.process);
    process.kill(-agent.pgid, 'SIGKILL');
    // The runner's final push carries the commit and the uncommitted file; the hub ends the attempt crashed there.
    const ended = await waitFor(() => {
      const attempt = getAttempt(s.hub.ctx, attemptId);
      return attempt.status === 'ended' && attempt;
    });
    expect(ended.endReason).toBe('crashed');
    // The agent wrote no handoff note: the hub assembled one, quoting the final push's commits (design 6.8).
    const notes = listTaskNotes(s.hub.ctx, second).filter((note) => note.kind === 'handoff');
    expect(notes).toEqual([expect.objectContaining({ author: 'system', attemptId })]);
    expect(notes[0]?.body).toStartWith('# Handoff note assembled by agflow');
    expect(notes[0]?.body).toContain('Start on the app');
    const wipRef = ended.wipRef as string;
    const wipSha = (await originSha(s.origin, wipRef)) as string;
    expect(await gitIn(s.origin.path, ['show', `${wipSha}:notes.txt`])).toBe('not committed yet');
    expect(getTask(s.hub.ctx, second)).toMatchObject({ status: 'ready', workRef: wipRef, workSha: wipSha });
    // The first task's agent never noticed.
    expect(getAttempt(s.hub.ctx, started[0]?.id as string).status).toBe('running');
    // A crash is an infra ending: the task waits out the first infra backoff, then the successor starts from that work
    // position.
    const backoff = (getTask(s.hub.ctx, second).nextDispatchAt as number) - s.hub.ctx.now();
    expect(backoff).toBe(s.hub.ctx.config.infraBackoffMs[0] as number);
    expect(s.hub.tick().started).toEqual([]);
    s.hub.clock.advance(backoff);
    const [successor] = s.hub.tick().started;
    expect(successor).toMatchObject({ taskId: second, startRef: wipRef, startSha: wipSha });
    const successorClone = s.paths.clone(s.project, successor?.id as string);
    await waitFor(() => getAttempt(s.hub.ctx, successor?.id as string).status === 'running');
    expect(getAttempt(s.hub.ctx, successor?.id as string).startSha).toBe(wipSha);
    expect(await gitIn(successorClone, ['rev-parse', 'HEAD'])).toBe(wipSha);
    expect(readFileSync(join(successorClone, 'notes.txt'), 'utf8')).toBe('not committed yet\n');
    expect(readFileSync(join(successorClone, 'src/app.ts'), 'utf8')).toBe('app, half done\n');
    // And with the handoff note: the successor's brief quotes it.
    expect(new AttemptStore(s.db()).get(successor?.id as string)?.spec.brief).toContain('No handoff note was written');
  });

  test("restarting the runner reconnects, replays retained events after the hub's acked position, and the hub applies none twice", async () => {
    const s = await setup({
      'T-1': {
        turns: [
          [
            { do: 'write', path: 'src/app.ts', content: 'app, tidied\n' },
            { do: 'commit', message: 'Tidy the app' },
          ],
        ],
      },
    });
    let signedIn = true;
    const first = await s.start({ credentials: () => (signedIn ? { ...s.hub.credentials } : null) });
    await waitFor(() => first.status().link === 'online');
    const runnerId = first.status().runnerId as string;
    const outbox = new Outbox(s.db());
    const taskId = readyTask(s.hub, 'Tidy the app');
    const attemptId = s.hub.tick().started[0]?.id as string;
    const clone = s.paths.clone(s.project, attemptId);
    await waitFor(() => first.status().attempts.find((entry) => entry.attemptId === attemptId)?.phase === 'idle');
    const [pushed] = await first.pushWipNow();
    const wipSha = pushed?.outcome.status === 'pushed' ? pushed.outcome.sha : null;
    await waitFor(() => getTask(s.hub.ctx, taskId).workSha === wipSha);
    await waitFor(() => hubAckedSeq(s.hub, runnerId, outbox.epoch) === outbox.lastSeq());
    const acked = outbox.lastSeq();
    const version = getRunner(s.hub.ctx, runnerId).settingsVersion;
    // The script's turn made two tool calls; the resumed session's own turn (no tool calls) may land at any time.
    const turns = () => logged(s.hub, attemptId, 'turn completed with 2');
    const applied = { wip: hubEvents(s.hub, 'attempt.wip'), turns: turns() };
    expect(applied).toEqual({ wip: 1, turns: 1 });
    // The link drops and cannot come back (the CLI is signed out); what the runner does meanwhile waits in its outbox.
    signedIn = false;
    s.hub.ctx.link.closeRunner(runnerId, 1012, 'the hub drops the link');
    await waitFor(() => first.status().link === 'needs_login');
    writeFileSync(join(clone, 'later.txt'), 'written while the hub was away\n');
    const [during] = await first.pushWipNow();
    expect(during?.outcome.status).toBe('pushed');
    expect(await first.changeSettings({ capacity: 1 })).toBe(outbox.lastSeq());
    // The service's restart: SIGTERM suspends the agents (design 6.4), and the process goes.
    const agent = first.status().attempts.find((entry) => entry.attemptId === attemptId)?.process;
    expect(await first.stopAgents('suspend', { handoff: false })).toEqual([outbox.lastSeq()]);
    await first.close();
    expect(await processIdentity(agent?.pid as number)).toBeNull();
    const unsent = outbox.eventsAfter(acked).map((event) => event.type);
    expect(unsent).toEqual(['attempt.wip', 'runner.settings', 'attempt.exited']);
    expect(hubAckedSeq(s.hub, runnerId, outbox.epoch)).toBe(acked);
    // The restarted runner says hello from the same outbox, which still holds the acknowledged events: the hub names
    // its acked position, and only what follows it is replayed.
    const welcomes: WelcomeMessage[] = [];
    const second = await s.start({ events: { welcome: (welcome) => welcomes.push(welcome) } });
    await waitFor(() => second.status().link === 'online');
    expect(welcomes[0]).toMatchObject({ runnerId, ackedSeq: acked });
    expect(new Outbox(s.db()).firstSeq()).toBeLessThan(acked);
    await waitFor(() => hubAckedSeq(s.hub, runnerId, outbox.epoch) === new Outbox(s.db()).lastSeq());
    // The local edit, kept in runner.json and replayed, made one new settings version.
    expect(getRunner(s.hub.ctx, runnerId)).toMatchObject({ capacity: 1, settingsVersion: version + 1 });
    // The hello reported the attempt suspended, and the hub resumed it at a new fence (design 6.3): the WIP and the
    // suspend's exit, replayed at the old fence, are each refused once as stale.
    expect(getAttempt(s.hub.ctx, attemptId).fence).toEqual({ epoch: 1, counter: 2 });
    expect(logged(s.hub, attemptId, 'attempt.wip at fence e1.1 ignored')).toBe(1);
    expect(logged(s.hub, attemptId, 'attempt.exited at fence e1.1 ignored')).toBe(1);
    // Nothing applied before the restart was applied again.
    expect({ wip: hubEvents(s.hub, 'attempt.wip'), turns: turns() }).toEqual(applied);
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run the tests and see them pass**

Run: `bun test packages/runner/test/integration.test.ts && bun test && bun run typecheck`
Expected: the task's tests pass; then the whole suite passes (`0 fail`) and `tsc` exits 0.

`tick()` calls `markHubAlive(ctx)` first, so a fake clock moved further than three ticks opens no recovery window. Runner leads and the housekeeping timers are off by default. `stopGraceMs` and `wipGraceMs` follow `handoffMs` and `runnerLeaseMs` unless set, and the owner is always among `allowedUsers`. The runner gets `cliVersion: fixtureCliVersion`, so the test runs where no CLI is pinned (CI's linux-x64). The fake agent submits through a tool step that runs `curl` with its own `AGFLOW_AGENT_TOKEN`. The restart scenario pins a known behaviour: a WIP push made while the link was down is refused as stale after the restart (Known behaviour 1). The 1011 regression uses a SQLite trigger to fail the runner inbox acknowledgement update and proves that both settings and acknowledgement roll back. After removing the trigger, replay applies the edit once and increments settingsVersion once. Task 7 also covers reconnect and replay at the link-client boundary.

### Task 41: HubClient for runner agents and the bridge header

The CLI's `HubClient` sends core's `BRIDGE_HEADER` with `BRIDGE_VERSION` on every request (design 10, X-19), so the hub lets this bridge claim tasks whose work position is a WIP ref. It gains the routes a runner agent's bridge needs (design 6.16): the two-phase submit and its polling, dependency preparation, staffing, stop and replace of runner agents, and the lead's handoffs and notes. A client whose bearer is an agent token never sends `X-Agflow-Agent` (design 6.5), and `HubClientError` keeps the reason of a 401 `attempt_ended`. The CLI test fixture gains `runnerAgent()`, an attempt with a minted token on its in-process hub.

**Files:**
- Modify: `packages/cli/src/hub-client.ts`
- Test: `packages/cli/test/fixture.ts`
- Test: `packages/cli/test/hub-client.test.ts`

### Task 42: agflow hook brief --runner

`agflow hook brief --runner` is the SessionStart command hook of Claude runner agents (design 10, 8.2). It reads the agent token, the hub URL, the clone and the config directory from its environment; its cwd is `<claudeHome>/agflow-empty`, an empty directory outside the clone and the base checkout that M2d gives it, and tells it nothing. It fetches `GET /api/brief`, appends 'Your working directory: <clone>' (X-17) and prints it as the session's additional context. It never reads the credentials file and never breaks the session: on any failure it prints an explanation as the context, using core's `BRIDGE_ANSWERS` for an ended or re-fenced attempt, logs to `AGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR/hook.log` and exits 0.

```diff
+/** What the brief hook of a runner agent reads, all from the environment the runner gave the agent (design 7.6). */
+const BRIEF_HOOK_ENV = ['AGFLOW_AGENT_TOKEN', 'AGFLOW_HUB_URL', 'AGFLOW_CLONE', 'AGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR'] as const;
+
+export interface RunBriefHookDeps {
+  env: Record<string, string | undefined>;
+  fetch?: FetchFn | undefined;
+}
+
+/** The context when the brief cannot be had: the hub's own answer to an attempt that must stop, or where to look. */
+function briefFailure(error: unknown, clone: string | undefined): string {
+  if (error instanceof HubClientError && error.code === 'attempt_ended') return BRIDGE_ANSWERS.attemptEnded(error.reason);
+  if (error instanceof HubClientError && error.code === 'attempt_refenced') return BRIDGE_ANSWERS.attemptRefenced;
+  const reason = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
+  const where = clone ? ` in ${clone}` : ' in your working directory';
+  return `agflow could not load your brief (${reason}). Read .agflow/run/brief.md and .agflow/run/task.md${where}; agflow tools may fail until the hub answers.`;
+}
+
+/**
+ * `agflow hook brief --runner`, the SessionStart hook of a Claude runner agent (design 10). Its cwd is
+ * `<claudeHome>/agflow-empty`, an empty directory outside the clone and the base checkout (M2d), and tells it
+ * nothing: the agent token in its environment names the attempt, and it reads no credentials file. The hub does not
+ * know the clone's path, so the hook adds AGFLOW_CLONE (X-17). Never throws: a failure becomes the context and a line
+ * of AGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR/hook.log, so the session still starts. Without AGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR nothing is logged: the
+ * default config directory is the owner's own CLI one (X-32).
+ */
+export async function runBriefHook(deps: RunBriefHookDeps): Promise<HookOutput> {
+  const { env } = deps;
+  try {
+    const missing = BRIEF_HOOK_ENV.find((name) => !env[name]);
+    if (missing) throw new Error(`${missing} is not set`);
+    const client = new HubClient({ baseUrl: env.AGFLOW_HUB_URL ?? '', token: env.AGFLOW_AGENT_TOKEN, fetch: deps.fetch, timeoutMs: 8000 });
+    const { brief } = await client.brief();
+    return withContext('SessionStart', `${brief.replace(/\n+$/, '')}\n\nYour working directory: ${env.AGFLOW_CLONE}`);
+  } catch (error) {
+    if (env.AGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR) logHookError(env.AGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR, 'brief', error);
+    return withContext('SessionStart', briefFailure(error, env.AGFLOW_CLONE));
+  }
+}

   const event = args.positional[1] ?? '';

   const role: AgentRole = args.flags.role === 'lead' ? 'lead' : 'worker';
```

### Task 43: Live claims start from the work position

Live chats continue where the last attempt left the work (design 10, 6.4, 6.14). `claim_task` and `resume_claim` read the work position from the claim answer's task (`workRef`, `workSha`), fetch it with the person's own credentials, create the task branch there and say where they started; without a position, M1's behaviour stays. The branch is named with the hub's epoch, and a recorded branch is reused only at epoch 1 or when `branchEpoch` gives the current epoch (X-28). The worktree is prepared before the claim, so a refused claim leaves nothing behind, and a newer position in the answer moves a branch this claim created.

Run: `bun test packages/cli/test/tools-git.test.ts && bun test && bun run typecheck`
Expected: the task's tests pass; then the whole suite passes (`0 fail`) and `tsc` exits 0.

An existing branch or worktree is the person's and is never moved; the answer says when it lacks the work position, with the merge command. A worktree on another branch is switched in place, keeping its commits and changes, and switched back if the hub refuses the claim. Following a newer position after a successful claim is best effort; when it fails, the answer says how to fetch it. Each claim makes one extra `GET /api/status`.

### Task 44: Runner bridge tools

The tools of a runner agent's bridge follow its role (design 10, 6.13, 7.7). Workers get the shared tools, report_progress, write_handoff, declare_blocked, declare_impossible, their own release_task, a two-phase submit and prepare_dependencies, without claim_task or resume_claim; leads get the shared and M1 lead tools plus request_agents, replace_agent, stop_agent, a lead write_handoff and get_lead_notes (X-34). submit polls the submission and answers 'submitted at', the refusal with what to fix, or 'submission pending'. Every refusal is an MCP error result, and success and pending are normal results, so adapters count a terminal tool only on success (X-19, X-33). In runner mode tools act without hello, because the token names the agent.

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { NewTaskSchema, type SubmitError } from '@agflow/core';
import { tx } from '@agflow/hub/src/context';
import { updateGoal } from '@agflow/hub/src/goal';
import { onPrepared } from '@agflow/hub/src/prepare';
import { runningWorkers } from '@agflow/hub/src/scheduler';
import { onSubmitted } from '@agflow/hub/src/submissions';
import { getTask } from '@agflow/hub/src/task-store';
import { createTasks } from '@agflow/hub/src/tasks';
import { Client } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js';
import { InMemoryTransport } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/inMemory.js';
// The runner's own list of these names, which its launches give the adapters; the CLI does not depend on the runner
// package, so the test reads its source.
import { BRIDGE_TOOL_NAMES } from '../../runner/src/adapters/bridge-tools';
import { type FetchFn, HubClient } from '../src/hub-client';
import { type RunnerToolContext, runnerLeadTools, runnerToolsFor, runnerWorkerTools } from '../src/mcp/runner-tools';
import { workerTools } from '../src/mcp/tools';
import { createMcpServer } from '../src/mcp/server';
import { HUB_URL, type HubFixture, type RunnerAgent, hubFixture } from './fixture';

const HEAD = 'a'.repeat(40);
const REMOTE = 'b'.repeat(40);

interface Bridge {
  /** Calls a tool as the agent's MCP client would: the text and whether it is an error result. */
  call(name: string, args?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<{ text: string; isError: boolean }>;
  /** GET requests to paths with this prefix, so far. */
  gets(prefix: string): number;
}

/**
 * The agent's runner bridge over MCP, served in process: the agent token as the bearer, no hello. Before the hub
 * answers the poll number `at` of a path with the prefix, decide runs, as the runner's outcome would arrive meanwhile;
 * the poll number `fail.at` finds the hub unreachable. The polls wait on a fake clock, so no test sleeps for real.
 */
async function bridgeFor(
  agent: RunnerAgent,
  options: { pollMaxMs?: number; decide?: { prefix: string; at: number; run: () => void }; fail?: { prefix: string; at: number } } = {},
): Promise<Bridge> {
  const hub = agentHub.get(agent) as HubFixture;
  const counts = new Map<string, number>();
  const fetchFn: FetchFn = async (input, init) => {
    const path = new URL(String(input)).pathname;
    if ((init?.method ?? 'GET') === 'GET') {
      for (const prefix of ['/api/submissions/', '/api/prepare/']) {
        if (!path.startsWith(prefix)) continue;
        const count = (counts.get(prefix) ?? 0) + 1;
        counts.set(prefix, count);
        if (options.fail?.prefix === prefix && options.fail.at === count) throw new Error('ECONNRESET');
        if (options.decide?.prefix === prefix && options.decide.at === count) options.decide.run();
      }
    }
    return hub.fetch(input, init);
  };
  const role = agent.attempt.role;
  const clock = { t: 0 };
  const ctx: RunnerToolContext = {
    client: new HubClient({ baseUrl: HUB_URL, token: agent.token, fetch: fetchFn }),
    state: { agentId: null, role: null },
    cwd: '/tmp',
    runner: {
      attemptId: agent.attempt.id,
      role,
      pollMs: 5,
      pollMaxMs: options.pollMaxMs ?? 5_000,
      now: () => clock.t,
      sleep: async (ms) => {
        clock.t += ms;
      },
    },
    pendingPrepareId: null,
  };
  const server = createMcpServer(ctx, runnerToolsFor(role));
  const [clientSide, serverSide] = InMemoryTransport.createLinkedPair();
  await server.connect(serverSide);
  const client = new Client({ name: 'agflow-test', version: '0.0.0' });
  await client.connect(clientSide);
  return {
    async call(name, args = {}) {
      const result = await client.callTool({ name, arguments: args });
      const content = result.content as { type: string; text: string }[];
      return { text: content.map((part) => part.text).join('\n'), isError: result.isError === true };
    },
    gets: (prefix) => counts.get(prefix) ?? 0,
  };
}

/** The hub each runner agent was made on. */
const agentHub = new WeakMap<RunnerAgent, HubFixture>();

function runnerAgent(hub: HubFixture, role: 'worker' | 'lead' = 'worker'): RunnerAgent {
  const agent = hub.runnerAgent({ role });
  agentHub.set(agent, hub);
  return agent;
}

/** The runner's attempt.submitted for the agent's pending submission, as the hub applies it. */
function submitted(hub: HubFixture, agent: RunnerAgent, outcome: { error: SubmitError | null; detail?: string | null }): void {
  const row = hub.ctx.db.query("SELECT id FROM submissions WHERE attempt_id = $attemptId AND status = 'pending'").get({ attemptId: agent.attempt.id }) as {
    id: string;
  };
  const ok = outcome.error === null;
  const data = { submissionId: row.id, ok, headSha: HEAD, remoteHead: ok ? null : REMOTE, error: outcome.error, detail: outcome.detail ?? null };
  tx(hub.ctx, (emit) => onSubmitted(hub.ctx, emit, agent.attempt.runnerId as string, agent.attempt, { attemptId: agent.attempt.id, data }));
}

/** The runner's attempt.prepared for the agent's pending request. */
function prepared(hub: HubFixture, agent: RunnerAgent, outcome: { ok: boolean; error: string | null; logTail: string | null }): void {
  const row = hub.ctx.db.query("SELECT id FROM runner_commands WHERE attempt_id = $attemptId AND kind = 'prepare_dependencies'").get({
    attemptId: agent.attempt.id,
  }) as { id: string };
  tx(hub.ctx, (emit) => onPrepared(hub.ctx, emit, agent.attempt, { requestId: row.id, ...outcome }));
}

      const answer = await bridge.call('submit', { task_id: worker.task?.id, summary: 'Done' });

      expect(answer.text).toContain(`was refused (${code}): ${detail}`);
    }
    // A refusal without the runner's detail still says what to fix.
    const bare = runnerAgent(hub);
    const bridge = await bridgeFor(bare, { decide: { prefix: '/api/submissions/', at: 1, run: () => submitted(hub, bare, { error: 'dirty' }) } });
    const answer = await bridge.call('submit', { task_id: bare.task?.id, summary: 'Done' });
    expect(answer).toEqual({ text: expect.stringContaining('uncommitted changes. Commit them'), isError: true });
  });

  test('branch_moved, remote and interrupted are error results that say the work is safe in its WIP ref', async () => {
    const hub = hubFixture();
    for (const code of ['branch_moved', 'remote', 'interrupted'] as const) {
      const worker = runnerAgent(hub);
      const bridge = await bridgeFor(worker, { decide: { prefix: '/api/submissions/', at: 1, run: () => submitted(hub, worker, { error: code, detail: 'the runner says why' }) } });
      const answer = await bridge.call('submit', { task_id: worker.task?.id, summary: 'Done' });
      expect(answer.isError).toBe(true);
      expect(answer.text).toContain(`(${code})`);
      expect(answer.text).toContain('Your work is safe in your WIP ref.');
      expect(answer.text).toContain('the runner says why');
    }
  });

  test('after the poll limit it answers the pending message as a normal result', async () => {
    const hub = hubFixture();
    const worker = runnerAgent(hub);
    const bridge = await bridgeFor(worker, { pollMaxMs: 60 });
    const answer = await bridge.call('submit', { task_id: worker.task?.id, summary: 'Done' });
    expect(answer).toEqual({
      text: expect.stringContaining('submission pending; do not submit again; the result will arrive as a message'),
      isError: false,
    });
    // pollMaxMs / pollMs polls, one every 5 ms of the fake clock.
    expect(bridge.gets('/api/submissions/')).toBe(12);
  });

  test('a poll that finds the hub unreachable leaves the submission pending, and the polls go on', async () => {
    const hub = hubFixture();
    const worker = runnerAgent(hub);
    const bridge = await bridgeFor(worker, {
      fail: { prefix: '/api/submissions/', at: 2 },
      decide: { prefix: '/api/submissions/', at: 3, run: () => submitted(hub, worker, { error: null }) },
    });
    expect(await bridge.call('submit', { task_id: worker.task?.id, summary: 'Done' })).toEqual({
      text: expect.stringContaining(`${worker.task?.id} submitted at ${HEAD}`),
      isError: false,
    });
    const unlucky = runnerAgent(hub);
    const failing = await bridgeFor(unlucky, { pollMaxMs: 10, fail: { prefix: '/api/submissions/', at: 2 } });
    expect(await failing.call('submit', { task_id: unlucky.task?.id, summary: 'Done' })).toEqual({
      text: expect.stringContaining('submission pending; do not submit again'),
      isError: false,
    });
  });
});

describe('prepare_dependencies', () => {
  test('polls its request and reports the outcome and the log tail', async () => {
    const hub = hubFixture();
    const worker = runnerAgent(hub);
    const done = { ok: true, error: null, logTail: 'bun install v1.3.11\n3 packages installed' };
    const bridge = await bridgeFor(worker, { decide: { prefix: '/api/prepare/', at: 2, run: () => prepared(hub, worker, done) } });
    const answer = await bridge.call('prepare_dependencies');
    expect(answer).toEqual({ text: expect.stringContaining('The dependencies are prepared'), isError: false });
    expect(answer.text).toContain('> bun install v1.3.11\n> 3 packages installed');
    expect(bridge.gets('/api/prepare/')).toBe(2);

    const failing = runnerAgent(hub);
    const failed = { ok: false, error: 'bun install exited with code 1', logTail: 'error: lockfile had changes' };
    const again = await bridgeFor(failing, { decide: { prefix: '/api/prepare/', at: 1, run: () => prepared(hub, failing, failed) } });
    const refused = await again.call('prepare_dependencies');
    expect(refused.isError).toBe(true);
    expect(refused.text).toContain('failed: bun install exited with code 1');
    expect(refused.text).toContain('> error: lockfile had changes');

    const slow = runnerAgent(hub);
    const slowBridge = await bridgeFor(slow, { pollMaxMs: 40 });
    const requestsOf = () =>
      hub.ctx.db.query("SELECT id FROM runner_commands WHERE attempt_id = $id AND kind = 'prepare_dependencies'").all({ id: slow.attempt.id }) as {
        id: string;
      }[];
    const pending = await slowBridge.call('prepare_dependencies');
    const [request] = requestsOf();
    expect(pending).toEqual({ text: expect.stringContaining(`${request?.id} is still running`), isError: false });
    expect(pending.text).toContain('that call starts no new preparation');
    // Asked again while it runs: the same request.
    expect(await slowBridge.call('prepare_dependencies')).toEqual({ text: expect.stringContaining(`${request?.id} is still running`), isError: false });
    // Once it has failed, the next call reports that, and asks for no second preparation.
    prepared(hub, slow, { ok: false, error: 'lockfile mismatch', logTail: null });
    expect(await slowBridge.call('prepare_dependencies')).toEqual({ text: `The dependency preparation ${request?.id} failed: lockfile mismatch.`, isError: true });
    expect(requestsOf()).toEqual([{ id: request?.id as string }]);
  });
});
```

```ts
// The tools of a runner agent's bridge, `agflow mcp --runner` (design 10, 6.13, 7.7). AGFLOW_ROLE chooses the set: a
// worker's task is assigned, so it has no claim_task or resume_claim, and submits in two phases, the runner pushing
// for it; a lead gets M1's lead tools and the staffing tools, and submits nothing. The agent token names the agent, so
// no tool waits for hello. Every refusal is an error result; success and the pending answers are normal results, as
// adapters count a terminal tool only on a normal result (X-19).
import {
  AgentIdSchema,
  type AgentRole,
  FIXABLE_SUBMIT_ERRORS,
  type PrepareRequest,
  StaffingInputSchema,
  type SubmissionRecord,
  type SubmitError,
  TaskIdSchema,
  VendorSchema,
  quoteLines,
  splitSubmitError,
} from '@agflow/core';
import { z } from 'zod';
import { HubClientError } from '../hub-client';
import { type ToolContext, type ToolDef, ToolError, asAgent, defineTool, leadTools, sharedTools, workerTools } from './tools';

/** What the runner tells its bridge through the agent environment. */
export interface RunnerBridgeSettings {
  /** AGFLOW_ATTEMPT_ID */
  attemptId: string;
  /** AGFLOW_ROLE */
  role: AgentRole;
  /** AGFLOW_BRIDGE_POLL_MS: how often submit and prepare_dependencies ask the hub how their request went. */
  pollMs: number;
  /** AGFLOW_BRIDGE_POLL_MAX_MS: how long they ask before they answer that it is still pending. */
  pollMaxMs: number;
  /** The polls' clock and wait: performance.now and Bun.sleep unless a test passes its own. */
  now?: (() => number) | undefined;
  sleep?: ((ms: number) => Promise<void>) | undefined;
}

export interface RunnerToolContext extends ToolContext {
  runner: RunnerBridgeSettings;
  /**
   * The preparation prepare_dependencies last answered as still running, until a later call reports how it went: the
   * hub hands back only a pending request, and never sends a preparation's outcome as a message.
   */
  pendingPrepareId: string | null;
}

/** A tool's context in runner mode; every runner tool is served in runner mode only. */
function runnerContext(ctx: ToolContext): RunnerToolContext {
  if (!(ctx as Partial<RunnerToolContext>).runner) throw new ToolError('This agflow tool is for agents on a runner only.');
  return ctx as RunnerToolContext;
}

/** A poll's failure that the next poll may not meet: the hub unreachable for a moment, or a server error. */
const isTransient = (error: unknown): boolean => error instanceof HubClientError && (error.code === 'unreachable' || error.status >= 500);

/**
 * Asks until the answer is decided or pollMaxMs has passed: the decided answer, or null when it is still pending. The
 * request is made by then, so a poll that fails for a moment leaves it pending rather than failing the tool; the hub's
 * refusals (an ended attempt, say) still end the tool at once.
 */
async function pollUntilDecided<T>(ask: () => Promise<T>, decided: (answer: T) => boolean, runner: RunnerBridgeSettings): Promise<T | null> {
  const now = runner.now ?? (() => performance.now());
  const sleep = runner.sleep ?? ((ms: number) => Bun.sleep(ms));
  const deadline = now() + runner.pollMaxMs;
  while (now() < deadline) {
    await sleep(Math.min(runner.pollMs, Math.max(0, deadline - now())));
    let answer: T;
    try {
      answer = await ask();
    } catch (error) {
      if (isTransient(error)) continue;
      throw error;
    }
    if (decided(answer)) return answer;
  }
  return null;
}

const SUBMISSION_PENDING = 'submission pending; do not submit again; the result will arrive as a message';

type FixableSubmitError = (typeof FIXABLE_SUBMIT_ERRORS)[number];

/** Core's list of the refusals the agent fixes, the one the hub's messages follow too. */
const isFixable = (code: SubmitError | null): code is FixableSubmitError => (FIXABLE_SUBMIT_ERRORS as readonly (string | null)[]).includes(code);

/** What the agent does about a refusal it can fix, when the runner sent no detail that says so. */
const FIX_BY_CODE: Record<FixableSubmitError, string> = {
  dirty: 'the clone has uncommitted changes. Commit them, or remove what does not belong in the submission, then submit again.',
  protected_paths:
    'your commits change protected paths, which agents may not change. Revert them to the versions your branch started from, or merge main if main changed them, then submit again.',
  needs_merge: 'someone added commits to the task branch on top of agflow work. Run `git fetch origin && git merge origin/<your branch>`, resolve any conflicts, then submit again.',
};

const SAFE_WORK = 'Your work is safe in your WIP ref. You may submit again, or call declare_blocked.';

/**
 * A failed submission as the agent reads it. A refusal it can fix passes the runner's detail on unchanged, as it
 * already says what to fix; any other failure says the work is safe. The hub's own words (an ended attempt) are quoted
 * as they came.
 */
export function submissionRefusal(submission: SubmissionRecord): string {
  const { code, detail } = splitSubmitError(submission.error ?? '');
  const which = `Your submission ${submission.id} of ${submission.taskId}`;
  if (isFixable(code)) return `${which} was refused (${code}): ${detail ?? FIX_BY_CODE[code]}`;
  switch (code) {
    case 'branch_moved':
      return (
        `${which} was refused (branch_moved): the task branch moved outside agflow. The task is blocked for people, and agflow stops this attempt: write a handoff note. ` +
        `Your work is safe in your WIP ref.${detail ? ` The runner said: ${detail}` : ''}`
      );
    case 'remote':
    case 'interrupted': {
      const why = code === 'interrupted' ? 'a stop or hold interrupted its push' : 'the runner could not push it';
      return `${which} failed (${code}): ${why}. ${SAFE_WORK}${detail ? ` The runner said: ${detail}` : ''}`;
    }
    case null:
      return `${which} failed: ${detail ?? 'no reason given'}. ${SAFE_WORK}`;
  }
}

/** A finished preparation's log tail, quoted: the package manager's output is not agflow's words. */
const logTailOf = (request: PrepareRequest): string => (request.logTail ? `\nThe end of its log:\n${quoteLines(request.logTail)}` : '');

const runnerHello = defineTool(
  'hello',
  'Not needed on a runner: this chat is already connected to agflow.',
  { code: z.string().max(20).optional() },
  async (_args, ctx) =>
    `You are already connected to agflow as attempt ${runnerContext(ctx).runner.attemptId}; there is no hello to do. Use get_brief to read your brief again.`,
);

const submit = defineTool(
  'submit',
  'Submit your task for review once every change is committed in your working directory. The runner pushes the task branch for you; wait for the answer, and do not submit again while it is pending.',
  {
    task_id: TaskIdSchema,
    summary: z.string().min(1).max(8000),
    evidence: z.array(z.string().min(1).max(2000)).max(50).optional(),
  },
  async ({ task_id, summary, evidence }, ctx) => {
    const { runner } = runnerContext(ctx);
    const client = asAgent(ctx);
    const { submission } = await client.submitWork(task_id, { summary, evidence: evidence ?? [] });
    const decided =
      submission.status === 'pending'
        ? (await pollUntilDecided(() => client.submission(submission.id), (answer) => answer.submission.status !== 'pending', runner))?.submission
        : submission;
    if (!decided) return `${SUBMISSION_PENDING} (${submission.id} of ${task_id}).`;
    if (decided.status === 'failed') throw new ToolError(submissionRefusal(decided));
    return `${decided.taskId} submitted at ${decided.headSha ?? 'an unknown commit'} (${decided.id}). The lead will review it; your work on it is done, so end your turn.`;
  },
);

const prepareDependencies = defineTool(
  'prepare_dependencies',
  "Ask the runner to install the project's dependencies into your working directory, as the project's .agflow/config.json says. Use it after you change a dependency manifest or lockfile; you have no network to install them yourself.",
  {},
  async (_args, ctx) => {
    const bridge = runnerContext(ctx);
    const client = asAgent(ctx);
    // A preparation answered as still running is reported before another is asked for.
    const earlier = bridge.pendingPrepareId;
    bridge.pendingPrepareId = null;
    const { request } = earlier ? await client.prepareRequest(earlier) : await client.requestPrepare();
    const decided =
      request.status === 'pending'
        ? (await pollUntilDecided(() => client.prepareRequest(request.id), (answer) => answer.request.status !== 'pending', bridge.runner))?.request
        : request;
    if (!decided) {
      bridge.pendingPrepareId = request.id;
      return `The dependency preparation ${request.id} is still running. Call prepare_dependencies again later to hear how it went; that call starts no new preparation.`;
    }
    if (decided.status === 'failed') {
      throw new ToolError(`The dependency preparation ${decided.id} failed: ${decided.error ?? 'no reason given'}.${logTailOf(decided)}`);
    }
    return `The dependencies are prepared (${decided.id}).${logTailOf(decided)}`;
  },
);

const requestAgents = defineTool(
  'request_agents',
  "Lead: set how many workers agflow runs on runners, of any vendor, and why; agflow caps it at the project's limit, and 0 stops new starts without pausing the project. vendor names the vendor new workers prefer for the next hour.",
  { count: StaffingInputSchema.shape.count, vendor: VendorSchema.optional(), reason: z.string().min(1).max(4000) },
  async ({ count, vendor, reason }, ctx) => {
    const { running, target } = await asAgent(ctx).staffing({ count, vendor, reason });
    return `The target is ${target} runner worker(s); ${running} running now.${vendor ? ` New workers prefer ${vendor} for the next hour.` : ''}`;
  },
);

const stopAgent = defineTool(
  'stop_agent',
  'Lead: stop a worker running on a runner. It writes a handoff note first; with hold, its task waits for people instead of going to the next worker.',
  { agent_id: AgentIdSchema, reason: z.string().min(1).max(4000), hold: z.boolean().optional() },
  async ({ agent_id, reason, hold }, ctx) => {
    const { attempt } = await asAgent(ctx).stopAgent(agent_id, { reason, hold: hold ?? false });
    const held = hold ? ', and its task is held for people' : '';
    const deferred = attempt.stopRequested?.deferred ? ' It waits until the submission it has pending is decided.' : '';
    return `Asked agflow to stop ${agent_id} (attempt ${attempt.id})${held}.${deferred}`;
  },
);

const replaceAgent = defineTool(
  'replace_agent',
  'Lead: replace a worker running on a runner with a fresh one, which continues from its handoff note and work.',
  { agent_id: AgentIdSchema, reason: z.string().min(1).max(4000) },
  async ({ agent_id, reason }, ctx) => {
    const { attempt } = await asAgent(ctx).replaceAgent(agent_id, reason);
    const deferred = attempt.stopRequested?.deferred ? ' It waits until the submission it has pending is decided.' : '';
    return `Asked agflow to replace ${agent_id} (attempt ${attempt.id}).${deferred}`;
  },
);

/**
 * The hub takes a handoff note on a task only from the task's holder (design 6.5), and a lead holds no task, so the
 * lead's handoff goes to the lead notes only. A task_id gets a refusal that says where a note on a task goes, rather
 * than a lead handoff the lead did not mean.
 */
const leadHandoff = defineTool(
  'write_handoff',
  "Leave your lead handoff for the next lead: the plan's state, decisions, what you are waiting for, the next step. A lead holds no task, so task_id is refused: for a note on a task, use send_message to \"task:T-<n>\".",
  { note: z.string().min(1).max(16_000), task_id: TaskIdSchema.optional() },
  async ({ note, task_id }, ctx) => {
    if (task_id) {
      throw new ToolError(
        `A lead's handoff goes on no task: nothing was saved. Call write_handoff without task_id for your lead handoff, or send_message to "task:${task_id}" for a note on ${task_id}.`,
      );
    }
    await asAgent(ctx).leadHandoff(note);
    return 'Lead handoff saved; the next lead reads it.';
  },
);

/**
 * M1's release_task answers that the task is ready again. A runner attempt's release only asks agflow to stop it: the
 * task goes back to ready once the agent has stopped (design 6.4).
 */
const runnerRelease = defineTool(
  'release_task',
  'Give your task back so someone else can take it. agflow then stops this attempt.',
  { task_id: TaskIdSchema, reason: z.string().min(1).max(4000) },
  async ({ task_id, reason }, ctx) => {
    await asAgent(ctx).release(task_id, reason);
    return `Released ${task_id}: agflow stops this attempt, and the task goes back to ready once it has stopped. End your turn.`;
  },
);

const getLeadNotes = defineTool('get_lead_notes', "Lead: the lead notes, newest first: earlier leads' handoffs and restatements.", {}, async (_args, ctx) => {
  const { notes } = await asAgent(ctx).leadNotes();
  if (notes.length === 0) return 'No lead notes yet.';
  return notes.map((note) => `[${note.kind}] by ${note.author} at ${new Date(note.createdAt).toISOString()}:\n${quoteLines(note.body)}`).join('\n\n');
});

const byName = (tools: ToolDef[], names: readonly string[]): ToolDef[] =>
  names.map((name) => {
    const tool = tools.find((candidate) => candidate.name === name);
    if (!tool) throw new Error(`no agflow tool ${name}`);
    return tool;
  });

/** The shared tools, with hello answering that the chat is connected already. */
const runnerShared: ToolDef[] = sharedTools.map((tool) => (tool.name === 'hello' ? runnerHello : tool));

const WORKER_TOOLS = ['report_progress', 'write_handoff', 'declare_blocked', 'declare_impossible'] as const;

/** A runner worker's tools (design 10): no claim_task or resume_claim, a release that stops the attempt, and a submit the runner pushes. */
export const runnerWorkerTools: ToolDef[] = [...runnerShared, ...byName(workerTools, WORKER_TOOLS), runnerRelease, submit, prepareDependencies];

/** A runner lead's tools (design 10): M1's lead tools and the staffing ones; no claim, resume or submit. */
export const runnerLeadTools: ToolDef[] = [...runnerShared, ...leadTools, requestAgents, replaceAgent, stopAgent, leadHandoff, getLeadNotes];

/** The tools AGFLOW_ROLE chooses. */
export function runnerToolsFor(role: AgentRole): ToolDef[] {
  return role === 'lead' ? runnerLeadTools : runnerWorkerTools;
}
```

Run: `bun test packages/cli/test/runner-tools.test.ts && bun test && bun run typecheck`
Expected: the task's tests pass; then the whole suite passes (`0 fail`) and `tsc` exits 0.

Refusals are read with core's `splitSubmitError` and classified with `FIXABLE_SUBMIT_ERRORS`. Polls treat an unreachable hub or a 5xx as not decided yet. prepare_dependencies remembers a pending request and asks about it on the next call instead of starting another. A lead's write_handoff with a `task_id` is refused with an error result that names `send_message` to `task:T-n`, because the hub takes a task's handoff note only from its holder (see Decisions). The test also checks that `runnerToolsFor(role)` serves exactly the runner's `BRIDGE_TOOL_NAMES[role]` (Task 23) for both roles, in any order, so a new or renamed tool changes both in one commit; it imports the runner source by relative path, so `packages/cli/package.json` is unchanged.

### Task 45: agflow mcp --runner

`agflow mcp --vendor claude|codex --runner` is the bridge's runner mode (design 10, 6.5), selected only by the flag. At startup it exits non-zero naming every missing variable of `REQUIRED_RUNNER_ENV` (`AGFLOW_AGENT_TOKEN`, `AGFLOW_HUB_URL`, `AGFLOW_ATTEMPT_ID`, `AGFLOW_ROLE`, `AGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR`), reads no credentials file and makes no hub call; then it serves the runner tools for its role. Hub answers become core's `BRIDGE_ANSWERS` as MCP error results (X-19): 401 `attempt_ended` with the hub's reason, 401 `attempt_refenced`, and an unreachable hub in every mode. The help lists both runner forms. The runner starts the bridge and Claude's brief hook outside the vendor sandbox, so agflow must load no `bunfig.toml` (whose preload runs code) and no `.env` from its working directory: M1's `selfCommand` source form becomes `bun --no-env-file --config=/dev/null <repo>/packages/cli/src/main.ts`, and the root `build:cli` script compiles with `--no-compile-autoload-bunfig --no-compile-autoload-dotenv`.
