```ts
import { afterEach, describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { mkdtempSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { BRIDGE_ANSWERS } from '@agflow/core';
import { updateAttempt } from '@agflow/hub/src/attempt-store';
import { Client } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js';
import { StdioClientTransport } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/stdio.js';
import { saveCredentials } from '../src/credentials';
import { REQUIRED_RUNNER_ENV } from '../src/mcp/server';
import { runnerLeadTools, runnerWorkerTools } from '../src/mcp/runner-tools';
import { type HubFixture, type RunnerAgent, hubFixture } from './fixture';

const MAIN = join(import.meta.dir, '..', 'src', 'main.ts');

/** This process's environment without the agflow variables, so a test sets exactly the ones it means. */
const baseEnv = (): Record<string, string> =>
  Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(process.env).filter((entry): entry is [string, string] => entry[1] !== undefined && !entry[0].startsWith('AGFLOW_')));

const cleanups: (() => Promise<void> | void)[] = [];
afterEach(async () => {
  for (const cleanup of cleanups.splice(0).reverse()) await cleanup();
});

interface ServedHub {
  hub: HubFixture;
  url: string;
  /** The requests the hub received, as 'METHOD /path'. */
  requests: string[];
}

/** The fixture's hub on a real port, counting the requests it gets. */
function serveHub(): ServedHub {
  const hub = hubFixture();
  const requests: string[] = [];
  const server = Bun.serve({
    port: 0,
    fetch: (request) => {
      requests.push(`${request.method} ${new URL(request.url).pathname}`);
      return hub.app.fetch(request);
    },
  });
  cleanups.push(() => server.stop(true));
  return { hub, url: `http://localhost:${server.port}`, requests };
}

/** A port nothing listens on. */
function closedPortUrl(): string {
  const server = Bun.serve({ port: 0, fetch: () => new Response() });
  const url = `http://localhost:${server.port}`;
  server.stop(true);
  return url;
}

/** The variables a runner gives the bridge of the agent's attempt. */
function runnerEnv(agent: RunnerAgent, hubUrl: string, configDir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'agflow-run-config-'))): Record<string, string> {
  return {
    AGFLOW_AGENT_TOKEN: agent.token,
    AGFLOW_HUB_URL: hubUrl,
    AGFLOW_ATTEMPT_ID: agent.attempt.id,
    AGFLOW_ROLE: agent.attempt.role,
    AGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR: configDir,
    AGFLOW_BRIDGE_POLL_MS: '10',
    AGFLOW_BRIDGE_POLL_MAX_MS: '1000',
  };
}

/** `agflow mcp` over stdio with these arguments and agflow variables. */
async function bridge(args: string[], env: Record<string, string>): Promise<Client> {
  const transport = new StdioClientTransport({ command: process.execPath, args: [MAIN, 'mcp', ...args], env: { ...baseEnv(), ...env }, stderr: 'ignore' });
  const client = new Client({ name: 'agflow-test', version: '0.0.0' });
  await client.connect(transport);
  cleanups.push(() => client.close());
  return client;
}

/** A tool call's text and whether it is an error result. */
async function call(client: Client, name: string, args: Record<string, unknown> = {}): Promise<{ text: string; isError: boolean }> {
  const result = await client.callTool({ name, arguments: args });
  const text = (result.content as { text: string }[]).map((part) => part.text).join('\n');
  return { text, isError: result.isError === true };
}

describe('agflow mcp --runner', () => {
  test('lists the worker or the lead tools according to AGFLOW_ROLE; without --runner the live bridge still lists its 27 tools, whatever the environment', async () => {
    const { hub, url } = serveHub();
    const names = async (client: Client) => (await client.listTools()).tools.map((tool) => tool.name);
    const worker = await bridge(['--vendor', 'claude', '--runner'], runnerEnv(hub.runnerAgent(), url));
    expect(await names(worker)).toEqual(runnerWorkerTools.map((tool) => tool.name));
    const lead = await bridge(['--vendor', 'codex', '--runner'], runnerEnv(hub.runnerAgent({ role: 'lead' }), url));
    expect(await names(lead)).toEqual(runnerLeadTools.map((tool) => tool.name));
    // Every runner variable, but no --runner: the runner mode is never inferred from the environment (design 10).
    const liveDir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'agflow-cfg-'));
    saveCredentials({ hubUrl: url, token: hub.tokenFor('alice'), user: 'alice' }, liveDir);
    const live = await bridge(['--vendor', 'claude'], { ...runnerEnv(hub.runnerAgent(), url), AGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR: liveDir });
    const liveNames = await names(live);
    expect(liveNames).toHaveLength(27);
    expect(liveNames).toContain('claim_task');
    expect(liveNames).not.toContain('request_agents');
    // M1's hello, which asks the hub about the code, not the runner's "already connected".
    const hello = await call(live, 'hello', { code: 'ZZZZZZ' });
    expect(hello.isError).toBe(true);
    expect(hello.text).toStartWith('agflow hub: ');
  }, 30_000);

  test('each missing required variable makes the process exit non-zero and name it', async () => {
    const { hub, url } = serveHub();
    const env = runnerEnv(hub.runnerAgent(), url);
    expect(REQUIRED_RUNNER_ENV).toEqual(['AGFLOW_AGENT_TOKEN', 'AGFLOW_HUB_URL', 'AGFLOW_ATTEMPT_ID', 'AGFLOW_ROLE', 'AGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR']);
    const runs = REQUIRED_RUNNER_ENV.map(async (name) => {
      const { [name]: _missing, ...rest } = env;
      const child = Bun.spawn([process.execPath, MAIN, 'mcp', '--vendor', 'claude', '--runner'], {
        env: { ...baseEnv(), ...rest },
        stdin: 'pipe',
        stdout: 'pipe',
        stderr: 'pipe',
      });
      const code = await child.exited;
      return { name, code, stderr: await new Response(child.stderr).text() };
    });
    for (const { name, code, stderr } of await Promise.all(runs)) {
      expect({ name, failed: code !== 0 }).toEqual({ name, failed: true });
      expect(stderr).toContain(name);
    }
    const child = Bun.spawn([process.execPath, MAIN, 'mcp', '--vendor', 'claude', '--runner'], {
      env: { ...baseEnv(), ...env, AGFLOW_ROLE: 'boss' },
      stdin: 'pipe',
      stderr: 'pipe',
    });
    expect(await child.exited).not.toBe(0);
    expect(await new Response(child.stderr).text()).toContain('AGFLOW_ROLE');
  }, 30_000);

  test('a credentials.json in AGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR is never read, and the hub receives no request until a tool is called', async () => {
    const served = serveHub();
    const other = serveHub();
    const configDir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'agflow-run-config-'));
    // The owner's sign-in to another hub, as if it had leaked into the attempt's config directory.
    saveCredentials({ hubUrl: other.url, token: other.hub.tokenFor('alice'), user: 'alice' }, configDir);
    const worker = served.hub.runnerAgent();
    const client = await bridge(['--vendor', 'claude', '--runner'], runnerEnv(worker, served.url, configDir));
    await client.listTools();
    expect(served.requests).toEqual([]);
    expect(await call(client, 'list_tasks')).toEqual({ text: expect.stringContaining(worker.task?.id as string), isError: false });
    expect(served.requests).toEqual(['GET /api/tasks']);
    expect(other.requests).toEqual([]);
  }, 30_000);

  test("hello answers 'already connected'", async () => {
    const { hub, url, requests } = serveHub();
    const client = await bridge(['--vendor', 'claude', '--runner'], runnerEnv(hub.runnerAgent(), url));
    expect(await call(client, 'hello', { code: 'ABC234' })).toEqual({ text: expect.stringContaining('already connected'), isError: false });
    expect(requests).toEqual([]);
  }, 30_000);

  test('401 attempt_ended answers with the hub reason, attempt_refenced the restarting text, and an unreachable hub the unreachable text in runner and live modes, each as an error result', async () => {
    const { hub, url } = serveHub();
    const ended = hub.runnerAgent();
    const endedBridge = await bridge(['--vendor', 'claude', '--runner'], runnerEnv(ended, url));
    updateAttempt(hub.ctx, ended.attempt.id, { status: 'ended', endReason: 'stopped', endedAt: hub.ctx.now() });
    expect(await call(endedBridge, 'list_tasks')).toEqual({ text: BRIDGE_ANSWERS.attemptEnded('stopped'), isError: true });
    expect(await call(endedBridge, 'submit', { task_id: ended.task?.id, summary: 'Done' })).toEqual({
      text: BRIDGE_ANSWERS.attemptEnded('stopped'),
      isError: true,
    });

    const refenced = hub.runnerAgent();
    const refencedBridge = await bridge(['--vendor', 'claude', '--runner'], runnerEnv(refenced, url));
    hub.ctx.db.run('UPDATE project SET epoch = 2');
    expect(await call(refencedBridge, 'check_inbox')).toEqual({ text: BRIDGE_ANSWERS.attemptRefenced, isError: true });

    const nowhere = closedPortUrl();
    const unreachable = await bridge(['--vendor', 'claude', '--runner'], runnerEnv(hubFixture().runnerAgent(), nowhere));
    expect(await call(unreachable, 'get_brief')).toEqual({ text: BRIDGE_ANSWERS.hubUnreachable, isError: true });
    const liveDir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'agflow-cfg-'));
    saveCredentials({ hubUrl: nowhere, token: 'cli_token', user: 'alice' }, liveDir);
    const live = await bridge(['--vendor', 'claude'], { AGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR: liveDir });
    expect(await call(live, 'list_tasks')).toEqual({ text: BRIDGE_ANSWERS.hubUnreachable, isError: true });
  }, 30_000);
});
```

## After the last task

### What works now

- A runner built with `createRunner` and the fake adapter links to the M2a hub over `/api/runner/ws`, says hello with its confirmed settings, vendors, profile, git readiness and recovered attempts, and runs every command of protocol 1. Its events wait in the outbox until the hub acknowledges them and are replayed after each welcome; its commands are journaled, so a resend joins or repeats the first run.
- Attempts run end to end: admission, a clone of the project's vault at the task's work position, the agent launched with an allowlisted environment, its brief and the bridge, WIP pushes under `canPushWip`, two-phase submissions, stops with handoff turns, holds, the runner's own stops and suspends, continuations, vendor-error retries, quota waits and the outage nudge, resumes at a new fence, take-over and hand-back, and cleanup.
- The runner never runs git with an agent's `.git`. Harvests go through a quarantine with `fsck`, uncommitted work becomes a snapshot commit, protected paths are restored, detected and stripped against the restore base, and every push is fenced. Work that cannot reach the WIP ref lands on a late-work ref, and stays recorded in runner.db until it has, across restarts and cleanups.
- The runner survives crashes and outages: a start-up kill and sweep of what the previous run left, the awake clock that leaves sleep out of every age, `needs_login` with credential re-reads, and the outbox replay. Task 40 shows it against the in-process hub: placement, WIP, submit, hold, accept, cleanup, a killed agent and its successor, a restart that replays without duplicates, and a whole events transaction failure that rolls back, closes with 1011 and replays from the acknowledged position with exactly one settings application.
- Settings edits made on the laptop (drain, undrain, a hand edit while the runner is down) and the owner's edits in the browser both survive, through echoes, refusals, reconnects and a restored hub, within the limits of Known behaviour 3. A seeded model checks the rule against M2a's.
- The bridge has its runner mode: `agflow mcp --vendor claude|codex --runner` with tools by role, the two-phase submit and core's answers as error results; `agflow hook brief --runner`; and live claims that start from the task's work position, with epoch-aware branch names and `X-Agflow-Bridge: 2`. agflow, from source or compiled, loads no `bunfig.toml` or `.env` from its working directory.

### How to run it

- The whole suite: `bun test && bun run typecheck`. The runner and testkit alone: `bun test packages/runner packages/testkit`.
- The runner against M2a's hub in process: `bun test packages/runner/test/integration.test.ts`. The settings sync model: `bun test packages/runner/test/settings-model.test.ts`. A failure names its seed: `MODEL_SEED=<n> MODEL_SEEDS=1` runs that one again, `MODEL_SEEDS=4000` runs more, and `MODEL_LOG` sets how many steps of a failing run's log show (60).
- The bridge in runner mode, as a runner starts it: `AGFLOW_AGENT_TOKEN=<agt_ token> AGFLOW_HUB_URL=<hub> AGFLOW_ATTEMPT_ID=<id> AGFLOW_ROLE=worker AGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR=<dir> bun --no-env-file --config=/dev/null packages/cli/src/main.ts mcp --vendor claude --runner`. With `AGFLOW_CLONE` also set, the same command with `hook brief --runner` in place of `mcp --vendor claude --runner` prints the runner brief as a SessionStart context. `bun run build:cli` builds `dist/agflow` with the same protection.
- There is no `agflow runner` command yet: plan M2c adds setup, start and the service around `createRunner`. The nine root scripts of M2c, M2d and M2e exist, and fail until their plans add the files they name.

### What the next plans build on

Other plans import these by name. After gate G2 (Task 39) a change to them needs a recorded decision and updates every importer in the same commit. The final chain builds each plan on the complete preceding plan; M2c starts at M2b `1a08041`. The gates describe interface availability within the plan; the contracts below apply to the complete chain.

If either fails, log, drop the link with normal backoff and return before commands or replay; the epoch remains unrecorded so the next welcome retries. Successful restore bookkeeping still reconnects immediately.
- **Configuration and layout:** `RunnerConfigSchema`, `RunnerConfig`, `RunnerTimings`, `loadRunnerConfig`, `saveRunnerConfig`, `isTestMode`, `vendorHomes`, `CONNECTIVITY_VARS`, `DEFAULT_TIMINGS`, and the settings rules `settingsOf`, `localSettingsEdits`, `localSettingsOf`, `editLocalSettings`, `settingsAfterEdits`, `applySettingsEcho(config, echo, { before, after })` and `isWholeSettings(settings, snapshot)` (`config.ts`); `SettingsSync` and `SettingsSyncOptions` (`settings-sync.ts`: `view`, `echo(update, arrivedAfter?)` giving false when the echo waits, `probeUnanswered`, `resent`, `welcomed({ ackedSeq })`, `change`); `runnerPaths`, `RunnerPaths` (with `agentTools`), `projectKey`, `agflowHome` and `makeAttemptTmpDir` (`paths.ts`); `VENDOR_PINS`, `vendorPlatform`, `vendorBinary` and `parseVendorVersion` (`vendor/pins.ts`), to which M2c adds integrity and the installer.
  - Whole settings must name every vendor the confirmed snapshot's per-vendor records hold. A vendor missing from the hub's record would stop its whole settings counting as whole; today that cannot happen, since the hub stores what the runner reported and merges vendor by vendor. If runner.json ever gains a vendor by migration (M2c), add it through a `runner.settings` edit, not straight into `confirmedSettings`.
  - `SettingsSyncOptions.saveConfig` (and the executor's): `config()` must give the new settings even when the write throws; `runner.ts` sets its config before it writes.
- **The agent environment:** `buildAgentEnv`, `userVariables` (M2e's Codex process options call it instead of keeping their own list) and `bridgeEnvOf` (`env.ts`); `PermissionProfile`, `standardProfile`, `profileOf`, `DeniedPath`, `deniedReadPaths` and `deniedWritePaths` (`profile.ts`); `writeRunDir`, `runDirOf`, `withWorkingDirectory` and `removeAgentTools` (`run-dir.ts`).
  - `writeRunDir` makes `paths.agentTools(project, attempt)`, `vaults/<project>.agent/<attempt>/`, read-only (directories 0555). Whatever deletes an `AGFLOW_HOME` or its `vaults/` must first call `removeAgentTools` on each `vaults/<project>.agent/<attempt>` (or make those directories writable); a plain recursive rm fails with EACCES. That covers M2c's `uninstall --purge` and retention, test cleanups that do not use `fixture.ts` or `runner-setup.ts`, M2d Task 24's and M2e Task 21's harnesses, and M2g's runner homes.
- **Git and processes:** `runGit`, `localGitEnv`, `remoteGitEnv` and `agentGitEnv` (`git/run.ts`); `Vault` with `acquireBaseCheckout`, `consolidate` and `withLock` (`git/vault.ts`); `createTaskClone` and `createLeadClone` (`git/clone.ts`); `resolveRestoreBase` and `restoreProtected` (`git/protect.ts`): M2b's controller resolves the base and passes it to M2c as `PrepareInput.baseSha`; M2c calls `restoreProtected` and `removeInClone`, not `resolveRestoreBase`. `restoreProtected` resolves a link at the clone path, so callers validate that path first; links inside the clone are not followed; `pushRefs`, `pushLateWork` and `deleteRefsFenced` (`git/push.ts`); `processIdentity`, `sameProcess`, `killGroup`, `drainToLog`, `boundedWait`, `listProcesses`, `parsePs`, `PsRow`, `PS_COLUMNS`, `PS_ENV` and `parseLsofCwds` (`processes.ts`; M2g reuses the parsers, X-42, and its rows and lstart match `processIdentity` only when `ps` runs with `PS_COLUMNS` under `PS_ENV`); `runStopLadder` and `killAndSweep` (`stop-ladder.ts`); `killRegisteredGroups`, `recoverOnStart` and `liveAttemptsForHello` (`recovery.ts`; M2c's uninstall uses the first).

- **Test entry points:**

M2c, M2d and M2e use it.

Keep portable cases enabled on Linux; macOS-only cases use test.skipIf(process.platform !== 'darwin') with the reason ‘the runner supports darwin-arm64 only; design 7.1’. Never omit individual safety assertions or return early because lsof is missing on macOS. Keep other cases platform-neutral: `exec <cmd>` for a tool's group leader, since dash does not exec a lone command, and events awaited instead of read at once.

The `@agflow/testkit` entry exports `FakeScript`, `OriginRepo`, `RefusingProxy` and `RefusedRequest`; the proxy types are also imported directly from `packages/testkit/src/refusing-proxy.ts`.

M2d's Claude MCP config and M2e's Codex config start `agflow mcp --vendor <v> --runner` with `launch.bridge`, and M2d's SessionStart hook runs `agflow hook brief --runner` (`runBriefHook` in `hooks.ts`). `runner-tools.test.ts` checks that `runnerToolsFor(role)` names equal `BRIDGE_TOOL_NAMES[role]`, in any order, so a new or renamed runner tool changes both in one commit. The runner still never imports `packages/cli`, and `packages/cli/package.json` is unchanged, so M2c's own `@agflow/runner` dependency line does not conflict.

- **Behaviour the other plans rely on:**
  - `resume_attempt` does not call `RunnerHealth.admit`; M2c's disk and battery guards stop such a resume at their next evaluation. Respecting battery holds during resume admission remains deferred.
  - A push of an ended attempt's submitted head is no new late work: M2a adds no `late_work` note, holder message or work-position change. Its WIP-ref SHA is recorded for cleanup; a non-WIP ref still produces `attempt.late_work` so retention can find it. Runner push reports remain necessary.
  - `hand_back` refused with `process_running` answers `{ ok: false, error: 'process_running', data: { pids } }`; `deliver` refusals are `stale_fence` or `not_running`; an unreadable command is answered `unsupported`.
  - A final push that moves the WIP ref reports `attempt.wip` before `attempt.exited` or `attempt.taken_over`, so exact outbox sequences after an exit with new work contain it.
  - A WIP push made while the link was down is refused as stale after a plain restart (Known behaviour 1); M2g's restart scenario must expect it.
  - While a live agent's clone is harvested (WIP pushes), its recorded process groups are paused with SIGSTOP and resumed after; `deliver`, `interrupt` and `decide_approval` reach it when the harvest ends (refinement 44).
  - `submit` and `prepare_dependencies` hold the MCP call open for up to `AGFLOW_BRIDGE_POLL_MAX_MS` (3 minutes by default) plus the last GET's 15 s. M2e's `mcp_servers.agflow` must set `tool_timeout_sec` to `ceil(AGFLOW_BRIDGE_POLL_MAX_MS / 1000) + 30` (Known behaviour 5), since Codex's default of 60 s would cut the pending answer short. Claude Code's default MCP tool timeout is long enough.
  - A new test file that uses these fixtures should call `setDefaultTimeout(30_000)` itself before registering hooks; 18 existing M2b files do not yet (Known behaviour 7). `fixture.ts`, `runner-setup.ts`, `hub-fixture.ts` and `fake-hub.ts` do not set it. `waitFor` waits 15 s by default, longer than Bun's own 5 s test limit.
- **M2a settings changes still open**: `reconcileHelloSettings` cannot tell different settings at an equal version on a restored hub, and needs a value comparison or a hub-epoch-qualified version; and the exact-echo protocol change (Known behaviour 3) would also remove the probes' limits.

- **M2c Task 25 integration requirement:** consume `finalizedAt` with `record.spec.role === 'worker' && (LIVE_STATES.includes(record.state) || record.finalizedAt === null)`, while preserving independent pending-SHA protection, error protection with an existing clone, and cleaned-record handling. Finalized synthetic fixtures use a numeric timestamp; crashed records stay null. Enable the normal regression `purge preserves unharvested work after startup recovery and a failed project lookup`, assert recovery leaves `finalizedAt: null`, and retain its exit-1, zero-external-calls, unpublished-file and runner.db-preserved assertions. Revalidate amended task commits, the full suite and Linux CI after any further integration changes. Other public interfaces are unchanged.
